Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple iPhone 14, 128GB, Midnight - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: It has the worst battery life of any iPhone I've ever owned, and I have owned ONLY iPhones since the
Review Content: It has the worst battery life of any iPhone I've ever owned, and I have owned ONLY iPhones since the first version was released 17 years ago. This is the second iPhone 14 that I've bought from the renewed store . The first one I bought on December 4th, 2023, and I could not have been happier with the phone. It arrived in brand new condition, and performed flawlessly. On the recommendation of a friend, I checked the battery health and charging after having it for MONTHS and it was at 100%! I was thrilled! Unfortunately, on July 30 of this year I dropped it, and it was beyond repair. I immediately went back to the Amazon renewed store and purchased another iPhone 14 because my experience with the first one was so fantastic. It arrived in new looking condition, exactly like the one I bought in December 2023. It was not scratched or anything really noticeable, it just seemed to be "worn" a little bit, but I fully understood that it was a renewed phone, and any cosmetic issues were not that important to me, including the color, which, when my iPhone is in its case, you cannot tell what color it is anyway. Unfortunately, I DID NOT look at the battery health and charging when I first got the phone 38 days ago, but I did look at it about two weeks ago, and it said 93%. I thought, ok, it's a renewed phone, it's not going to have 100% battery life. Well, I just looked at it today and it's now at 90% battery health and charging. I have it completely set up for optimized battery life. I have lost emails and messages that I was in the middle of composing, and the phone just dies. I've been in the middle of important phone calls when the phone dies, simply because I had just fully charged it a few hours before that, and thought I would be fine for hours to come. I just had a total shoulder replacement surgery a week ago, and I was on the phone with my doctors office yesterday about my first post-op appointment, and my phone died in the middle of it. I thought I had HOURS left before the phone would die. Then I had to plug it in, and wait for it to come back alive, so I could call my doctor back and hopefully not wait a half hour after losing my place in line. On top of that is also has issues with the touchscreen being glitchy, and sometimes I have to tap on things several times to get them to work. As I said, I have been an iPhone owner/user since the very first version came out 17 years ago. I've always loved all my iPhones, and I will continue to be an iPhone user for the rest of my life. This is in no way reflection on Apple iPhones whatsoever. They are an amazing and fantastic piece of technology. I think I just got a bad one for the first time in my life. Luckily, I have just checked and I have until November 6th to return this phone, and I WILL be returning it. Review Title: I originally got a Renewed/Refurbished iPhone 12, but the battery life was disappointing when compar
Review Content: I originally got a Renewed/Refurbished iPhone 12, but the battery life was disappointing when compared to iPhone 6S Plus. I paid a few bucks more and upgraded to the iPhone 13 Renewed Premium. It was really worth it! A renewed premium/refurbished iPhone 13 has everything you need for a modern smartphone in 2026: 1. One-year warranty/return period with Amazon. It came with a checklist and a list of all the refurbished/replacements done to the device in the Service History in the About screen on the iPhone. I got 100% battery life since the battery and logic board were replaced. 2. It can run iOS 26, which has a lot of cool, quality-of-life features compared to my iPhone 6S Plus: MagSafe wireless charging, StandBy mode to turn it into a desk calendar/clock screen when horizontal and charging with MagSafe, Category grouping in Mail, Face ID unlock is quick and easy to set up and is blazing fast unlocking the iPhone. 3. The 6.1-inch screen and power button did have hairline scratches, but they disappear with a screen protector and a case, so I don't mind. The display still looks great for 60 Hz! I do not play games on my smartphones, so I don't care about it. 1. iPhone 13 is heavier and thicker than the iPhone 12. 2. I don't think the camera focus of either back lens is as sharp as the iPhone 6S Plus. It takes a long time to focus, especially for close-up shots, and boke is not reliable. I am hoping to keep it for another 5 years, as I trust the quality of Apple and its refurbishment partners. Review Title: Two days later my dad called asking for help because the phone was inundated with weird pop ups (min
Review Content: Two days later my dad called asking for help because the phone was inundated with weird pop ups (mind you, I only know what he was able to articulate to me, because when you're close to 80 years old, technology is confusing). He could not answer any calls on the phone. I asked him to wait until I could make another trip to sort the phone out. At that point, the phone started overheating. Impatient, my dad took it to a Verizon store and they told him that the battery was shot, extremely overheated. My dad shut the phone off and let it sit for a while. Fast forward to turning the phone back on and all the same issues kept happening. He couldn't make any calls from the phone and any calls that came in, the phone would not answer them. In frustration over missing calls for two weeks (since we activated the phone), my dad threw it, smashed it and shattered it to smithereens. I clearly couldn't return it for replacement at that point. Probably would have gotten more runaround and aggravation anyway. I've personally had mostly good luck with Amazon pre-owned phones. Unfortunately, this one was a complete loss. It wasn't in the condition that was advertised and showed more visible defects than described and didn't even come with a charging cable. Nothing, just a used and clearly non-functional phone in the box. Dad dug an old flip phone out of the junk drawer and he's using that now and happy as a clam...despite wasting over $200 on this phone and an additional $50 for a case and charging cables that he doesn't need now. I can't recommend the seller that sold this phone. The phone clearly hadn't been tested or inspected. If it had, they would have found the overheating issue immediately. I hate buying phones and avoid it whenever possible. 99% of mine belonged to someone in my family first. And i was good with that. Needless to say, my cat didn’t wait for someone in my family to upgrade. I was on my own this time. Okay.... that’s not entirely true. My grandma had an iPhone 7 sitting around so that held me over in the meantime. Going from an iPhone 11 Pro Max to an iPhone 7 was….bad. It was too dam small, in every possible way. 32 gigs of memory!! I needed an upgrade. Fast. My 11 year old was bullying me relentlessly. And that’s on me. They had my old XR (formerly my dad’s) I scoured FB marketplace. I’d decided upgrade a little, so I could feel better about the switch. I didn’t want to feel backed me into a corner by my cat’s recklessness. I would get a slightly newer model in a fun colour. Marketplace had plenty. Sending message after message from my iPhone 7, I worried. “This person seems too eager”, “this one has been posted so long”, “I want a purple, but the only purple one listed has less storage space” and “the pretty green one has a small crack”, “this guy lives 2 hours from me” and “Battery life? Errr last time I checked it was like 74%?….no, I can’t take a screenshot of it, it’s turned off”…. “cash only please” Etc. So much pressure. What happens if the thing doesn’t work? That’s $300+ down the drain. I knew I couldn’t afford new. But I hated the idea of buying something used from a stranger on Facebook. I didn’t want to get scammed, and I also didn’t want to settle. That’s when I remembered good ol’ Amazon. Maybe I’d check there. Just for funsies. Probably out of my budget, but it couldn’t hurt. Sure enough, refurbished devices selling “like new!” Mostly same cost or less than what I’d found so far. Surely there was a catch? I read through everything, tested by Amazon, includes all the specs, unlocked, I can pick the colour, the storage size, the condition, etc. AND I could have it delivered to me tomorrow??! With a warranty?!! I recovered from my brief stint of disappointment after learning the 12’s don’t come in yellow. Then fought hard to decide between mint and lavender. The lavender would take an extra day to arrive. Mint it was!! As promised, it arrived the next day. It was in beautiful shape. 128g’s, mint green, not a single scratch, 86% battery life. All for less than I would have paid to some stranger for a 64g with some “small scratches” Once my case and screen protector arrived I excitedly set it up and synced my data. After becoming used to facial recognition, having that yanked away, and dealing with a 7 for over 2 weeks— I was desperate for the convenience of Face ID. I had been using my fingerprint. Like a *caveman*. Not to mention I have Blink 182 tickets, and it specifically states facial recognition is required to access the mobile tickets. Idk if that’s true, but I needed Face ID!! I googled, I contacted apple support. Fixing it could be upwards of $300. That’s almost what I paid for the whole phone!! I realllllly didn’t want to be stuck without a phone again. But I also wanted one fully functioning. So I reached out to Amazon support and explained. The rep was incredibly helpful (as most Amazon reps are) and after bts failed, she advised the ship was a 3rd party seller, and she send a message to them. “If they don’t fix it by (insert date) contact us back and we’ll make this right” she encouraged. I’m ngl. I was nervous. I didn’t have high hopes, having dealt with 3p sellers on Amazon in the past. At least Amazon had my back, ig. The concert wasn’t till July. Even without facial recognition, it was loads better than the 7. I could make do in the meantime. The seller came in clutch though, and my worry was unwarranted. They responded within minutes. They were receptive, apologetic, and more than willing to help. As I’d anticipated, they offered a refund or exchange, as soon as they received the return. I explained my concern with not having a phone for several days or more; and the merchant offered to overnight a replacement as soon as the return was dropped off. I could deal with one day without a phone! I gratefully accepted. That was Saturday night, we made plans to catch up Monday for the return instructions and for them to overnight it. Monday I reached back out; and they were ready to ship, BUT they *had no more green….* 🫢 SHOCK THIS WAS A HUGE BUMMER.It’s silly I know, and the definition of *first world problems “.. but I mean…. My change of heart about this whole phone thing HINGED ON THE FUN COLOUR. Without it, I was just a person…out $350… because my cat was thirsty while I was watching YouTube while washing dishes. I needed a cool colour. Plus, I’d already gotten the matching case! Clear with mint green borders. It wasn’t even a fun blue… it was a dark, serious, navy blue. It was pretty and classy, but I wanted something fun. I even asked if he had any older models in yellow 😭😭 no luck, They told me they’d be restocking in a day or so. Still, no greens or purples came in. Ugh. Reality was setting in. I was going to have to settle. It was fine, I thought. At least it would be a fully functioning phone. No. I wasn’t ready to let go. They assured me I could take my time to decide, and I asked if we could wait another week in case one came in. If it didn’t, *then* I would choose from the options available. I messaged them Wednesday afternoon, bracing myself for the answer…. THEY GOT IN PURPLE! YAY. They sent a label, I dropped it off, sent a photo, and had my new phone the next morning. they’d said overnight shipping… but wow! I’d dropped off the return around 3pm, and had the replacement by noon the next day. I didn’t even have my new case yet 😅 Despite the Barney-Esque colour scheme my mint green case created, the lavender is GORGEOUS and I’m actually sort of glad the green didn’t work out. Don’t get me wrong, the green is also gorgeous.. but in the end I’m glad I ended up with the lavender. I was overjoyed when I was prompted to set Face ID during setup. Worked brilliantly, as did everything else. Great packaging, no cosmetic flaws, amazing battery life, customer service was great, and best of all… ITS PURPLE! Can’t wait to pair it with the new case. I’m so glad I went this route where I have some peace of mind as a buyer. I’m grateful to the seller for being so helpful and patient with me as insufferable as I must have seemed making such a fuss over colour preference If you’re nervous buying a phone used or refurbished too, hopefully you can take comfort in knowing- this seller is legit. You receive a good quality product, and, speaking from experience, they’ll gladly help resolve any issues you may run into. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple AirPods Pro - 1st Gen (Renewed) : Electronics
Review Title: However, this is the first time I’ve ever purchased a used/refurbished/ renewed pair
Review Content: However, this is the first time I’ve ever purchased a used/refurbished/ renewed pair. But since I lose them all the time, I thought it may be a cost effective option for me. Unfortunately, my device was defective out of the box! My Airpods Pro didn’t come with all of the materials that come in the original box and the charger I received [packaged separately] was not even an apple brand. This didn’t bother me much, as I have more than enough accessories for this item. The device itself appeared clean and undamaged. When I opened the device to check the battery status, it was dead [Apple has a policy of not sending their devices fully charged for shipping safety reasons, so I assumed the previous owner received the item new and returned them without charging it more]. I connected the airpods to my OFFICIAL Apple charger from a previous device and the battery light immediately glowed green. Confused, I then proceeded to pair it to my phone. The first attempt was successful. I checked my battery notification screen on my iPhone and the airpods case displayed a full 100% charge, yet the airpods themselves were each dead at 1%. After a few seconds of charge, they reached 7% [charging speed rare, but not completely unheard of], so I took the case off the charger and went to test out the sound quality. As soon as I took an earpiece out- the entire device went off. The case and pods still read as charging on my phone even though I had removed them from charging moments before. I could not find the devise in my drop menu, so I went into settings to manually pair the AirPods again- but they wouldn’t sync. After 4/5 times connecting and forgetting device, I attempted to reattach the charger- NOW the AirPods case is on 0% but the earpieces are both on 13% 🙄. As soon as I plug them back in, the airpods sync again and I am able to hear the pairing chime on my earpiece. SECONDS LATER the airpods die and the phone shows they are on 0% *charging* WHILE they are still in my ears! Like I said, I’ve had a ton of airpods, I know how to troubleshoot most any problem they give me. I’ve never had to deal with this kind of headache before- ESPECIALLY on day 1. I’m so over it! I’m going to an Apple store first thing in the morning. This was a horrible experience. Review Title: I bought this for one main, directed purpose: to use Sonos' TruePlay function to calibrate my old So
Review Content: I bought this for one main, directed purpose: to use Sonos' TruePlay function to calibrate my old Sonos system after a major move (the TruePlay is only available on iOS), At the time, I was also considering using it as a "home remote" kind of thing instead of cluttering up my main phone, but pretty much the only role has been my main go-to interface for Sonos as well as being a 2nd eSim home phone. I prefer keeping my main cell phone on mute whenever I am home (lots of junk calls), but for those calls I really, really want to always catch, particularly my bosses (lol), I decided to activate a line through this phone. Since the thing is always home, usually by my bedside while my main phone is in the living room, charging, it nicely fits the desire. Only had to use it a few times as an actual phone, but no issues. I did buy a MagSafe case (pretty cheap) and use my Ugreen Magsafe charger for it. Works a charm every time. No issues with anything at all, in fact. It functions without problems or hiccupping irritations... yet, again, this isn't a workhorse for me, but a QOL convenience. So yes, my usage probably doesn't mirror most, yet for those who are looking just for a lowkey, hang-about 2nd smartphone without breaking the bank (or contract), I am quite happy with it. It lets me sleep knowing that if I hear a phone ringing, it's going to be something *very* important about the lab. Review Title: Delivery was very good
Review Content: Delivery was very good. I saw it was shipped on the 25th. On the 30th, I received an SMS from DHL saying they planned delivery on Oct. 3rd, but on the same day I got an email asking for copy of national ID and content description for clearing customs. I am not a Morocco residents nor citizen, so I sent my foreign passport instead. On the 3rd, Amazon tracking info said clearing custom was delayed as additional documents were needed. So I called DHL, and the rep said it would be delivered on the 4th instead. On the 4th, I saw a newly posted message about delay on Amazon tracking. I called DHL various times but couldn't get to anyone. I then sent an inquiry by email and get a response shortly saying it was being taking care of. Then late afternoon, I got the package. Upon arriving, the seal of the packing had an opening large enough to put in a hand but not for getting the phone out, so I didn't complain. Unpacked, the inner packing of the phone was in excellent condition, very much like the original packing but had no Samsung marking, rather, it had a marking of "amazonrenewed". There was a film covering the screen, like on a new phone. The phone appeared in excellent condition, only had a small scratch at the back when I looked in detail, and a hair of scratch on the screen that is only visible under bright light and in a particular angle. I tried but couldn't turn on the phone - there was no response. The box also included a USB-C cable and a cheap non-Samsung charger made in China. I used my own Samsung Charger to charge the phone. After plugged in, it showed the battery was at 0. So I let it charge to full. After started, it turned out fully unlocked. My Morocco sim card works with 4G. The phone's software looked already reset, but I reset it myself anyhow. Then updated to the latest system with Android 12, and loaded many apps I need. During about the first week, the battery appeared quite poor. With medium usage it lasted about a day. I tried all necessary settings to conserve battery, but it didn't seem to help much. These couple days, it becomes much better, lasting about 45 hours. I read it was likely due to some AI processes either from Android 12 or Samsung doing the learning work at first. But it's pretty bad the phone doesn't show any info. I would say I am very happy with the phone. And this is after having a terrible experience in the past with Samsung. The last Samsung phone I had was S7 Edge bought in Thailand (I am a traveler), new at a Samsung store for perhaps ~$800. I actually wanted the normal S7 (without the "edge"), but it was out of stock then. I never liked the "edge", it was a silly design in my mind. The phone worked well initially, but in the coming couple of years I had a terrible experience. About 5 months later when I was in Vietnam, the screen started to show shaded bands across. As I was wondering how or if I should return to Thailand to get the phone serviced, the bands disappeared after a month. Then about another 7 months later when I was in Azerbaijan, the phone couldn't start after I did a system update. So I couldn't use the phone for a couple weeks until I reached Tbilisi in Georgia when I had someone flashed it. About a year later, it died on me again when I was in Morocco. I had someone re-flashed it, but it was not successful. About 1 month later I reached the city of Fes where there is a Samsung service center. After checking, they said there was something wrong with the motherboard. Very shocking! I've never had such problem in my life with all the phones and computers, cheap or dear, and this was a flagship! So eventually, I sold it to a local repair shop for $200, for which they said they only needed the screen. That was end of 2017. So I never bought a Samsung again, and would definitely not buy one at the full price. I admit the S series is not worthless. At least, I like the camera. But I never had a chance to buy one at a largely reduced price (I won't buy from just any second-hand sellers). So now, the Amazon reviewed phone with some warranty got me interested. Yes, I have some risk, but to me with the past experience, the risk is not much higher than getting a new phone from Samsung, plus, I am putting in a much lower bet now. Review Title: From the moment you lay eyes on the Galaxy S21, it’s evident that Samsung has crafted a device meant
Review Content: From the moment you lay eyes on the Galaxy S21, it’s evident that Samsung has crafted a device meant for the high-end market. The sleek contours and premium materials give it an unmistakable aura of luxury. The 6.2-inch Dynamic AMOLED display is nothing short of breathtaking, offering vibrant colors, deep blacks, and impressive brightness levels. Whether you are streaming your favorite series or scrolling through social media, every experience is elevated by this stunning showcase of visual brilliance. Underneath the hood, the Galaxy S21 5G is powered by the latest Exynos or Snapdragon chipset (depending on your region), ensuring lightning-fast performance for multitasking and gaming alike. The device handles everything with remarkable ease, and the inclusion of 5G capabilities means you can harness incredibly fast download and upload speeds. With options for up to 256GB of storage and 8GB of RAM, you won't find yourself wanting for space or speed. Samsung’s camera system is one of the standout features of the S21. The triple-lens setup, including a 12MP ultra-wide, a 12MP wide, and a 64MP telephoto lens, allows users to capture stunning images in various conditions. The Night Mode is particularly impressive, ensuring that low-light photos are as crisp as those taken in bright daylight. The addition of advanced video features, including 8K recording, cements the Galaxy S21’s status as a powerhouse for mobile photography enthusiasts. While the battery life is generally sufficient to get through a full day with moderate use, heavy users may find themselves reaching for a charger by late afternoon. The 4000mAh battery powers some serious capabilities, but if you plan on extensively utilizing 5G and the phone's camera, be prepared for a potential drop in endurance. Fast charging and wireless charging options are a plus, but the slightly underwhelming battery performance keeps the S21 from achieving a perfect score. Herein lies the crux of the matter—while the Samsung Galaxy S21 5G dazzles with features, performance, and design, it comes at a steep price. For many, this puts it out of reach, especially considering the current market of other high-quality smartphones that offer comparable features at a lower cost. The premium branding does lend a certain prestige, but that may not be enough to sway budget-conscious consumers.

Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple AirPods Pro (2nd Generation) (Renewed) : Electronics
Review Title: So, when I received these, I did not imagine it being boxed nicely
Review Content: So, when I received these, I did not imagine it being boxed nicely. But was I dead wrong. When I opened the Amazon packaging, I saw an Apple AirPods Pro boxed sealed and in pristine condition. I unwrapped it and opened the box and it was like opening a box for a pair of brand new AirPods. Everything down to the cable was properly placed and the headphones along with the case didn’t even look like they had been touched! AND THESE ARE RENEWED! It’s like I bought a pair brand new for less amount of money. A4C Online is absolutely amazing for how they packaged this product and the condition of these renewed AirPods Pro is beyond my belief. I truly didn’t expect the quality I received. As for the headphones themselves, jaw dropping amazement. From the noise cancellation, to the quality of the headphones, it’s all amazing. The noise cancellation is beyond belief. I set these up, put them in my ears while I listened to my fan, and turned on noise cancellation. Boom. The sound of the fan disappeared, like magic! The noise cancellation doesn’t block out every loud noise like movies, but it’s much better than anything I’ve ever used. Transparency is wonderful and definitely allows me to hear around me while I still listen to the music or video I’m listening to. I’m not sure if their are better headphones out there that do transparency better, but seeing how I’ve never seen headphones have this kind of feature, it’s definitely one of the reasons I bought these, especially so I can be at work and keep both headphones in without having to just leave one in so I may listen to what’s around me. The sound quality is crystal clear and makes me hear more of the music than I ever thought I could. The spatial sound turns music into a surround sound experience that was way better than I expected. The spatial sound was a little hard to setup, but that may just be because I’m an idiot. May take a few times, but you’ll get it eventually if you have the same problems I had. So far using these headphones, the only bad thing I can say about them is that the bass might be a little lower than I expected? But it’s not a big deal to me as I enjoy more of the quality of the sound rather than heavy bass, so if you really need to have heavy bass in your headphones, these might not be for you. As for the battery life, I haven’t had them long enough to know how well they are especially since these are also renewed. Thank you A4C Online for these wonderful headphones. I still cannot believe these are renewed headphones and am so glad I bought these from you! Thanks again. If you’re looking for a pair of AirPod Pros, you’re definitely making the right choice buying from them. The battery life is quite decent. After about 4 or 5 hours the battery life will drop to about 75%. Much more than I expected from a renewed product. Transparency is not as affective as I had originally thought. I have to turn down my music if I want to be able to hear anyone else. I wish they made it so you could increase the transparency to be louder otherwise I have to keep my music down low. Otherwise an excellent product still and I recommend buying these renewed AirPods.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

(I ordered another pair to see if every pair had that issue, but the second pair worked fine.) So I tried returning the first pair that was defective. Amazon was helpful in starting the return process, and I returned the AirPods in the same condition in which I received them. However, I NEVER got a refund. It's been 4 months. I called Customer Service 5 separate times, and each time they instructed me to fill out an appeal form. I did this multiple times, and even a couple customer service agents issued appeals from their end. But nothing came of it. With each appeal, I received an automated response saying that they can't issue a refund because they received a damaged item, but that's exactly why I returned it in the first place! They said I returned the item in a different condition than I received it, which is untrue and I've wasted hours trying to explain this but the customer service agents can't do anything about it. I'm not sure if it got damaged along the way back or if the people who process returns are just too unwilling to admit they've made a mistake. But either way, Amazon received my product worth $162.18, and I never saw a penny of the refund. They essentially stole from me by not holding up their end of the return deal, and not even offering to send the product back to me. This makes me very wary to order from Amazon Renewed again, and quite frustrated at their unwillingness to understand. Amazon, you are sitting on trillions of dollars. I don't care what budget it comes from, but I'd appreciate if you could spare $162.18 to one long-time customer who really wants to keep believing that Amazon has great customer service. Please make this right. NOTE: If I hear back from Amazon and get a full refund, I will edit my review to reflect the good pair I got instead of this bad experience... not to mention have my faith in their refund policy restored. Review Title: Next, the quality of the AirPods
Review Content: Next, the quality of the AirPods. They sound amazing. According to the app on the iPhone the large tips work best with my ears and form the best seal. I paid $171 for this refurbished set and that deal is amazing for what you get. The build quality makes me feel that with a little care these will last for years in my ears. Review Title: First and foremost, the sound quality of the AirPods Pro 2nd Gen is outstanding
Review Content: First and foremost, the sound quality of the AirPods Pro 2nd Gen is outstanding. The audio is crisp, clear, and immersive, allowing me to fully appreciate my favorite music, podcasts, and movies. The active noise cancellation feature is a game-changer, effectively blocking out unwanted background noise and allowing me to focus on what I'm listening to. The transparency mode is also impressive, seamlessly blending the surrounding sounds with my audio for enhanced awareness. Comfort is another area where the AirPods Pro excel. The earbuds come with three different sizes of silicone tips, allowing for a customized and secure fit. They sit comfortably in my ears, and I can wear them for extended periods without any discomfort. The lightweight design adds to the overall comfort, making them a pleasure to use throughout the day. The integration with the Apple ecosystem is seamless and convenient. Setting up the AirPods Pro with my iPhone was a breeze, and the automatic pairing and connection feature is incredibly convenient. The earbuds intelligently switch between my devices, whether it's my iPhone, iPad, or MacBook, ensuring a seamless transition without any manual intervention. Additionally, the hands-free "Hey Siri" functionality is a game-changer, allowing me to control my music or make calls with just my voice. Battery life is impressive on the AirPods Pro. They provide around 4.5 hours of continuous listening time, and with the charging case, I can extend it to more than 24 hours. The quick charging feature is a lifesaver, providing me with about an hour of listening time with just a 5-minute charge. This is perfect for those times when I'm in a hurry and need a quick boost of battery power. Choosing the refurbished option for the AirPods Pro 2nd Gen was a great decision. They look and function like new, and I appreciate the cost savings compared to buying them brand new. Apple's refurbishing process ensures that the product meets high standards, and I haven't experienced any issues or concerns with the refurbished pair I received. In terms of convenience, the AirPods Pro's wireless charging case is a game-changer. It allows me to charge the earbuds effortlessly using Qi-compatible wireless chargers, eliminating the need for cables and making charging a hassle-free experience. The case itself is compact and easy to carry, protecting the earbuds when not in use. Overall, I am thoroughly impressed with the Apple AirPods Pro 2nd Gen (Refurbished). Their exceptional sound quality, comfortable fit, seamless integration, and convenient features make them a top-tier wireless earbud option. Whether you're an Apple enthusiast or simply looking for a premium audio experience, these refurbished AirPods Pro deliver on all fronts. Don't hesitate to get your hands on them and enjoy a truly immersive and wireless listening experience. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple iPhone 11, 64GB, Black - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: ##### Better Than I Expected for a Refurbished Phone
Review Content: ##### Better Than I Expected for a Refurbished Phone I picked this up as a backup phone, so I wasn’t expecting it to be perfect. Since it’s an older model, I figured it would probably have some scratches or small dents, but nope... this baby was in way better shape than I expected. The screen looked really good, and I had to actually look closely to find any signs that it had been used. I did put a screen protector and case on it right away because, once I saw the condition it came in, I wanted to keep it that way. Another impressive thing was how easy it was to get everything set up. It powered on with no issues, and transferring my stuff from my old phone was pretty simple. Everything has been running smoothly so far, and I haven’t noticed any overheating, even while setting it up, downloading apps, and using it for a while. And oh man, talk about the screen size. It’s big enough for browsing, watching videos, and reading without making the phone feel huge or awkward to hold. The phone size is actually pretty comfortable, and it still feels durable enough for everyday use. The battery life is not the same as a brand-new iPhone, but that’s expected with a refurbished phone. It still gets me through a normal day, which is really all I needed. For the price and the condition it came in, I’d say it was a solid deal. [More](javascript:void(0))[Hide](javascript:void(0)) There was a problem filtering reviews. Please reload the page.

Review Title: I was hesitant about buying a renewed phone, but decided to give it a shot on Amazon since their ret
Review Content: I was hesitant about buying a renewed phone, but decided to give it a shot on Amazon since their return policy is pretty good and I gotta say, I’m genuinely impressed with this device. I got the “Renewed Premium” version. The phone came unlocked, so I was able to activate it on T-Mobile with zero issues. It arrived in excellent condition and has performed flawlessly. The phone is practically pristine. There’s a tiny scratch on the screen that’s only visible when you look closely, but you can’t see it while using the phone, so it’s not an issue for daily use. The body, back, and all edges are in great condition with no other visible imperfections. The battery arrived at 100% health with only 1 cycle count, which is basically new. I ran the full iOS diagnostics test and everything passed: the battery, sensors, camera, display, speakers, microphone, and all other hardware components checked out perfectly. No hardware issues whatsoever. I did have to switch to a 30W Apple charger since my old third-party one wasn’t powerful enough, but that’s a minor inconvenience. Paired with the USB-C cable that comes with the phone, it charges really quickly and the battery life is excellent, lasting me the whole day. Review Title: They came to me in a small cardboard box that was unmarked
Review Content: They came to me in a small cardboard box that was unmarked. Fine, I get it they were refurbished. But not even a little bit of bubble wrap to keep them broom banging around the entire time they were in transit? I work for fed ex I know how stuff gets knocked around. Came with a charger cord which is cool except it was a usb-c and I ordered a pair of lightning port AirPods sooooo yeah. The sound quality was what you would expect if you took a tin can, tied a string to it and had someone scream into it from another tin can tied to the other end of the string. I tried to have a conversation with my husband and he could register approximately one out of every 4 words I said. When he spoke, it sounded like he had a mouthful of dry crackers. So the sound quality was trash. None of the controls on the pods worked. Volume? Nope. One push mute? Also nope. I went into the app to make sure *I* wasn’t the problem and also nope. So that was a fail. The battery also was terrible. Two hours max per pod. This is my third set of pods (I’m on my phone A LOT) and I’ve never seen battery deplete so quickly. Not only that but there was NO WARNING before they just died. Normally you get two heads up warnings that your battery is depleting. Not so with this pair. After 2 hours of use just BOOM dead. So mid conversation I had to scramble to remember where I had left my phone or while I was at work I had to stop what I was doing to change out the pod. Just a mess all around. I had gotten a refurb phone so I thought this would be a great way to save a little bit of cash while also cutting down on electronics waste but this was just trash from one end to the other. And let’s not forget the return procedure. It used to be a simple act of taking them to one of the return places in my area. Drop them off, get my money back. Simple. Now, I have to box them up, print a label and BE HOME for UPS to come get them. What a headache, since as I said I work for fed ex M-F. I’m heading to Best Buy to get a new pair of these and give myself a break from this whole trashy experience. Unpaid Balances: The phone may be linked to an unpaid bill or financial obligation, which also leads to its blacklisting. Activation Issues: Carriers will not allow activation of a blacklisted device, making it unusable for calls, texts, or data services. Purchasing a phone with a blacklisted ESN can lead to significant issues: Immediate Deactivation: The phone may initially activate but will stop working shortly after. Review Title: Let me first state the bad experience I dealt with this watch
Review Content: Let me first state the bad experience I dealt with this watch. When I first received this watch came with some random “smart watch” box doesn’t come with the original Apple box, it also comes with 2 cheap unofficial Apple products which is a charger and wrist band. I’ve heard in the reviews the chargers don’t charge properly with this Apple Watch and it’s true it doesn’t and the band breaks easily, luckily I had an actual solid charger to charge this watch since it also came straight up dead no charge at all, so I was like “okay no big deal” just let it charge for a few mins Apple Watches should always charge quick as they say. 5 mins passes by the watch finally turns on and I was looking to pair it with my phone, it was going well until it was time to update and I left it there so it can update there was like 2 updates to this Apple Watch so i let the first update go, and it just kept repeating and repeating like it was not updating so I had to literally stay on my watch and see it update but it took SOO LONG it was pissing me off until it finally did the first update now the second update required my phone to stay at least 50% charge or it can stay on the charger while it update. So I did that, I let my watch sit on the charge and it kept telling me AGAIN to make sure my watch is at least on 50% charge or stay on the charger while updating but none of that worked at all meaning my watch was on the charger and it still kept telling me to keep it charged if it’s not at least 50%, so I left it there for at least 20 minutes. 20 minutes passes by and it’s barely 20%!!! I was already looking to refunding this watch already and while it was charging I was looking at reviews having the same issue. Finally 1 hour and 20 minutes it’s 50% and the second update started thank goodness, when everything was done I finally paired it to my phone but battery was not good at all so I was still thinking on refunding this watch since I had to spend more on battery change. But what can I say the watch was smooth, screen and edges were clean clean no damage but my issue was just the battery but I had faith in this watch so I just kept it. After a week of wearing this watch, the battery slowly started getting solid, it charges quicker now first time I charged it yes it did heat up a lot but it’s normal after all the updates it received and to this day no it doesn’t heat that much no more in fact after charging it all night the next morning my watch is on 100% cool not heated up and lasts longer. After a 12 hour shift the battery still is holding at 80% I was shocked at the performance and the watch itself is just beautiful, Siri worked, my calls went through. Though this is still a risk on buying since not everybody has the same performance, I’m guessing my watch was just not updated and turned on for a while that i received a bad experience the first time I got it. I’d say stay patience and see it slowly work. Sorry, we failed to record your vote. Please try again Sorry, We failed to report this review. Please try again

Review Title: First off, the sound quality is crisp
Review Content: First off, the sound quality is crisp. Music, podcasts, even phone calls—everything comes through clear without that “cheap headphone” feel. Now, because they’re renewed, I did go in with realistic expectations. They didn’t come in fancy packaging, but they looked clean and worked perfectly right out of the box. Battery life has been good so far, and I haven’t had any connectivity issues. If you’re trying to save money but still want that Apple experience, these are definitely worth it. Just make sure you’re buying from a reliable seller. I’d buy them again. Review Title: I’ve been using the Samsung Galaxy A14 5G for a while now, and I’m honestly very impressed with what
Review Content: I’ve been using the Samsung Galaxy A14 5G for a while now, and I’m honestly very impressed with what it offers for the price. The phone looks modern and feels solid in the hand, with a nice large display that’s perfect for watching videos, browsing social media, and everyday use. Performance has been smooth for my daily tasks like calls, messages, apps, banking, and streaming. It handles multitasking better than I expected for a budget-friendly device. The 5G connectivity is also a big plus—it provides fast internet speeds when I’m out and about, which makes streaming and downloads much quicker. The battery life is one of my favorite features. It easily lasts me a full day (and sometimes more) without needing to recharge, even with regular use. That’s a huge advantage if you’re busy or travel often. Charging time is reasonable, and I like not having to worry about carrying a charger everywhere. The camera does a really good job for the price range. Photos come out sharp in good lighting, and the different camera modes are fun to use. It’s great for casual pictures, social media posts, and video calls. Setup was simple, the phone came unlocked, and it worked perfectly with my carrier. Overall, I think this is an excellent smartphone for anyone looking for reliability, modern features, and 5G capability without spending a fortune. Definitely a great value purchase—I would recommend it to family and friends. Review Title: Meaning to improve something continuously and by that making gradually worse and eventually useless
Review Content: Meaning to improve something continuously and by that making gradually worse and eventually useless. In our "update mania" world this here is a classic case. The phone has a way to sensitive touchscreen and no matter what you try from the gazillion settings there is only one to increase the sensitivity but not to decrease it! You can search online that issue. Tests I did show that the touchscreen responds when the finger is actually is not touching the screen but is 0.5- 1mm ( 1/52" - 2/52") away from it! This leads of course to an absurd overreaction when you handle the phone, even with the palm protection on, it reacts unintentionally. Often even it responses before you have actually touched anything simply because you moved your finger without touching the screen! Then there is the OS, by now Android 14. Another effort to overload an overdo many functions and poorly organize them. all of course in the eternal other obsession "security". The [settings] interface is not intuitive and straightforward anymore like it used to be in older android OSs. Whereas like in earlier versions you could customize and prioritize which icon functions you wanted where, that no longer seems to be possible. And then of course the confirmation pop-up window mania. Say you want to turn something off or delete a message/email. You have to go on a regular basis through three confirmations! DUH? Say you select an email or SMS and click on delete, then it asks you first if you want to delete it, and then and then again were you wanted deleted to and finally you need to confirm that! Really? Seriously? notwithstanding that the new and improved absolutely outlandish privacy terms and all other terms all of them with their 10,000 links to other terms about terms and privacy etc. blah blah... I really feel being raped on a daily basis. Furthermore for some reason despite larger screen all the fonts are smaller but layout spacing is larger with more wasted space. (yes I tried the font sizing). Total useless another feature is, that you can choose from an endless variety of different fonts... Any app you start needs a gazillion confirmations requesting permission to give access to this and that, here and there etc. etc. Overall straightforward sensible layout of the interface and functionality is gone. Before I upgraded to this phone I had a Samsung S5 with OS Android 6.01. Everything worked fine I never had an issue SMS and MMS sent out instantaneously and everything else worked. Of course with new apps the phone became, aside from artificial incompatibilities, slower and slower. P part of a marketing ploy probably. Now I have a Samsung A14 5G with Android 14. MMS take much longer and needs two or three confirmations... And when executing a functioning in an app, next time I open the app I have to navigate back as it doesn't go back like previously by default. There's more but that would take up too much space to writeup here. Remember the peaceful relaxed time when we had a Bell telephone and a typewriter? We were able to communicate and even managed to fly two men to the moon and bring them safely back... Review Title: ##### Remanufacturado: Excelencia y Funcionalidad a un Precio Asequible
Review Content: ##### Remanufacturado: Excelencia y Funcionalidad a un Precio Asequible La capacidad de 128GB puede ser una gran limitante si consideramos la ausencia de una bandeja de expansión por medio de microSD, especialmente cuando se trata de buena calidad de fotografías y videos que demandan mayor capacidad de almacenamiento. Esto te obliga a ser más ordenado y a depurar entre las cientos de fotos que puedas tomar, utilizar almacenamiento en la nube, entre otras opciones. Si tienes control en ello, puede ser más que suficiente. Afortunadamente, este equipo dispone aún de actualizaciones, lo cual es un punto que me forzó a abandonar mi anterior equipo, aun encontrándose en buen estado. Seguramente algo así ocurrirá con este. Cargarlo sin protección de un case puede ser tentador, ya que deja a la vista su diseño elegante. Sin embargo, puede resultar riesgoso ya que es bastante resbaladizo. Minimamente se recomienda algún protector de pantalla. En mi caso, adquirí un case de uso rudo con una especie de imán que me ha resultado bastante práctico para colocar el equipo en distintas áreas e incluso en la carrocería del auto para tomar fotos a distancia. Por último, al comprar este tipo de equipos puede que te den un cargador compatible, algo que te será de utilidad si tomamos en cuenta que la marca ya no lo incluye. Otro punto a considerar es revisar el estado en el que se encuentra, el cual se indica en la sección de ofertas. En mi caso, elegí uno que se encontraba en "excelentes condiciones". Otro detalle en contra es que el "duende azul" aun no dispone de eSIM para el equipo y dado a que es extranjero la reparación, asi como el uso de esta tecnologia estara limitada en México, por otro lado, sin mayor complejidad. Review Title: ##### Great condition! UNLOCKED, one issue called a network unlock code, read review!!
Review Content: ##### Great condition! UNLOCKED, one issue called a network unlock code, read review!! I took photos of the phone the day of arrival but now cant find them.. but the phone came in EXCELLENT condition although the packaging was just a box with little to ensure a safe delivery. The phone was unlocked but a **NETWORK UNLOCK CODE** kept popping up when sim card was insterted. (Thats the photo in this review.) So I swore the phone wasnt unlocked. Reached out to the seller and my carrier which was walmart family mobile. I was told by my carrier i needed a new sim card. So i ordered it and when it finally arrived, boom same error. My carrier reset the sim many times and still no luck. When i had messaged the seller they gave me a code that wasnt right and when i reached out again, still another wrong code. What the phone fails to warn you is that only after a few attempts it will lock you out completely. It will then say **MASTER KEY CODE** needed. I googled what that was and it seemed like a hopeless code to obtain. The startup on the phone says AT & T. So i took it to their store and they had said that yes the phone was unlocked!! But the network was locked to walmart family mobile which was my carrier . So come to find out the code i needed, the first code, the network unlock code, I needed from my carrier! They absolutely missed it and after days of this mess and ongoing phone calls, finally the walmart family mobile agent on that day in the At&T store had told me the codes i needed from day one. Idk how they just skipped the option and blamed my sim card. The codes arent a secret and im still unsure why they didnt recommend theirs to fix it. I guess they just assumed it wasnt their codes needed. But it was!!! Unbelievable right!! So then were now stuck on master key code and no one, my carrier, nor AT&T, nor samsung can help with that. Due to the sellers wrong codes, me googling the wrong codes, and most of all my carriers support line not mentioning their codes, I was locked out and was gonna return the phone. However AT&T did show me other sim cards put into the phone by other carriers were working. It was still unlocked but just couldnt now be used on family mobile and possibly all tracphone carriers due to the master key code lock. So with that said I swapped to AT&T prepaid and got their sim card and it all worked great! It was recommended to get the sim card from the AT&T store directly because sometimes those sim kits at walmart dont always work correctly and are nonrefundable. So if this issue happens to you just be sure to ask your carrier for those network codes!! The seller now knows what to suggest if this happens to another and I'm telling you that the carrier has the codes and all will be fine. Also the seller offered me a replacement phone and partial refund for this issue. I declined a replacement only because I couldnt send this phone back and await a new one. I was already without a phone long enough dealing with this for days. So the seller at least still gave me a partial refund and that was okay with me. So the customer service is well and fair from them!!! Also even AT&T said the phone itself was in such great shape! So far so good on the phone itself, everything is working as it should. In my research, I have determined that they most likely simply didn't put a new seal on the phone when putting it back together. That, my friends, is a crappy 'renew' job. I don't recommend others buy these simply because they are so poorly repaired... unless you able to fix them. Then go for it. Review Title: The included cable (no brick included) does NOT charge my phone
Review Content: The included cable (no brick included) does NOT charge my phone. They included a very cheap-o charging cable & this phone is PICKY! Actually I found ALL Samsung phones that we have/ have tried are... they only accept a USB C cable with a thicker wall to the plug in part. Any of the cheapo cables will NOT work. On the plus side, I was able to determine that this phone came with 92% battery life by using the ACU battery app...which was a huge concern for me buying a used phone. That was a happy relief! The camera is pretty nice! I tried & returned a brand new A23 before buying this used phone, and that camera was absolutely horrible.. worse than my very first LG cell phone that I got 8 years ago... yes, WORSE than that! After seeing what a piece of junk the A23 was & after talking to someone at the T-Mobile store, they told me that the A series phones are very bottom of the barrel and poor quality. I came to the realization that in order to get a phone that was decent, I was going to have to buy a used phone. I opted for the S20 FE instead of the S21, because the s20 is able to be expanded with a microSD card & the S21 can't be. I am not about to put all my stuff on some cloud or pay for extra storage. I opted out of an iPhone for that very reason. If Samsung doesn't allow for storage cards to expand their phones' memories in the future, I will buy a different brand that does. After reading several reviews, I know there are others who feel the same way. I sure hope Samsung listens & doesn't go the disappointing route Apple does with their phones & lack of storage expansion. Overall, I'm happy with my used phone & the seller, minus the fact that they didn't even check to see if the charging cable worked that they sent with the phone. It did not & I had to buy new ones just for this phone. I WOULD purchase the phone again, although I'm not super fond of such a finicky phone in regards to the charging cable. I know it's a Samsung thing because my hubby's old S8 is the same as was the A23 I tried & returned. I don't like feeling like I have to carry a spare charging cable with me everywhere in the event that my main charging cable doesn't work with my phone for some reason. I never had that issue with my other brand USB C charged phones. Samsung phones seem to only work with cables that have a thicker wall to the C part of the charging cable. If LG was still making phones, I would have purchased one of those instead. We've tried TCL & Motorola...& Apple is a hard pass, so that left me with Samsung. Review Title: The phone was not damaged in any way
Review Content: The phone was not damaged in any way. It looked like a brand new phone, right out of the box! Not only that, but it functions flawlessly. I don't use all of the features (and it has a lot of them), mostly because I don't do social media stuff, or take many pictures. However, taking pictures is absolutely amazing! There are sooooo many options: like filters, colors, cropping, picture size, frame size, etc. There's just a ton of them. There is also Biometric features, which I appreciate. I had the S9+ and the fingerprint reader was on the back. If you use the fingerprint feature on this phone, make sure you set a passcode or pin as well. The fingerprint reader is on the screen. It shows as a pop-up. Of course you have to go through the fingerprint set-up first, and can choose more than one finger/thumb. My concern is that if the screen gets damaged where the reader is, the screen probably wouldn't be able to be able to read your print. It does NOT have an iris scanner. This IS a 5G phone, but it can connect to 4G and other networks as well. I believe there might have been a SIM card, but I honestly don't remember. I took the SIM from my other phone and put it in this one, so I didn't need it anyway. I use AT&T pre-paid, and it works fine. Right out of the box. I don't know if it's unlocked to a variety of different network or service providers. My service provider is AT&T, and the phone I got from this seller is also AT&T. My recommendation to anyone considering purchasing this phone, would be to contact the seller, first and ask about supported service providers. If you have AT&T, it's a total win! :) This phone charges super fast, and the battery life is fabulous. For my usage, anyway. You absolutely have to use a fast charging cable, or you'll ruin your phone. I believe it came with a USB cable, but I can't remember if the block was included. Either way, if you need to get a charging block, and/or cable, MAKE SURE they're fast charging!!! I thought the cable it came with was too short for my needs, so I bought a new one on Amazon that is specifically for the S23+...and phones like it. Another recommendation I have is to get an Otterbox. BEFORE you start using the phone. If you drop it, then a lot of money was spent for nothing. The camera lenses on the back protrude. I personally have the Otterbox Defender series, as the case itself prevents the camera lenses from touching any surface when you lay the phone down. It's the same if you lay it face down. The cover prevents the face from touching the surface of anything. I would seriously consider getting a high quality case with this phone, instead of a cheap knock-off. (Not all cases are created equal.) The phone is constructed of metal, not plastic, so it feels very well made. It's not a light phone, but not super heavy, either. At least to me. The phone doesn't come in an original box. At least mine didn't. It came with the phone and charging cable. I can't remember if it came with the little key that opens the SIM slot. If it doesn't, you'll need to get one. It also doesn't come with a manual. Also, unless you get the S23 Ultra, there is no stylus. If that's what you're looking for, the S23+ doesn't have that capability at all. You aren't able to get an S Pen with it, as the S Pen wouldn't function, even if you bought one and tried. I would also like to mention that it's super easy to transfer your data and contacts (and whatever else) to the S23+. I don't have any idea about transferring from an Apple product, though. Samsung is my go-to for phones. As for settings, there are too many to list. There is a specific one for the battery that I would like to mention, however. It makes it so your phone doesn't charge over 80% when fully charged, which is important. The phone won't overcharge that way and end up ruining your battery. As for call settings, there are a lot of those as well. For people that are hard of hearing, there are options for that. If, on the other hand, you'd like to protect your hearing and how loud the phone can get while listening to music or talking on it, you can limit the volume. It has features for the blind, but I don't know what that entails. It also has the car feature, but I don't know anything about that. I don't drive. I hope this review was helpful. :)       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))       71 people found this helpful Helpful  Sending feedback...Thank you for your feedback. Review Title: I was hesitant, even though it says unlocked, because there are thousands of reviews out there of pe
Review Content: I was hesitant, even though it says unlocked, because there are thousands of reviews out there of people having to try to refund their renewed/refurbished purchases because it's not TRULY unlocked. So I messaged the seller and asked for verification that the phone would work with my carrier ( Verizon). They quickly responded, and verified that it was actually a Verizon unlocked phone. Perfect! I put my order in and received my phone a couple of days later. It arrived in a box very much like a brand new phone would. This phone was SPOTLESS. Not a single scratch anywhere on the surface and no discoloration. I had a hiccup during setup where I didn't think it was going to work, but I waited until ALL, and I must stress ALL, of my information was synced and everything was done updating. I used my old SIM card, though this phone offers eSIM, and was able to get it working properly without needing either the seller support ( they included a card with the packaging for such cases ), or Verizon. I've had no wifi or bluetooth connectivity issues, and the fingerprint reader works flawlessly. The camera is a huge step up from my previous 5 year old phone, and the UI is intuitive as I've only ever had Samsung. Literally my ONLY gripe about this phone is actually the Verizon app itself. It'll glitch to the point I often have to completely close and reopen it several times if I want to check my data usage or pay the bill manually. I've uninstalled and reinstalled it, cleared cache and data, and the issue persists. HOWEVER, this is not really a big issue for me personally. I can easily open my account via a chrome tab and work with my info that way. TLDR; Was very skeptical ordering a phone online, did tons of research and found the seller SoonerSoft. Shot them a compatibility question and ordered the phone. Phone was in like new condition and I had no issues after having ALL of my data transferred over. It's been running near flawlessly ( save for my carrier app ) for the past 4 months. I can solidly recommend this seller for renewed electronics. They're also very responsive to questions if you want to verify what carrier it's unlocked from. Review Title: As a real hearing aid, something to hear others talk? For me, worthless
Review Content: As a real hearing aid, something to hear others talk? For me, worthless. I hear people better when I take them out. For that I should give 1 or 2 star rating. I hoped while my reg hearings were being repaired these would get me by. Nope. But. The sound quality for TV, computer, phone, and MUSIC! GREAT! I can enjoy music again. Our pellet stove is 8 feet away and noisy. The noise suppression all but blocks it out. The set up was super easy. I had my audiologist print out my hearing chart, or lack of hearing chart, took a pic with my I-phone, it quickly programed the Airpods and suddenly Janis Joplin sounded good again! Outside noise is blocked. I tried every ear pad that came with this and find the fit, ehh, so so. I have to be careful or they fall out. Left ear hurts after a half hour or so. Not the inner ear, but where it pushes on the cartridge. Getting used to it. Why did I keep them? Because of the sound quality when I do use them. Oh, and whoever designed the case after a greased water melon seed should be beat with something slick and hard to hold on to. A little embossed pattern on the case would have done a lot. And a better latch. If you drop these even a few inches the lid opens and the Airpods make a dash for the door. Dam near dropped one in the toilet. Caught it just in time. Luckily many aftermarket cases out there. And of course in Apple's weird system, a charger wasn't included and it takes a different one than my I-phone. Luckily I found one that fit and ordered a couple more. Youtube videos for how to set up are a must. I do have issues switching between my reg hearing aids and these, but usually not too bad. One time it's automatic, next time I'm in settings on my phone. But really not a big deal. Would be 5 star if they stayed in my ear and actually worked as a low grade hearing aid. But worth it for everything else. By programming like a hearing aid, sound quality is great!!! And blocking background noise is very nice. Might save on marriage counseling by not hearing each other. Review Title: The screen size was larger than the iPhone 8, even though the chassis was smaller
Review Content: The screen size was larger than the iPhone 8, even though the chassis was smaller. It was weird moving to a device without a home button, but I got used to it quickly. The cameras are pretty good, and hold up well especially with more modern phones. The size is amazing. It's super convenient to use one handed, and it's so light compared to other phones. You can often forget you even have it on you. The 256GB version has lasted me forever. I'm still barely at around 100gb of usage, and I do take a large amount of photographs on it. It has gained quite a few scratches, especially around the cameras or on the edges of the frame. It is a 6-year-old phone however, so while the exist they're nothing more than cosmetic issues. Charges fairly well, the age of the device does mean that charging can cause it to overheat. Battery life itself isn't great either. I luckily have it charging periodically throughout the day, but with minimal usage you'll still barely get back to bed with about 20% left sometimes. Definitely invest in a battery replacement if you're considering going with one of these. Asides from that it's a pretty good purchase. Lasted me from 2023 until 2026. They may potentially drop support on the mini, so if you're worried about that then potentially aim for the 13 mini instead. Review Title: (These are the reasons I couldn't give 5 stars
Review Content: (These are the reasons I couldn't give 5 stars. Had I not caught these issues — especially the charger — I would likely have been frustrated enough for 1 or 2 stars.) I'm coming from the S22 Ultra so the UI was immediately familiar, with many similar features and an easy transition. The biggest improvement is the processor — App installation, gaming without lag, browsing, music from the internal speakers, all noticeably better across the board. Most notably for my usual activities, game downloads that took 2+ minutes on my S22 Ultra now complete in approximately 10 seconds on the S23 Ultra. The difference is genuinely dramatic. I transferred approximately 128GB of apps and data wirelessly from my S22 Ultra in about 40 minutes. A USB-C to C cable would have been faster, but after the water detection warning I didn't want to use a cord for that step. The 40 minutes was likely influenced by the transfer speed of the older S22 Ultra as the source device. After the transfer, everything was loaded exactly as it was on my previous phone — it connected to my WiFi without entering a password, and my Samsung biometrics remembered passwords for each app, making it seamless to use immediately. The battery does not overheat the way the S22 Ultra is well known to do, which was a major concern of mine going in. The condition was as described. There were two very small micro cracks near the edge, but after applying a screen protector they are completely invisible. If they ever become visible I'll simply use a liquid glass repair solution. After extensive research I'm not concerned about the screen integrity. The camera is phenomenal. I was always impressed with the S22 Ultra camera, but the increased resolution makes every shot noticeably more vivid. Photos look almost better than real life, with no extra steps needed — just point and shoot. The 512GB storage is more than I'll likely ever need, even with a heavy volume of photos, videos and apps. I don't see myself coming close to capacity. I spent considerable time deciding between the S23 and S24 Ultra. Review Title: I severely cracked the screen on my older phone and the screen replacement was pretty expensive
Review Content: I severely cracked the screen on my older phone and the screen replacement was pretty expensive. This slightly newer model offered a significant upgrade ( I had an S22 Ultra and the S23 Ultra was a big jump in improvements) So instead of sinking money into the screen, I could get a newer model and more memory than I had before. I was upgrading from 256GB to 512GB so this seemed like a great deal. Because the phone is older, it took hours to download what felt like a million updates and get the phone up to date. Then doing Samsung Smart Switch took a while too. So I had hours into this before I even tried to activate it with Xfinity Mobile. When I did finally get to that part, I entered the IMEI number Xfinity Mobile said "Your phone is compatible but may be locked to another carrier". At that point I was crushed, I already was behind and needed a working phone. I immediately messaged the seller through Amazon to find out what could be going on. They replied a few hours later only to say they were sorry and offer a refund or replacement. So now I would be looking at more days without a working phone . I would have to spend hours wiping the phone data, mailing it back and then more hours to install updates and switch everything again on a new device. I really didn't want to send it back if there was any way for it to work. After reading more on Xfinity's site I saw this "Some carriers will automatically unlock their customers' phones after a period of time. Some carriers will only unlock your phone if you ask them to." and there are unlock services out there as well. The unlock services do not seem to be doing anything any different than your carrier can do so I decided to call Xfinity Mobile and see if they could help. But I also have to wonder why these mobile phone resellers do not just truly unlock the phones with a service since this is their business. They seem fine to put the burden on whoever buys it to figure it out. Xfinity Mobile was able to successfully get the phone active after about an hour on the phone with them. So I am really glad I didn't just send it back. Who is to say the replacement would not be the same thing all over again?This was an education in renewed phones but if this was my business I would offer this guidance right away in a troubleshooting section or email before I would have someone send back a "locked" phone. My time is valuable so all this messing around with the phone still costs me. It took time away from work and caused stress. This does take away from the value of the renewed phone being cheaper than a brand new one. Overall though the device itself was mostly as expected. The color is nice. The screen was in good shape with no scratches. It had a plastic sticker cover on it. The only minor scratches I saw were around the camera lenses on the back and around the edge of the lens. (not like the listing says - no scratches from 12 inches away as per the "excellent" description) Not a deal breaker though either as the camera appears to work fine. See my photo. The battery arrived not charged and at about 12% which was not that big of a deal. It charged fast and has held a charge. So as far as the device itself goes, it is a good device and matches the listing.

Review Title: I inspected it
Review Content: I inspected it. There are wear marks on the case and crown but the face was fine. I put a screen and case protector on it and it looks fine. I checked the battery life and it’s down to 85%. I’m sure that’s going to be fine. I know it can be replaced it I want to later. The sports band is not an Apple product but I don’t care. I quit buying Apple Watch bands years ago. I can buy 3 or 4 of these perfectly fine knockoffs for the price of one Apple. Other than the scuffs and battery it works as it should. Down with overpriced stuff and thumbs up for cheaper rebuilt semi quality stuff. Kinda like a rebuilt transmission. As for the functionality of the watch, it's fine except for the battery life. I have to charge it part way through the day IF I want it to last all day. On more than one occasion, by 4:00 pm, I got the 10% battery left message and then it is dead until I get it on a charger. Now, I'm going to have to spend $100 to get the battery replaced. AND - the watch charger that came with it, does not work. Yes, I took the piece of plastic off of it before trying it out. I'm beginning to regret my purchase. I guess I could see if I can replace the battery myself but I don't want to perform surgery on a piece of electronics at my age. The battery will be around $25 and the tool kit will be around $30 plus shipping and handling. Still saving money though. Maybe I can start a side hustle replacing apple watch batteries and save enough to go on vacation in the tropics or buy a small can of pineapple juice. Found a video tutorial that walked me through turning off a number of the functions of the watch to save on battery. I am pleased to report that after doing that, I can now wear it 10 or 11 hours and the watch will still have mid 70's battery left. I shouldn't have to do this but I did so Now I can wear it and not worry about taking a charger to work with me so I can charge it over my lunch break. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple iPhone 14 Pro Max, 128GB, Space Black - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: Unfortunately, the phone I received was nowhere near "Excellent
Review Content: Unfortunately, the phone I received was nowhere near "Excellent." The biggest issue is the camera system. One of the main reasons I chose the iPhone 14 Pro Max was for its three-camera setup. However, only one camera works properly in Photo mode. In Video mode, two cameras work, while the third doesn't work at all. The 0.5x ultra-wide camera is completely unavailable, and the 5x zoom function doesn't work either. This is especially frustrating because I'm an up-and-coming mechanic, and I regularly use the 0.5x camera to take photos in tight spaces while working on customers' vehicles. It's an important tool for my job, not just a feature I wanted. I upgraded from an iPhone 13 Pro Max where two of the cameras had failed, so I was excited to finally have a phone with all three cameras working. Instead, I ended up with another phone that has camera issues. At that point, I could have saved money by buying an iPhone 14 Plus with only two cameras and probably received a phone that actually worked. Another concern was that the phone was not properly factory reset. The packaging states that Amazon Renewed devices are supposed to be factory reset before being resold. However, when I powered it on, it started up like a normal phone instead of taking me through the initial setup process. It appeared the previous owner had simply signed out of their Apple ID rather than the phone being completely erased and reset. I contacted Amazon Customer Support to request a replacement since the phone was defective. I was told there were no more iPhone 14 Pro Max devices in Excellent condition available to send as a replacement. However, when I checked the same Amazon listing, it still showed the exact same phone in Excellent condition available for purchase. I don't understand why replacements weren't available when the listing indicated more were in stock. I would have been happy to return the defective phone in exchange for a properly functioning one. I understand that Amazon Renewed products are used, and I wasn't expecting a brand-new phone. However, I did expect to receive the condition I paid for and a device with all advertised features working correctly. A phone with a partially functioning camera system should never pass inspection as "Excellent," especially when customers are paying a premium for that condition. Overall, this experience was extremely disappointing. Amazon Renewed is supposed to give customers confidence that devices have been inspected and tested. Based on my experience, the inspection process failed, and customer service did not provide a reasonable solution. I still get through a full day without scrambling for a charger, which is exactly what you want from a daily driver. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple iPhone 14 Pro, 256GB, Space Black - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: It was a lovely phone, in outstanding cosmetic condition - it appeared brand new
Review Content: It was a lovely phone, in outstanding cosmetic condition - it appeared brand new. The seller was also very gracious to include a screen protector, and I have no complaints regarding the seller, delivery, or customer service. It functioned perfectly when it first arrived, with no glitches and an easy transfer process. I was not satisfied with the camera; I am uncertain if this is a characteristic of the iPhone 14, but I do not believe the photo quality surpasses that of my previous phone, which was an iPhone 12. I expected it to produce higher quality images, but perhaps it was returned for refurbishment due to the camera issues? After 2-3 weeks, the phone started to shut down unexpectedly, even when fully charged, and when it powered back on after a few seconds, it would show only 10% battery life? This was peculiar. The battery health was reported to be at 90%, which I found surprising, but later discovered that this percentage can be manipulated to reflect better battery health, even if that is not the reality. Aside from the random shutdowns, my phone required charging every 3 hours, and within 2 weeks, the battery health dropped from 90% to 80%. It would have been an amazing deal and worth the money for a 1TB phone in great exterior condition , and I’m sad I had to return it . I could not handle the random shut downs and constant charging and the photo quality was also a big factor (it might just have been my phone and not all iPhone 14’s). I’m bummed! But return was easy & just a friendly reminder that whenever you do drop off a pricey item like this for returns, get a print out of the receipt ! Had nothing to do with my return , just throwing it out there. They connect to 2 different devices, but they do switch between which device is playing when you play audio from two devices at the same time. The noise cancelling is excellent and soundcore always makes earbuds and headphones that have quiet ‘connecting’ and acknowledgement sounds, such as when using its touch controls or when connecting to a new device. I prefer it when the earbud sounds are quieter so these are a relief compared to other earbuds that have extremely loud ‘connecting’ sounds. These only have soft pleasant chimes instead. When I bought a second pair for my sister, that one did get a strange mechanical buzzing in one ear but I returned that one. We suspect it is because she got them wet in the shower, so be careful with it around water because they can break, or maybe it was just a defective unit. A few things to note, the touch control is very sensitive and sometimes just lying down on the side can trigger it, which is annoying. However, they and their case have survived several drops so durability is good. Sometimes they randomly cannot connect to the devices and you must reconnect them, I would say this occurs about once a week, but they are worth it because the sound is good and they are comfortable in my ears. They come with three ear tips for better fit. I will say, the blue color is very soothing and unmistakeable. The ‘phone stand’ functionality of the earbud case is questionable, it can stand but cannot support a really heavy phone on an uneven surface especially if the earbuds are in use, although this is a minor gripe as it works well on a desk. Battery life is about 6-8 hours, but the case charges them so it is not so bad, it is only irritating when it happens. They are earbuds and not earphones, after all. I have also used them for meetings and have had no comments about the microphone so I assume it works fine. Honestly when they are on sale, there’s no better headphones for the price.
