Review Title: - The drivers (and active noise cancelling) burn out and go berserk in about a year
Review Content: - The drivers (and active noise cancelling) burn out and go berserk in about a year - You cannot reasonably pair them to more than one device, as they freak out - You absolutely must use the soundcore app to EQ out most of the bass in order to get proper sound quality I have two pairs, one about a year old and one a couple months old. The year old ones will crunch and screech (literally like an alien screaming in your ear) when music has a loud or busy mix, or when you lie down on your ear on a pillow while ANC is on, or if they're turned up too high. They also occasionally go into "earthquake" mode, as I call it, with ANC on, where it sounds like an earthquake in your ears until you take them out and put them back in. They're only useful as backups for when the other ones die or get lost for, say, a quiet podcast. If them paired to my phone and laptop at the same time, and come into range of one device while they are paired to another, they will always panic and act unpredictably. Sometimes they disconnect from both entirely, or half their volume and "connect to both" but really they are connected to one and unstable. There is zero upside to having them paired to more than one device. I think only Apple Airpods have really figured this out and its because they write the firmware for all three devices, so. Not a fair fight really. The microphones are AMAZING. An actual replacement for a bluetooth headset, and better than my regular iPhone mic. I used these at work for a while when I was doing phone sales. 100x better than any Airpods I've used. I bought my first pair on TikTok for $15 and my second for $25. Both a fine price to pay. I see these trade offs as pretty much fine for me. I've owned every type of airpod except the maxes and wear headphones 10+ hours a day 5 days a week. When EQ'd, these are pretty much as good as Airpod Pro 2nd gens. Without the EQ they are a bassy mudfest. They last like 5+ hours on one charge even when they're old. My #1 reccomendation for bluetooth headphones. The tiny little hearing aid batteries die in them all anyway, whether you get $300 ones or $20 ones. And these are 100x better than the no name ones you'd get at a discount store for the same price.

Review Title: Needed to replace an aging IPhone which was still working great, but a lot of apps needing newer IOS
Review Content: Needed to replace an aging IPhone which was still working great, but a lot of apps needing newer IOS. So, not looking for the lastest/greatest, just a good update. Decided IPh 14+ was a good option. 1) I purchased an “Excellent” OPEN BOX phone from Best Buy. It came in a box sealed with Geek Squad tape. When opened, the phone had tons of fingerprints all over it, front and back; not a great first impression. After going through the startup process I was greeted with a screen that informed me that the phone had remote management software installed on it. Basically unusable. 2) I returned it and they replaced it with another “Excellent” OPEN BOX. Same thing – both phones had been previously owned by some company (now out of business) who had loaded remote management software on the phones. So… these are expensive, unusable bricks, and shame on BB/Geek Squad for selling these phones to the public. 3) After that experience I decided to give Amazon a try and bought a phone supplied by WOOT, as I have had good experiences with other Woot purchases. The phone arrived in a beat up generic box with the inside packaging worse than the outside. On the positive side, the phone was cosmetically very good with no obvious scratches, etc. So, everything looked good until I checked the battery health. 81%. NOT GOOD. Yes, it meets the described spec of >80% for their “Excellent” condition, but will going to be into the Apple service condition in a couple of weeks. Returned to Amazon/Woot and waiting for refund. After reading a ton of reviews I decided to give it one more shot and get a “Premium” condition directly from Amazon.com. Most of the reviews of these phones were much better than all of the other vendors. They are definitely more expensive but come with a 365 day warranty vs 90 day and spec at >90% battery life. Phone arrived today. It was VERY nicely packaged in a SEALED shrink wrapped professional looking box. Opened the box and found a phone with what appeared to be the original Apple protective film still in place on the front and back. Battery was dead so after a quick charge I was able to check battery health…… 100% and 0 charge cycles. Basically this is a brand NEW, NEVER USED phone. I can’t say how impressed I was after three bad experiences. I saved a couple $hundred compared to BB or Apple and got a brand new phone ….. It’s all about the journey  !!! Review Content: When I got the package in the mail I hesitated even opening the box and contemplated just returning it back without giving it a chance. I still wasn’t too impressed with the iPhone just yet, but I gave it a chance. As I began using it and saw the battery life was at 98 % I thought, WOW, nice iPhone with a pretty decent battery too. I also noticed it still has an Apple warranty until March of 2026. The phone is beautiful and works great thus far, but my niece said I should get the iPhone 17 Pro Max. So I looked it up and didn’t see why I should go into a 2k debt for an iPhone 17 pro max with a 1 terabyte storage drive. After all, my iPhone 16 Pro Max still gets another 6 years of updates on the iOS software. I have to say I still have time to return this iPhone, but, right now, this is a well made and solid purchase and I feel very comfortable with it after 2 weeks of use. I still have my android Galaxy S25 Ultra, and I’m gonna keep it too, but the seller of this iPhone certainly does ship out beautiful and quality iPhones to the buyers. No scratches or dings and a great battery life too. The item arrived with great packaging and I am impressed with this seller. Now my niece with the iPhone 17 pro max with 256 gig of storage loves her phone, she’s had it for about a month now, and yes,she paid more than me and I have a 1 terabyte storage drive on mine, and her first complaint about the iPhone 17 is, the aluminum casing gets scratched up easily forcing her to get a cover so she doesn’t have to look at the scratched up case on her new iPhone. The IPhone 16 Pro Max has a titanium frame that is solid, and I do have a case over it to protect it from drops or falls. Would I recommend this iPhone and seller on Amazon. ABSOLUTELY YES! Review Title: I ordered my iPhone 16 pro max couple of days back and got it yesterday
Review Content: I ordered my iPhone 16 pro max couple of days back and got it yesterday. I was very excited as I was getting 512GB storage with an amazon backed brand to claim that renewed premium category is like a new. Now as I received my phone, it all looks very nice and I start begin the setup as well as checked everything from the physical perspective if nothing is damaged, I didn’t notice anything major till my son noticed that of the lens on the back side camera have a small chip cut that can easily be observed in day light as well as buy touching it with finger. Anyway I proceed with complete setup, and begin testing the phone, everything looks to be fine, batter at 95% which is good. But then I majorly stuck on side camera button, which was not functional. I did some research on YouTube and google if some setting or config needs to change, and I followed all the steps but nothing works and the conclusion that some sensor or side button is damaged and not functioning properly and this is big red flag if I am spending close to 1000$ on renewed premium product and expecting it to at least work 4 to 5 years. I also want to mention that, amazon send me the lighting cable, instead of usb C cable. Anyway next morning I called customer care to report my feedback and explain all the details, my concern was not that I can’t return it or can’t get the refund. But my biggest concern was of Trust in the branding for renewed premium category of product. Because if Vendor is claiming what they are selling then it supposed to be that way. Because if I have to buy a renewed premium category product I may think twice or more before taking that decision, and I think used premium category is a big market, so seller should focus on quality and maintaining the brand and not to sell the defective product to customer and create so much frustration. But the good thing is at least Renewed premium category is claiming to return and refund upto 365 days that customer support specialist also told me to not worry and return and try order another one, because its rare that such kind of issue come, but anyway I see 11% of customers report bad experience so this matters. Anyway I am retuning this phone today with less than 14 hours of receiving, I am not sure if I will order again, because of all such a big hassle in the whole experience of waiting the product to arrive, setup everything, and test out and its all about experience how much you want to invest in that effort. I am updating my review on May 22 regarding my experience with customer service while following up on my refund. It has now been two days since my return. On May 20, I spoke with an Amazon specialist about a defective product and requested a replacement. I was advised that the best option would be to initiate a return and return at Whole Foods and that I would receive a refund within a week, after which I could place a new order. However, today, when I contacted customer support to check the status of my refund, I had a very disappointing experience. The representative was rude, yelled her voice, and informed me that the refund would take up to 30 days. So be prepare, if you get a defective product then you stuck with your money and wont be able to buy another unless you get your money back. This is one of the worst experience i had as i cant use the product that i paid for, and the money also stuck for a month, that i cant use to buy another phone She also stated that the previous information I received about a 7-day refund was incorrect. She was not willing to listen to my concerns and ended the call abruptly. I have never encountered such poor customer service from Amazon before. This experience was frustrating and does not align with Amazon’s stated commitment to being customer-obsessed. Review Title: The condition was as if brand new, the S pen was included
Review Content: The condition was as if brand new, the S pen was included. And 512GB of memory? Wow! No more dealing with SD cards and figuring out where things are stored. All for $424 and 12 months to pay with no interest on my Amazon CC. My history of of cellular phones goes back almost 40 years to car phones. As to PCS hand held phones, 25 years. Many Nokias, then Windows Phone, then very grudgingly, Android, only because my beloved 950XL does not have voice over data and technology moved on. I got a Samsung A52. I have had phones that I didn't particularly like, but none have I hated as much as that A52. SO many stupid things, constant misbehaviors. I can't tell you how many times I threw that puppy against the wall. Good thing it has a great case. Well, Mr. Samsung. All is forgiven with this S22 Ultra. This is the first phone I've ever had that did not allow a "no lock" option. I've never had reason to lock my phone from prying eyes or fingers. No big secrets and I don't lose my phones. Anyway, this phone requires some form of security...god, I've come to hate that word...but I found the fingerprint unlock to work well, so that hurdle crossed without pain. I really, really hate doing things on the tiny screen and keyboard of a phone. The Microsoft Phone Link has been a god send, letting me use a big monitor, keyboard and mouse for messages and other purposes. SO much nicer and easier. Well, it just got better with the Samsung DeX feature. Plug the phone into a USB port on the PC and now you have a work station. (Historical note: My Windows Phone could do this with the optional docking station a decade ago.) Now I can use the Samsung Snapseed (like Adobe Lightroom, but FREE!) and ExpertRAW apps with the comfort of a real keyboard and mouse. A number of YT reviewers complained about the battery life. Gee, I'm running video games and movies all day, why does the battery suck? Even then, they reported that it could run all day. I'm happy to report that with the light duty of phone, text, some GPS, and other odds and ends, the battery life is great. Down 20-30% after a day of that kind of use. The Samsung Camera app is thorough and easy to use. I say this having tried other camera apps, and even a short lived Pixel 8 phone. I ditched that in less than a day, the camera app was SO clunky. Then in the hardware background, the Ultra claims to have a larger sensor...this is always good...than its S22 cousins and with a higher pixel count. 108MP? Wow. My first digital camera had 2.1MP. The S pen and note feature is amazing and I'm just starting to learn all of its capabilities. The phone updated to Android 14 and 6.1 OneUI w/o issue. Samsung guarantees several more years of OS upgrades and seven years of security upgrades. The summary is that for only the third time in 25 years do I love a phone and not just tolerate it. I can't imagine someone not liking this phone, and the differences between this and the just out S25 are not worth $1000 bucks. Review Content: I bought this phone in refurbished/excellent condition. After reading multiple reviews on multiple refurbished phone listings on Amazon, my biggest concern was (always is) getting one with a damaged screen, cameras, or having it not truly be unlocked. I've had this phone less than 24 hours, but here's my take SO far (I can't speak for other people, these are just my experiences): 1) Yes, it was (for me) truly, 100% unlocked. Not even an ex-carrier logo when I first turned it on! (My previous 'unlocked' refurbished phone has a T-Mobile logo when turned on) I was quite happy/impressed about this. 2) No scratches (that I could see) on the front/touchscreen. There are multiple, TINY scuffs on the sides (not part of the touchscreen)/top edge/bottom edge of the phone - which I fully expected w/ a refurbished phone, and I'm totally fine with it (and this is if I'm REALLY nitpicking - they're really not that bad, though. Review Title: My main issues are with the hardware condition and cellular connectivity
Review Content: My main issues are with the hardware condition and cellular connectivity. I purchased this phone in the highest refurbished condition, listed as Excellent / Like New, so I expected it to be in very good physical condition. Unfortunately, the outer rings around the camera modules are visibly shattered. The cameras themselves still work perfectly, and since I use a case, the damage doesn’t really affect me in everyday use. However, it is quite obvious that the phone was dropped at some point, and I don’t think this level of physical damage should be present on a device advertised as Excellent / Like New. My second, and more significant, issue is the cellular network connection. Calls work without much of a problem, but I cannot reliably get mobile data from the carriers I’ve tried. When I’m away from Wi-Fi, the phone frequently shows Emergency Calls Only or has a signal but cannot actually connect to the mobile data network. I’ve tried multiple carriers, and none have worked properly for data. This is frustrating because it essentially means I have to rely on Wi-Fi for internet access.

Review Title: I ordered the iPhone 15 Pro Max refurbished and it arrived last night
Review Content: I ordered the iPhone 15 Pro Max refurbished and it arrived last night. After spending a good 3+ hours setting it up, I realized the lens for the main camera was broken. From the outside, you can’t see any issue. It wasn’t until I opened up the camera app that I actually saw it didn’t work. “Renewed Premium” carries a certain standard with it, and this certainly does not meet that in the slightest. On top of that, upon calling customer support, I was told that I would not be able to do anything unless I deactivated the phone and remove my Apple ID from it. Wouldn’t have been the end of the world if I needed to go back to my other phone for a bit, however, in order to set up this phone with the eSIM, deactivated my previous SIM card. Upon explaining all of that to customer support, I was told there was nothing they could do unless I deactivated this phone (leaving me without a phone until they received this and shipped me a new one) I was then told to call Apple to see what they can do, when honestly, this is their mistake. Either way, I called apple and it was going to be another set of hoops to jump through with scheduling appointments and all that. Plus since I didn’t have apple care, if they needed to repair the camera, I would still be without a phone. So even if Apple was able to help fix this, the issue of me not having a phone would still be there. Had I broken this camera myself - I would certainly except those terms given there’s not much else I could do. However, this was given to me in this condition and for Amazon to leave me with the responsibility of fixing their mistake due to carelessness in inspection and quality control is absurd. So whether I like it or not, I am now STUCK with the responsibility of cleaning this up since my account is connected to this phone now. What at one point could have been a great gift to myself has turned into the biggest hassle I’ve experienced buying/returning anything, probably ever. I’m going to give this one more shot as I’ve now ordered another iPhone from them to be delivered shortly, however, it’s also required me to spend another ~$1000 in having that iPhone sent prior to me getting my refund. This is absolutely ridiculous and unacceptable. Even if this next phone is perfect, I’m likely never going to order from the Amazon refurbished store again. I’ll either go straight to Apple refurbished, or brand new, for any of my future phone/laptop/device purchases. On top of all this hassle, I’ll certainly have to spend another few hours setting up my replacement phone once it arrives. All the time I’ve invested into this so far has NOT been even close worth the “nice discount” on a premium refurbished phone that should have arrived without issue to begin with. Amazon - take note. Change your policies. Making this the customer’s mess to clean up is not acceptable. I’ll plan to update this review if anything changes. But like I said, even if the next phone I ordered is perfect, I still give this a 1-star review for all the hassle and lack of responsibility the company took to resolve this. P.s. i’ll also add that I am a quite understanding and peaceful person. The person I spoke with from customer support was doing his absolute best to help me, but this was clearly a bigger issue than he had the power to solve. I requested to have this escalated to upper management and was told the same thing. Whoever is the one making decisions about what can and can’t be done needs to hear about this. Review Title: I purchased a refurbished Apple Watch 8 in excellent condition
Review Content: I purchased a refurbished Apple Watch 8 in excellent condition. The watch arrived with a scratch on the screen and a cheap knockoff wrist band that was hard to get fitted onto the watch. I was willing to let that go. I set up the watch. Charged it and took it off charger around 10pm and went to bed. I woke up the next morning at 8 am and put on the watch which had already went down to 88% battery life. By 4pm it was down to 42%. By this time I’m frustrated so I pull up the source code for the Apple Watch to find out how many battery cycles this watch has been though and the count was 409. As we all know batteries have finite lives. They can only handle being drained and charged so many times then they need to be replaced. An Apple Watch that has been drained and charged 409 times does not fit the bill of a refurbished item to me. Not by a long shot and Apple should be ashamed of themselves for letting this take place via an Amazon store with Apple in the name. Review Title: El Samsung Galaxy A32 es un smartphone que ofrece una excelente relación calidad-precio dentro de la
Review Content: El Samsung Galaxy A32 es un smartphone que ofrece una excelente relación calidad-precio dentro de la gama media. Su diseño elegante y pantalla Super AMOLED de 6.4 pulgadas con resolución Full HD+ lo convierten en un dispositivo ideal para quienes buscan una experiencia visual vibrante y fluida, especialmente gracias a su tasa de refresco de 90 Hz. En el apartado fotográfico, cuenta con una cámara cuádruple (64 MP principal, 8 MP ultra gran angular, 5 MP macro y 5 MP de profundidad), lo que permite capturar imágenes nítidas y con buen nivel de detalle en distintas condiciones de luz. Su cámara frontal de 20 MP es perfecta para selfies y videollamadas. En cuanto a rendimiento, el A32 incorpora un procesador MediaTek Helio G80, acompañado de 4 GB o 6 GB de RAM (según versión) y almacenamiento interno desde 64 GB hasta 128 GB, ampliable mediante tarjeta microSD. Es ideal para un uso cotidiano: redes sociales, navegación, streaming y algunos juegos ligeros. Review Title: I bought this product because my ears get fatigued from AirPods (Pro) sometimes but I want to still
Review Content: I bought this product because my ears get fatigued from AirPods (Pro) sometimes but I want to still listen to my audiobooks. I also wanted something for airplane trips. Sleeping with earbuds on the plane is painful and then I’ve had one or both fall out and roll under my seat or way back under someone else’s seat, which is really gross. Even though they are a bit heavy, they are very comfortable.I have small ears, so these fit really well—right inside with no pressure on the cartilage. If you have big ears or a big head, I don’t know. It might be worth a try anyway. I love being able to control the volume on the device, unlike my AirPods where you have to pull out the phone to control the volume. I have a few cons though. I can’t really wear these outside or for intense workouts because if I get sweaty, they slide around on my ears. My son would wear these while mowing the lawn and I thought I could too, but it didn’t work well. I got sweaty and they slid around and broke the audio seal, letting in a lot of background noise. And they don’t have the noise cancelling capability that AirPods do. When I mow with the AirPods, I only hear a little background noise. With these headphones I still hear a lot of background noise. Same thing goes for using the vacuum cleaner and even at the car wash. With AirPods, I hear nothing. With these, I have to turn the volume way up to drown out the background noise. This concerns me for flights because I want everything tuned out except my audiobook or maybe a movie. But the Bluetooth range is awesome!! With my AirPods, the phone has to be in fairly close proximity or it will lose connectivity. With these headphones I can go way down the street away from my phone and they will still be connected! I will have my phone plugged in inside the basement and go all the way out to the mailbox or to the neighbor’s house and still be connected. It’s like a dream! I can go places around my home and property with these headphones I couldn’t go before (with the phone left inside somewhere). They also are comparable to AirPods in regards to phone calls, Google meet, or FaceTime. I haven’t worn them long enough to determine battery life. Review Title: After a bad drop of a OnePlus 7T that killed the screen of my wife's phone, it was time to order two
Review Content: After a bad drop of a OnePlus 7T that killed the screen of my wife's phone, it was time to order two new phones [that is, new for us], one for her and one for me. I'm a tech guy and I always order two of the same phones since it's easier for me to support a single model of phone. Having used Samsung phones years ago but then moving to ZTE and the OnePlus, these S21 FE phones have been terrific after one month of use and renewed my interest in Samsung phones. The phones arrived in like new condition without any marks or scratches on either phone. Unlike the new models these both came with 20W chargers and good quality 5ft cables. These phones have a plastic case which I prefer, as plastic is less fragile than glass, which is another reason for me to NOT buy flagship phones. I am also not so concerned with the appearance or color of the phones since I immediately put them in a case and install tempered glass screen protectors on all my phones. Among the many positives are the 120HZ screen response is a pleasure to use, battery life has been excellent lasting for more than a day for normal use including text, calls, email, YouTube and some streaming, terrific camera, good stereo speakers, charges very quickly with the supplied chargers but also with the 25W aftermarket chargers that I have for these phones. Both Fingerprint and Face recognition work consistently and more quickly than other phones I have used. Bluetooth and WiFi connect quickly without any dropouts, and speed on T-Mobile 5g for phone and Home Internet has been consistent within the T-Mobile performance spec for my location. I am not a gamer so I can't provide a meaningful review for that. The only negative I can report is for the amount of Samsung bloatware and the numerous and annoying notifications, which can luckily be turned off. These are two excellent phones that I bought for less than half the price of one new one. And the Amazon renewed program is a good and safe option for many purchases as it also includes a 90-day return policy if there is any dissatisfaction with the product. Review Title: I’m writing this review with a few caveats I will get to
Review Content: I’m writing this review with a few caveats I will get to. First of all, the iPhone 13 mini is truly the best iPhone for people who want a phone that feels like a phone and not like they are carrying around a tablet. I have been using the iPhone 16 Pro since it came out and had no idea what I was missing in this older model until I was talking to a friend about his. He told me it was the best phone ever made and he would not get rid of his until he couldn’t get replacement parts or unless they made a new updated mini, which it sounds like they have no plans to do (a shame). I was telling him that I have been traveling with work and when I’m pulling a bag, I need to be able to work my phone well with one hand. The 16 Pro is not good for this. I don’t like cases, I don’t want to use a pop socket - I just want a pretty sleek unencumbered iPhone. So I was on a mission and it’s not an easy one when you’re picky about the condition and the phone can only be found in the used/renewed/refurbished channels. I had hesitations about buying from Amazon resale because of other items I’ve gotten from them that didn’t seem like they were inspected. I took a risk. I purchased the starlight 256gb from Amazon (not a marketplace seller). It was still a pretty penny considering the age of the mini, but the minis hold their value due to the cult following they have. I received it and it was absolutely perfect - didn’t look like it had ever been used, though the battery capacity was 85%…which was okay but nothing wonderful. In the meantime, I decided I would prefer the 512gb since I plan to keep this a long time, so I decided to order one, also from Amazon resale, since the 256 was in such pristine condition and I knew I had 90 days to decide regardless. The 512gb through Amazon was a crazy price…marked as excellent but over $550 with taxes (I had paid $330 for the 256gb). Cut to a day later, I see that a seller has the 512 starlight marked as excellent and it was $385. I reached out to them and asked them about the battery health and they were wonderful - got back to me really quickly and said 99%. So I thought, well, for $385 vs $550, I’ll cancel the Amazon order and order this one. Unfortunately it was too late to cancel the Amazon one - it had already shipped - so my intention was to just send it straight back as soon as it was delivered. The one from the actual cellphone reseller got here quickly and for the price, was represented well - it did have 2 corners with blemishes that look like they’re from a drop, but they weren’t terrible but having seen the pristine 256gb version from Amazon, I was being overly picky. The battery was 100%, as they had told me, which was great, but what I noticed was the screen had been replaced. I’m okay with screen replacements - any phone from 2021 has probably had one, as well as any battery that shows 100% on a phone from 2021 is a replaced battery. These are not bad things. What I do know from having a screen replaced years ago through one of the shops that uses an aftermarket part is the screens are not as flat as apple’s genuine screen if you get a replacement from them. It almost has waves in it, especially along the edges. They look fine if you aren’t picky to the degree I am, or looking at the phone from an angle, but I’ve found they are not always reliable screens with regard to the responsiveness. As soon as I saw this, I packed it back up and set up a return through the seller and took it straight to the UPS store. Cut to my next Amazon delivery, the 512gb model that I had been unable to cancel arrives. Since the one from the reseller didn’t work out for me, I said, well, let’s check this out because if it’s perfect, then I guess it’s worth the $550 spent. Open it up and WOW! The body of it is just like the 256 I had gotten. Pristine - not a drop ding or scratch in sight. Perfect screen…remarkable…but I wanted to check the battery. When I got it up and running, I checked the battery capacity and it was at 100%. Under the battery details it even lists it as a Genuine battery, so it was “renewed” with Apple OEM. I could not be more thrilled even though it cost way more than a phone from 2021 should. But I’m keeping it for the long haul so it’s worth it knowing I don’t have a battery replacement in the near future. I’ve got the 90 days to see how it functions but I feel pretty good about this one. TL;DR - the iPhone mini is a phone you will be addicted to after use. It’s so functional and what a “phone” should be. Do not hesitate to order one shipped from and sold by Amazon.com. I can confirm they have fantastic quality control when it comes to their phones. If you pick a reseller other than Amazon, just make sure you get the 90 day return and that there aren’t “restocking” fees buried in their policies. Review Title: The supplier was TECHMINT, Amazon the purchase portal
Review Content: The supplier was TECHMINT, Amazon the purchase portal. There seems to be a number of 'Amazon-qualified suppliers' involved. To know who you're buying from, the 'ships from/sold by' info. is on the right side of the product page. There may also be differences in packaging and accessories. Best to read through the advertising to know exactly what you're buying. Or contact the supplier before purchasing. Given that Amazon backs these purchases, not a concern. It arrived without scratches, dings, or apparent wear. Looks like new. That said, those buying a 'Renewed' phone should expect varying degrees of condition within the parameters of Amazon's advertising. I'd suggest buying a 'Renewed Premium' for your best chance of a like-new phone. I probably got lucky with a 'Renewed'. It shipped in a *very* well designed and protective box designed for phones. Not much larger than the boxes Apple packages iPhones in and similarly sturdy. Well suited for protecting the phone during shipping. If you plan on shipping your phone or storing a back-up, I'd suggest keeping it. The box has spacers to accommodate different sizes. Kudos to the packaging engineers. Well done. It was delivered with 100% battery health which almost certainly means that the phone was opened up and the battery replaced. The likelihood of a 'renewed' 13 Mini arriving with battery health at 100% is slim to none. I assume that they did this because the phone was traded in with < 80% battery health. Amazon advertising states that the phone will arrive with battery health of ≥ 80%. Notably, the battery was recognized by iOS as 'genuine' (thanks TECHMINT). Batteries that are not can lead to various issues, most importantly, safety issues. Look up "how to check if an iPhone battery is genuine". If it isn't, I'd suggest returning it to the supplier. Side note about iPhone battery replacement: If/when you have an iPhone battery replaced, I'd highly recommend scheduling it through Apple. Apple often contracts with third parties to do this in addition to Apple stores. When third parties sign up for this, they're held to a high standard and you're guaranteed to receive a 'genuine' battery. More importantly, if there's a problem you'll have the full weight of Apple behind you to resolve any issues. I'd also suggest reaching out to the supplier before purchase and asking what the battery health will be. In my experience with the iPhone 12 Mini, once you drop into the high 80% range, battery life becomes more noticeable. Note that Apple recommends replacing an iPhone battery when it reaches 80% battery health. I ran two diagnostics to check functions. In both cases, no issues. One of the diagnostics is built into iOS. You'll need iOS 17 or later and not a beta release. Search for 'built in iPhone diagnostic' for instructions. There's another which makes doing this quite a bit easier. From the Apple app store search for 'Phone Doctor Plus'. It's not a diagnostic as much as it's a function check but good for making sure everything works. There's a free and paid version. There are others but these are the only two I've tried. The advertising stated that an MFi certified charging/data cable ships with the phone. Mine shipped with a 3ft braided USB C to Lightning charging cable. No branding or print on the cable, no included documentation, no packaging. It appears similar to what you'll sometimes see without packaging and hanging from peg racks in convenience stores. I have no reason to believe that the provided cable isn't MFi certified and from a reliable manufacturer but without more information, best to use an Apple product or something from an established aftermarket supplier such as Belkin or Anker. Look for 'MFi certified' especially if you want fast charging capability. There are reasons USB C cables can be pricey, especially those designed for high power delivery. Mine shipped without a charger. I'd say the same about a charger as I did about the cable - MFi certified and from a reputable manufacturer - Apple, Belkin, Anker, etc. For the 13 Mini, Apple recommends a minimum of a 20 watt charger for optimal/fast charging . Apple's is about 20 dollars. It's also what Apple recommends for powering *the original* MagSafe accessory. The updated version of the MagSafe charger supports faster charging and according to Apple, a minimum of a 30 watt charger for optimal performance. Some suppliers advertise that a sim card removal tool is included. Mine didn't. If yours shipped with a sim card (mine did not), I'd suggest reading through the pros and cons of SIM vs eSIM. If eSIM meets your needs, I'd recommend removing the SIM and switching to eSIM. Switching to eSIM can be done in your phone's settings. No expertise or hardware required. Although unlikely if buying from an 'Amazon-qualified supplier' (I assume), SIM cards can be compromised. If you need a SIM card, best to get one from your carrier instead of a mystery SIM. The Apple leather case has been my go-to for the last 2-3 iPhones. Very well designed, doesn't add significant bulk, comfortable to grip, no sharp edges and it slips into and out of a pocket easily. The drop protection has proven to be excellent. Great case for all but extreme circumstances. They're relatively pricey so If you're looking to save, there are often Amazon customer returns available. eBay is another good source. The iPhone 12 mini and 13 mini cases are not interchangeable. I tried. The camera lens housings are different. The 12 mini case will not fit the 13 mini. The 13 mini case will fit the 12 mini but there will be a gap on the right side of the lens housing. Not to overstate it but If you're considering both the 12 mini and 13 mini, battery life may be problematic for heavy users. If you have a full size phone with a larger battery at ≥ 90% battery health (guesstimate) and often find yourself scrambling to find a charger, the Mini may not be for you. If you're on the move a lot without convenient charging options, a small power bank (≤ 5000mAh) will bring some peace of mind and a lot of convenience. Great when traveling. Definitely stick with time tested manufacturers. Anker and Belkin sell a wide variety. Note that the TSA only allows powerbanks in carry-ons. Apple discontinued it's iPhone power banks (Magsafe Battery Pack). As of this writing, you can still find them new from third party sources such as Walmart and eBay. Never buy used. There are confirmed and very convincing counterfeits out there so I'd be cautious about which supplier you choose. Look up "how to check if an Apple Magsafe Battery Pack is counterfeit". *Update* Apple reintroduced it's magsafe battery pack now called the iPhone Air MagSafe Battery. It was designed specifically for the iPhone Air and reportedly works with other iPhones - sort of. Not recommended. Fit issues. If you're looking at both the 12 and 13 Minis, the 13 Mini uses an A15 processor which is somewhat more energy efficient and slightly faster. It also has a ~10% larger battery. There are quite a few other differences including an upgraded camera. In day to day use, I found the differences to be negligible. I suspect that most people wouldn't be able to tell the difference without knowing what to look for. Definitely worth reading comparison reviews. Some of the updates will be important for some, less so for others. Search for "iPhone 13 mini vs iPhone 12 mini". If you read only one, Laptopmag.com published a well grounded, real-world comparison, no hype. Long term, the 13 Mini will receive system/feature updates from Apple for about a year longer. This may be the most value added difference. Generally speaking, Apple devices continue to receive security updates beyond the point that they are no longer supported with system/feature updates. Current estimates seem to be late 2027 for system/feature updates and 2030/2031 for security updates. When the security updates stop, best to replace the phone. If Apple's AI (Apple Intelligence) is a feature you want, it isn't supported in the Mini's. You can still use cloud based AI services but without the privacy and security features Apple bakes into it's AI. You'll need a minimum of an iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max to use Apple's AI. Happy customer. I'm fully committed to the Mini form factor/dimensions. I carry it all day in a front or back pocket and barely know it's there. Having a phone with more screen, battery and features is nice but after the novelty wears off, having a phone that disappears into a pocket is more important for some of us. Sadly, not enough of us for Apple to justify continued production. When I need to replace it, perhaps Mini's will be back in the menu from Apple. Hope so. Review Title: I purchased & received this refurbished Samsung Galaxy phone around September 15,2024, for something
Review Content: I purchased & received this refurbished Samsung Galaxy phone around September 15,2024, for something like $225.00. I noticed the phone had a few glitches after a month. I attributed it to my learning how the phone worked & learning the new apps. After a few more glitches & adjusting the settings for several weeks. I knew this phone was defective. I lost keep-sake pictures, apps,typing on a website page screen & losing the page & info,the keys to type would freeze up, the home screen would freeze up, the pages would disappear as I read an article, the websites would stall, backspacing key would not backspace, typing was hard because at times some of the keys wouldn't work, space bar froze up at times, two different Samsung techs remotely checked my phone to no avail and my content was not found. I tried to get a replacement but one of the Samsung techs said my warranty had expired. On Amazon.com the last return day was December 12, 2024. Yet, the Top Notch Tech company would not replace the defective cell phone. A 3 month old phone that stopped working properly! Now I'm in communication with Amazon about their A to Z policy. I'm in the process of appealing the denied decision for replacing my phone or my refund by the seller. This $225.00 refurbished cell phone was a piece of junk. The phone is 3 months old no where being a year old for the warranty to expire. The refund or replacement policy is NOT TRUE for all involved. I shouldn't have to pay for repairs. Very dissapointed in both companies, especially, the sellers. Honesty should be a policy. Don't make advertisements that are dishonest. For the stress this has caused me needing my vital life line phone for health reasons....a new phone should be given to me of my choice. First review about this camera. I liked the larger screen but think I'll be returning the current model for a larger screen but the same model. I think the screen length is 6.9, for the largest screen which is best for my vision. The only things I didn't like for this refurbished cellphone was that no instructional manual booklet was enclosed. I Googled everything that I needed info or instructions on. The battery is good, the picture quality is good, & for an unlocked refurbished cellphone it was in great condition & easy to transfer over to my carrier. I give this phone an 9.0, because I had problems with transferring my apps to my newer phone. I had to download a wireless transfer app to get the job done. Review Title: ##### Well worth the money to go with Renewed Premium
Review Content: ##### Well worth the money to go with Renewed Premium. Edit to add: this is my 2nd phone I’ve bought from Amazon. My last phone (a renewed “good” SE 2nd gen) was bought at the end of 2022 and has been a reliable phone, I just wanted to upgrade and let the SE 2 (which after 3 years has 77% battery health) become my spare / back-up phone. I’m very happy with this seller & phone. Getting set up is proving challenging, but I’m thinking that’s an issue with my old phone & carrier that I’ll have to sort out after Christmas, not this phone itself so I’ll skip over the set up / switching from my old phone to this phone. (Edit: the issues I was having switching over from my old phone to this phone was I wasn’t paying attention to my account being locked to prevent unauthorized sim / phone number changes; once I went in my account and unlocked it, the switch went smoothly) Phone was shipped quickly (arrived the day after I ordered it) and arrived looking brand new, no scratches or scuffs, 98% battery health. (By contrast, I got my teenage daughter an iPhone 14 as well from another seller in “good” condition, her battery health was 87% which is still really good for a renewed phone) So far from what I’ve been able to tell with fairly limited use, I love the speed. It’s way faster than my SE 2 that I’m upgrading from. The battery holds charge pretty good. Since it had been charging during my set up & attempt to transfer from my old phone, it was at 100% so I unplugged it. 10 hrs later it’s at 96% (have used it some to take video and see what apps have successfully downloaded (transferred from iCloud because “transfer from another device” didn’t seem to be working—again very possible an issue with my old). (First initial charge to 100%, moderate use because I was still primarily using my SE2, battery lasted 36 hours 100% to 15%; now that everything has been switched over and I’m 100% using this phone, I’m expecting battery to be ok for all-day and ready to charge at night) — first full day of use near “typical” for me (took off charger around 5 AM, intermittent usage during the day; with no recharging during the day at 8:30 PM it was at 20%) After my experience with the SE 2 & the few days I’ve been using this 14, I will definitely be looking to buy my next phone on Amazon. Review Title: Finally the iPhone arrived, and in absolute perfect condition
Review Content: Finally the iPhone arrived, and in absolute perfect condition. I went with the “premium refurbished” option. The delivery was incredibly secure and the driver was extra helpful before they arrived so we could time it. I opened the box and there is not one scratch or thing that would tell you that this isn’t a brand new phone. It comes with a charger, block and the phone information on a leaflet (that would otherwise be in the original iPhone packaging). I did wait to activate it, until I had time to go into a physical carrier store, but I backed up everything before I did that in my old phone. It took maybe 5 minutes for the associate at my carrier store, to set the iPhone up and transfer everything I wanted from my galaxy and the service, to the iPhone. I was worried based on other reviews that it could possibly not be unlocked to all carriers, but it was. One of the main reasons I chose to buy the refurbished option from the sold by/ships by Amazon option, because I trusted the accuracy of the description more. ALL THAT SAID beautiful phone, looks brand new, works like it’s brand new, has 100% battery life out of the box and is very easy to get used to (even if you have had an android all your adult life). I definitely recommend this product and Amazon as the seller to ensure you get what you are looking for. I am SO happy with my purchase and when it comes time to get a new phone a few years from now, I will be starting here this time! The RED color is beautiful!!! Great sound, and they stay in the ear better than Bose’s fancier separate wireless earbuds. One of Bose’s big advantages is the shape of the part that holds them securely in the ear. They are also comfortable for long periods. I have no idea why the company decided to use a less effective shape when they upgraded to the fancy separates. When I was putting Christmas decorations up on a balcony last year, one of them fell out and landed in the bushes below. I rooted around the leaves looking for it, but I didn’t find it until I looked again the next morning. The newer models have some great features, and the microphone is better, but for anything involving physical activity—exercise, yard work, obviously Christmas decorations—I prefer these. They stay in better—really well—and if one falls out, it stays connected by the other one, so it doesn’t leave you. I don’t think Bose makes them anymore, so the ones I got recently are refurbished. That made me a little nervous, but they have turned out fine. The only thing I don’t like—and this may be true of any of them—is that the rubber parts that insert eventually break. The first to go is the connection to the plug that covers the charging port. That isn’t such a problem, because unless you’re going to expose them to a lot of dirt or water, you don’t really need a cover for that. Much more of a problem is when the rubber button that you press to push the power button breaks off, because then you have to use something to reach in and push it. I still have the original pair I got years ago, and I use them, but I use one of those plastic tooth flossers to push the on-off button. It is supposedly possible to replace the whole rubber piece, but it looked hard enough, and the parts would cost enough, that I decided to spend a little more to get a new (refurbished) set. Review Content: What I reviewed was an absolutely perfect iPhone. Even with a magnifying glass I could not find the slightest sign that it had ever been used before. It did have the current ios 26.5 on it suggesting the seller took the time to do a software update and make it so that i can go directly to settings to confirm everything then immediately start device to device transfer, this thoughtfulness saved me a lot of time. I did a direct device to device transfer instead of messing with iCloud. My old phone was an iPhone 13 with a physical version sim card inserted. It was first necessary to convert the physical SIM to an eSIM on the 13, this is easy and fast. Then the version account and phone number easily transferred along with absolutely everything from my old phone. Needless to say i am extremely happy with this iPhone and i am pleased i took a chance. As well this iPhone was a few hundred dollars cheaper then the other sellers, so i was expecting a beat up iPhone as that is what i paid for. I was certainly not expecting the perfect iPhone that I received. Product Title: Amazon.com: Samsung Galaxy S22 5G, US Version, 128GB, Pink Gold - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: It would seem my only option now is to take a risk with leaked / pirated firmware flashing, which I'
Review Content: It would seem my only option now is to take a risk with leaked / pirated firmware flashing, which I'm worried will trip the Knox security (which is the only reason I bought the phone in the first place, as Knox security was required by my employer). The phone itself is also disappointing. I started with a OnePlus 5t, which I was very happy with. When I was required to get a Samsung, I went to an A52 5g. The fingerprint sensor and face recognition were both so bad that unlocking the phone was a massive chore (something I do dozens of times a day). I suffered through this for a little while before upgrading to the S22. I very much resent the trend of under-display sensors which do not perform as well as their more visible counterparts. The S22 ultrasonic fingerprint sensor is vastly better than the optical one on the A52, but it still is inferior compared to a sensor on the back of the phone like on my older OnePlus. Heck, even my old galaxy S5 had a better fingerprint sensor. The face detection is a little better than the A52, but not as good as the OnePlus 5t. It really struggles in low light, and must be directly in front of your face. Nobody does face detection as well as Apple, but that's probably due to patent limitations (and I refuse to go back to iphone until they allow sideloading). One notable issue both the A52 and S22 suffer is an inability to detect they are in my pocket. I must deliberately place the phone with the screen facing outwards or else the fingerprint reader will constantly register false attempts against my leg (which will lock you out of using biometrics) Battery life is not impressive. Once again the 5t was better. This may not be entirely fair b/c I do use the always-on display, but on the other hand the processor should be much more efficient for how much newer it is. I mostly believe this is similar to the issue of constantly waking up in my pocket. A proper proximity sensor could have solved this rather than just using the selfie camera, which is again another example of form over function (It also seems like samsung doesn't even attempt to detect being in you pocket in order to reduce battery / ignore touch screen). Product Title: Amazon.com: Samsung Galaxy S22 5G, US Version, 128GB, Pink Gold - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: Even so, this hasn't been an absolute win for me
Review Content: Even so, this hasn't been an absolute win for me. This is my first Samsung phone in many years. I think the S4 or S5 may have been my last Galaxy. I've loved Moto phones for the last several years, and this definitely lacks some of the functionality that I've come to enjoy from Motorola: shaking for the flashlight, side button screenshots, hovering over for the time on lockscreen. The camera is an improvement over my Moto Z4. And the processor does seem to be quite effective. But the battery is far weaker than I was expecting, and I'm a little worried about how bad it may get after a year or two of use if it's this much of a challenge now (6 weeks of use). Additionally, the fingerprint sensor is very finicky. I'm guessing I have about a 30% success rate with it. I have a screen protector on, which may be a factor, but it's the same brand of protector that I have used for years without issue on my Motos. (And I did try another brand of protector, but it brought the success rate down to about 5%.) Set-up was more challenging than Moto set ups are. The Samsung app promised to reset my screen and everything, but I had to manually set it up after running the Samsung setup process. Perhaps it was challenged by having to move from a different brand, but I wasn't impressed. Samsung is supposed to be top of the line for Android, but I'll be seriously considering other options when this wears out. My hope is that Moto will catch up to industry standards, but if not, I may be willing to accept a slower processor in exchange for a better overall user experience. If I change my mind, I'll come back and update this review. Review Title: But even worse is all the other problems! Even after a software update, the software is ancient and
Review Content: But even worse is all the other problems! Even after a software update, the software is ancient and has glitches/problems everywhere. Many times while navigating with google maps, the software will glitch where you cannot use the back or home button which means if you were full screen for navigation, which I usually am, you cannot multi-task or even back out of the app when you arrive at your destination! I had to shut down the phone and reboot several times because of this. Other times the phone would just randomly lose the ability to zoom in or out with your fingers. Whether using a map, looking at pictures, websites, etc, the phone just "forgot" how to recognize two-finger zoom in and zoom out capability. Across all apps. Yet, had no issue swiping up, down, left or right, it wasn't a phone cleanliness issue or anything. Lastly it just started doing weird stuff, like if i pull up contacts and choose one name, it loads a different one. If i pick this option it does that. It just has a mind of its own and is frustrating. The battery life issue was immediate, but these other issues didn't start for a month or two, and I'm SO glad I kept the box and everything, today was the last day of the return window and I was able to return it. I would put up with a lot to not have to return a phone, it's a hassle, make sure all your stuff is on the SD card, factory reset, get your old cracked phone up and going again, yada yada, but this garbage phone was absolutely getting returned, no questions asked.GARBAGE! It feels like Samsung took a flagship, shaved off the price, and left the important stuff intact. No gimmicks, no weird corners cut, no regret spiral after checkout. Samsung knew exactly what they were doing with this one—and they did it right. Review Title: Out of the box, the screen wouldn't work correctly while charging
Review Content: Out of the box, the screen wouldn't work correctly while charging. It would randomly touch or swipe until you unplug it. I opened it up and replaced the charging port hoping that would fix it but no. While it was open, I saw that over half the screws inside were missing or in the wrong place. But the most concerning part: one screw had come loose and was pushing against the battery! It was already inflating so I replaced the battery right then and there. Another issue: the screen would occasionally become covered in static for a few frames during use. Due to this issue and the charging issue, I though maybe a replacement screen would fix both. It did not, and that turned out to be yet another waste of money into this endless pit of a device. Every single part in the phone is terrible. The aftermarket cameras are worthless, the motherboard is horribly glitchy and slow, the speakers sound awful, the original screen was terrible, and the antennae are constantly losing connection (eventually I was no longer able to receive calls at all!). Less than a year into ownership this phone is going into the garbage. I should've gotten a new A-series phone instead of this.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Product Title: Amazon.com: Samsung Galaxy S21 Ultra 5G, US Version, 128GB, Phantom Black - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: I decided to keep with Samsung as I rarely is ever have issues with them
Review Content: I decided to keep with Samsung as I rarely is ever have issues with them. I had an LG Stylo for less than a week before I went with the S8 after my S6. Found this deal. Advertised as 'Renewed - Excellent', and I knew what quality that would be as that's what my S8 was when I picked it up. So I went a little over budget to pay that premium. It wasn't quite worth it. Pros : Battery seems to be great, lasts about as long as the first ads for the S21 Ultra when it first dropped. It's now day 4 since I decided to test the battery and keep it off the charger. With light use, I'm still at 39%. The fingerprint scanner hasn't given me an issue yet, Audio quality on calls and playing music is better than I was expecting to be honest. The 5G is a lot better than the 4G I was at with my previous phone. The camera is working pretty well, though the 100x is a bit too blurry, but at 50x, for example, it's definitely usable. Screen quality still lives up to the hype, though I still need to tinker with the phone settings as the color seems a bit oversaturated. And, for a user of Boost Mobile, this has been the fastest switchover from phone to phone I've ever had. No calling in, no visiting a physical store, not even punching some numbers into an internet portal, just literally took the SIM from my S8, slid it into the new phone, and in seconds I was active. Even the Boost Mobile site had the updated phone information already registered. Cons: Here's where my praise kind of ends. As I said, it's not in Excellent condition. There are two noticeable scratches on the screen. On mid way up the phone from left to center that I can see at arm's length, and one in the lower right quadrant that I can see when the light hits it just right. At lest you can't see them with the screen on. Man, those two hard to get clear images of. I might not have noticed them if I didn't remove the ill-fitting screen protector with plans to replace it. There's some deformation in the bottom right corner as if that's where they used a metal tool to pry up the old screen. It's not sharp, but you definitely notice if you run your finger over it. The charge port is deformed as well. Slight bend on the rear side towards the front. Not enough to interfere with plugging it in, but it's there. And speaking of ill-fitting protections, the camera were covered with a piece of tape. Even after I removed it, it took more than a little work to clean off the adhesive that was left behind. They seller was 'nice' enough to include a cable and charger. The cable is a sub-standard 4 wire USB-A to USB-C. At least the data lines were connected so I could get SOME use out of it, but no chance of any change plugging it into a USB 3.0 port, as opposed to USB 2.0. The charger itself was a basic 5 volt 2.1 amp mini brick. I'm glad I already had the proper charger and cable so I could get the proper charging speed. So understand that you might not get what's advertised. According to Amazon's own policies, this should have been 'Renewed - Acceptable' at best. That $40 difference, from sellers providing the same, I could have put toward a case, proper screen protector, and maybe even a charge/cable bundle. Definitely not worth the full price I paid. Review Title: Several hours of backing up, transferring data and sim - now the phone is truly working and picking
Review Content: Several hours of backing up, transferring data and sim - now the phone is truly working and picking up where the prior phone handed off to the latest one. The challenge of course is you have a new phone - and its always a bit steep for the first few days trying to learn the new hardware/software and audit that the used phone does not have some hidden defect that is going to cost you more time and money. So, I'm happy for a few days and then one evening I discover that the bottom speaker (the top earpiece speaker is actually called the receiver) was not working well. scratchy and little to no volume - this had missed my attention entirely. A panic search online revealed Apple 12 speaker problems and them being repaired by Apple - crap! I went to a repair shop the next day, they ran Apple diagnostics on the phone and sure enough - speaker needed to be replaced - $120 for generic parts, $180 for Apple parts - they're not familiar with the Apple repair program (found out later that was for receiver speakers) - so this is half of the cost of the phone. No I'm committed to the new phone, don't want to lose it, but don't want to pay this either. Reach out to seller and explain the issue - they can even confirm the Apple diagnostic through the serial number - They offer $25 refund if I'll keep the phone. - So this tells me that they don't run diagnostics on the phones themselves - or do and hope that people will simply miss small items or accept them once they have sweat equity in the phone - or, it's all honest and by buying/selling a used phone both parties are taking a gamble. I chose to believe the latter. And accepted their offer. And here's the takeaway - the speaker now works - once in a while I might think I hear some scratchy, but unsure due to surrounding conditions. So for now, it's good, we'll see how long it lasts - but if I have to get it repaired - I took a chance - I say take a chance - you might get a perfect phone and save a lot in the meantime - I typically stay a few models behind the curve and benefit from software updates and people abandoning perfectly working phones for the latest models - AT&T typically had new old stock and I took advantage of that, but I have a grandfathered plan that they no longer make good money on, so I'm no longer eligible for that. Hope your experience is a good one - all the best, Don       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))       216 people found this helpful Helpful  Sending feedback...Thank you for your feedback. Review Title: While they go above and beyond in the marketing of the device “factory re-manufactured” and “certifi
Review Content: While they go above and beyond in the marketing of the device “factory re-manufactured” and “certified pre-owned” and ETC are all fancy wording for SECOND HAND, and USED. That said, with high hopes I purchased this device in May 2024 for my birthday, everything seemed to work fine, even though I noticed that the Maximum Battery Capacity was below 90%. —- Now in late January 2025 roughly only 8 months of use and the MBC has fallen to 77%, which has shown extreme degradation in that it cannot hold a charge. In addition, I have noticed that the touch screen is intermittent-Meaning that sometimes it works, and sometimes it does not. Sometimes no have to press multiple times and extremely firm—Note that all softer is up to day on the iOS, as well as the Apps used. Also note that I have equipped this phone with a highend sturdy case, which has kept it well protected, although it has not suffered any falls or drops of any kind. Additionally, the screen is and has been protected and covered since the day I received the phone and it still intact with NO cracks or scratches —- All that said, aside from the disappointment of the battery not being at 99% when received and now not holding a charge through the day even with a mid day recharge, I am surprised that I could not get to at least a full 2 years before minor or even major hardware degradation had set in. The question then lies with the company who is selling the phones vs the Apple product itself. I can say ALL my Apple iPhone devices have held the test of time and I’ve never had to upgrade due to hardware, but due to obsoletion. SO, it is my assessment that the company selling the second hand item needs to do a better job checking the devices before resale, as well as fairly pricing it for its age and prior use.-not to mention changing the battery component if it is below 90%. The one, and only good thing I can say was the phone appeared relatively new with little evidence of use meaning just monor scratches on the metal chassis housing, although this goes completely unnoticed as the phone is covered completely with protection. The status of the companies integrity is still up for debate, if they can accommodate my request for a replacement to a newer iPhone model, for which I will pay the difference I will then say happy shopping to all customers, if not, I will say be WEARY of buying used, older model iPhone devices by smaller relatively unknown companies. Review Title: Prime day comes along and I see this phone from this seller
Review Content: Prime day comes along and I see this phone from this seller. It was roughly $200 more than the regular IPhone 12 that we bought for my son but it was the Pro model and it did have 512k of storage. Due to the positive experience we had with the earlier purchase, I decided to pull the trigger. Fulfillment was great. I had ordered the phone on 7/11 and it was scheduled to arrive on 7/14 but to my surprise it hit my house on 7/13 which was a nice surprise. When I picked up the package I got worried because I could hear and feel something rattling in the box that was shipped in a form fitting padded envelope. To my relief I found the phone to be intact. It arrived with protective plastic on the screen, a SIM port tool, and a lightning charging cable that was loose in the box. Upon inspection I found the screen to be free of scratches or gouges but there is some slight surface marring on a small section of the screen that you have to look for in order to see. The bezel was clean except for a couple of nicks. The worst sign of usage is a chip above the top of the highest camera lens. It’s not huge but you can definitely see it and it looks like a chip in a car windshield since the back of the phone is finished in glass. The only other thing to mention is that there was a bit of what looks like green metal tape that was poking out of the side of the phone between the screen and bezel which I was able to rub off with my fingernail. It looked like the refurb process was not as clean as it could have been. Going into the settings I found that the max battery life was only 85% which was kind of a bummer. Setting up the phone was a breeze with ICloud but I haven’t figured out how to pull down the pictures that resided on my old phone. My apps came over but know I had to re-enter my passwords in most cases. After only a couple of day usage, everything seems to work fine. Amazon gives 90 days to return for any issues. The camera on the pro is a definite improvement over the 7+. Size wise the unit is smaller than the 7+ but the screen is bigger on the 12 since it doesn’t have the home button at the bottom which I keep wanting to press out of habit. Overall the purchase was better than ok. If the phone has another 10% of battery life and the nick on the camera was not present then I would rate the item as excellent. I’ll always wonder if I should have purchased a phone from the other seller that sold a phone in perfect condition. I will update this review should anything major happen with the phone. Review Title: Comenzando por su diseño, el iPhone 12 Pro exhibe una estética elegante y sofisticada
Review Content: Comenzando por su diseño, el iPhone 12 Pro exhibe una estética elegante y sofisticada. Su construcción de vidrio y acero inoxidable le brinda una sensación de calidad y durabilidad, mientras que los bordes planos y la pantalla OLED sin bordes le dan un aspecto moderno y atractivo. Además, cuenta con la certificación IP68, lo que significa que es resistente al agua y al polvo, brindando tranquilidad en situaciones cotidianas. La pantalla Super Retina XDR de 6.1 pulgadas es simplemente impresionante. La resolución de 2532 x 1170 píxeles y la tecnología HDR permiten una reproducción de colores vibrante y contrastes intensos, lo que hace que ver contenido multimedia sea una experiencia gratificante. Además, la tecnología Ceramic Shield proporciona una mayor resistencia a caídas y arañazos, protegiendo la pantalla de posibles accidentes. El rendimiento del iPhone 12 Pro no se queda atrás. Equipado con el potente chip A14 Bionic de Apple y 6 GB de RAM, este dispositivo ofrece un rendimiento rápido y fluido en todas las tareas. Ya sea que estés navegando por la web, jugando juegos intensivos en gráficos o utilizando aplicaciones exigentes, el iPhone 12 Pro responde de manera ágil y eficiente. Además, la compatibilidad con la red 5G brinda velocidades de descarga y carga impresionantes, lo que hace que la experiencia en línea sea aún más satisfactoria. La cámara del iPhone 12 Pro es otro de sus puntos destacados. Con su sistema de triple cámara de 12 megapíxeles, que incluye un sensor principal, un ultra gran angular y un teleobjetivo, este teléfono te permite capturar imágenes y videos impresionantes en cualquier situación. La tecnología de estabilización de imagen óptica y el modo Noche mejorado hacen que las fotos con poca luz sean nítidas y detalladas. Además, la capacidad de grabar videos en calidad Dolby Vision HDR a 60 fps añade un nivel adicional de calidad cinematográfica a tus creaciones. En cuanto a la duración de la batería, el iPhone 12 Pro cumple con creces las expectativas. Su batería de iones de litio ofrece suficiente energía para todo el día de uso moderado, y la carga rápida de hasta 50% en 30 minutos es extremadamente conveniente cuando necesitas cargar el teléfono rápidamente. En resumen, el Apple iPhone 12 Pro de 128GB es un dispositivo impresionante en todos los aspectos. Su diseño elegante, rendimiento poderoso, pantalla deslumbrante y cámara de alta calidad se combinan para ofrecer una experiencia premium. Si estás buscando lo último en tecnología móvil y estás dispuesto a invertir en un dispositivo de gama alta, el iPhone 12 Pro es una opción que no te defraudará. Review Title: I have a series 4 that has been my main watch for a while, now
Review Content: I have a series 4 that has been my main watch for a while, now. It does most of what I need it to do, and it is reliable in the things it does well. But the battery life is not great, as you probably already know. I wanted a backup to wear while I charge it. I tried a cheaper alternative, but I have grown accustomed to certain features, so I got this series 6 to use alternately with my series 4. The "always on" display option might be helpful at work where I look at my watch often. when I synced to my phone, it gave me the option to use my current watch settings, so I did that, which was very convenient. However, both watches have the same name, now, which is less convenient. Not a deal breaker, however. It is disappointing that the spo2 has been disabled by apple. But again, not a deal breaker for me. I am more concerned about the heart rate monitoring, which works pretty well for my purposes. I will try the sleep monitoring, as well, to see if I find it useful. there are plenty of useful watch faces and I like that they can be customized to some extent. I have one for work, and a few others for personal use. I haven't used many other smart watches other than a fitbit, which became glitchy, especially in reading my heart rate. The apple watches have been reliable and work well with my iphone. So I decided to stick with what works for me. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple Watch Series 6 (GPS + Cellular, 44mm) - Space Gray Aluminum Case with Black Sport Band (Renewed) : Electronics
Review Title: Protected by the same 6-pack of snap-on protectors, the capabilities far outweigh the inconvenience
Review Content: Protected by the same 6-pack of snap-on protectors, the capabilities far outweigh the inconvenience of keeping a device on my wrist. I used to not wear a watch at all, for lack of utility, and lack of comfort. Elastic fabric bands, and cheap snap-on protectors have provided much more protection and convenience than their cost. The battery still gets me through a whole day, and charges in an evening between returning from work and going to bed. Apple needs to come out with something spectacularly better for me to care about upgrading. Firstly, I’ve never liked wearing a watch, especially because I don’t like most bands available. So this was a big leap of faith. As for value, $260 (at time of purchase) seems reasonable for a backup cellular device like this. There’s a 1x3mm scuff right beside one of the band-slots, but no functionality is hindered, and a case covers it. -no other negative quality issues are noticed (yet). -It gives me volume control on my AirPods Pro through, which is the only feature AirPods Pro are lacking in built-in features. -I’m able to get important info without spending time on my phone’s screen (reducing overall usage of screens in a day). -the alarm sounds are well-thought, and the vibration feels like someone is sweetly grabbing my wrist and gently wiggling it to wake me up. On that note, even for me, the watch (and the bands I bought in addition to the stock band) is comfortable enough to sleep in. -watch faces aren’t as diverse and artistic as I hoped, but they’re still decent. I have one that shows me the sun’s relative position in the sky on a time-scale of the day (one of the Solar Dial faces), which makes me think differently about chronologically when I am in my waking hours. -If you’re going to use it for a phone call, don’t lift your elbow high like an antenna to listen on the same side. Cross over your chest and use the opposite ear like a proper Starfleet cadet. -I’m not a wristwatch kind of person, neither am I particularly fashionable. But this is comfy, and the availability of 3rd party cases and bands make it easy to add an essence of expression to your daily demeanor. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple Watch Series 6 (GPS + Cellular, 44mm) - Space Gray Aluminum Case with Black Sport Band (Renewed) : Electronics
Review Title: I come from using a Samsung Active 2 and there are SO MANY more apps
Review Content: I come from using a Samsung Active 2 and there are SO MANY more apps. Apps that they both have work better too. For example on my samsung, I could only respond to a facebook message if someone sent me a message. On the Apple Watch 6 I can find the app on the list and view all the messages, even pictures! I love that you can handwrite responses. Voice input is better as well. ECG: I have atrial fibrillation, so that was my biggest reason for buying the watch. I bought the Samsung Active 2 because I suspected heart issues but we could never catch them. The ECG on Samsung worked only when you put your finger on it. It often was really picky about the pressure you put on it resulting in lots of reading errors and artifacts. I switched to Apple because many other afib people said it can detect and alert you to an episode. I haven't had an alert yet but I think my afib is under control at the moment. Still, it gives much cleaner ECGs with almost no artifacts. Doesn't do the crazy up and downs that Samsung did if you didn't keep the pressure perfect when taking a measurement. The amount of health data that can be tracked is unreal. I was able to link my patient charts from my doctors which shows and takes into account health data. I have continuous glucose monitoring and log my readings in it also. It even links up with my pokemon go so much better. I'm super happy with this purchase. I saw it as an investment in my health and I got on top of that so many great additions that I didn't realize I was missing on Android/Samsung. I am now an Apple convert. Review Title: Upon arrival, I was satisfied with the phone despite the phone having much more extensive screen wea
Review Content: Upon arrival, I was satisfied with the phone despite the phone having much more extensive screen wear than expected AND a pretty poor excuse for a screen protector meant to cover up the screen wear. It is however an old model, refurbished phone, so that is to be expected. Upon receiving the iphone I promptly turned it on and tested the device, including the battery life. 91%. Given they guarantee 80% I thought I got really lucky and hit the refurbished jackpot. Well, fast forward not even a week and I decided to check the battery life again. 82%???? Now I am no engineer, but 9% battery degradation in less than a week sounds excessive. I figured its still above 80%(what was advertised) so I still got the product I payed for. I can live with a shorter battery life. Fast forward 7 more months of minimal use. The phone is on daily with very limited screen time. Work related texts and calls. Occasionally audible, or spotify use. Monitored all my charging to prevent over charging. Im not sure what rate of degradation is normal but given my use case mine seems to have died unreasonably quickly. I bought this as a cheaper alternative to a new iphone but 300 is by no means cheap and for a device that is quickly dying 8 months later. I am always a bit nervous buying refurbished tech, especially from Amazon. Buying refurbished is a flip of a coin and you may get luckier than me but this left a sour taste in my mouth and left me feeling inclined to leave this review as a disclaimer. In the future I will either buy new, or go the ebay refurbished route given their refurbs tend to be a bit cheaper and come with a 1 year warranty on all ebay certified refurbished tech. Good luck to all those in the market. If you decide to go this route, I hope you get luckier than I did. They were quick to identify the problem, took full responsibility for the customer experience, and immediately provided clear instructions and a prepaid return label for a full refund. This was 8 months after purchase, well beyond any normal return window. They followed through with every single action they said they would do, without delay or excuses. Things can go wrong with used phones, especially with carrier financing issues that don't show up at first. What defines a company is how they handle it. YY Wireless does what is best for the customer. I would buy from them again with complete confidence and this experience reflects very well on Amazon as a marketplace for sellers like them.
