Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple iPhone 17 Pro, US Version, 256GB, eSIM, Deep Blue- Unlocked (Renewed Premium) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: ##### Scary transaction w/ empty delivered box, but Customer Service replaced it
Review Content: ##### Scary transaction w/ empty delivered box, but Customer Service replaced it I had not purchased an Amazon Refurbished product before. But we were looking for a large capacity 1TB iPhone 17 Pro, and didn't find one available for under $1300 + tax at local Apple Stores. With the new iPhones coming out at the end of the summer, we didn't want to pay full price, but our old iPhone was full and wasn't working very well. So, during Prime Day sales, we decided to order a Renewed Premium iPhone 17 Pro 1TB from Amazon. It wasn't available for next day or 2 day delivery, but the priced was great under $1300. When delivery came, I was waiting by the front door like a little kid during Christmas. I opened the Amazon box showing 2 items inside and I grabbed the Renewed Premium box and there was no shrink wrap, no sealed close tape to prevent the box from being opened. In my hast, I didn't even record the box opening process. I just flipped open the lid and was shocked to find an empty box with just a charge cable and no iPhone 17 Pro. I looked at the Amazon outside brown box to check for tampering, looked good, one layer of table, not cut open and resealed. I called Amazon Customer service immediately, she said the driver made a mistake and would deliver it the following day (a weekend delivery). My order showed as delivered. - about $1300 and all I had was an emplty box with a USB-C charge cable. That's it. Did I just make the biggest mistake on this on-line order? Why didn't I. record opening the box? I felt bad, and thought driver error??? No way, the outside brown box was sealed. The refurbished box had to have been tampered with in the packing and shipping stage, not during the delivery. I called Amazon Customer Service again, explaining the empty box. They asked for photos which I took shortly after the delivery. They agreed to send a replacement. We got the replacement and were quite happy with it's like new quality. No signs of use, no nics or scratches and it's battery was at 100% capacity with I think 1 cycle on it. Amazon came through with a great replacement. It took several hours to restore and then add it to our account. But all works great now. So, it was a little scary with no product in an empty box, but Amazon Customer Service (my second - third calls) did fix the order and it was a great deal. Look at the refurbished details carefully, and video opening the box and the package contents so you have some evidence on what was was actually in the box. Especially if it is not shrink wrapped or sealed with tape. My video of the replacement didn't show the shrink wrapping well in the photo grab of the opening of the shrink wrap. Thanks to my 2nd and 3rd contact of Customer Service to resolve this purchase. And PS the iPHone 17 Pro is awesome and has lot so space to record kids and concerts. Review Title: Upgrading to iPhone 13 Pro Max which is the latest iphone that can take an actual sim card
Review Content: Upgrading to iPhone 13 Pro Max which is the latest iphone that can take an actual sim card. It's about the same/bigger physical size as my old iPhone 8 Plus (with a case on the 8 Plus) -- and so holding the new iPhone 13 Pro Max is like same in the hand for me -- but with the better iPhone 13 Pro Max. Easy to transfer apps & settings & data etc to the new iPhone. Bought this "Renewed" iPhone as "Refurbished - Excellent" from amazon marketplace seller MOBILESUPPLY whose 99% positive rating gave me the confidence that the condition of this iPhone 13 Pro Max would indeed be excellent & be like almost new. (NOTE: you have to dig into the amazon listing for this iphone to scrutinize all the sellers selling via this amazon iphone listing.) Review Title: The phone is as good as everyone reviews it to be
Review Content: The phone is as good as everyone reviews it to be. The camera is great, though this time it can actually auto focus unlike my s20 being sporadic. I really like the direction samsung is taking their software experience. Very useful apps and features, I don't feel like I'm missing out on anything important. Device care is one of my favorite tools. Maintenance mode is such an important feature. Diagnostics comes in clutch, I use it all the time to make sure my phone is in top shape and it does tell you when the battery life gets low as it did for me. When I got the phone, it got to work and automatically updated it's software to the latest versions all the way up to One UI 7 and android 15. Samsung plans to allow 7 years of updates I believe, which I'm all in favor for. I almost exclusively buy phones used or refurbished and even though 7+ years of updates may sound like a lot to some people or even excessive, it is perfect for people like I and many others who rely on used or refurbished phones. Last time I bought a refurbished phone, the s20 and I could only used it for 2 years before it will stop getting updates. Thank you samsung for being a top contender in this area. I appreciate the fact they finally are keeping flat screens at least on some of their phone models. Curved screens became one of the most annoying things I've ever come across with a phone because it doesn't offer any improvements on function or easy of use and exposes my phone to more damage from drops and open sides. I want my phone case to fully protect my phone. Apple doesn't even do curved screens, get rid of them all samsung. I was hesistant to buy refurbished/renewed from amazon as you always hear mixed reviews for this kind of stuff, anywhere really. I did an exhaustive amount of research and finally got familiar with the pros, cons and what to actually look out for when buying refurbished so you have the best chance as getting what you actually want. Once you know what to look for, it's pretty simple, you just have to know which specific seller to buy from, but most importantly which to avoid. There are some red flag sellers out there and here on amazon, I suggest you do your due diligence and figure out who they all are. Macalegin or whatever their name is, is a great one though, just look at the seller's reviews and that should tell you most of what you need to know. I've been using samsung off and on since 2012 and they have improved so much over the years. Starting with the s20, I finally felt like I was able to experience the way android is supposed to be, smooth, fast, etc. Now with the s24, I feel as though I don't need to continue looking for a better android experience. It's already here.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))       46 people found this helpful Helpful  Sending feedback...Thank you for your feedback.   Sorry, we failed to record your vote. Review Title: Unfortunately, Samsung's alternative is the 4-platform Notes and there is no direct conversion of me
Review Content: Unfortunately, Samsung's alternative is the 4-platform Notes and there is no direct conversion of memos to notes. I had to go through the process of converting each memo to a note and then allowing the 2 phones to synch it to the new one. This was a VERY long process and took days using all kinds of spare moments until it was done. I can work with Notes, and it has some good features, but the transfer from PC to Notes doesn't seem to work. Of course, despite the auto transfer program between the old and new phone being quite easy most of the apps require re-signing in again. The ONLY real complaint is that Samsung changed the architecture JUST enough, totally unnecessarily, so that my old Otter box and replacement screen shields won't fit, even though the phones are pretty much the same size. I should point out that the fingerprint recognition SW on the S24 is FAR superior to the S22, which worked better than Apple's (which they have abandoned solely to have face recognition), but still was weak. The physical reader on the S10 was fool-proof, but it didn't support 5G or dual SIM chips. So far, once Notes was completed, the only problem is STILL having to enter passwords all over again, and setting up fingerprint recognition again as well. Ironically, on the S22, app-specific fingerprint recognition worked FAR better than on the login screen. Product Title: Amazon.com: Samsung Galaxy A71 5G, 128GB, Prism Cube Black - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: First, I always thoroughly research reviews and weigh the negative reviews seriously, and discerning
Review Content: First, I always thoroughly research reviews and weigh the negative reviews seriously, and discerning if there is an theme of overall dissatisfaction-especially on specifics. So, although I did see some negative ones...the majority of reviews were pretty good! So although I understand reviews can be subjective based on preferences and expectations, I have to say my experience with this phone and purchase has been ABSOLUTELY INCREDIBLE! 10 STARS!!! **Second, I did order this one after I made the mistake of not realizing I needed to check compatibility of the carrier on an unlocked phone. I know, I know....but to be fair, before this purchase I haven't had a phone upgrade since 2016-not even 4G, sooo. So if you are looking to upgrade a phone and stay with your carrier, make certain your unlocked phone is also compatible with the carrier you use!** Anyway, back to the review. I ordered this 9pm on a Sunday and received it at 8am Monday via Prime. The box it came in was in excellent condition; completely sealed and not a mark on it. I opened the box, saw what looked to be a phone that was in perfect/brand new condition. No kidding! This phone had not a scratch, scrape, fingerprint on it. It had a clear plastic cover over the screen and came with one SIM/SD card key, one USB plug and one USB cord (in original package). As soon as I plugged it in, it was already charged at 44%. Popped in my SIM/SD card. I powered it on and it was FULLY UNLOCKED for T-Mobile. I started the Smart Switch to transfer my data from my old Samsung. Within less than 20 minutes; all of my data, pictures, videos, apps, messages and all other data was fully transferred to the new Galaxy A71 5G. I unplugged the phone when it was at around 88% and have been using it nonstop for about 7 hours to sign in to all of my apps, take many personal and business calls (long ones), many texts as well as customizing my preferences; and it is STILL only at 36%! Calls are crisp, speed with everything is lightening fast, ringers and sounds are perfect and the phone on speaker and Duo/Meet for video calls are amazing. Creative and vibrant screen/colors make this an extra special gift to myself even better and more enjoyable. I am over the moon with this purchase and my teens can't believe I am now in the Cell Phone 21st Century! KUDOS TO THIS SELLER, WELL DONE!! Review Title: I had this phone for 5 days
Review Content: I had this phone for 5 days. 3 days I did nothing with it. After I charged it each day the battery went down maybe 3 to 5%. The day I added everything to it it kept connecting to the charger. Then I started using it and it seemed like it was being recorded while I was on the phone. The speaker phone seemed to sound like it was under water. So the second day actually using it I came here to get a replacement. Mind you nothing was wrong with the charging of the battery. I plugged it up last night (right after ordering a replacement) and it charged fine. and I went to bed. I woke up to the phone bring almost dead. I unplugged and replaced. Nothing. I realized I needed to factory reset the phone to send it back. As all my personal information is now on the phone. So I tried to factor reset it. It was at 9%. So it wouldn't. Because it needed to be at 10%. The phone began to rapidly lose charged until it got to 3%. I realized the wifi and location was off. So I turned those off. At 3% I was able to remove all the things from the phone but couldn't find the trash to make sure. So I canceled the replacement and I'm charging the money I paid for this one as a NEVER AGAIN LOST! Because I WILL NOT send it back with the possibility of all my information being in the phone. I don't trust this. I feel like this was done on purpose to get information when we send them back. Review Content: The performance is just as quick as I had hoped, and all the functionalities like the camera and fingerprint scanner are operating superbly. While it could have been my own fault, I rely way too much on my phones for security to risk the chance that it wasn't. So for now, I found arguably an even better deal from the same seller for the s10+. I'll be losing 5G and a better camera. If the impact on my 5G>4G experience is noticeable, I may go back to the a71 at a later time. **Went ahead and began return process, but again this probably should not reflect poorly on the seller or the phone itself. The shut-off could have entirely been some sort of missclick that I didn't see, but I will never know and don't want to find out. Product Title: Amazon.com: Samsung Galaxy A71 5G, 128GB, Prism Cube Black - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: Like everyone else I did a ton of research on this phone before I decided to purchase it
Review Content: Like everyone else I did a ton of research on this phone before I decided to purchase it. I compared it to the non 5G A71, the A51, and the S20FE and this phone takes the cake. The price, the features, and 5G along with customer reviews and YouTube reviews gave me hope to take a chance. If it didn't turn out to be what I wanted I knew I could always send it back. Great screen - the AMOLED is stunning and its 6.7 inches Camera - actually exceeded my expectations pictures come out crisp and you have the macro camera for close ups Face recognition - Almost instantly unlocks my phone, faster than my S10e Plastic/Glass back - Actually feels just like a glass back but you can tell its plastic. Did a great job on it though. Processor/Ram - Nothing to fancy but its quick and never lags. Gaming is no issue if you're into that. Headphone jack - yup, you get one on this phone. I find it convenient. Superfast charging - It takes about an hour for a full charge. Battery life - its pretty good. Easily get you through a day and into your next Fingerprint sensor - a bit hard for it to read my finger sometimes (Face ID is faster) Speaker - Almost worthless. I rarely use it anyways but you can tell Samsung didn't do much with it. Non-waterproof - this is a bit of a bummer. For my job I'm out in the elements and I don't have that peace of mind like I did with my last phone but I got a case which helps in case it does get wet. I honestly almost cannot tell its not a Samsung flagship model and my friends ALL thought it was an S20+ when I showed it to them. At around $360 after tax with all the goodie features from the flagship phones and with 5G you really are getting a deal here. They say it's a "midrange phone" but it truly is a luxury phone. For the case I bought the Otterbox Symmetry clear case. 10/10 I recommend buying. It looks brand new, performs perfectly, and delivers the full Apple experience without compromise. If you’re thinking about going the refurbished route, don’t hesitate—this is 100% worth it. If you’re after a powerful, premium smartphone that performs just like new but without the full retail cost, the Apple iPhone 16 Pro (256 GB, Black Titanium, Unlocked and Renewed) is an excellent choice. Review Title: I use Mint Mobile, so I needed an unlocked phone, hence why I purchased here
Review Content: I use Mint Mobile, so I needed an unlocked phone, hence why I purchased here. I bought a listing being sold and shipped directly by amazon.com instead of a third party seller. I had originally bought a listing from the seller "Wcell" but they never shipped it, then gave me a new shipping estimate of another month... So I canceled and reordered directly from amazon. I figured it would be less hassle to skip a third party seller if I needed to return the phone, anyway. I paid for shipping so I would get it sooner. I did NOT get it sooner (or even soon in general) and it was shipped via USPS instead of UPS or Fedex, which shocked me. I've never had something so expensive shipped parcel select before. Why did I even pay shipping? Phone arrived in an unassuming box aside from the giant lithium battery warning sticker, which gives away that it's an electronic no matter how discreet they try to be. Inside package was another plain box with a serial number sticker on it, containing the phone and an unbranded double USB C charging cable. Nothing else. No paper, no invoice, not even an Amazon Renewed flyer I've seen in other reviews. It sat in my mailbox under the hot sun for a few hours before I could get to it, which is Not Great for the battery, and when I opened it the phone was hot to the touch. So keep this in mind when ordering. The phone's outer condition is okay, but not quite up to the standard promised. This phone was listed as REFURBISHED - EXCELLENT, which states it should have "no visible cosmetic imperfections when held at an arm's length". However there are multiple scrapes on the titanium trim around the screen, leaving highly visible shiny silver specks against the black titanium, and a large scratch in the screen itself (pictured) The placement of the scratches lead me to believe the screen has been removed and the metal was scraped by a jimmy tool while prying it open. Maybe the screen was replaced? Maybe the screen had to be removed for another repair? Who knows. I would be surprised if it was a replacement unless they managed to scratch the new screen immediately after. The battery is GREAT. It arrived to me at 1%, but that's the mail's fault. Phone has been anctive since December 2024 but battery only has TWO (2) cycles on it and 100% capacity. The battery was definitely freshly replaced. I personally don't mind the cosmetic damage enough to worry about trying to get a replacement, it took long enough to get it as is and the phone itself works just fine. If anything now I won't feel bad if I add a flaw in the future, but I know a lot of people won't feel the same way I do so I wanted to put my experience out there. So to recap, phone is what I would call Repaired. Brand new battery replacement, suspected screen replacement, with some cosmetic damage. Otherwise perfectly fine phone. I'll update if anything changes with normal use. RIP in peace banana phone. You served me well 🍌 🫡       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Review Title: I run and used to track my progress with my iPhone but I don’t really like carrying with me
Review Content: I run and used to track my progress with my iPhone but I don’t really like carrying with me. The fitness data collection such as steps, heart rate and workouts have really helped me out. The durability of the watch is outstanding and although I have dropped it twice I have yet to scratch it. Though I did break a screen protector that I put on it when I dropped it. Calling on the watch is nice when I have to take the call and I haven’t had any complaints about being able to hear me. My only complaint is I am not wild about the band that came with it. It appears to be an Apple original band but it is easy for the c shape clasps to come off during heavy usage such as pushups when the hand is angled backward the metal clip pushes off the band and falls off. I have had this happen a few times and caused the watch to fall off onto the floor. I’m not too worried about this as I plan on replacing the band when I find one I like. It is really clever and easy to remove the bands for replacement. Nice engineering on that. I don’t really use much of the other apps other than fitness or weather and of course time. But there are many and with the large screen they are easy to use and the interface easy to navigate. When it comes time to replace the watch I am sure I will purchase another Apple Watch, though I am uncertain if it will be new since I had good luck with this renewed purchase. Product Title: Amazon.com: Motorola Moto G Power 2025, 128GB + 8GB RAM, Slate Gray - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: ##### Great value for the price — just know what you’re getting
Review Content: ##### Great value for the price — just know what you’re getting Okay, let me start by saying that I've been browsing refurbished/reconditioned phones on Amazon for some time, so I know exactly what to expect when I press the "buy" button on the refurbished device. With that in mind, this Moto G Power 2025 made a bigger impression on me than I thought it would. The good things first. The performance is solid in relation to the price. I'm not an avid player, but I broadcast on YouTube, I use TikTok, I use Google Maps all the time and I send text messages all day, and this phone can handle everything without sweating. The battery life is really excellent, which is kind of a whole Motorola thing with the G Power line, and it provides it. Constantly, I spent a whole day and a half with a single load. 8 GB of RAM also means that it is not delayed when switching between applications, which was a pleasant surprise in this price range. Now "renewed" the control of reality, and I'm not saying this as a complaint, but as a sincere warning to anyone who hasn't ordered refurbished phones before. This phone came with visible scratches on the back panel, some small scratches around the edges, and a very light hair feature on the bottom corner of the screen (visible only when the screen is off). Nothing that doesn't affect functionality ABSOLUTELY, but if you're someone who needs to make your phone look flawless, then that's not for you. I saw that the previous owner definitely used this phone every day. The screen itself works perfectly, there are no dead pixels, there is no exhaustion that you can detect. To be honest, the gray color hides the scratches better than the lighter color. It arrived unlocked as announced, I inserted the SIM card and it was ready to work in a few minutes. The camera is decent, nothing that competes with the flagship, but it is completely good for daily photos and video calls. Conclusion: When it comes to the price difference compared to buying a new one, the small consumption of cosmetics is, in my opinion, a compromise without zastu. If you buy refurbished, you buy for value, and that's what it provides. Just don't wait for a call in the living room, and you won't be disappointed. Would I buy it again? Yes, without hesitation. Review Title: My only problem is with Bluetooth, and that might just be the older devices I'm connecting to
Review Content: My only problem is with Bluetooth, and that might just be the older devices I'm connecting to. (It always throws an error when connecting to my car stereo, but if i disconnect and then connect manually, it connects just fine - this would be a massive problem for a music-obsessed getaway driver, since i can't just get in and go; it takes a couple of minutes to complete the autoconnect, and manually disconnect & connect. Thankfully I'm not a getaway driver, just someone who would prefer to get in and go without this hassle. Again, could be a problem with the car stereo, or just a compatibility issue.) Also, sometimes when i'm connected to my 5.1 home theater audio system, the audio is super choppy. Another thing that COULD well be the other device and not the phone. I wish Android made it easier to dump BT cache and turn off BT autoconnect, which would probably solve these issues. You'll want to always shoot in Pro mode, or use a 3rd party camera app. Motorola's stock camera app refuses to not apply stupid beauty filtering, which smears faces and makes it look like people are wearing uncanny leather masks. Using a 3rd party camera or shooting in Pro mode alleviates this. Pro mode doesn't require a photog degree; most settings do have an auto function. Even then, the camera still lacks detail. If you're getting this for photography, you might want to consider a different model. The Google Pixel phones are real standouts in that regard. This is just a budget phone with otherwise good-to-surprisingly great specs after all. It's genuinely a very good phone - not a stellar phone, but definitely not a crappy phone by any stretch either. It's replacing a Pixel 4a 5G. I got it for the headphone jack, the fat battery, the ruggedness, and the microSD slot. Overall: I’m incredibly satisfied with my purchase. Review Content: I've never owned a smart watch because I'm really hard on watches and I just thought they were expensive, fragile gadgets. It also makes it fun competing against myself. I put the watch on my cellular service and it works well. I enjoy having access to my phone and many apps without bringing my iPhone. Based on my experience, I definitely recommend the refurb watch. No problems and it came in an excellent, like new condition. I also recommend the Ultra 2 for watch face size, longer battery and low power mode, brighter screen, waterproof depth and ruggedness. Review Title: The bad

Review Title: This watch is incredible
Review Content: This watch is incredible. I have done the following since having the watch: Outdoor work (chopping wood, cleaning a nasty chicken coop, setting up a treestand) I’m sure there is more but I wanted to emphasize I’ve done A LOT with this watch. I also did a run on the beach but I took the watch off when going in the ocean. I possibly didn’t need to but salt water is just so corrosive I didn’t want to risk it. This watch has performed flawlessly the entire time. I’m more than impressed. My son bought one of these new when they first came out and paid double what I paid. My cons list is short: (and really not the seller but the watch itself) I didn’t realize if you have a tattoo where the sensor sits it will not read correctly. I thought something was wrong with my watch but did a little research and found it was the tattoos on my wrist…I verified this by moving the watch to an area with then without and watching the watch shut off. I now choke the watch up a little closer to my hand (which can be annoying sometimes when working out) and it works perfectly. Also…I think sunscreen might affect the sensor as well. I had sunscreen on and the watch was doing a similar thing that it did with the tattoo. I wiped the sensor and my wrist off and it started working fine. Lastly I do wish the watch came with a little better charger…the one they sent me works just fine but it’s slow as can be. The charger my son has charges our watched in 1.5-2 hours. Overall…everything I’ve said below is just as (if not more) relevant. I wouldn’t hesitate to buy this watch again. I’m extremely satisfied. I would have shared a picture or 2 but amazon asked permission to all my pictures and that isn’t happening. I’m writing this knowing I’ve only had the watch for 3 days. I plan to update my review before the 90 day return runs out and after I’ve had more time with the watch. I got this watch specifically from seller prime mobility. They have very high feedback ratings so I was happy to take a chance with them in this watch. I bought the watch in “like new” condition. The seller was prompt with shipping and communication. At this point I would recommend them highly. I did a lot of research on what watch to get for fitness and overall health. It seems with all my research, for people who aren’t super techy and have an iPhone the Apple Watch is the way to go. I’ve never owned an apple or any other smart watch/smart device. I wanted this to track my 5 day a week gym workouts, sleep, and heart rate with running, meditation, and cold plunging. I honestly only have 1 con at this point. The watch came with a sticker right on the health tracker and the glue was annoying (really not hard just annoying) to have to remove. The pros are many: the watch came with %100 battery health witch I was surprised about. I’ve been using it and I’ve only had to charge it every 1.5 days. It also looks great. No visible issues, problems, blemishes at all. Lastly, the first day I had it I did a 10 minute cold plunge. The watch was under water for 10 minutes and had no issues. The watch quality meets my expectations completely and even exceeded them regarding battery life. I’m incredibly happy with my purchase. I can’t speak for other sellers but I feel prime mobility did me well in this purchase. Again, I will be updating my review before the 90 day return runs out but at this point I don’t have any concerns or apprehensions. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple Watch Series 6 (GPS, 44mm) - Blue Aluminum Case with Deep Navy Sport Band (Renewed) : Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry
Review Title: Battery life - Better than anticipated
Review Content: Battery life - Better than anticipated. Apple promises 24hrs, I’m seeing more than 36hrs. Resolution - V good. Sharp & clear. Better than a lot of friends watches. Touch sensitivity- Excellent. Accurate (even on the smallest of icons/text). V responsive and no lag no matter how quick or lightly u touch it. Brightness - V good. I haven’t had it fade-out in the Florida sun and can always read it. Fitness tracker - Excellent. The native work out app has multiple modes (gym, tennis, rowing, cycling) and can detect what activity ur doing. It displays pulse, active calories and total calories. Health tracker - Excellent. The watch comes w blood oxygen monitoring, heart rate monitoring and more. I’ve only used the HR & BO and have found the pair to be accurate. Additionally, the latter have helped me fine tune some eating habits as I wasn’t aware how much certain foods affected my HR & BO. Sleep monitor - V Good. I’ve found this has helped me drive towards a better nights sleep. Apps - Excellent. Apple Watch has more apps than u can shake a stick at, and they work well. Apple Pay - Excellent. The convenience of using ur watch over fumbling for a wallet or phone is off the charts. Additionally, it works perfectly. Telephone calls - Excellent. Receiving and making calls is a breeze and has worked flawlessly. I never expected to use this feature but the watch speaker is loud/clear and the person at the other can’t tell I’m calling from an external device. This is especially impressive since the call is relayed through my iPhone. Texting - Excellent. The Siri/dictation features are excellent. I can send receive texts flawlessly (no more phone fumbling) and the manual input works flawlessly too. The only drawback is u can’t select emojis but if u say “happy face”, Siri will insert the latter in character form. Setup - It’s pretty much a breeze. Charge the watch, download the Apple watch app to ur phone. Put the watch by the phone and follow the instructions. Any apps that can b transferred from ur phone will be transferred. Usefulness - Off the charts. This is not so much a watch but a miniature digital Swiss Army knife. The watch is unobtrusive and having so many of our daily digital-needs on a wrist makes life a lot easier. There r a lot more features to suit how u would use it. I thought I would find the short battery life a nuisance, not at all. Plus I don’t use the watch everyday….at times my wrist will go commando or I’ll wear a real watch to mix it up. I would recommend purchasing a protective case for it….the one I have is a chrome silicon thingy that protects against scratches, dings and has a raised lip to protect the screen. I am so glad I gave this ‘6’ a try before purchasing a 7. The leap between the two is marginal (despite what the marketing dept would have u believe). V happy w purchase and hope to keep the device for a long time.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Review Title: That said, the phone seems larger and heavier than I expected
Review Content: That said, the phone seems larger and heavier than I expected. It also needs more charging than I would have liked since most of the time it sits in my purse, unused. I didn't realize that the usual usb cables wouldn't work to charge the phone in the car. I bought a Tello card so I could sign up for the cheapest ($8/month) account. There seems to be no way to know how many minutes or data I have used without checking on my computer. This is not terrible but it is a nuisance. If iPhones weren't so outrageously expensive I would have bought another one of those but this will do for a backup. Also, I ordered a sage green phone but the one I received looks more gray so I bought a cover. Update - after trying several different options (downloading android auto, plugging in the usb cable, unplugging the cable for my iPhone, activating Bluetooth, etc.) I gave up and decided this phone is just not making me happy so I'm returning it. Review Title: When the watch arrived, I was pleasantly surprised by its condition
Review Content: When the watch arrived, I was pleasantly surprised by its condition. The screen looked great with no noticeable scratches during normal use, and the aluminum case was in excellent shape. If I hadn't known it was renewed, I would have assumed it was new or very lightly used. Setup with my iPhone was quick and straightforward. Within minutes I had notifications, fitness tracking, Apple Pay, and my favorite apps synced and ready to go. The watch feels responsive, and navigating menus is smooth with no lag or performance issues. The 44mm size strikes a nice balance between screen space and comfort. The display is easy to read, whether I'm checking messages, tracking workouts, or glancing at the weather. The Midnight aluminum case and matching sport band also give it a clean, modern look that works well for both casual and professional settings. Battery life has been consistent throughout the day. I typically wear it from morning until bedtime for activity tracking, notifications, and occasional workouts, and I still have battery remaining at the end of the day. Charging overnight has become part of my routine. One of the biggest benefits has been the fitness and health tracking. Activity rings, step counts, heart rate monitoring, and workout tracking provide useful information without being complicated. It has helped me stay more aware of my daily activity levels. Battery health may vary slightly between renewed units Does not include some premium features found on higher-end Apple Watch models Overall, the Apple Watch SE (2nd Gen) delivers a great smartwatch experience at a more affordable price point. If you're already in the Apple ecosystem and want reliable notifications, fitness tracking, and everyday convenience, the renewed version is an excellent value and performs much like a new device. Review Title: Pairing to my iPhone 15 was as simple as placing the watch next to the iPhone, with Blue tooth enabl
Review Content: Pairing to my iPhone 15 was as simple as placing the watch next to the iPhone, with Blue tooth enabled, and following on-screen instructions. The watch did require updating the iOS to 26 before pairing could be completed. So, don't be in a hurry to use the watch after you receive. Give it time to update and pair. The watch did come with a new band, and a wireless charger with USB C connector. I have already taken advantage of the many health features of the Apple Watch. It's been great so far. If I am to dock any points off this purchase, it will be 0.5 pts for the wireless charger. It seems to be low Wattage as it took about 4 hours or more to first charge the watch. I was using a power block rated 35 watts, so it wasn't my power supply. I recommend to anyone buying an Apple watch to purchase a screen protector of some type. I also recommend purchasing a wireless charger with higher output. I did end up purchasing a 22W 3 in 1 wall charger with built-in magnetic Wireless charger for Apple watches. The wireless charger is rated 2.5 Watts, and it charges the Apple Watch SE much quicker than the corded charger provided with the watch. Product Title: Amazon.com: Samsung Galaxy S22+ Plus 5G, US Version, 256GB, Phantom Black - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: EDIT2: 7/9/2023 Okay the line is not going away after locking and waking the phone like it did befor
Review Content: EDIT2: 7/9/2023 Okay the line is not going away after locking and waking the phone like it did before. You can see in the second picture, it's faint, but it's there (ignore the orange glow, that's from my old s7 that can't take pictures of other screens without struggling). The fact that it wouldn't go away makes me think it's getting worse. I had to restart it this time to make it disappear. Went ahead and started the refund process because it seems like it's getting worse. Unfortunate because this was labeled as an excellent condition phone too. I guess it's hit or miss what you get when you buy refurbished. I'm not a phone repairman, so I'm not going to be able to open it up and figure it out. I'm just gonna refund this and get a different phone to avoid the problem happening again. EDIT: Okay, it's been 4 days since the review. Woke this morning and unlocked my phone, typical. Was adjusting notification volume settings then all of a sudden BAM, bright PINK (not green this time) line right through the same spot as usually from top to bottom of the screen. Wanted to take a picture with my old phone but was afraid of leaving the error on the screen for too long (was busy using restroom) so I locked the phone and unlocked it again and the line went away. Man... I might return this thing because this is scaring me. So far the phone has been pretty great. One thing's for sure though, it's crazy the difference (s7 to s22+) 2 oz of weight (including cases) can feel while holding it. This thing feels like I'm holding a brick compared to my old phone lol. All of these things that I am giving it accolades for are, of course, from a biased perspective of somebody who has used the s7 since it's launch, so take it with a grain of salt if you are coming from something like an s20 or later. Great/Solid battery, Great performance, Great visuals. Little heavy though. Those are the main points. Since it is refurbished, the only actual visible damage you can see well is the small scratch at the bottom left corner of the screen (as seen in picture) that is on the glass for a length of about 2mm and then goes off to the side a bit. Not a problem though, it's quite out of the way. Saving around $350 just to have a scratch on the screen is quite the deal. I make my phones last, so this thing is going to be built like a tank by the time I'm done putting protective layers and cases on it. (This is the reason for the 4/5 and not 5/5) So far my only real scare with this phone (purchased as an excellent condition renewed s22+ with 256gb storage from Macalegin Electronics) is, since I've received it as of June 29th, it's now July 3rd, it's had this very thin vertical green line from the top of the screen to the bottom of the screen 3 times upon waking the phone. Seems to really only happen when I wake the phone. If I see it again I'll try to take a picture with my old phone and add it to the review. First time it happened I kinda had a mini freak-out, thinking that this is the end of having this phone and I gotta return it before it's too late and it gets worse. If it does get worse and more frequent, then I will get the refund because that's unacceptable as an excellent condition phone. Some people online say that it is because of a loose connection from the motherboard to the screen panel (I don't know the actual technical lingo), usually caused by the phone being dropped. Well, it's "brand new" to me, so it wasn't me who dropped it. Either way, the phone is great except for that scare. To be honest though, I do miss my more compact and sleek phone designs. I do kinda wish I had gotten the s22 instead, but I wanted to see what it's like having a bigger screen. Well, we'll see as the years go by.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Review Title: I was a Samsung owner from the start but I recently just had the pixel 6 for 2 years before it tragi
Review Content: I was a Samsung owner from the start but I recently just had the pixel 6 for 2 years before it tragically broke. Coming off a pixel there is really only a few things I miss. In pretty much every other way tho this phone outclasses the pixel 6 in every way. The one thing that works much better on this phone is the fingerprint sensor. It's fast and super responsive. If you have any problems with it after you put a screen protector on, you can change a setting in your phone that accounts for that. This phone is great and works just as well as a new phone even tho it's renewed. The only issue I have with it is that i said that it was in excellent condition but when I got it the was a few chips on the top of the camera bump, but that doesn't really bother me tbh cuz I already wear a case all the time. Another thing is the battery life isn't the greatest on this device but it gets the job done. Power saving mode works well on it so I usually have no issues, plus if you have a fast charging block the phone can charge literally like lighting fast Overall other than the chips on the device I would give it a five St⭐r. Only reason I actually dock a star is because it said excellent which means pretty much brand new, and for some people that matters more to them. Review Title: Everything seemed to be going well when I got the item
Review Content: Everything seemed to be going well when I got the item. It is in fantastic external condition, but within the first day, I realized that the battery would not hold charge. I inspected it after it happened the second day and found that the battery capacity is significantly degraded, down to almost 70%. This is refurbished, so I definitely don’t expect 100%, but I think it’s reasonable to expect 85% or above. What is the point of having this watch if I can’t even wear it long enough for it to get a read before I have to charge it again? Then, four days after its arrival, the side button started malfunctioning. It kept showing the “emergency services” screen when it was just sitting on the nightstand, constantly. The screen showed that the little side icon for the button was held down, even though the button was not stuck at all. This led me to shut the entire thing down every night so that it wouldn’t accidentally call the police! The two days after that, the screen suddenly went black (full charge) and the device entered an infinite boot loop. Just the Apple logo, black screen, Apple logo… etc. every ten seconds. It will not turn on or off, it will not hard reset or force reset. I’ve watched every video. I chatted with Apple support (where Amazon sent me to solve the issue, strangely), who told me it would cost almost $400 to fix the watch. Why on earth would I do that? Review Title: As for Apple's iPhone Touchscreen, again, I find it sorely lacking
Review Content: As for Apple's iPhone Touchscreen, again, I find it sorely lacking. There's no such thing as the simple pinch & zoom on it. That particular luxury seems to be found only within the Camera & Picture sections. You'd think it'd at least be within the iBook section but it's not. On most everything Windows or Google, every app is not just touch & activate, but also affords the luxury of pinch & zoom as well as easy swipe & easy app close & dismiss. Can't say that about the Apple iPhone. And for some unknown reason its WiFi also keeps turning itself on. I can't seem to keep it off no matter how often I manually turn it off. For Apple being so USER-FRIENDLY, I cannot at all say that it is. In fact, IT IS ANYTHING BUT USER-FRIENDLY. If the Apple World was so user-friendly, then it would be a very simple and easy transition from the Windows or Google platform to Apple. And I can honestly say it is Not at all simple or easy. I was so hoping it would be as simple & easy as my Windows machine & Android phone, but sadly, it's actually quite maddening. If you enjoy Kindle reads, you'll need to install the app for it. But I can also tell you, Apple's iBook seriously pales in comparison to Kindle. Ironically, the Google Search Engine is installed on Apple's iPhone but Kindle is not. I avoid Google anything & everything as much as can be done. But for Apple to deny Amazon's Kindle Apple on its phones, seems almost a crime. I have yet to install the Kindle reading app or to test out the camera on the iPhone. When I do I'll update my review. But currently I can't say it's anything to brag about. And I most certainly did not expect to see Google's Search Engine/Web Browser on it. Size wise, it's the exact same size as my Sony Xperia Z3v. It still functions quite well. Not perfect, but well enough for me since I have it locked to call, text, Kindle reads & camera. I can easily read, pinch & zoom & highlight my Kindle reads, pictures & text messages on it. Can only do that with pictures on the iPhone. So for it being so great, I actually find it quite limiting. Not because it's an iPhone, but because the Apple creators decided to create a platform that is quite complex and extremely arduous to use. Apple created its own "language" that must be learned in order to navigate the complexities of its Eco-system. Even now, trying to login to the Apple App Store, no keyboard appears so I can actually install Apps necessary for my personal use. Yet you're required to sign in to it. How can you sign into the App Store when NO KEYBOARD APPEARS TO LET YOU?! So, even if I did not want to use the phone feature, but instead use it as a computer tablet, I cannot because it won't let me login to the App Store. ... Like I said, to anyone new to the Apple world, it's quite a infuriatingly maddening conundrum. If Apple wants to gain new customers and retain them, then Apple needs to change how it operates. And if Apple is supposed to be the safest of all online platforms, then it should not sport Google's web browser. The phone I received was/is like brand new. Operating it though, takes considerable patients as it is quite the learning curve. It should not be so difficult to transition from Windows, Android or Google to Apple. They all made sense to everybody from the moment they came out because they were in simple English and easily understood and simple to navigate because of it. Apple on the other hand, not by a long shot. Even Apple's touchscreen capabilities sorely lacks in comparison. And that's sad. You'd think their touchscreen capabilities would be at least on-par with Windows, Google & Android but it is not. You'd think Apple's touchscreen capabilities might even be better than Windows, Android & Google, but no. Thus far I can find nothing to brag about regarding Apple anything. I was so hoping to find something better about Apple. Instead, I'm greatly disappointed and left seriously frustrated. The iPhone itself came fully charged and appears in brand new condition. It also came with an original Apple Charger.

Review Title: On first listening I was completely underwhelmed, preferring the ancient B&W P5's that these were to
Review Content: On first listening I was completely underwhelmed, preferring the ancient B&W P5's that these were to replace. After extensive listening I have grown to love them. The noise cancelling is unbelievably good, with no real difference to sound quality. The sound quality is very, very good and can be tailored to personal taste by the Sony app. They are expensive but worth every penny! First class sonically, with absolutely no perceivable distortion of any kind. A very classy sound which seems to grow better with use. Very easy to set up, no problems with bluetooth connection or loss of signal. The indicators for left and right are miniscule, I found them really hard to see even when wearing reading glasses. Not a fan of the satin finish which seems to be a grease magnet, making them look scruffy very quickly. I found the touch sensitive "swipe and hold" volume control very hit and miss, but to be fair, I have sausage sized fingers. The universal joint which joins the headband to phones looks very flimsy and prone to failure. I would have expected real leather earpads on a flagship model. Any negative comments are just minor niggles and subject to personal preference. I would definitely recommend this product if you are looking for high end sound quality. Review Content: After much research, I decided to choose Amazon's refurbished program over Apple, Best Buy, or Walmart. I don't even know how I got the first two cracks on the screen (chose iPhone over other brands because the screen is supposedly so much sturdier), but the final blow followed shortly. The shattered spot happened when it fell out from under my arm, landing on the side of the case. I went to the local Batteries Plus to ask a price for screen replacement; the employee took the protective case off to take a look, and we discovered the rear phone cover was shattered! Fast forward about a month, now the battery is failing. One minute it will show 90%, then all of a sudden it shuts down, restarts, and shows 10%. My phone is essential for so many reasons - work, communication with aged parents on-call emergencies, and so much more. Amazon should be ashamed of calling a product "Refurbished Excellent", when it falls apart after only a few months of use! Over $400, and now it will take more than that to repair! Review Title: This year - being entirely comfortable with the i13 level specs - I decided to upgrade to an i13 Pro
Review Content: This year - being entirely comfortable with the i13 level specs - I decided to upgrade to an i13 Pro... and - because of last year's experience - went elsewhere first. What I got from them this time was definitely not what I ordered (it was supposed to be "pristine"... what I got was scratched up junk). So I came back to Amazon, and ordered the only "used-like new" offering on the i13 Pro "list" that day. What I got, well, wasn't (i.e., wasn't "used-like new"). Again. Sigh. (I have a ton of experience with buying "used-like new" stuff from Amazon over the years, and I know what to expect... and this wasn't it.) What I received was a "refurbished-excellent" i13 Pro (the same category as the i13 I ordered last year... which was again, anything but, back then, lol). The category which is is now listed on the order form. (Why would they change the category? When it wasn't what I ordered? -Dunno.) It was... almost... perfect: a few tiny scratches around the lightning port is all a minute examination found wrong (the previous owner had mostly used mag-charging I imagine). And... the battery health - while entirely within the spec for Amazon refurbished (i.e., "80% or greater") - was still a disappointment at only 84%. Still. Cosmetic-wise... acceptable. More than acceptable, even. Agreeably nice... obviously: as I kept it. (Note: I wouldn't review it if I hadn't kept it.) Note: For long term use of any iPhone, to avoid battery related issues, Apple recommends replacing the battery when its below 80% battery health... which repair cost from Apple is about $90 or so... iow, not a big deal. Look, I'm not the target demographic for a new Apple phone anyways; especially their Pro. So sending the phone in for a new battery, especially for what I paid for the 1TB version, is a-okay. And figured into the price. But - other than battery health... and those few tiny [mostly unnoticeable] scratches - I paid quite a bit less (saved a couple of hundred over the "other guys" offerings) at Amazon for a truly ultra-clean i13 Pro - with 1TB capacity - which is in otherwise almost perfect condition. And while its minor flaws render it most certainly NOT in the "used-like new" category... the savings over market costs for a 1TB version rendered my objections to the category moot: it was more than good enough as "refurbished-like new" lol. While YMMV, well... after all... in the final analysis... this one is a keeper. Just keep in mind: all refurb's are "luck of the draw". Amazon is great about their return policy. Take a chance. You'll save money... maybe a bunch of money. Final word: recommend. Review Title: The iPhone Pro 13 features the older emergency SOS function but it is only as good as one's cell tow
Review Content: The iPhone Pro 13 features the older emergency SOS function but it is only as good as one's cell tower connectivity, whereas the 14 and newer also have SOS and roadside assistance functionality via satellite. Based on where I live (mountains, bad cell coverage) I was torn between this purchase and the iPhone 14 Pro series, especially after I realized that a third party seller here on Amazon was offering a "excellent condition" renewed model for what I paid for this older model. Having said this, the iPhone Pro 14 has had reports of overheating and/or lackluster battery performance compared to the iPhone 13 Pro. I also like the fact that the iPhone 13 Pro does NOT have the "always on" screen common to newer Pro models. Another notable difference is that the iPhone 13 Pro (and earlier) have a physical SIM tray whereas the newer 15 Pros are eSIMs. Finally, the iPhone Pro 13 and earlier uses a lightening cord vs. USB-C on current-generation iPhones. (I'm not interested in using a different charging cord/setup than my spouse, especially while traveling.) I very much appreciate the excellent cosmetic appearance — there were no scratches or gouges to be found anywhere on the phone I received — but keeping the Pro 13 was not an option. In a video I took of a flock of birds flying just after the sun set behind a hillside, I could make out a round dust spot visible against the cloudless, pale gold sky — dead center in the bottom of the frame (landscape mode). Honestly, I probably never would have seen it in broad daylight because the HDR takes the blue sky and darkens it down so much the dust spot would have been masked — but the light I was shooting against at dusk was just a tad bit paler than the dust spot, allowing me to appreciate that the lenses were not in the perfect shape they initially appeared. Upon further inspection, using a flashlight, I noted some kind of residue *behind* two out of the three lenses. (Supposedly these lenses are sealed but per the reviews here mine is not the first report of dust spots in photos.) Overall, I don't feel like I received the "premium renewed" experience, in part because the shipping was slow (nearly four days before Amazon assigned tracking) and battery health was less than expected (others here reported at or near 100%!). Ultimately, I returned the Pro 13 and bought an iPhone Pro 12 from another seller. Not only did I pay less and end up with a slimmer, lightweight phone that feels better in the hand, but I actually like the camera quality better because it is among a very small number of iPhones where it is actually possible to turn off the HDR. Review Title: I'd definitely buy it again
Review Content: I'd definitely buy it again. Screen looks great. It does better with memory management than my S10+ did, even though both have 8GB RAM. I wouldn't say it has the BEST battery life by any means, but it lasts. And if you turn on power saving (the regular power saving option), it really just sips on the battery. Then without power saving, you have 3x levels of power settings to choose from. So far, for me, I've been happy with "Optimized" the lowest level. Anyways, to cut it short, I've had zero issues with the phone. No overheating, no crashes, freezes, glitches, stutters, nothing. It's a great phone, with a great screen and amazing cameras. Review Content: I absolutely LOVE these earbuds. I also like the feature that allows me to live translate conversations using these earbuds. I am always curious what people are saying when they are speaking different languages but now I don't have to be since I know what they are saying. Overall they are the best earbuds i have ever owned compared to the bose qc, beats, Sony, airpod pro, and even better than the razer earbuds I used for pc gaming. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple Watch SE (2nd Gen) (GPS + Cellular, 40mm) - Midnight Aluminum Case with Midnight Sport Band, S/M (Renewed) : Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry
Review Title: I initially bought two of these
Review Content: I initially bought two of these. One for me and my 9 year old but had to return the second pair because I previously bought iwatches from a different seller. I was told they are lost in transit after two weeks so I went ahead and get these from Amazon. Lo and behold, those lost watches arrived while this order is in transit. The seller told me to keep the watches but when these arrived, my son decided that he doesn’t want the starlight watch and wants this shiny black one. lol Anyway, I only activated one of them and had to return the other. As per usual.. the initial set up takes forever but after all that step, the watch works well. As you can see, the battery is 100% capacity. Appearance: theres minimal scratches but nothing that stands out or can be considered as an eyesore . Connection: I have yet to turn on the cellular data on this thing so I can’t say anything about that yet but as far as WiFi.. it connects well. My son used it a lot last night to play with the walkie talkie. Messages sent through WiFi arrives fast.. so are the calls. Speaker and microphone works well. Features: As mentioned, my son absolutely loves the walkie talkie app. He was sending both me and his Dad some texts using the WiFi connectivity. Made calls. It’s set up as a kid account so there’s limited features in there than you would usually have as an adult. As a parent though.. I love that it has a school time feature that allows me to lock his watch whenever he is in school. Actually, I like ALL of the parental controls in this thing. Durability: it’s made of ionX glass. While it claims to be durable, it is still made out of glass. It can scratch easily and will shatter with impact. As this is set up as a child watch.. I went ahead and bought him a protective case. The watch band that came with it is a little flimsy but you can always get new ones here anyway.. and cheap. The charger cord that came with it is a USB-A which has its pros and cons. USB-A is still very popular and can come in handy especially when traveling. however, it charges slower than USB-C chargers. If that is something you don’t want to deal with, you can always buy a better charger here. Overall, he is very happy with this watch. It looks almost brand new, works well, function as it should be. Review Title: We can set school time hours for the school year so messages don’t get through - except from parents
Review Content: We can set school time hours for the school year so messages don’t get through - except from parents, but can easily make adjustments to that for things like field day or early release. Downtime hours are set for evening as well. It isn’t an internet browser (yay) but does send and receive gifs. This watch does not have all of the health metrics a # series does but he doesn’t need that. It does steps and heart and workouts etc. it doesn’t track blood O2 or arrhythmias which is fine. As much as I think apple is pretty intuitive as a company for set up- that is less so when setting up a family watch. I googled a lot of things. Including how to get parent messages to break through school time. Not intuitive. And it can’t play music if not linked to its own phone. Oh well. Overall works great for a middle schooler. Helps us hold off on a phone longer than purchasing a different brand kid watch. We’ve had it for 3-4 months. It does need daily charging. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple iPhone 12 Pro Max, 128GB, Pacific Blue - Fully Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: Whenever I buy previously used devices, I wait a bit before leaving a review
Review Content: Whenever I buy previously used devices, I wait a bit before leaving a review. But I can't even wait for this one! I am so pleased. I placed my order July 4th and got the phone just 4 days later. They shipped FAST! I ordered RENEWED (not Renewed PREMIUM) and I was second guessing myself while awaiting delivery. I worried about the battery health. I was so pleasantly surprised when I checked and saw that it was at 88% health. That is not bad at all. I am more than glad to have the battery replaced eventually when needed considering I saved hundreds of dollars buying a previously used phone AND also sold my old iPhone 8 Plus on eBay. It's only $89 for Apple to replace the battery which is, to me, a good deal considering how many years they last. I'm not bothering to share any photos of the phone itself because there are plenty of those in other reviews here. The phone is virtually flawless. A few very minor scratches around the edges, but I don't care about that. It's covered by the Otterbox case I have it in. Another note is that it was delivered with a tempered glass screen protector already installed. I replaced it with a new one, but it just goes to show they think of everything. They could have removed it but it was a little extra protection while it was in transit. I've been doing my best (and will continue) to try every single feature of the phone before the warranty is up to make sure I don't have any surprises down the road, but I am confident this is going to be my 'new' baby for the next 3 to 4 years. That's about how long I keep a phone before upgrading. I honestly would have kept my old iPhone 8 Plus if not for the fact that I couldn't get iOS 17 on it and I loved the new features of the operating system upgrade. I also wanted a better camera. The sound quality is excellent. the touch screen is completely responsive and I LOVE the beautiful blue color. I implore you to take a chance on renewed/refurbished devices. I have been buying 'like new' devices for decades now and I am rarely disappointed. Any minor aggravations I've encountered have been generously offset by the money I've saved. I always stay a few models behind the newest to get the most savings. Oh! One more thing. If you Google it, many complain of how long it takes the iPhone 12 models to charge. I had the same complaint initially but I just stopped using my convenient bedside USB hub and started using the Anker 60W PIQ wall charger I keep in my living room. That DRAMATICALLY decreased the time it takes to charge. I bought a super long cord here on Amazon so I can charge from a distance and that's all it took. The Anker 60W PIQ charger (also here on Amazon) is lightning fast compared to standard chargers. [More](javascript:void(0))[Hide](javascript:void(0)) There was a problem filtering reviews. Review Title: So this is my first experience with Amazon's renewed premium program where you pay between $50-$100
Review Content: So this is my first experience with Amazon's renewed premium program where you pay between $50-$100 more than the renewed price but for that you get an item whose battery is at least at 90% capacity relative to a new one and instead of a 90 day warranty you get a year warranty and a year to return the item. For less than $100 I thought that was definitely worth it. However the first iPhone 12 pro they sent me had a battery that was at 85% capacity which really pissed me off because I felt cheated so I returned it and purchased it again and I'm glad I did because the 2nd ones battery was at 100% capacity and for all intents and purposes it was a brand new phone at a used price. Granted it's still really expensive it was $900 before tax but I got this to be future proof at least for the next several years. This is my first iPhone before I was all android phones but it seemed like every year I was having to buy another phone because something out of my control always happened but my parents still had their iPhone 8 that they bought new and it was still working perfectly. I haven't had this phone for more than a few days but so far I'm very impressed with it. The facial recognition capabilities are so good. My phone can recognize me when I'm in a dark room whereas my Samsung tablet can't recognize my face without all the lights on. One feature this phone doesn't have that really surprised me was that there is no built in fingerprint scanner and I think that was a mistake on apple's part. The battery is supposed to only last 21 hours but a full charge is lasting me a little over 2 days. The screen is gorgeous is it HDR Dolby Vision and HLG compatible and not even my 4k tv supports all of those so it makes streaming look brilliant. You can see every detail even though the screen is 6.7inches. it seems like everyday I'm finding out a new function that this phone has granted a lot them I'll never use because I don't use my phone that way but it's cool to know that if I wanted to I could if I so choosed. I guess I'll stop my review here because you get the gist and I hate it when people on Amazon beat a dead horse and I don't want to be one of those so Amazon renewed premium is a worthwhile program and the iPhone 12 pro max is an awesome phone that's worth the investment. Review Title: The battery life is excellent
Review Content: The battery life is excellent. I feel like I never have to charge them. I always have the noise cancellation turned on, so I imagine if you were using them without that, they'd be the legit energizer bunny of the headphone world. These don't have the newest bluetooth tech, but they can be connected to different devices at the same time. If I'm listening to spotify at work on my computer, I can just move right over to my phone when I'm walking around. No unpairing and repairing. Obviously not a necessity, but I am realllly spoiled on that capability now. I got this pair (blue, renewed) to replace my old pair that I lost while traveling (pink, renewed). I had the pink pair for over a year and wore them pretty much every day, and they still looked and worked as good as new the whole time. The zipper case that comes with the headphones helps protect them in your backpack or bag, but a lot of the time I just folded them down and tossed them in my bag. Even with that added wear and tear, they held up like champs! No cracking or wearing out in the ear pads, either. The controls on the actual headphones are pretty straightforward. I don't typically use them, but they work as expected and aren't overly cumbersome to access. The noise cancellation on these is great –helped, I imagine, by the over-ear style that provides some mechanical noise isolation. They perform really well on planes (for the constant, droning background sounds) and actually perform surprisingly well for blocking out sound and chatter at places like the office or a coffee shop. The only other headphones I've tried that had better noise cancelling were $300+ Bose headphones. The long-wear comfort is another thing I love about these. They don't feel too tight or hot. I can comfortably wear them while wearing my glasses, too. Out the box, I think the sound quality is great– solid, rich bass and generally well rounded sound. I have used the equalizer app for some specific endeavors, so that's a nice option to have on deck. I have recommended this model to friends and I will keep doing so. Super pleased with the performance for a price that feels actually reasonable. Review Title: About 6 months ago they developed a stress fracture on the sliding mechanism above the right ear up
Review Content: About 6 months ago they developed a stress fracture on the sliding mechanism above the right ear up. Unlike other reviewers, I have not had any issues with any of padding lifting or coming off the headphones. The connectivity is overall solid - I can walk pretty far away from my device and still have audio. However, about 2 years into owning them, about 3-5 times a week, the sound becomes garbled (like someone talking into an oscillating fan). Turning the headphones off and then back on again fixes the issue, but it is bit annoying. They are VERY comfortable and I can wear them for 12+ hours with no issues or contact fatigue. The biggest selling point for me. The sound is pretty good, and meet my needs. I’ve had no complaints from anyone regarding the sound of the microphone on their end. They are by far my favorite sounding headphones, but I’m not an audiophile, so I’ll leave those opinions to others. The battery life is excellent and I can get through about 10 business days without charging them. The case that they come with is great and I use it any time I take them out of the house. Overall, for a refurbished pair, these are an excellent choice with great long-lasting comfort. My only reservation is the durability given that I take excellent care of them. I would (and do so regularly ) recommend these to others, particularly at the sixty-ish dollar price point. They are an excellent value, despite the issues above. Review Title: Our house is on a budget so I couldn't spend too much, but I also didn't want to end up wasting mone
Review Content: Our house is on a budget so I couldn't spend too much, but I also didn't want to end up wasting money on a cheap pair of headphones that I wouldn't end up liking or using. I finally ended up settling on these. Unfortunately the first pair of headphones I received didn't work right. BUT I easily started the return/replacement process, and I received the replacement before I even returned the first pair. It was nice to be able to make sure the first pair was faulty and that it wasn't the headphones in general that felt... wrong on my ears. Fortunately the second pair was *chefs kiss* SO much better and I have basically been living in them since. (which also speaks to the battery life because I have had these for about two weeks and have only had to charge them once) They have fairly decent passive noise cancelling, active noise cancelling is really neat (you can connect to the soundcore app so you can adjust that, plus there's an equalizer in the app to adjust sound too), and the transparency mode is my absolute favourite. Just quickly touching the right ear for a second switches it to transparency mode so you can tune into your surroundings without stopping your audio or taking the headphones off--and I absolutely love that, as a parent and someone who is just on high alert a lot. The microphone works well for phone calls, I've been told that the sound is clear. I like that you can connect to two devices, at the same time, so I can use my Nintendo Switch and just switch over to my phone if I get a call. Pairing them was fairly straightforward. Oh, and they come with a case so you can travel with them too, and I'm sure I'm forgetting about other things I like about these. Honestly my only "complaint" is that I have a small head and the smallest size setting still concerns me that they might fly off my head if I turn too quickly--because they definitely make threats to fly off my head when I "headbang" even a little to my music. I'm no expert but these are absolutely quality for the price point. Just be wary not to shake them off if you have a small head. Review Title: The screen is absolutely stunning
Review Content: The screen is absolutely stunning. The high-refresh AMOLED display makes everything feel buttery smooth, from scrolling social media to gaming. Colors are vibrant without looking cartoonish, and the brightness is strong enough that I can see it clearly outdoors in direct sunlight. Watching YouTube, Netflix, or TikTok on this phone honestly feels like a mini high-end TV in my hand. Everyday performance is flawless. Apps open instantly, multitasking is effortless, and the phone doesn’t stutter even when I’m switching between games, streaming, and messaging. It handles heavy games and multitasking like it’s nothing. I haven’t noticed any real lag or slowdown, and everything just feels incredibly responsive. Battery life has been excellent. I can go a full day of normal to heavy use (streaming music, videos, maps, social media, photos, and messages) and still have power left at night. Charging is quick enough that a short top-off gets me comfortably through the rest of the day. It’s the kind of phone you don’t have to babysit or constantly worry about charging. The camera system is super reliable. Photos come out sharp with good color and solid dynamic range, whether I’m shooting in daylight or indoors. Product Title: Amazon.com: JBL Charge 6 Portable Waterproof Speaker with Powerbank and Strap - Black (Renewed) : Electronics
Review Title: Seriously — if you’re even thinking about it, just get two and use the stereo pairing mode
Review Content: Seriously — if you’re even thinking about it, just get two and use the stereo pairing mode. The stereo separation completely changes the experience. It goes from “nice Bluetooth speaker” to “legit sound system.” I listen to a lot of NTS.LIVE with these and it’s an incredible experience. The clarity, the low end, the space between left and right channels — it just feels immersive. For electronic sets, ambient mixes, or anything with spatial detail, stereo mode is where these really shine. Sound-wise, these have great range from treble to mids to bass. The highs are crisp without being harsh, the mids are clear, and the bass has real weight for a portable speaker. Nothing feels missing, and nothing feels overhyped — it’s just a really satisfying, full sound. With a pair in stereo mode, it honestly feels like having a high-fidelity stereo system that I can use while sitting at the table inside or sitting on the patio. I can move them wherever I want and still get that spacious, balanced sound. I haven’t tried the JBL Xtreme 4 or the Boombox 3, but here’s what I love about a pair of Charge 6s compared to an all-in-one stereo speaker: you can physically separate the left and right channels. Put them on opposite sides of the room. Put them on opposite sides of the couch. Take them to the beach and spread them out in the sand. Put them on either side of you. You get real stereo imaging instead of everything coming from a single box. You can use Auracast to connect more than two, but that runs in mono, which I personally don’t use much. My Samsung phone lets me output to two Bluetooth devices at once, so sometimes I run a stereo pair of Charge 6s as one Bluetooth output and a pair of JBL Go 4s as the second output. It’s kind of ridiculous — but in the best way. One Charge 6 sounds great on its own. But for me, the stereo pair is really the complete product. That’s how I think of them. Review Content: 5. Bought the over the ear beats version for my girl, 3yrs ago she loves them, always in her ears. 6. Stop complaining about over the ear vs ear buds...duh. I have spent $$$$$$$$$ on others, some good some bad. Didn't want to invest $200 for ear buds but I've already did that over time with others. I use the smaller ear section/part that goes into the ear drum. I do sweat and they stay in with no physical working out and they work fine (if your a gym nut, these are not for you(duh they don't hook over the actual ear). If not in the gym 24-7/365 and not doing any kind of sports then buy them. I've had the $20 buds $50 buds etc., at the time I got these buds for $90(renewed). I can get 6hrs out of 1 bud then switch out, the base is ok(i use them for office work, and talking with clients. No issues with people not hearing my voice, outside noise will always be there regardless(these do help with not so much of that). Others have complained about this and that...there is NO perfect ear bud(unless you can invent your own ear bud non-over the ear, that don't fall out when sweating or any kind of hard sporting exercise, buy the over the head version if that's the case...duh). If your not a gym buff then these are awesome, losing connection not so much for me, I can have my phone in the basement or backyard and I can get 5 steps into my driveway to the car and still be good. Calls are clear and not annoying to others not hearing you. I have not connected to my tv via bluetooth(I have others for that). My biggest fault is the battery life, but that's why you have the other 1 in the case. All in all, it was a solid investment @($90) and I just bought the black pair for $160 as I waited for the price drop from $199( smiley face!). Pending on your life style and what you would be using the actual product for then that is what your purchase will actually be on...duh. OVERALL my experience 5*s. Review Title: Everything seems to be in like-new condition
Review Content: Everything seems to be in like-new condition. The packaging was missing, so it was just some plastic bags in a generic USPS cardboard box, but that makes no difference to me. (I only mention it because the set of XM5 over ear headphones I bought refurbished even came in the Sony packaging). It's the middle of winter in WI right now, so when they were delivered, the battery was too cold to charge normally. It turns out they recommend the battery be close to 60°F to charge. But, they warmed up quickly, and I'm not going to dock points for that. Sound quality is good, but not great. I'm coming from owning multiple sets of over the ear headphones, including the XM3 and XM5 Sony models, and there's really no comparison. The over the ear versions are miles better. Bass on the earbuds is lacking in both clarity and volume. I was surprised by the frequency range - one of my test tracks has prominent sub-bass, and I was still present and discernible even when it was in the background of a variety of other tones. Treble is clear enough, but the soundstage is very limited. This may be an earbud issue in general, I'm not sure. Most of my complaints about the bass can be fixed with the "Clear Bass" function, which is found under the equalizer. I'm currently running with the mid and treble sliders increased by a couple notches, and the clear bass almost all the way up. Comfort-wise, they're good so far. They seem to stay in place, even with the wrong size earpieces (I've experimented with all but the smallest, more tapered size.) I will also say, the earpieces make a significant difference in the sound quality. If they're too big, they don't fit in your ear far enough, and the sound suffers greatly. Noise reduction seems sufficient. Haven't taken them on a plane yet, though I plan to in a couple weeks, so maybe I'll update this review. The foam tips make pretty good earplugs even without the noise cancelling on. So, in short, dock one star for the sound quality and the fact that I had to spend half an hour adjusting the equalizer to get it to meet my expectations. Everything else is good!
