Review Title: The headphones themselves are phenomenal
Review Content: The headphones themselves are phenomenal. These are the only earbuds I've ever used which I could not improve with EQ. I'm literally using the default, flat EQ because that sounds best to my ear. Incredible. I bought these as an upgrade over the Anker Soundcore Space A40, which compare favourably for the money. I can EQ the Anker to sound fairly close to the Sony, but the Anker lacks a sparkle and clarity which I can only seem to get out of the Sony. If you can't afford the Sony, the Anker would be a decent alternative if you're comfortable with a slight decrease in sound quality. Sony's Android software is horrible. Sony needs to fire every product manager and director involved in that abomination. Installing the software, one is bombarded with seven thousand modal dialog boxes informing the user of a million different features, asking intrusive questions, and generally just being annoying. The spam doesn't stop once you proceed through the initial setup. At all times, weird popups appear to distract you from your task. The UI controls feel clunky and severely lacking polish, like something made by a garage startup company. There are a limited number of EQ presets, and you cannot add more. There are only 3 slots for custom EQ configurations, a pointless limitation in the age of software. Changing between EQ presets causes the sound to cut out for about 500 milliseconds, which severely impedes the ability to compare custom EQ and fine-tune them. Astonishingly, the "Flat" EQ preset does NOT sound identical to a "Custom" EQ preset which is set to a flat configuration. Two flat EQ profiles that do not sound the same. I have no idea what is going on, but this makes no sense. I personally find the default "Flat" EQ to sound best, but I would like to boost the bass very slightly, and I can't do this, because as soon as I move that slider, the Sony software forces me to start editing the "Custom" EQ preset, beginning from a flat EQ profile, which does NOT sound the same as the "Flat" profile. It is thus impossible to modify the default, "Flat" EQ profile, which is pretty infuriating because these headphones are very expensive. The sound isolation is phenomenal. The memory foam ear tips appear to be doing almost all of the heavy lifting. I have a large box fan near me, and when I insert the headphones with noise cancellation disabled, I can barely hear the (normally quite loud) fan. Activating noise cancellation removes all remaining noise. I can't speak to the rest of the frequency spectrum, but compared to the Anker Soundcore Space A40, these Sony earbuds are SILENT. It's an eerie silence. I wasn't expecting the noise cancellation to be this good. Note that it will depend heavily on whether the earbuds seal your canal correctly. On initial insertion, I didn't get a good seal, and I wondered if the noise cancellation was working at all. Overall I think these earbuds have incredible potential. Their performance reputation is well deserved. However, Sony clearly does not care about its customers and their day-to-day experience. Incredible hardware paired with infuriatingly bad software. Sony is lucky that the default performance of these buds is so good, otherwise I would want to return them. Update #1: I did some research and found that Sony makes replacement ear tips, model EP-NI1010, but Sony's authorized online reseller in Canada does not sell them! These ear tips appear unavailable within Canada, and will cost over $100 to import from overseas. Total customer service disaster. I contacted Amazon customer support, who offered a partial refund for the missing earbud tips, or a full refund if I return the product. They also recommended that I reach out to the seller to ask them to send the missing tips, which I have done. Update #2: I discovered, buried within the Sony Headphones Connect Android app, that I can request replacement ear tips from Sony! Tap the "System" tab, then scroll down and tap on the text "Determines Optimal Earbud Tips". Do the "Test The Wearing Condition" test. After the test has failed, you will see an option: "The earbud tips may be too small ... If none of the supplied earbud tips fit, you can request other types of earbud tips. Click here to order." You can then select your country and fill out a form to request replacement earbud tips. After entering my address, I received the message: "We have received your request for new earbud tips. Please allow 7 to 10 business days for processing and delivery." I didn't enter my credit card information, so it appears that these will be free. We'll see what happens. I should note that after filling out this form once, the option does not appear again, even if you reinstall the app. To get the option to order replacements again, go to the "System" tab within the Sony Headphones Connect app, scroll to the bottom and select "Initialize Settings", then choose "Initialize App/Headphone Settings". Update #3: On the recommendation of other buyers, I bought the SpinFit Omni ear tips as a replacement. I got the small size, which is about 1 mm smaller than the medium Sony ear tips size that I have access to. On comparative listening, there is a slightly better sound from the Sony memory foam ear tips, but the SpinFit Omni are quite competitive. The Sonys are warmer and give better punch to bass frequencies. The sound isolation is also slightly better, but only slightly. Memory foam surprisingly seems to make a difference! Update #4: Sony reached out to me via email to clarify my shipping address, and have confirmed that they are shipping replacement ear tips to me. Yay! Update #5: Sony did not provide any tracking information for the replacement ear tips, and I received phone calls from FedEx indicating that I was not home to receive the package. It turns out that Sony sent the ear tips using FedEx Direct Signature requirement, and they are now being held at some location, and I must physically go there with my ID. I am disabled and cannot travel to this location, and FedEx will not allow another person to pick up the package instead. It makes no sense to ship a cheap replacement part with an expensive and inconvenient signature requirement. I get Amazon packages left at my front door every day without issue. I emailed Sony to request that they call FedEx to waive the signature requirement, and ask FedEx to make a redelivery, which is how FedEx insists upon resolving such situations. Update #6: I called Sony and, to their credit, had one of the best customer support experiences of my life. Their phone tree is a horrible labyrinth of pain and suffering, but once I got through to a human on my THIRD call, that human was truly wonderful and clarified that Sony had contacted FedEx with my request, but was waiting on a response. Sony said they would email me when there is a resolution. Update #7: The package finally arrived, but with no notice. I found it in my mailbox when I checked my mail. It contained the WRONG replacement ear tips. The replacements are silicone, but the XM5 earbuds are supposed to come with memory foam ear tips. I am heartbroken. This ordeal has wasted way too much of my time. This is a terrible way to treat customers who keep giving unlimited second chances to make things right. I have emailed Sony to ask them to send the correct part. Update #8: I did some comparative listening between the new silicone replacement ear tips that Sony sent (YY2963/BQ-TPKIT), the original Sony memory foam tips (EP-NI1010), the SpinFit Omni, and my Sennheiser HD-600 open back headphones. The new Sony silicones seal much easier and better in my ear canal compared to the Sony memory foam ones, providing shockingly improved noise cancellation. These are by far the best noise cancelling ear tips currently in my possession, however this may be due to fitting my ear canal better. Recall that the Sony memory foam ear tips I currently have are one size too large for me. The SpinFit Omni feel slightly too small by comparison. The Sony silicone tips are very competitive with the Sony memory foam tips, but have slightly less clarity, slightly muddier bass, and louder bass. The Sony memory foam tips have tighter bass which can sound punchier at times, and add a high end clarity and sparkle which, although very slight, really elevates the immersiveness of the sound for certain tracks. Going back and forth, I really feel the silicone tips are very competitive, and ultimately it comes down to a matter of taste: do you prefer a warmer tone, or a tone with more sparkle and clarity? I prefer clarity, especially now because I suffer from derealization due to prior COVID infection, so my conscious experience feels distant and removed from reality, as if I am experiencing reality through a television screen. Enhanced clarity of sound brings my conscious experience closer to what I used to experience before my disability. So I still give the edge to the Sony memory foam tips, although when listening to a panel of several songs, I'm not confident that I could tell them apart from the Sony silicone in a blind listening test. The SpinFit Omni featured noticeably less bass, higher treble, sounding almost tinny and a little bit shrill, and very noticeably inferior noise cancellation. However, to SpinFit's credit, the Omni tips still provide very good performance, especially when compared to other headphones such as the Anker Soundcore Space A40 mentioned earlier in this review. The Sony silicone tips sounded clearly superior to the SpinFit, however only when wearing the medium size; the small size sounded very similar to the SpinFit, suggesting that the seal quality within the ear canal is a critical factor, and the next larger size of SpinFit may be competitive with the Sony silicone. The Sennheiser HD-600 open-back headphones performed surprisingly poorly, and while I do prefer them to the SpinFit, and while they do sound very good, they featured weaker bass and slightly too elevated treble tones for my taste. My conclusion is that the Sony WF-1000XM5 with Sony memory foam ear tips remain the gold standard. I would really like Sony to send me the correct ear tips that I bought and paid for, because the memory foam seems integral to the sound of the XM5 earbuds. The only reason to pay so much money for a pair of wireless earbuds is to achieve the best possible sound quality, and achieving this is now a critical accessibility need for me since my disability compromises the way that I perceive sound. I actually require the product to perform at its best in order to enjoy music in the way that an able-bodied person could with inferior earbuds. Update #9: It has been 3 months since my purchase. I tried to make Sony's replacement tips work for a while, but they keep sliding out of my ears when I am just a little bit sweaty, or for about an hour after I take a shower. I gave up and requested a partial refund from Amazon. After some convincing, they relented and gave me the refund, which I have now immediately spent on a pair of AZLA SednaEarfit MAX Standard tips. Despite being silicone, these tips produce a frequency response nearly identical to the original XM5 foam tips. @aaronloudnwireless on YouTube has a video comparing the frequency response of the original Sonys, the AZLA, and also the Comply TrueGrip Pro. At this point, I have paid almost as much out of pocket to make up the difference between new and used XM5s, and purchasing the used model was a waste of time. To Amazon's credit, they are the only party who provided meaningful customer service on this issue; both Sony and the seller let me down. I don't know if I would recommend purchasing XM5s based on the experience so far, though the sound quality remains stellar. I popped in the original ear tips for another quick listen today, and the improvement in quality between those and Sony's replacement silicone tips is noticeable. This product is such a hot mess.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))       [Report](javascript:void(0)) Sending feedback...Thanks, we'll investigate in the next few days. Review Title: ##### eSIM not working from 1 of 3 Sellers! Otherwise still best Samsung Flagship with SD Card
Review Content: ##### eSIM not working from 1 of 3 Sellers! Otherwise still best Samsung Flagship with SD Card I ordered over the past year 3 Phones from this exact same listing (same Color Bronze). The Problem is, that they are sold by independant refurbisher they all claim to be "SM-N986U1" = Factory unlocked Phones US Market. The first one I ordered in June2023 for my Cousin that was travelling and her Note9 broke down. The Phone was sold by "ELECTRONIC DEALS" . Wonderful Phone all is working great. As it was such a wonderful experience I thought I order one for myseld as a Backup in case my original European Note 20 Ultra would break down one day... This came 2 weeks later sold by "WirelessGlobe" again absoluetly amazing Condition and all worked. But when I ordered one this December 2023 again, the phone was sold by "HUMAN TECH". Again looked in perfect excellent condition. BUT I was unable to add an eSIM, regular SIM was no problem (So there was no SIM Lock!). As it turns out after contacting Samsung US - Support and them asking for the IMEI number, the Phone was actually built as a AT&T variant (SM-N986U and not U1) and was SIM-Locked once but now unlocked. Unfortuantely deep down in the system somehow eSIM was still locked and there is nothing that they can do about that, although the Phone About Screen has clearly mentioned the SM-N986U1, it was unusable with a eSim. So be careful when you even get a beatiful phone, and today you don't need eSIM maybe in the future you are travelling and then you find out you can't add eSIM... so test within the Return Window from Amazon if eSIM is working!!! In my case whn scanning QR Code of E-Sim it would just loop back to intital screen in SIM Manger. After upgrading to last Firmware, when clicking add eSIM I would only get the 4 Dots circling forever and nothing would happen. So beware of Sellers probably masking a SM-N986U unlocked AT&T Version as a Factory unlocked U1... Unfortunately NOT THE SAME!!! Attched picture1 shows in the older firmware the Scan eSIM is coming up, but will loop back to attached picture 2. After Firmware Upgrade it loops from the beginning. Review Title: Upon booting the phone it was not fully charged, where it already had an account on the phone
Review Content: Upon booting the phone it was not fully charged, where it already had an account on the phone. The seller claimed the phone was unlocked, however, the phone booted with t-mobile software and was not factory reset. This prompted me to reach out to Samsung to confirm if the phone was unlocked or not where I was told by the rep after providing the IMEI information that the phone is locked to T-mobile carrier. I next contacted t-mobile and the rep stated that the phone is not eligible to be unlocked, which rendered the phone unusable. This ordeal has been a huge inconvenience due to the fact I spent money on the phone with guarantee it would be unlocked and working. The seller had responsibility to ensure the phone was wiped of all previous user data, as well as ensuring the phone was not restricted to any carrier. If so, I would not be writing my review to warn others. I should not have had to go through so many hoops to confirm the validity of the phone when the phone should have been in the 'unlocked condition' as described on Amazon. I am recommending that AMAZON put in place a system that requires the SELLER to verify that the phone is unlocked by loading IMEI info before we as the CUSTOMER complete the purchase to prevent this from reoccurring. I have reached out to the seller to resolve this issue and have sent the phone back to receive a full refund. This experience has made me question Amazon's standards in regards to electronics where I do not have confidence or faith in purchasing any phone that is claimed to be unlocked from its Amazon sellers. Not until Amazon can guarantee that sellers will be true to their listings. In addition, the seller should be more mindful and considerate of the phones they are selling to people as we are spending real money and trusting that they will send us a phone that works and is truly unlocked with no restrictions as described. Please be aware of the risks you are taking when purchasing a "refurbished" or "renewed" phone from Amazon as you may not recieve the item as it is described on Amazon. Review Title: Came as advertised
Review Content: Came as advertised. It has two defects on the silver casing but nothing major. It came completely dead, which is expected with refurbished devices because I’m pretty sure they change the battery and clear them before you buy it. Listen to me when I say this because I’ve seen people complain about the device or charger not working; MAKE SURE YOU TAKE THE PLASTIC PROTECTIVE COVERINGS OFF OF THE CHARGER PLATE BECAUSE IT WILL NOT CHARGE IF YOU DON’T, OR COULD POSSIBLY MELT THE PLASTIC ON THE NON-MAGNETIC SIDE. I was so ready to return this device because it wouldn’t charge or turn on, I somehow was looking at the charging plate and found out that it was because of the very very very thin invisible plastic on the magnetic plate (and the other side). After I got it charged, it worked and set up/connecting wasn’t an issue. The battery did go down quickly the first time, but I didn’t charge it all the way to 100: I tracked my sleep and heart rate for the first time, and it gave me lots of insights on my sleep that I didn’t know about (I ended up buying another app that goes way more in detail). Review Title: I bought a gas-powered golf cart last year
Review Content: I bought a gas-powered golf cart last year. I recently developed Tinittus in my left ear and needed to give my ears additional protection to ride in the golf cart. Knowing Bose is a good brand, but not wanting to pay full price, I took my chances on this refurbished headset. They arrived in like-new condition. They were missing instructions but I was easily able to figure it out and had them charged and connected with my Bluetooth and the app downloaded within a matter of minutes. The real test was going to be in how well they cancelled noise to protect my ears, so I put them on and took my golf cart out for a test drive. I could still hear but the noise was much softer. The option to to reduce or increase the noise cancelling option was amazing. The button is very easy to click while using them. Overall I am extremely happy with this headset! Review Content: I bought them reconditioned from Amazon, something I never do, buy used electronics but since cash wasn't flowing in my direction at the time I decided to give them a try - it has payed off. They are extremely comfortable, easy to adjust and the sound and mic quality are superb, no cracking or popping. As a matter of fact I have discovered words that I didn't even know were in my favorite songs! The volume control is great and I love the sound cancelling feature which comes in handy on long airplane flights, bus rides and preschool musicals. Also love the easy blue tooth connectivity to my iPhone, fast charging speed and battery life - seriously as long as you don't forget to toggle the switch to "off" they seem to stay charged for days! Then there is the way they look - sharp with black and silver detail, the "BOSE" name visible, stating the obvious that you like to buy expensive stuff. Then there is the thoughtfully printed enormous "R" and "L" on the inside of the ear cuffs so you, like me, won't wear them on your head backwards. They come with a charging cable (granted it's short with no plug) and also one of those early plug-in cables for old stuff that still uses them like the tvs on airplanes and your walkman. (you know what I'm talking about right?) All of this comes in a sleek designed - clam shell - zipper - hard case which is super awesome once you figure out how to fold the head phones up correctly to fit inside - you will love it even more! So give it up to Bose's for these great headphones - now scroll down and buy them!! They stay put during movement, don’t pinch, and are comfortable enough to wear for long periods without fatigue. No sore ears, no pressure — just effortless wear. Sound quality is impressive for bone conduction headphones. The bass is stronger than expected, vocals are crisp, and call quality is excellent. Battery life easily gets me through multiple conference calls and busy days, and the quick charge feature is appreciated. . They’re lightweight, sweat-resistant, easy to use, and well designed. If you want headphones that balance comfort, safety, durability, and great sound, these are absolutely worth it. Highly recommend — I’d buy them again without hesitation. I should point out that I did try two other brands of bone conducting headphones phones that were “highly” rated and HATED them. I don’t think the folks reviewing them have experienced the high quality of Shokz. It was a night and day difference. Review Title: I purchased this Motorola Razr+ 2025 through Amazon on April 20, 2026
Review Content: I purchased this Motorola Razr+ 2025 through Amazon on April 20, 2026. The phone was not even four months old when it developed a line along the edge and became increasingly difficult to close. The phone was otherwise in good condition. I contacted the seller expecting a reasonable resolution, but the seller did not take responsibility for the problem. I then contacted Amazon Customer Service multiple times. This is where the experience became extremely frustrating. Amazon representatives repeatedly told me they would help. I was told the seller would assist with a replacement or refund. When that did not happen, another Amazon representative told me the warranty team had been contacted and that I would receive refund/replacement confirmation within 72 hours. I waited, and no one contacted me. I contacted Amazon again and was then told that the seller was not helpful and that Amazon had filed an A-to-z claim against the seller. The representative specifically told me that the guarantee reimbursement would be credited to my original payment method and that I would receive confirmation within three business days. I have since spoken with multiple additional Amazon representatives, including a manager. I have been sent links that lead me in circles, told to contact different departments, and even had one representative tell me she was submitting an appeal before leaving the conversation without providing confirmation or a reference number. At this point, I have spent far too much time trying to get a resolution for a phone that should not have developed this type of problem after less than four months. The most disappointing part is not just the defective phone—it is the lack of accountability and the repeated runaround after purchasing an expensive product through Amazon. I would strongly recommend that Amazon and the seller take responsibility for resolving defective products instead of making customers repeatedly explain the same situation to different representatives. I purchased this phone expecting it to last much longer than four months. Instead, I have spent weeks trying to get someone to take responsibility. Very disappointing experience. A total mess       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Review Title: Note for Verizon customers: I activated it on Verizon and swapped in my sim from my old S10 and come
Review Content: Note for Verizon customers: I activated it on Verizon and swapped in my sim from my old S10 and come to find out 5G appears to work out of the box with no changes to my plan or anything so I'll take it. One annoyance with Verizon is they use their own visual voicemail app that comes pre-loaded on their locked phones. Unfortunately there's no way to install it on an unlocked phone so now I don't get notifications for voicemail and I have to call in to check messages. I even tried sideloading the APK but it doesn't work so not sure if it's possible to fix or not. Kind of annoying atm but maybe that will push me over the fence to switch to another carrier (like one that offers their voicemail app on the playstore - ie pretty much every other carrier). Coming from an S10 that got a white screen of death after a small drop this phone is better in every way and can't be beat at the price. Even mid tier phones cost over 350-400 new and this phone is way superior being a top of the line phone when it launched and half the price. I'm glad I took the plunge and tried a renewed phone since I found my new way to upgrade my phone. No thanks to signing contracts and getting locked into a network. Buying a previous gen phone is the way to go for me for sure. I'm very happy with my purchase and just think you really got nothing to lose to try it out! Product Title: Amazon.com: Samsung Galaxy S20 5G, 128GB, Cosmic Gray - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: I have had it for over a month and it works great
Review Content: I have had it for over a month and it works great. Overall. 1. The finger reader under the screen is really bad. My old LG had it on the back and it was 100% reliable and super fast. You grab the phone and it's ON. With the Samsung, it's hit and miss. Maybe 50% success and you have to look where you put the finger and how. It's not intuitive at all and makers should go back to normal readers. 2. The face recognition is useless as the camera has to face you and you have to face the camera. Forget unlocking the phone while on the table (must be tilted first), or next to your body. Or if you wear sunglasses. Or with facial cover (in winter) or while you drink or eat... I would take back or side fingerprint reader any time. And no, Apple is not any better. 3. The USB port is very loose and detaches from USB cable (many tested) with the slightest touch. Forget charging in your bag. 4. The camera app is not user friendly. Like you have to switch between photo and video settings to take video. My phone 10 yrs ago had a dedicated video button in photo settings for a quick video snap. 5. The general UI is wonky. Not my first Samsung but I don;t remember the last one S6 was this bad. 2. It doesn't lag. It has 12 GB RAM. Much better than most of new phones. 3. It's cheap! It's so much better deal than virtually any new cheap phone and better than new phone double or triple its price.

Review Content: The bottom line for me is the phone works okay. I have to dial in to get my voicemail now and had to have all of that reset, there is no voicemail icon. Review Title: First thing - my unlocked phone came to life with the AT&T boot up screen
Review Content: First thing - my unlocked phone came to life with the AT&T boot up screen. That scared me, and I came back to the listing to read again to be sure it was supposed to be unlocked. I proceeded to set up the phone for use, in my own way. I won't go into details, but setup wasn't exactly standard. The phone upgraded from Android 14 to Android 16, then downloaded several security updates. I logged into her Google account, and added the phone, then used Samsung's utility to transfer all files and data via USB cable. Losing the grandchildren's photos would be worth more than my life, but that worked quite well. With the phone almost ready for use, I went to her former carrier, and requested that the phone number be released for transfer to my own carrier. Wait, and wait, and wait and finally they came through. The moment of truth was upon me. I went to my carrier's site, and started activation of the unlocked AT&T phone. That went smoothly. I guess the phone really is unlocked. This IS a refurbished phone, I must assume that someone installed the AT&T app and other software before returning the phone for some reason. Factory reset didn't rid the phone of AT&T branding for some reason. I am pretty impressed with this device, so far. I love the 12 gig of RAM - quickly disabled the RAM boost because virtual memory can and will wear out your - cough - "disk drive". I refuse to call the storage "memory", even when being misused for virtual memory. I fully expect this phone to last to 2030, and beyond. (Our budget phones have always been pushed a year past end of support, without scratches and other damage.) Overall, it took me about six hours to get this device ready for my wife to continue setting it up. I did some minimal debloating. Why do phones come with so much pre-installed crap? I still have some stuff to remove, but that will require installing ADB, and digging deeper into the OS. I will return at some point to update this review. She will find any and all problems with this phone in short order! I will most likely return in a few months to get another one for myself. (I'm always 8 to 10 months behind her on upgrading to a newer phone!) For the price, this refurbished or renewed phone seems a great bargain! Merry Christmas everyone! I had to basically press down or hold the button really hard to get it to respond, and eventually it did, but even that some 5 minutes. Then when the phone turns back on, I couldn't unlock it. Review Title: This was was an upgrade purchase for my daughter
Review Content: This was was an upgrade purchase for my daughter. We don't believe in buying $1,000+ phones for teenagers. Amazon's Refurbished was a welcomed gift! The phone comes well packaged and is in great shape. It works like new, as promised! But, it took us MANY HOURS to finally get this phone set-up and info transfered over. Here are some learned tips for set-up: First, fully charge the new phone and your old phone. If possible, leave them both plugged in during the process. We learned that your old phone needs to be at least 50% charged before it will even start the transfer process. Don't bother backing up your old phone to the iCloud beforehand. It's much faster to wait and do that with the new phone after all is said and done. Your first step, go into the new phone and in Settings, go into General, then update the software to the latest version. We had many issues with the process stalling and then we would finally get an error message? This wasted a lot of time! It's so much quicker to update that software first, though it will take awhile (not lying). Once the software on the new phone is updated, then start the transfer process with your old phone. It will take a while (maybe 30 minutes). Once the whole thing transfers, your new phone will work and everything on the screen will look like your old phone. Here's the one thing we did not think about, you will still need a new SIM card from your Carrier. They are free. Simply go to your Carrier's store and explain that you bought a used phone and they will give you one. After everything is all set-up, call your carrier with your old phone and they will talk you through the process of installing the new SIM into the new phone. They will even test it out with you online until it works. Amazon Refurbished is guarranteed and definitally cheaper than other sites. The phone arrives fast too! After all is said and done, wipe the old phone to factory settings and remove the SIM card. Then you are all set! Newer phone at a cheaper price, it's guarranteed, and my daughter is totally happy with it! [More](javascript:void(0))[Hide](javascript:void(0)) There was a problem filtering reviews. Review Content: The package arrived a day early, which was nice and unexpected. I have the means to be able to get it replaced when the time comes, and to be honest was a relief after my last IPhone 11 from another seller had 100% battery health, just for it to be a non-Apple battery and cause all sorts of problems. Overall, I have no complaints with this phone. It’s in great condition in my book. Mic, speakers, cameras, haptics, everything (as far as I’ve been using it) has been in perfect order. Based on other reviews, whatever phone you get from this seller honestly depends on luck. It’s trivial, and that should never be the case, but if you can, I’d say take the risk. Worse case scenario you return it and get a full refund and try again. Overall, I’m very happy with my purchase. Review Title: We got the phone and it looked great, seemed to work fine
Review Content: We got the phone and it looked great, seemed to work fine. Except it would not connect to cellular. We initiated a return and were told we would be refunded when the phone was received and checked. I was initially told by the Amazon CSR I spoke to that as a courtesy, they would issue the refund as soon as the item showed it was picked up by UPS. After waiting a few days and no sign of refund, I called again. I was told by this CSR that I was given incorrect info, Amazons policy was to issue the refund when it’s received and checked. OK. So I wait again. I was told that once the phone was received, it could be up to 30 business days for it to be checked and refunded—but it rarely takes that long. I was given the date it was received. More waiting, then a full 30 business days after it had been received I called again to check on refund. It had not been initiated, but that CSR was initiating it. It literally took a full month and a half from the time Amazon received it (not from the time UPS picked it up—from the time Amazon actually received it back at their facility) for my refund to post. And the reason it was being returned was because it was misrepresented in the listing (not being fully unlocked), not because we changed our mind or anything frivolous. That did not matter and there was no courtesy or concession for what was their mistake in the first place. If you do get anything Amazon renewed, beware. If it works (like the 2nd phone we ordered did), it’s great and a wonderful option if you can’t afford fully new. But if there’s a problem you will get the run around, delays and misinformation from Amazon’s CSRs. They claim to stand behind all renewed products, but they will absolutely drag their feet and claim “it’s our policy” while you’re left waiting endlessly. So when it comes to Amazon renewed, don’t be blinded by the great prices and guarantees…it’s definitely “buyer beware”! Product Title: Amazon.com: Google Pixel 8 Pro, 128GB, Black - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: Screen: after two days I finally found a micro scratch in the lower right corner of the screen
Review Content: Screen: after two days I finally found a micro scratch in the lower right corner of the screen. The only way I found it was when affixing a screen protector, cleaning the screen I noticed it at a certain angle when the phone was off. Affixed the screen and the micro scratch is completely invisible regardless if the phone is on or off. To me that's as good as flawless. There were no scratches or dents on the rear facing camera, which surprised me given how far this protrudes on the Pixel 8 Pro Body: No dents, scratches, cracks, or damage of any kind. No objects obstructing or damage to any of the ports including microphone, USB-C, speakers. Buttons worked flawlessly Internal components: Screen free of any dead pixels, spots, etc. If there's any kind of screen bleed I haven't noticed it. I ran a battery gauge app for five days. Separately I used Android's system apps to measure the battery life. Everything stated the battery was in great condition. This was just as important to me as the screen; I plan to use this phone for the next three years at least so having a healthy battery was critical. On my phone and my tablets I always turn on Charge Optimization - battery charge limit set to 80% to prolong the life of the battery as much as possible. I'm not on my phone all day, my total screen time for any given day never exceeds 4 hours (usually less) but I have yet to use more than 40% of the battery per day. Phone arrived partially set up, the welcome screen for Android setup had been bypassed by someone and the phone was on the home screen. Of course I had no idea who partially set it up so for safety's sake I did a full factory reset. Always factory reset your devices when you get them if they haven't been reset already. Overall I'm extremely impressed. I loved my Pixel 5a and managed to get three years of use before a manufacturer's defect finally killed it. I also shudder at paying $1000 or more for a phone, obviously okay with buying last year's model after all of the updates/glitches have been worked out and the next shiny new thing has been released to drive down the price of the older model. Getting a one year old Pixel flagship phone for a fraction of the cost when new, this is absolutely worth it. Disclaimer: there were a number of things I didn't test nor will I do so. I don't play games on my phone, can't test the battery drain or the excess heat generated. This review covers how I use my phones. As long as I can use it to text, access the web, run my various apps, watch some media, video conference, and even upon rare occasion make phone calls (weird I know) I'm content. Update: The phone works fine installing a physical SIM card from any carrier. However the eSIM was locked by T-Mobile. I wouldn't expect the seller to know this and truthfully it took me a year to discover this as the Pixel 8 Pro does support dual SIMs. In such a situation calling the carrier is the only way to resolve the issue       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))       20 people found this helpful Helpful  Sending feedback...Thank you for your feedback. Review Title: The one I ordered from this seller was labeled as “Good” on Amazon
Review Content: The one I ordered from this seller was labeled as “Good” on Amazon. I feel it should have been labeled as "Acceptable" as I'll explain below. When I received the phone, however, I was a little disappointed. The screen wasn’t cracked, the color was Bay, and it came with a charger and SIM opener. But around the outer edges of the screen were sticky smudges of what I can only assume was glue or sealant from the screen being repaired. I was able to clean some of it off, so no harm done. Upon using the device, everything was pretty self-explanatory. The software updated, and I was able to transfer my information easily. All of the phone’s hardware was operational EXCEPT the fingerprint recognition. I tried multiple times and was met with a prompt saying that I needed to have it professionally repaired. This was one deciding factor in whether I was going to return the phone. Truthfully, I didn’t feel like going through the hassle. I was really excited about this device, and I can/will find other ways to unlock my phone faster, whether through another unlock method or my Pixel Watch. Lastly, as a note for anyone else, the phone initially charged unbearably slowly—1% every 8 minutes! That was another factor I considered when deciding whether to return it. I did some digging through the settings and turned off Battery Optimization, which returned the device to charging at a regular, reasonable rate. Overall, I love the device! It sucks that the fingerprint recognition doesn’t work, but the rest of the phone is functional enough that it wasn’t a dealbreaker for me. Product Title: Amazon.com: SAMSUNG Galaxy S21+ Plus 5G, US Version, 128GB, Phantom Black - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: The phone arrived in excellent condition, with no scratches or dents
Review Content: The phone arrived in excellent condition, with no scratches or dents. The screen appeared to have been replaced. After setting it up, I tested it by installing SIM cards from AT&T and TELLO, both worked perfectly - it's definitely unlocked. Right before the trip, I installed the "Orange" SIM card with the phone powered down. Upon arrival in Italy I powered it up, and it immediately connected to the local service. We used Google Maps to get from the airport to our hotel some 50km's away, no problems at all. Photos taken on the trip were excellent. We installed Google Translate and Microsoft Translator which worked perfectly and were a real asset in helping us navigate the foreign signs, menus, etc. We also set up Hot Spot and Tethering, and used that along with wireless calling on our US SIM based phones to make and receive free calls and texts to/from US numbers. It all worked as expected with no issues. The battery life was OK, I would start each day at 100% but by end of day it typically had around 30% remaining. My new (locked) S23+ easily gets two days on a single charge. I did notice a minor blemish on the screen after a week of using it. At first I thought it was just a greasy smear, but no amount of cleaning has managed to remove it. I didn't notice this when I first received the phone so it most likely manifested after use. It would seem to be a flaw with the screen itself. I did not use a screen protector, which may or may not have helped to prevent it from occurring. Fortunately it's close to the bottom of the screen and has not really affected the viewing area, nor has it affected the touch screen in the area of the blemish. All-in-all I am happy with this phone. I plan to use it for future international trips as it can do what I need without having to pay the $10-a-day AT&T International Roaming plan - that soon gets very expensive with 2 or more phones. Review Title: Battery life is terrible
Review Content: Battery life is terrible. My phone was fully charged at 100% this morning when I left for work. My phone has been in my pocket, not being used at all, for 10 hours. When I got home from work, my phone is now at 26%. I would hate to see what the battery looked like if I actually used my phone for the whole day. The speaker is horrendous. It's very quiet and muffled, and has no way to adjust it's settings. One of my biggest issues is how laggy the screen is. I have tried numerous keyboards, including the one the phone came with. Also with and without a screen protector. I basically have to mash on the phone to make it type. It is very frustrating. In fact, the only way that I am able to "type" this review, is because i'm using talk-to-text. While you're typing, the keyboard will decide to randomly start swiping and making nonsense up that you're not actually saying. There are no modes. I personally use work mode on my old phone a lot, I love all the settings that it comes with. But this phone only has Do Not Disturb mode, which you cannot personalize at all. And its features are subpar at best. I barely have anything installed on it and it's acting like it's out of memory and a decade old instead of a brand new phone. As I have been attempting to write this review, the phone has decided to delete the entire thing, input a bunch of random words, numbers, and letters, delete entire paragraphs, etc. It's a darn good thing I copied my review as I spoke it. I do not even have one good thing to say about this phone, it is a huge waste of money and do not purchase. Product Title: Amazon.com: Bose QuietComfort Earbuds II, Wireless, Bluetooth, World’s Best Noise Cancelling In-Ear Headphones with Personalized Noise Cancellation & Sound, Triple Black (Renewed) : Electronics
Review Title: ANC - active noise cancelation is next level
Review Content: ANC - active noise cancelation is next level. Unless you own a pair of Bose earbuds, this is most likely going to be one of its most impressive features. Multiple people I've shown this feature to are stunned by the ANC quality. It's like the whole world shuts down around you. You can hear if someone is speaking to you, but background noises are entirely muted or very, very quiet. It's insane. There is a small caveat: When nothing is playing in the earbuds and it's currently relatively quiet in your environment, there is a very apparent white noise that plays in the earbuds. It's an audible hiss. I've researched it and it seems it's the ANC microphones doing their thing and no company has discovered the technology to prevent that yet. Not sure why you'd be wearing these in a quiet room with nothing playing through them, but just know that it does that. Comfort - my ears are very sensitive to cartilage fatigue and these are outstandingly comfortable. I wear them for hours at a time. Connectivity - connecting to my phone was a clusterflup! It was glitchy, twitchy, and I was close to giving up returning the earbuds after trying for like an hour! Im an android user (Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra), so maybe Apple has a better connection quality with these buds. I'm not sure if it's a "Bose" issue or a "Refurbished" issue. Controls - the controls of the earbuds aren't confusing and actually seem pretty cool. Tap once to pause/play, twice to go to next song, thrice to backtrack a song, swipe upward on the earbud stick to raise volume, downward to lower volume, hold left earbud to change between ANC Quiet mode and Transparent mode, hold right earbud to engage AI assistant. They are great ONLY WHEN THEY WORK PROPERLY. It has happened endless times where I'll try to pause a track and it'll instead skip to the next one. Or I'll slightly adjust my earbuds and it'll stop, and I mean STOP not "pause", the audio entirely (which is not supposed to be an option??) and I have to trigger the AI assistant to get the audio going again so I don't have to get my phone. Sometimes the left earbud will just suddenly stop being in Quiet mode and will go Transparent. Today, I received a phone call and I single-tapped the earbud to answer, just to hear the AI assistant tell me "Call Ignored." Very frustrating and a big reason why I ended up returning these earbuds and won't be gambling on getting a different refurbished pair. Phone App: Bose's app could definitely use an upgrade. The connection is a little shoddy with the earbuds, but overall the app is does not have an engaging interface and it's not intuitive to navigate or understand all the options. Battery life - is okay. I only use it with ANC on max, which drains the battery faster but it lasts for a few hours which is what it promises but just keep that in mind. If you throw them in the case unplugged (assuming the case is charged) it'll charge them up pretty fast. While I highly recommend Bose Quietcomfort, I cannot comfortably recommend this generation refurbished, even in excellent condition. Although I am ultimately returning this pair, I am absolutely hooked on Bose Quietcomfort line of earbuds and have just decided to look elsewhere. Ended up finding a brand new unopened box of Bose Quietcomfort Ultra Earbuds 1st Gen at the same price as these ($140) on eBay. Only complaint I have is that I didn’t get the Ear Plugs and Nose Clip. I mentioned I am not a swimmer, but I may go in the pool in the future and those would have been nice. However, starting with the iPhone 8 (i think), Apple started sealing the cases, which requires a heat gun to separate the case because of the extra waterproofing adhesive. Review Title: I’m very disappointed with the noise canceling on the JBL Tune 770 headphones
Review Content: I’m very disappointed with the noise canceling on the JBL Tune 770 headphones. They struggled to eliminate deep airplane engine roar during a normal flight. Most of the engine noise seemed to be converted into loud white noise, except for the very deep thrum. I actually checked to make sure the headphones weren’t touching the seat and conducting the thrum directly to my ears. When the engines roared even more during landing, the JBL crackled as they tried to maintain the noise canceling. As for the rest of the sounds around me, nearby conversations were more understandable than with my AKG headphones. In comparison, my AKG N60nc can nearly eliminate the deep roar of plane engines during flight. The roar of braking plane engines comes through somewhat, but the AKG have never crackled. High frequencies come through fairly well (crying children, for example), but the mids are more muffled than the JBL. Due to the size of the ear cups, I would classify these JBL headphones as on-ear, not “over ear”. They’re very comfortable! They have a pad on the headband where the AKG dig into my head, so that problem is fixed. The sound quality was satisfying when I tested both music and video. But the noise canceling is a dealbreaker for me. My AKG are also on-ear, and its ear cups are even smaller, and yet somehow it manages to do a much nicer job with the noise canceling. Maybe I shouldn’t have bought refurbished JBL. I expected much better for headphones at this retail price range. Review Title: Android 13 installed
Review Content: Android 13 installed. Phone was well packed and came in a plain box with a nice 5Volt 2Amp (9Volt 1.87Amp) charger, USB C charging cable, and SIM Tray removal tool. The box was labeled NEW. The model I received is SM-G986U1. It is NEW, Pristine, Looks and Performs Flawlessly. The phone is Fully Unlocked for all US carriers GSM and CDMA. I put my SIM card and SD card in the dual SIM tray, powered up and in a short while I was up and running. I used the included Smart Switch app to transfer everything from my old Samsung phone. The phone is fast, color and graphics are great. WiFi and Bluetooth connect easily and work flawlessly. Phone connects quickly to Tracfone/Verizon mobile network and switches smoothly between LTE and 5G as I travel along. My Cell service is Tracfone through Verizon. The S20+ supports most of the LTE bands and 5G bands used by Verizon. This is important especially if you live or travel in a weak signal area with Verizon or other CDMA carrier. I don’t know about GSM carriers. I first ordered the S20 FE, which, I found out, does not support the mmWave bands needed for the fastest 5G Verizon service or reliably connect to Verizon in my weak signal home location. As a result I couldn’t get connected unless I walked outside my house into my driveway. Someone living in a strong signal area would not notice unless they travel into a weak signal area. This seems to be a problem with the design of the S20 FE and not the fault of the Renewer or Amazon. I wasn't willing to wait and try a replacement S20 Fe 5G so, unfortunately I had to send the S20 FE 5G back, I ordered the S20+ 5G instead. I'm very happy with my decision and with my S20+ 5G which supports 5G mmWave and reliably connects to Verizon in my weak signal area. I can’t say enough good about Stalion Requip. All Renewers are not created equal. Stalion Requip includes a printout of all the internal specs and test results so you know what you're getting. Purchase your phone from Stalion Requip and you won’t be disappointed. Review Title: I ordered an Amazon Renewed Galaxy s20+ 5G Unlocked in November of 2023
Review Content: I ordered an Amazon Renewed Galaxy s20+ 5G Unlocked in November of 2023. I got a $1000 phone for $400. The phone is freaking awesome! Screen quality and camera are exceptionally great. Even better than many of Samsung's flagship phones that have come out since the s20+ was released in 2020. The phone has become an important tool for my landscaping business (mobile check deposits, plant identification, and work documentation). However, I dropped it a few months ago and the camera stopped working. So I happily ordered another Amazon Renewed Galaxy s20+ 5G Unlocked. But much to my despair, the phone I received had a cheap, very low resolution screen and poor quality camera in it. I've ordered three of the renewed phones over the last few months in the hope of getting a true Galaxy s20+ 5G that isn't full of junk replacement parts. All three phones I ordered were advertised as having the same quality screen and camera as an original manufactured s20+ direct from Samsung. But all three of them contained cheap, junk components!!! The first of the three phones I ordered was dropped by me about a week after receiving it. The cheap screen in it shattered to pieces. I probably could've lied about the damage and returned the phone for a refund, but that would've been very dishonest behavior. So, I took the loss. I returned the second phone I ordered soon after receiving it and learning that it too contained junk components. I attempted to resolve my concerns about the poor quality components installed in the third phone I ordered by emailing the small business that sold it to me through Amazon. They placed a card in the box with the phone that said to contact them directly. However, Stallion ReQuip's reps failed to provide a resolution to the problem. They kept asking me for information I had already provided to them and they never sent me the return shipping label they said they would send to me. I don't know if their reading comprehension is lacking or they know they are selling phones that are different than what they are advertised as being and they had no intention of fixing the problem. So I initiated a return through Amazon and am now writing this review. If you are looking for a cheap, junk version of a Galaxy s20+, which isn't actually a true s20+, then feel free to order one of these falsely advertised phones. Or, you might be better off buying a lessor quality new phone for the money that will actually contain the parts it is supposed to have in it. But if you're looking for a great deal on a previous flagship model phone with original quality replacement parts, then go elsewhere. These businesses are not fully honest and transparent about what they're selling. And, Amazon Renewed phones, at least for me, are no longer the great and exciting bargain they once were. As for my original renewed purchased s20+, I took it to a local small business electronics repair shop today and got the camera replaced for $95. It only took about 45 minutes. So much better than burning through $600+ and wasting days and weeks dealing with sellers and making returns. Review Title: But I was still wanting to check out the APM
Review Content: But I was still wanting to check out the APM. Price is a bit crazy but I decided to order renewed and insurance again JIC. Now that I’ve had them about 4 days (I’m sorry Sony) I’m in love all over again! They sound absolutely amazing. The spatial audio really works well (Sony has a similar feature but it’s only supported by certain streaming services not including Apple). The soundstage opens up to something really fantastic sounding. Now reasons not to buy and why others may have returned theirs (thank you whoever sent mine back). THIS IS VERY IMPORTANT, if you don’t have an Apple device to connect to any only android or a PC, DO NOT BUY THESE! You will be seriously disappointed. You won’t be able to EQ them at all unless you use a 3rd party app or your device has EQ built in. I was very disappointed when I first connected and listened so some music, they were not good. Flat sounding with hardly any bass or treble! Like WTF, this can’t be right. Googled some information and instructions on how to properly set up Apple AirPods and the Max. You have to go into settings and go through a hearing test procedure that tunes the EQ specifically to your own ears. Listening to tones very similar to going to an audiologist. The results after that were WOW, what a difference nice broad response, solid bass, not quite as good as Sony who allows EQ from their app and have a special bass enhancement system, but solid and good definition. The soundstage opened up also with any stereo material. Then when you turn on spatial audio it’s WOW again, Apple did a really good job of processing the music and not messing it up. It goes from just headphones to room phones, the sound is around you! You can opt to let the headphones track your head movements or not. If you turn the music stays where it was, but after a few seconds of you don’t turn back they recenter you again. I really held off a long time as the price on these is really extreme compared to what the competition are selling as “equivalents”. The build quality on the Apple really separates them from the pack. With steel headband and aluminum components they should be very durable. Sony and Bose are, well… just plastic. As to lack of folding ability, I really don’t care, 99% of my listening is at home. I use earbuds if I’m outside or working out. The holder is… interesting. Different than what I’m used to but seems to work just fine around the house. Now I’ll try to wrap up with a comment about other reviews complaining about no power cords or chargers…I DON’T CARE!! I HAVE TOO MANY NOW!! lol, really if you have Apple products around you’re going to have a lightning cable and charger somewhere! Then, noise cancellation reaction…can I say WOW again? Really, my Sony are good but these are significantly better. Things I can’t hear or barely heard around the house with Sony that I don’t hear with APM. The TV, my wife, fans, well almost anything! Sony works well but their around ear system still rest on my Dumbo sized ears! lol. The Apple are really around the ear with a little room! This helps with noise control and comfort. And finally, comfort…the Sony are very comfortable but the plastic cups get hot and sweaty after a few minutes. The Apple are much better in that respect. My only criticism I guess would be comfort though. The clamping force on my head is significant by I’m getting used to it. I know my ears are large enough but I don’t think my head is oversized! Not ridiculous but definitely more than Sony, but the do stay in place well. If you have an iPhone or Apple devices to use these with and take the time to set them up properly you’ll be very happy. 3 months later and the refurbished Max went bad. Could not stay connected with Bluetooth so fortunately within the Amazon return window. Returned, credited and also reimbursed for the Asurion warranty. So, this was bad but I liked them a lot so I went out and picked up a brand new Pro Max. Not using the spatial sound much but the noise cancellation on the Max is awesome! Having foundation repairs done and staying in an upstairs bedroom with these on and I can hardly hear the industrial tools in use. These are far and away the best NC headphones I’ve owned. Still highly recommended but didn’t want to roll the dice on refurbished this time around! Even worse is that (2.) the dust screen in both tips were torn (see photo). Even though I don't need the original packaging, these buds came in only a plain white box with a computer-printed label saying what was inside. I don't consider this a con because it is not relevant to me. Evidently my definition of 'Refurbished - Excellent' is a bit different than those at the Amazon Refurbished Store. That being said, everything else about these buds is great. Of course I had to charge the case after it arrived and after I did I paired it with my Galaxy phone, which was simple. I already had the Wear app on my phone and just opening the buds' case alerted my phone of their presence. Wear opened up and asked if I wanted to pair, I responded in the positive and we were set to go. I was unhappy with the fit of the ear tips on the buds so I had to wait a few days for the new ear tips I bought from Amazon to arrive. Once the new tips were on the buds I went about configuring the them the way I wanted (in the Wear app) and I was happy with the results. A few years ago I purchased the Galaxy Buds2 Refurbished from Amazon but had to replace them because of a bad reaction they had to a software update a few weeks ago. After much research I decided on the Galaxy Buds2 Pro. The primary reason was the improved ANC feature. I read nothing but good reviews concerning that feature, and it was the quality of the ANC in the Galaxy Buds2 that sold me on that model. I often listen to audio books as I walk, and my walks often take me along busy roads that generate a lot of noise. I took my walk with the new Galaxy Buds2 Pro and was not disappointed! The quality of sound was excellent (for MY 77-year-old ears!) and the ANC feature didn't let me down. In fact I felt that it worked better than the Galaxy Buds2 I was replacing. And the price difference between these refurbished buds and a new pair allowed me to purchase the Asurion 3-yr warranty and a new set of ear tips of premium memory foam. With those ear tips and ANC turned on it's hard to hear anything around me, so it's just me and my book or music. I didn't get a pair of silicone ear tips that fit me right to compare, but these Comply foam tips were very comfortable throughout my 2 hours of walking. If you buy these buds, be careful to double-check what you receive, because I originally ordered a white pair but received the Galaxy Buds Pro, NOT the Buds2 Pro I ordered. I returned the Buds Pro I received and they refunded my money, but still, it cost me an extra week with no buds. Sorry, we failed to record your vote. More binds for the controls. It'd be nice to hold for volume up/down per ear and have it smoothly adjust without it being only one adjustment per input 6. The default sound levels are way too high. These shouldn't be able to get as loud as they can. It could damage hearing to unknowing people. It also makes it hard to get quiet unless you do a custom eq that lowers the whole board. 7. The find device feature should have a password or challenge to enter before activation to add more friction between people and dangerous volume levels. 8. Just thought of this days later. A silence toggle switch on the case, so you can physically stop the controls from functioning (or whatever you bind it to) with a toggle. It would be really nice to not have to take out my phone every time I want to disable the controls. Review Title: I recently got very into cycling, and my beloved Sennheisers were not suitable for the task to my wo
Review Content: I recently got very into cycling, and my beloved Sennheisers were not suitable for the task to my woe. I was content to just not cycle with any audio, until people started calling me when I was out! Stopping the whole bike and scrambling to pull my phone out of its holder was a nightmare. So I gambled on OpenRun Minis. They're fantastic!!! The position outside of the ear allows you to wear them literally all day and feel no different, they fit snugly over the ear and across the back of the head. And I mean really snugly. I got crashed into by a pickup truck rolling through a stop sign and they stayed on my head. The battery lasts long enough for a full day -- I've never had them run out on me, but I also charge them every night after I use them. They also seem pretty waterproof -- I sweat a lot when cycling, and they're fine. Wouldn't test them underwater though! My only issue (and it is a minor one) is with the sound quality -- I would say it's more than enough for podcasts, but it leaves a little to be desired in terms of real music. They're a little too bassy and a little muddy-sounding, almost? It makes sense considering your flesh is literally muffling them and it's honestly better than some cheap headphones I've used (looking at you, literally anything sold in Staples) but for the price point it's worth noting. Review Content: Headphones are heavier than my daughter's Q30 phones so if weight matters to you, choose those instead. Sound has more mids and treble the other but I swear I can hear more details than the Q30. Bluetooth is very quick to connect and is great with the EQ app. I use this both on my phone and on TV as well as talking with customers as a headset and works great on all. Noise cancelling is VERY good as well as transparency mode. Normal mode not so much as it lacks punch in comparison but only at high volumes. I prefer the depth of sound on these over the Anker Life Q30, but both are great choices and Q30 is definitely better for long term use as it weighs less. On my phone, music does sound extremely clear and position matters, I feel it sound a bit better slightly tilting backwards ( found this out by simply lying down wearing them ). Battery life is fantastic. Time will tell how well these hold up. No phones are perfect, but for the $60 price tag these are my current go to phones. Review Title: I am in love with these headphones
Review Content: I am in love with these headphones. They look brand spanking new, work beautifully, and I am SO happy with this purchase. It did come with original case and packaging (package did have some wear/tear but the headphones were flawless so I don't care). It didn't include a charging cord (not worried about that either because I already have one) but it did include two of the talking cords which made me laugh because that was just so silly. I had Beats Solo3 before these but was tired of having the headphones constantly on my ears which gets very uncomfortable after awhile of use. So I decided to try Studio3 and I am sooo much happier with these. The sound is definitely an improvement from the Solo3, in terms of quality and the bass as well, not to mention so much more comfortable on my head longterm. The noise cancellation is definitely not the greatest, I've had $40 headphones that do better with noise cancellation but I wasn't really concerned about that. The quality of the music is what I look for the most and these headphones definitely nailed that. I love love love them. Product Title: Amazon.com: Beats Studio3 Wireless Headphones - Matte Black (Renewed) : Electronics
Review Title: Both the quality of the audio and noise cancellation to my “average” ear is pretty great
Review Content: Both the quality of the audio and noise cancellation to my “average” ear is pretty great. The sense I got from reading reviews of competing products on Amazon (namely the Bose Quiet Comfort & Sony 1000s) was that the Beats looked and sounded good but weren’t very strong in the noise cancellation department. I’ve now had a chance to use these on my weekly commute (2+ hr flight each way) and the noise cancellation on these has not disappointed. As other reviewers have noted, all noise is not eliminated, but a lot of the lower rumbling engine noise (on the plane) or fan noise (in my office) is blocked out. The only thing I’ve noticed isn’t blocked out as much are human voices (more noticeable if I’m not playing any music/audio). I mainly use these with my iPhone but haven’t had any issues pairing with an Android phone (Pixel 2 XL) or laptop (a Chromebook). It’s amazing how much lower volume I can have these on compared to the standard Apple earbuds that came with my iPhone 7. My ONLY complaint after 5-6 weeks of use is that the noise cancelling feature on the first pair that I received from Amazon would periodically fade off and on during flights. I went through all of the troubleshooting (updating software, etc) but nothing fixed the problem so I took them in to an Apple store for repair, and was sent a replacement pair the following week at no charge that have worked great. This was definitely a hassle, but for me was worth saving the $$$ taking a chance on the refurbished item. It’s also worth noting that I’ve purchased 5-6 refurbished items on Amazon and this is the first time that I have had any sort of technical issue with a purchase. All in all I’ve been very satisfied with the look, sound, and noise cancelling capabilities of these headphones. This is my second pair of Beats (bought my first ones way back in 2008) and love having the Bluetooth connection/ditching the cord. If you’re looking for an all-around solid pair of wireless noise-cancelling headphones then I’d definitely recommend getting these ... you might just want to shell out the extra money for a brand new pair if you don’t want to deal w/potential issue on refurb front. Review Title: Todos los intentos de actualizar el dispositivo fallaron y hubo errores que me decían que «acudiera
Review Content: Todos los intentos de actualizar el dispositivo fallaron y hubo errores que me decían que «acudiera a un centro de servicio», lo cual es inaceptable si se trata de un teléfono que se supone que está listo para usarse sin usar. Este tipo de problema suele estar asociado con el flasheo incorrecto del firmware o con dispositivos que se han modificado fuera de los canales oficiales del fabricante o del operador. Cuando las configuraciones del firmware y el hardware no se alinean correctamente (por ejemplo, los cargadores de arranque específicos de un operador frente al firmware desbloqueado genérico), pueden interrumpirse las rutas de actualización, inhabilitar funciones e incluso crear riesgos de estabilidad a largo plazo. Pasé dos días enteros solucionando problemas (probando diferentes métodos de actualización, restablecimientos y opciones de recuperación), básicamente haciendo el tipo de trabajo que cabría esperar de un técnico, no de un cliente. Ni siquiera las opciones de asistencia profesional, como Geek Squad, estarían a la altura, lo que demuestra lo problemáticos que pueden ser estos dispositivos una vez que se modifican de esta manera. Después de investigar más a fondo, encontré muchas otras reseñas que describían exactamente el mismo problema, lo que sugiere claramente que no se trata de un error puntual, sino que forma parte de un patrón. Parece que algunos vendedores externos están tomando atajos restaurando o «desbloqueando» dispositivos de forma inadecuada, lo que compromete su funcionalidad. Esto puede infringir las políticas de la plataforma sobre el estado de los dispositivos y las descripciones precisas de los anuncios. En resumen: no se trataba de un producto reacondicionado correctamente, sino de un dispositivo mal modificado que no debería haberse vendido como «renovado». Si estás pensando en comprarle a este vendedor, no lo hagas. Ahórrate tiempo, frustraciones y riesgos, y opta por una fuente confiable. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple Watch Series 8 [GPS, 41mm] - Midnight Aluminum Case with Midnight Sport Band, S/M (Renewed) : Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry
Review Title: Compré este reloj en condición "Excelente", pero de excelente no tiene casi nada
Review Content: Compré este reloj en condición "Excelente", pero de excelente no tiene casi nada. Debería estar catalogado como "Bueno" o "Regular", porque siendo sinceros, sí tiene rayones bastante perceptibles que incluso se sienten al pasar el dedo. Entiendo que es un producto reacondicionado; el problema es que lo venden como “Excelente” y no debería ser así. En cuanto a funcionalidad, llegó impecable. Todo funciona sin problema y la salud de la batería llegó al 87%. En las fotos que agregué se puede ver que desconecté el reloj a las 11:40 a.m. y para las 11:41 p.m. aún tenía el 48% de batería restante. Esto, claramente, con la pantalla siempre activa (AOD) apagada. Con el AOD encendido noté que la batería sí se descarga muchísimo más rápido; le calculo que en vez del 48%, a esa misma hora me habría quedado un 18% o incluso menos. Algo que no me gustó para nada es el cargador genérico incluido. Supuestamente es de la marca Steren, aunque lo dudo, porque la verdad se siente de muy mala calidad (como un cargador muy barato de los que ves en el tianguis). Tardó más de una hora solo en lograr encender el reloj, ya que el equipo llegó con la batería completamente muerta. Llegué incluso a pensar que el reloj estaba defectuoso porque no encendía, pero después de un largo rato por fin lo hizo. Este cargador es de muy baja potencia y provoca que el reloj se caliente bastante; la carga de 0 a 100% tomó más de 2 horas. Si consigues el cable de carga rápida original de Apple, este modelo se carga por completo en unos 45 minutos, ya que el Series 8 sí soporta esta tecnología (me parece que está disponible del Series 7 en adelante). Conclusión: Sí recomiendo la compra (lo compré por un precio de $3,530.27 MXN), pero hagan la inversión de adquirir el cable original (cuesta $649 MXN) para que puedan aprovechar la carga rápida y no tengan que estar esperando más de 2 horas. Por mi parte, aún estoy indeciso sobre si regresarlo o quedármelo, únicamente por los rayones, ya que se perciben demasiado, si no hubiese sido una excelente compra. Bueno, esa fue mi experiencia espero y les sirva.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Review Title: Finally, as the screen sizes have increased, I decided, ok, there are apps that I may find useful as
Review Content: Finally, as the screen sizes have increased, I decided, ok, there are apps that I may find useful as well as the integration of my Google Calander and Contacts with my phone. But, while sure, I could spend over a grand on a new phone, it just did not seem to me to be a wise use of my money. I had read that a lot of smartphone addict aficionados look for the latest and greatest.....or maybe they did not like the color of their new phone....so they sent it back. Rather than winding up in landfills as a lot of returned Amazon merchandise does, unfortunately, Amazon was wise enough to create their refurbished division in which various refurbishers compete for customer's business. I thought, why not give it a try. I purchased the phone from a company named Kiss in Manhattan where I grew up. They had a high positive rating so I picked them My phone arrived the next day despite the fact that I did not pay for overnight shipping. Unfortunately, as I understand it, the ripples of the COVID situation put them out of business. As for the phone, when I opened up the box, I was shocked. In terms of appearance, there was absolutely no way I would have known it was a refurb....not a mark on it. As far as function is concerned, I used various apps to test it, and it passed. I have been using it since the first week of August. My estimate of battery life remaining is upwards of 90 percent. Of note, at Batteries and Bulbs, I can replace the battery for something like 70 dollars still putting me way ahead of the game since the phone was under 400 dollars. Add a Microcenter 512 MicroSD card for about 50 dollars and I have a phone with 3/4 of a terabyte, far more storage than I anticipate ever using.

Review Title: The phone is very elegant looking, especially with its curved display
Review Content: The phone is very elegant looking, especially with its curved display. As such, it would look very nice put upon a pedestal in our living room. However, I did not find the phone in an art store. I purchased it to use every day as my mobile phone. What is the Note 9 made of? Simply put, it is basically glass placed over a metal frame which again is fine if you want to display it on your bookshelf, but not particularly practical. Unless a person is downright foolish, just about everyone puts a case on it. You can forget about using one of those clear cases that let the beauty of the phone shine through. Drop it and you are facing an expensive repair. I was using the Unicorn Beetle Pro case with a belt clip which I never used. The phone dropped on the stairs and the inner part of the case broke. I was not really upset about that for the simple reason it saved the phone. Now I am trying an Outbox Defender which looks pretty robust. How about the curved display? Yes, it looks rather elegant, but does one really need it for functionality? The answer is absolutely not. It only serves to make designing a screen protector problematic. As for screen protectors go, I think they are necessary and I have just resigned myself to the fact that the edge adhesives are going to wear out and to simply replace them every once and awhile. They are not particularly expensive. We as consumers really should not put up with this nonsense. Most of the smartphones made these days have similar designs. They reinforce the notion of built-in obsolescence, or in actuality, built-in fragility. Yes, technology changes very rapidly. But, the basic technology of how these phones communicate does not. There is absolutely no reason that we should have to get a new phone every year. They should last far longer than that in my humble opinion. The question is how can we communicate this to the manufacturers? We can't boycott them because they all pretty much do the same thing. It is something it think about.....just saying. I hate it so much I haven't bothered trying to set up anything else except fingerprint recognition to unlock it. This is the first time ever, a Samsung device has let me down.
