Review Title: I got the Note 20 because it's the last Note (currently) that has an SD card slot; I'm absolutely ag
Review Content: I got the Note 20 because it's the last Note (currently) that has an SD card slot; I'm absolutely against some company gouging me hundreds of dollars extra for a 256GB phone when a 512GB SD card is under 50 bucks. The drawback to that is this phone came with pretty much nothing at all but a charging cable, which isn't really adding any value. It took me some time to find a way to get the SD card slot open, without their custom tool, because on this phone at least the hole is waaayyyy too small for a paper clip. I finally unwound the spring from an ink pen, which was small enough and stiff enough to release it. Seriously leave out the cable that probably everyone in the world has by now and put that tool in! It's needed for the SIM even without an SD card. Speaking of SIM, moving my line to this phone was trivially simple. The phone was apparently on T-Mobile previouisly and I'm on Verizon, and everything worked flawlessly right from the phone. Put the SIM in, turned it on, and followed the instructions. Done. I got a Note because, well, I've been a Note fanboy since the 4, when my old Droid with the hardware keyboard gave up the ghost, because of the S-Pen. It's not something I use every day, but when I do use it, there is literally no alternative that works like the S-Pen. If Samsung ever stops putting that on their phone I'll probably move on to something more affordable. This is my first ever refurb, and this one at least is exactly what one would hope; it physically indistinguishable from a brand new phone. Even close observation in the light reveals no scratches or blemishes, it hasn't crashed or exhibited any wonky behaviour (knocks on head), and it's significantly snappier than the old one. That's not just because it has more resources, I think it's because the UI has been tweaked. For example when scrolling a long list this phone's "inertia", how long it scrolls untouched after a flick up or down, is much higher than the old phone, so it's considerably faster to browse by scrolling. I'm sure other improvements have been made as well, and together they translate into a much more responsive feel. The OS itself is similar to the Note 8, really, but it has even more bloat and unremovable cruft in it. For exampe there's "AR" functionality now, but even though I have nothing AR, and if I do it's highly unlikely I'll use this phone in conjunction with it. There's an "AR Zone" that can't be disabled, can't be removed, can't be told not to nag me with notifications, can't be managed in the slightest. Seriously Samsung, get off your high horse. You don't know what I want my phone to do; fine if you want to have that enabled by default, why do I care? But can't disable it or remove all the massively huge list of permissions? Want to rub some salt in there for me? It's also considerably more in-your-face nagging about things; like I haven't figured out how to get it to stop nagging me to save passwords for web sites, as if the last fifteen times I'd change my mind. Stuff like that isn't helpful, it's obtuse and rude. Migration was a PitA, but that's normal, so I mention it anecdotally. Samsung's "Smart Switch" does make it less than heinously atrocious, but "Everything" isn't (everything), and it still took me days to get all my appointments and other things loaded in. Once I find my browser bookmarks and get them in I'll finally be done. Least favorite part of getting a new phone is setting the @*&#% up. I can back up and restore a computer with trivial ease but no phone maker yet is smart enough to do that with a phone. Pathetic. I considered only four stars because of the missing SD card tool. Not sure how many folks would be able to figure out how to open it with the hole being about 2/3 the diameter of a paper clip, which is by the way what Verizon recommends using if one can't find the tool. I have no straight pins so I don't know if they work, but if I did I'd still want to file the point off to be sure I didn't damage anything. But overall a VERY happy camper. If you like Android it's likely you'll be satisfied with this phone, and if you've never had an S-pen you'll probably be hooked. lol       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))       235 people found this helpful Helpful  Sending feedback...Thank you for your feedback. Product Title: Amazon.com: Samsung Galaxy S20 Ultra, 128GB, Cosmic Black - Fully Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: 1: The camera isn't flush with the back of the phone
Review Content: 1: The camera isn't flush with the back of the phone. unnecessarily Bulky. 2: I HATE the on screen fingerprint reader. Hate it. I could unlock my old phone instantly with my eyes closed by feel alone. With the S20 Ultra, You have to make sure your finger is in exactly the right area of the phone, in just the right position and keep it there for exactly the right length of time and it will work the first try maybe 3/4 of the time. 3- Flashlight sucks. Considerably. Might as well just use a candle. 4- the touch response is too good. If you think about swiping the wrong thing, you get a new window or changed settings. Relax. 5-the screen and back of the phone, I'm convinced were specifically designed to attract dust, debris, fingerprints, smears etc. It's disgusting. If I were a stranger and saw my phone I'd immediately think I was a slob. A case is a necessity, not only because the phone I'm pretty sure is plastic. I thought the S20's were aluminum, maybe I just don't know how cheap aluminum is? I'm not confident at all in the durability of this phone or the screen, I'm glad I bought the protection plan. (The covering over the precious camera however, is in fact resistant to debris and fingerprints). 6-why is this screen so big, but my status bar with the time and battery life so unreasonably tiny? I'm looking down my nose holding my phone out like I'm 90 years old trying to read the paper, it's absurd? Can you change that? 7-simplified and boring drop down menu/notification screen. Feels dumbed down for boring people. Less personal 1- Arrived in pristine condition. You'd never know it was refurbished. I can't find a flaw or scratch anywhere. And after seeing reviews and pictures, I looked for them. 3-battery life is phenomenal. I had no memory of how long a full charge should actually last until I took my S20 ultra out for it's first day on the town. 4-It has an SD card slot. I was able to switch over a lot of information from my old phone. I am not in fact 90, I'm only 39, but I still don't like all this saved information in clouds or saved to Google acts etc. Doesn't feel right, I want my information on an object I can hold in my hand. 5-it's not an iPhone. I think we can all agree that's a win. 6- it's 5G. Turns out 5G isn't as widespread as the TV lead me to believe. I've seen it connect to 5G once and I drive all around Western New York. But that's still fun 7- other than little changes to the UI, updates and external components... It's virtually the same thing as my S9+. Which I loved. So that's a big deal for me. I don't have to spend time relearning how to use it. With the difference in generations, I was expecting bigger changes. I liked my S9+ better. If they could have kept that design and just upgraded the insides over the years instead of needing new actual phones designs, I'd have been thrilled. If my S9+ was still functional, that would be ideal really (I'll miss you S9+ 💋) Having only dealt with the S9+ galaxy, that it the standard I'm judging from. The S20 Ultra feels genuinely fragile in my hands as opposed to the S9+. It feels like a lower quality phone and I do not anticipate the screen or case holding up over the years that I plan on keeping it. So I would recommend the protection plan offered. Review Title: Fully unlocked Galaxy S20 Ultra (Renewed) ordered from thegadgetdeals on Amazon Marketplace to repla
Review Content: Fully unlocked Galaxy S20 Ultra (Renewed) ordered from thegadgetdeals on Amazon Marketplace to replace my Galaxy S9, which I have really enjoyed over the last 3 years but is now too slow and not enough storage for my liking. I went with the S20 rather than upgrading to an S21 primarily because of the expandable storage available with the S20 [I'm bummed Samsung is going away from this - it was one of the great things that set them apart from Apple... boooo!]. Anyway, Verizon has pretty much refused to restock their S21 Ultra 512 GB during the last 4-6 months, hence I ultimately pulled the trigger on this phone. Regarding the product according to the seller: arrived quickly and as promised. Few scratches on back cover that I care nothing about at all (expected as this is a refurb). Otherwise, seems in great condition. Came with a charger as promised. I was nervous about ordering unlocked phone as I have always purchased through my carrier, but I inserted my Verizon sim card, and it seems to be working great. Regarding the phone itself (S20 Ultra versus my old S9): FAST - by far what I'm happiest about. My old phone was really dragging in responsiveness. Front (selfie) camera noticeably WAY better. Rear camera - I'm sure is better, but I expected to notice a huge difference and other than the fact that I can zoom in a lot more, the quality when I zoom in isn't just over the moon better than my old phone (ie, on 8x zoom, photos from the 2 phones look similar). But I will say, the "live focus" that resembles the "portrait mode" of an iPhone makes me excited. Plus there's other nice features, like zooming out (wide view), etc. Overall happy with this. NEGATIVES..... my only complaint that I hope doesn't ruin my experience with this phone is the FINGERPRINT READER. The actual reader on the back of the S9 was seemingly perfect. I LOVED it - almost never had issues. Why, WHY?! did they go to a digital one. It seems to work fine without a case or screen protector. I've tried a few cases thus far that all claim to work well with the reader but NO. With case on, it works like 25% of the time (followed all the directions). And honestly, I'm not sure I blame the cases - seems like everyone is having issues with this. I'm ordering some screen protectors that have decent reviews and *fingers crossed*. Oh, also, this phone is big, like huge. I think (hope) I'll get used to it, but wow. Samsung, please review the size of female pockets before designing your next phone. Product Title: Amazon.com: Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra 5G, 512GB, Lavender - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: The screen is ridiculous in the best way
Review Content: The screen is ridiculous in the best way. That 6.8-inch Dynamic AMOLED with the super-smooth 120Hz refresh rate feels like butter, whether I'm doom-scrolling X at 2 a.m. or editing photos outside in bright sunlight (the brightness is no joke, it legit gets stupidly bright). Colors pop without looking cartoonish, and watching anything HDR on it is basically a religious experience. The cameras… okay, look, I’m that annoying friend who takes way too many pictures, and this thing spoils you rotten. The 200MP main sensor is overkill in the best possible way—zoom in on a photo you took from across the street and you can still read the text on someone’s shirt. 100x Space Zoom is mostly a party trick (it gets shaky past 30x unless you’ve got tripod arms), but 10x optical is actually usable and looks clean. Night mode is straight-up witchcraft; I’ve taken shots in near darkness that look like they were taken at dusk. Performance is boring in the best way possible—it just never stutters. I’ve got 50+ tabs open in Chrome, Spotify running, editing 4K video in CapCut, and it doesn’t even break a sweat. Battery life surprised me too. With heavy use (always-on display, 5G, location on, lots of camera), I’m still ending most days with 30-40% left. Throw it on a 45W charger and it’s at 70% in like 30 minutes. The S Pen is lowkey one of my favorite things. I use it for quick notes when I’m too lazy to type, doodling on screenshots, and signing PDFs without printing anything. Feels way more natural than I expected. - It’s a big boy. One-handed use is a stretch (literally). - Fingerprint magnet on the back, but a case fixes that. - Still some Samsung bloatware, though it’s gotten better. If you’re the kind of person who wants the absolute best Android phone and doesn’t mind the size or the price tag, the S23 Ultra is still holding the crown going into late 2025. Even with the S24 Ultra and S25 Ultra out, I’m not feeling upgrade itch at all. This thing is just that good. 9.5/10, would (and probably will) buy again. Review Title: The reason I wanted a flip phone is because I constantly break/crack the screen on the standard phon
Review Content: The reason I wanted a flip phone is because I constantly break/crack the screen on the standard phones. It does not matter if I buy the most expensive bulletproof phone case. Those cases only protect the phone/screen if the phone falls on an edge or back side. If the phone lands on an object anywhere on the screen, they automatically crack the screen. Not with a flip phone. Once closed, the screen is protected and if you buy a case for it like I did, now it's truly bulletproof. I've accidentally dropped my phone so many times and no damage to the screen at all. My phone case also protects the small outside screen. I actually like this version with the small screen in the front. Makes it harder to damage it. The larger the screen, the bigger the chances of damaging it like the standard phones. When flipped closed, takes up way less space in my pants pockets compared to a non flip phone. No chance of it slipping out my pocket. The phone case I added does make it bulkier but if you're not using one or a really thin skin type cover, pretty thin sleek phone. It does not have an external SD card slot for memory. Whatever memory the phone comes with, that's it. This also makes it harder to track, save, and transfer files like pics and videos. It does have wireless charging (I wouldn't have bought it if it didn't) however, it is slow. I believe the wireless charging is rated at 5W max. Wired charging is fast though (30W max). I just prefer wireless charging because all charging ports (on all phones) do wear out over time and eventually fail preventing from charging the phone. The crease in the middle of the screen starts becoming noticeable on the screen after so much use, abuse, and flips. This doesn't bother me and I don't really notice it when watching videos but others are super sensitive to this and want perfect screen clarity always, so keep that in mind. This tradeoff for having a flip phone is worth it to me. This flip phone screen technology is still new so I expect the screens to only get better in the future. Overall, love my phone and don't regret this purchase.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))       4 people found this helpful Helpful  Sending feedback...Thank you for your feedback. While low-light performance isn't its strongest suit, it's still decent for the price point. The macro lens adds a fun element for close-up shots! You can capture details you'd otherwise miss. Beyond the basics, I appreciate the expandable storage via microSD card. This is a lifesaver, allowing you to store tons of photos, videos, and apps without worrying about running out of space. The One UI skin is clean, intuitive, and packed with features. Samsung has done a great job optimizing it for this device. The phone runs smoothly and reliably for my day-to-day tasks. Overall, the Samsung Galaxy A13 5G is a fantastic budget-friendly smartphone that delivers on its promises. If you're looking for a reliable phone with 5G connectivity, a smooth display, and great battery life, this is definitely worth considering. Highly recommended! Review Title: The Flip 7 is a really well-made speaker
Review Content: The Flip 7 is a really well-made speaker. It's smaller, lighter, looks better in my opinion, and is easier to throw in a backpack or even a bike bottle holder. If portability is your top priority, JBL did a great job. Sound-wise, though, I ended up preferring the Bose for the way I listen to music. In a small to medium-sized room, the Bose sounds fuller and deeper. It almost feels like it has a tiny built-in subwoofer. The JBL has punchier mid-bass and can hit a little harder, but it doesn't reach into the lower sub-bass the same way the Bose does. In a larger room, the Flip 7 does project a little better, but for me the difference wasn't big enough to outweigh what I liked about the Bose. Outside, neither speaker really produces the kind of low-end that I'd want for an open environment, so the slight advantage the JBL has in projection wasn't enough to change my mind. For some context, I'm coming from an older Anker Soundcore Boost that finally gave up. Surprisingly, I still think the Soundcore Boost has more "thump" than either the JBL or the Bose. Both of these newer speakers are much cleaner and clearer, though, with better overall sound quality. I think the Flip 7 is a great speaker for someone who values portability and durability. If you're riding a bike, traveling, spending time at the park, or just want something that's easy to carry around, it's an excellent choice. If your primary use is listening indoors in a small or medium-sized room, I personally preferred the Bose SoundLink Plus enough that I decided to keep it instead. Neither speaker is bad, they just excel in different areas, and for my use case the Bose was the better fit. Review Title: Installed and used Samsung Smart Switch app to transfer all my old S8+ phone apps, settings and file
Review Content: Installed and used Samsung Smart Switch app to transfer all my old S8+ phone apps, settings and files to the new one, using wifi direct phone-to-phone. Easy to do but took almost 5 hours to complete due to lots of apps plus huge number of files on the old phones SD card, which automatically transferred to the main 128gb system storage on the new phone. A few settings, like themes and wallpapers, were not applied during this process, but were easy to fix after. I also have a couple of apps that are licensed and locked to a specific device, (Norton360 and IGO Navigation) and had to uninstall them from both phones then reinstall on the new one. For Norton, I also had to go to my Norton account on PC, remove the old phone and add the new one. Not an issue, just a consideration and a few extra steps. Would have liked to have SD card support, but had researched and knew going in that the 128gb built-in storage would be more than adequate for my needs, including for about 70gb of photos and MP3 audio files I had on the 128gb SD card of my old S8+ phone. I do wonder why it needs 39gb of storage for system files though. Almost 4GB more than on the old phone. That seems extremely excessive to me, but might just be the difference between Android 9 on the old phone vs Android 13 on the new one (after all system updates). Another consideration, which is not really a complaint, as I knew it would happen, is that getting all of the 30+ OS, security and other updates took almost 2 full days to accomplish from a freshly factory reset phone, which this is. This is something that should not be allowed to happen according to the default automatic processes and schedule, as that could take weeks. You need to manually go to Settings / Software Update / Check for Updates, and download and install the recommended system update. Then repeat and repeat and repeat again, as many times as needed, until it says no more updates are needed. If you ever need to do a factory reset, you may need to do it all over again. If you ever sell your phone, remember to do a factory reset to remove all of your personal apps, settings and data, and let the new owner know that they might need to redo this system software update process. Final note: If you are upgrading to 5G for the first time, and have an old 4G SIM card in your old phone, you will need to get a new 5G SIM from your carrier in order to have 5G capability. For the phone I bought, and my carrier, this was Verizon. I chose to do this only after finishing all of the Smart Switch and system upgrades described above, which only needed wifi. Verizon swapped out my SIM card for no charge.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))       34 people found this helpful Helpful  Sending feedback...Thank you for your feedback. Review Title: Ive bought this as a renewed at $27
Review Content: Ive bought this as a renewed at $27.06 after tax, it came shipped in a small white plastic envelope bag with the manufacturer's box. Did not have any visual or techical problem with the controller. Well, This is my first gaming controller for my iphone 16 pro, tho I've been a playstation controller guy so these felt alright for something that is meant to be more portable and on-the-go, Overall, I'm very satisfied with this controller. I did a lot of research, mainly because I saw it how was affordable it was compare to other controllers on amazon. I wasnt sure if cheap meant good, but this exceed my expectation. My hands are small and thin for guy so these felt good in my hands. The texture in the back of the controller makes gripping it feel like it wont slip out of my hands. It made my gameplay 100x better on fortnite and also in Genshin Impact, I didn't want overspend too much for a controller. It connects only via USB-C which in my opinion is the best choice when it comes to fast input latency. Now I dont have to worry about any weird disconnections or laggish input because of bluetooth cause this controller has none. The USB-C's flexible dongle is a mindful addition, it is very flexible for when you connect or remove your phone from it. If I could compare the quality of contoller with the PS controllers that this would be below it, it doesn't have the premium, dense feel of higher end controllers. I feel like if I were to drop this, it may possibly break. I also read that some people experienced stick drift as well, there is a way to fix it and it’s by calibrating it, read the instructions in the manual booklet they’ve provided. Review Title: As for the speaker itself, the Charge 5 is less portable than the JBL flip
Review Content: As for the speaker itself, the Charge 5 is less portable than the JBL flip. It's clearly not designed to be carried around when hiking or jogging and such. It has no handle or strap, though one can be purchased separately for about $15. It has set of rubber "feet" on its bottom that keep it from rolling when placed flat. It's ideal for sitting on a table or bench when having a picnic or BBQ party (this is what I use it for). It has very good bass and mid-range sound and it's plenty loud. Even at high volumes, I don't hear a lot of distortion. I would rate the speaker sound performance as very good. They claim it will play for 20 hours. I've never used it for that long, but I've used it for several hours at high volume and it never died. It also recharges to full battery in just a few hours. It's very quick to link up via Wi-Fi and I've walked a good distance from it and it doesn't lose connection. There are cheaper Wi-Fi speakers on the market, but from what I've read, the sound quality isn't usually as good as this product. I would recommend spending a few extra bucks for this one. If you want something you can walk around with, look at the JBL flip 5 or 6. If you want a huge block-party type speaker, this one might be a little small. However, if you're in the middle and want a nice backyard speaker, this is definitely the one. When used indoors, it is really loud. Review Title: Since I was perfectly content with my old phone, except for the badly aging battery, I decided to tr
Review Content: Since I was perfectly content with my old phone, except for the badly aging battery, I decided to try this refurb, especially since it promised a battery in good shape (80% or better of a new battery). I'm extremely pleased with it. I was able to move the SIM card (still functional) from the old one, boot it up, and completely restore everything from existing backups - apps, screen layouts, photos, contacts, bookmarks, everything. The saved wireless connections and a few apps needed new sign-ins but that was about the extent of the recovery. The phone is in perfect cosmetic condition. (It does NOT come with a screen protector; you'll need to install one yourself.) From a functional standpoint it works perfectly. I cannot vouch for the 80% or greater battery capacity of a new phone, but even if not good, it is far better than the old one, which was 4 1/2 years old. Replacing the battery in the old one would have cost at least as much as this phone, or else the time and effort of a complicated and risky disassembly on my part. I'd buy another one of these refurbished phones without hesitation. Review Title: After inserting my SIM card, I kept receiving network errors
Review Content: After inserting my SIM card, I kept receiving network errors. I contacted multiple carriers, including Sprint, T-Mobile, and even Samsung support, trying to resolve the issue. After all that troubleshooting, I was informed that the phone was actually locked to Verizon. To make matters worse, Verizon explained that the device was still tied to a previous account holder. They even attempted to contact the original owner to authorize the unlock, but she declined to assist. This left me completely unable to use the phone on any network. This was extremely frustrating and a huge inconvenience. The product was clearly misrepresented, as it was not truly unlocked as advertised. I spent a significant amount of time going back and forth with different companies, only to end up with a device I couldn’t use. I would strongly caution others to verify the authenticity of “unlocked” claims before purchasing. Unfortunately, this experience did not meet expectations at all. Review Title: I recently upgraded from a 45mm Series 9 to the new Black Titanium Apple Watch Ultra 3
Review Content: I recently upgraded from a 45mm Series 9 to the new Black Titanium Apple Watch Ultra 3. Instead of paying the $799 retail price, I decided to take a gamble on an "Open Box" unit from iPower Resale for $609. The gamble paid off flawlessly. The watch arrived in its original box, and the included charger and watch band were still sealed in Apple's factory packaging. Checking the settings, the battery health is sitting dead-on at exactly 100%, and the device still has an active Apple Limited Warranty until January 2027. For all intents and purposes, I saved $190 on a brand-new watch. Size & The Screen Upgrade A lot of the online consensus claims that jumping from a 45mm Series watch to the 49mm Ultra isn't that noticeable of a screen difference. I completely disagree. The switch to the flat sapphire crystal glass changes the entire experience. Because it doesn't curve off at the edges like the Series 9, the usable screen real estate feels massive. Add in the 3,000 nits of brightness, and the display is incredibly crisp and visible from across the room. Comfort & Battery Life Is the watch huge? Yes, it is objectively a large, thick piece of titanium. But despite the visual bulk, it is surprisingly balanced on the wrist. It doesn't feel like you are wearing a brick, and it is comfortable enough that I sleep in it every single night without any discomfort. The biggest quality-of-life improvement coming from the Series 9 is the battery. Being able to track sleep all night and wake up without needing a "panic charge" to get through the workday is a game-changer. The Verdict: 5/5 Stars If you are on the fence about the 49mm size, it is worth the jump. The Black Titanium finish looks incredibly premium, the flat screen is a massive functional upgrade, and if you can find a verifiable mint open-box deal with the factory warranty intact, it is an absolute steal. Review Title: ##### Excelente pantalla y carga rápida, ¡vale totalmente la pena!
Review Content: ##### Excelente pantalla y carga rápida, ¡vale totalmente la pena! He estado usando el Apple Watch Series 7 y la experiencia ha sido fantástica. Lo que más destaca a primera vista es la pantalla: los marcos son superdelgados y se aprovecha muchísimo mejor el espacio en comparación con modelos anteriores. La función de pantalla siempre activa (Always-On) ahora es más brillante en interiores, por lo que se puede ver la hora de un vistazo sin tener que levantar exageradamente el brazo. Otro gran acierto es la carga rápida. Aunque la batería sigue durando un día completo (lo normal en estos relojes), se carga muchísimo más rápido con su cable USB-C incluido; en unos 45 minutos recuperas casi toda la energía. En cuanto a salud, las mediciones de oxígeno en sangre, el sensor de ritmo cardíaco y los electrocardiogramas funcionan de maravilla. Es un reloj resistente (tiene mejor protección contra el polvo y golpes en el cristal) y muy fluido. Si buscas un smartwatch completo, deportivo y elegante, es una compra 10/10. Review Title: My husband has Shokz headphones and I kept borrowing his for my runs and workouts, but he asked me t
Review Content: My husband has Shokz headphones and I kept borrowing his for my runs and workouts, but he asked me to buy my own. I didn't want to pay what Shokz cost, so I tried a few different Shokz knockoffs from Amazon and then kept returning them because they were not even close. These are so much better. These Anker Soundcore have better quality sound than my husband's Shokz. I am incredibly impressed. They feel a bit looser on my ear than the Shokz but they are actually secure and hold up to full workouts, including burpees, and my runs without getting loose or falling off. They are surprisingly comfortable and exceed any expectations I had for performance. They seem well made and like they will hold up over time at least as well as his Shokz. Call quality on these is much better than the Shokz. The mic is clear and the sound is clear. It is great. They charge and store in a proprietary case. The case itself just connects to any USB cord. It holds a charge for 12 hours though so it hasn't been an issue for me. I probably need the case anyway so I don't lose them when I take them off. To connect to the phone for the first time, you do need to download the Soundcore app. It has different equalizers you can choose it you want more bass, more sports, more spoken word, pop vs jazz, and other options. I just left it on the default one because I really like it. You can also customize how you answer the phone, skip to the next song, change volume, etc (1 tap, 2 taps, long hold on right or left ear bud). I just kept the defaults but it is really easy to use and really easy to change at any time. After you use the app the first time to connect, you never have to use it again and they just autoconnect easily when your Bluetooth is on. I like them. I really like the price point too, but even if they cost the same as my husband's Shokz, I'd probably still pick these because the sound is better. You can probably tell I don't borrow his anymore. I can't tell any difference between refurbished and new. The box and all it contents definitely looked new. I would buy these again, and am considering getting another pair to cycle through. Quick pairing, I have several devices that I use them with. Review Title: ##### Spitzenmäßige/r Qualität/Klang - Soundcore V30i Over-Ear-Bluetooth-Kopfhörer (generalüberholt)
Review Content: ##### Spitzenmäßige/r Qualität/Klang - Soundcore V30i Over-Ear-Bluetooth-Kopfhörer (generalüberholt) - absolut problemloses Verbinden mit allen möglichen Geräten (Android und Apple) und einfache App-Konfigurierung (Standard-App von Soundcore/Anker für Bluetooth-Lautsprecher) - wahrscheinlich bestes Preisleistungsverhältnis in dieser Kategorie, wenn man nicht absolut besten HiFi-Sound wie bei Hochpreiskopfhörern braucht; im Vergleich zu No-Name-Geräten für unter 30 € sind diese Hörer um Welten besser mit absolut vollem und natürlichem Klang und guten Bässen, ich behaupte, dass sie sogar mit anderen teureren Marken-Kopfhörern locker mithalten können - optimaler Sitz am Ohr eines Erwachsenen, auch mit Brille, aber nicht für Kleinkinderohren geeignet - optimale Nutzung im Verkehr und bei Spaziergängen oder generell, wenn man seine Umwelt noch hören will oder muss; Nachteil bei allen Over-Ear-Kopfhörern - muss einem beim Kauf bewusst sein: Umweltgeräusche beeinträchtigen den Klang, aber genau dies ist hier gewollt; ansonsten muss unbedingt zu einer anderen Art von Kopfhörer gegriffen werden - scheinbar und leider gibt es die hier nur noch als "generalüberholt", habe sie für ca. 33 € bekommen, was ein bei dieser Qualität unschlagbarer Preis ist; meine Hörer waren sogar originalverpackt und scheinbar noch ganz neu - warum auch immer; daher kann man hier ruhigen Gewissens zugreifen - daher verstehe ich auch nicht, dass diese hier nicht mehr als Neuware angeboten werden; vielleicht aber auch weil sie ein absoluter Verkaufsschlager waren, aber nicht mehr produziert werden, was Anker sich dann noch einmal überlegen sollte - es gibt sicherlich Funktionen, die manchen Leuten fehlen werden, wie ein noch individueller anpassbares Ohrgestänge (Halterung), oder ein noch wertigerer Aufbewahrungs- und Ladebehälter, jedoch ist dies aus meiner Sicht hier nicht notwendig Fazit: absolut überzeugend und damit unbedingte Kaufempfehlung       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))       [Report](javascript:void(0)) Sending feedback...Thanks, we'll investigate in the next few days. Review Title: I bought this phone with the hope that it would work with US Mobile's service, which it does
Review Content: I bought this phone with the hope that it would work with US Mobile's service, which it does. I really like my pooled data plan with them, but I wanted a device on T-Mobile's network, as I have had very good service from a T-Mobile 4G WAP at some rural locations. At my home, neither Verizon nor AT&T work very well as a backup for my Internet service, but T-Mobile has 5G coverage in my area. I had a "Dark Star" SIM that was already activated, and dropped it into this phone. Once the battery was charged, I was able to power the phone on and place phone calls and send text messages. However Internet didn't work, even using Chrome browser on the phone itself. I've already become familiar with adding an APN to other devices, so I followed the instructions from US Mobile's site to add the "Darkstar" APN, and configure it for tethering, which is the main purpose of this device. The disappointing part has nothing to do with this phone, which seems to be working perfectly well. The phone is running on AT&T's network, not T-Mobile. While the service is still poor at my home, I tried it at a few different locations, and found a couple of places nearby where the speedtest.net results were very impressive, with download speeds over 120Mbps and upload speeds over 80Mbps. However, I also found places that were essentially "dead zones" for data, even though the phone still showed a 5G connection. I briefly tried this phone with a US Mobile "Warp" SIM, which connected to Verizon's network. I was able to place a call, send a text message, and connect to the 4G service available here. The speed is similar to another 5G smartphone I have from another reseller. I did not have to make any APN adjustments, it just worked. SUCCESS!!! Took some time, but I am finally on T-Mobile's network (using US Mobile's "Light Speed" network) and now have weak 5G coverage at my home. I have to put the phone in a window to get the 5G service. If I move it to the interior, I get 4G service which is actually slightly faster than Verizon's 4G. A VoIP call while tethered on the 5G network was a bit spotty. My speedtest.net speed is showing 24Mbps down and 3Mbps up with 648ms latency while on 5G and tethered via WiFi. Unlike the "Dark Star" and "Warp" networks, I had a good deal of trouble switching to the "Light Speed" (T-Mobile) network. I did two 1-hour long support chat sessions, but still didn't have phone, sms, nor mms service. By adding the correct APN, I did get Internet service. I inadvertently left the phone on while charging it after the last troubleshooting session. While it was charging, it downloaded a 1.9GB update. I'm not sure what all updated, but the OS updated from Android 11 to Android 12. The phone service started working after the requested reboot. It requested a WiFi connection to complete updating, so I set that up and ran the update option from the Android settings menu. The sms & mms services started working about 20 minutes later. One of the notifications seemed to suggest the carrier initiated the update, but I don't know if that was the OS update, or something else. This phone does seem to work well in the car while tethered via WiFi to my Android radio for Waze maps and YouTube streaming while driving. I haven't done any long trips, but I have gone through areas I know to have poor coverage, and didn't notice any interruptions. I chose the bold red, and it looks fantastic. It's great to have a speaker that not only sounds good but also looks stylish. Overall, the JBL GO3 is a fantastic portable speaker that offers excellent sound quality, durability, and convenience in a compact package. Whether you're at home, on the go, or enjoying the outdoors, this speaker is a reliable companion. I highly recommend it to anyone in need of a high-quality portable audio solution. Review Title: There was some white noise in the ANC and in Transparency mode that definitely was not supposed to b
Review Content: There was some white noise in the ANC and in Transparency mode that definitely was not supposed to be present. There was echoing of my own voice that overpowered outside noises when in transparency mode. I think all the issues with these two modes was from the lack of sealant in the bud itself, that was not sealed properly during cleaning. It also was missing the mesh covers that go on the outside of the earbud to the rubber eartip. Personally the earbuds did hurt my ears after extended periods of use I did not receive any extra ear tips in other sides, I am on the smaller side for ears so it proved to be an issue. The box the Beats were shipped to me in was not the original box, it did not have the instructions or stickers most beats products would come with which isnt an issue for me as I have had their products before and know they are very easy to use and integrate well with apple since they got bought out by them. Overall, not bad buds if it is more “casual” usage. The earbuds came quickly, they sounded fine apart from the mode issues and missing seal, I do wish they fit better. I did notice a bit of grime located on the internal case that didn’t get cleaned fully, and you would need to unseal the lid and unplug some of the internal ribbons to clean it. Pictures are after I wiped down and cleaned the case. There is normal wear and tear like scratches and scuffs on the case from regular use.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Review Title: For my ear type (medium sized, don’t stick out from my head over an inch rounded out, and a bit narr
Review Content: For my ear type (medium sized, don’t stick out from my head over an inch rounded out, and a bit narrow) I do not experience any discomfort. Though at first I did feel a small strain.. They seem to have adjusted slightly to my ear. Despite the fact that Apple now owns Beats... unlike AirPods with their much more efficient magnet method of placing the headphones into the case: you may find a 3 second delay in putting the PowerBeats Pro back in the charging case to begin with... I guess you can say it gives your mind a slight workout haha. But you’ll get used to it. 3 seconds is not too long. I love the button configuration - makes it very easy to change whatever I am listening to, pause, play, and toggle the volume. I also love the look and aesthetic overall. I personally purchased the ivory color and I am very happy with my choice. Some may not have a liking to the size of the charging case which is honestly pretty bulky and about the size of my palm. Though as mentioned in my recommendation, If you get a case you can have the option of having a small carabiner hook which may help some in carrying it around. No scratches, blemishes, or issues at all. A great way to save an extra few coins if you’d like. Along with the fact that naturally... the normal price for the Power Beat Pros are slightly lower than the commonly compared Airpod Pros. As for any device (phone, tablet, laptop) I would recommend getting a case for them. My last AirPods always found a way to get scratched in my bag or from falling. I don’t believe they have a way of tracking hilt into them. If there is I’m unaware of it. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple Powerbeats Pro Totally Wireless & High-Performance Bluetooth Earphone, Ivory (Renewed) : Electronics
Review Content: 1. Not sure if it's just an updated design or if the earpieces were replaced with inferior materials, but these felt thinner and less sturdy than my original pair. The others hugged my ears perfectly after molding the earpiece into place, but these never felt as secure or comfortable. 2. The sensor that detects whether or not it's in your ear does not work well and results in my phone continuously playing through them when I take them out of my ear, and also picking up calls through the buds when I'm not using them, even though they're not supposed to do that when they're out of your ear! 3. After three months, the bluetooth speakerphone, which I loved for making work calls, has completely stopped working. 4. The battery life started out bad and has only gotten worse in the last three months. My old pair would last basically from when I got up in the morning until the end of the work day, so 8-10hrs. These crap out in the middle of the workday, and the battery time gets shorter and shorter. Occasionally, if I'm wearing them but not playing anything through them or talking on the phone, they will just disconnect randomly. I hope I can get some new ones that are the same quality as my old set. But it may just be another unfortunate by-product of the tech industry pushing out more poor quality products for suckers like me to buy. Review Title: Unlike the Apple Studio headphones which are great…but have too many moving parts that make them sus
Review Content: Unlike the Apple Studio headphones which are great…but have too many moving parts that make them susceptible to inevitable damage/malfunction. I’m sure the Powerbeats Pro2 headphones are great, but not $250 great. If you need to know your heart beat rhythm and listen to music like a bat then I guess. I don’t like product that are to tech heavy…These Powerbeats Pro are my third pair. The first pair I broke because I accidental stepped on them . The second pair are still going 3 years strong! If any headphones last more than a year in a half…you got your moneys worth. These head phones work with all my Apple products and really help my work flow. I take all calls hands free and wear these all day. At first the headphones annoyed my ears… a long time ago. Now, my ears feel weird not having them in my ears. Noise cancellation is 7 out of 10. Just experiment with the different ear pieces. No head phones will truly block out sound totally. Product Title: Amazon.com: Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra 5G, US Version, 512GB, Titanium Violet - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: I just received this last night and I'm pretty happy with it so far
Review Content: I just received this last night and I'm pretty happy with it so far. This is the first time buying a refurbished phone or any unlocked phone, so was slightly concerned but it looks good and is working great. The bad, if I want to nitpick: There is one little, maybe 1/8", scratch on the screen that I noted in the picture. It is not at all noticeable when the phone is on and I had to try to even capture it in a photo with the phone off. It sits so low on the screen that I will probably never even feel it during normal operation. The good, everything works and is in great shape other than the tiny scratch. Every function test through the Samsung Members app checks out. The Battery test shows it as "Good" and is down to only 82% today after running it all day with the screen appearance cranked to max so pretty sure that isn't going to be a problem. All buttons feel good with solid response and no visible signs that the screen was removed or replaced. It appears to be a carrier unlocked phone originally with AT&T, gauging from the splash screen. I was able to just put my old Verizon SIM card in and that prompted to switch the carrier software over so now it appears like any other verizon phone on startup. I didn't have any problem with it still being a locked phone and didn't need to contact any carrier to perform the switch over. Data transfer was also easy using Samsung Smart Switch, aside from a lot of photos and music I decided to transfer manually off the old sdcard from the old Note9 because hundreds of gigs is going to take a while. But all apps and data so far appear to have come over seamlessly. I had been looking at the S26 Ultra as well as an upgrade but decided I wasn't ready to give up on a bluetooth S-pen yet. Under $700 taxed and shipped was a pretty good deal for this phone and it is still a very large upgrade from my old phone. I will probably buy another few year old refurbished phone again once this reaches end of life support on updates. Direct Certified was the seller on this and I would recommend. Review Title: The watch seems okay on the outside (no visible issues) and it arrived faster than expected, but I c
Review Content: The watch seems okay on the outside (no visible issues) and it arrived faster than expected, but I cannot pair it with the iphone so I cannot test to make sure it works properly. When I purchased this watch, I never saw any mention of on the product page that the watch must be paired with an iphone 11 or later. It's my mistake for not doing more research before purchasing this watch, but the Rufus AI chat on Amazon's website says the Apple Watch series 11 will pair with iphone xs max. This appears to be incorrect. When the watch did not pair, I wasted a lot of time trying to watch videos on the Amazon website to troubleshoot this, but finally gave up and did an outside search where I learned series 11 watches won't work with iphone xs max. So.... for anyone with an older phone like the xs max, be warned that this watch will not work! I bought this for my elderly mom to track some health concerns. I have a series 9 watch and decided if she didn't like the watch, I'd just take her series 11 watch and sell the series 9. We both have iphone xs max phones so now I need to either return this watch or buy an upgraded phone. I'm so frustrated and disappointed that I couldn't just pair this watch with her phone. I will update this review if I end up keeping it and pairing with a newer phone, but for now, I want to warn others in a similar situation with older iphones. Review Title: In practise, these earbuds connect to my FireTV and when it detects I am asleep it pauses the TV, di
Review Content: In practise, these earbuds connect to my FireTV and when it detects I am asleep it pauses the TV, disconnects bluetooth and goes into a noise cancellation. The battery doesn't last through the night for the noise cancellation but that doesn't matter to me - it's does me enough whereby I wake up fully rested, not disturbed, and I just put the earbuds in the case to charge ready for the next night. Another bonus is that when watching TV, the earbuds at first sound a bit odd - then I realised it was just that I wasn't used to watching TV with earbuds in as it feels so much more intimate. In terms of fitment, there are different wings and tips but I found the smallest foam tip and no wings was best for me - I have woken up once with one fallen out - and I use them every night and also for naps during the day most days. In summary, these earbuds aren't perfect but if mine went faulty I'd buy another pair to be delivered tomorrow - and there aren't many things I say that about (and I'm so pleased I've written a review!) In future I'd want longer battery, better ANC and multi-point pairing - if they did that I'd buy another pair straight away. For now though, I love these. Review Title: This isnt just deceptive advertising (from Amazon renewed) but a public health risk
Review Content: This isnt just deceptive advertising (from Amazon renewed) but a public health risk. The lithium battery warning sticker on the box should have been next to a biohazard warning. Edit: Amazon told me I couldn't post the above review of this product. Well, since writing the review I have purchased a pair of new, clean Bose QC ultra earbuds from a different retailer. Here's my review of the earbuds: The sound quality is remarkable and combined with the noise cancelling it's almost unnerving. The buds themselves are so comfortable it doesn't feel like I am wearing anything (I have smaller, fairly sensitive ears too). Several times I had to take one out just to assure myself I was hearing sound through them and not accidentally blasting surround sound, only to remember I had windows open to traffic noises and a fan on, etc. I found that I needed a combination of sizes of ear plug and ear wing (I don't know the technical terms for the silicone bits). Despite my small ears, I needed a larger ear plug on one side and it made the noise cancelling absolute. The app, and I have other Bose products with poorly performing apps, so I was concerned, worked well. Tip: if you started trying them out before using the app, go ahead and put them back in the case and follow the instructions it gives you pair to Bluetooth, even if you're already paired. That was the only hiccup I found. From there put them on and go through the options, learn and try the gestures. It gives in app demos and training. I read ppl had problems with it shutting off while listening to asmr or meditation, I haven't had that issue. But I have found that side lying with higher noise cancelling gives weird soft techno-noise feedback because of the pillow on the anc sensors. A few said the "floor" (sound of noise cancelling without audio) had a hum-- try other ear plug sizes and create a custom "mode" and adjust the noise cancelling to a level without any floor hum. Also make sure hair or head coverings aren't brushing against the earbuds if you're getting weird anc sounds. So far I am very happy with my new /clean/ Bose QC ultra earbuds. I highly recommend them for ppl who need the quiet in noisy environments and/or who want to be immersed in soundscape/music/ cinematic settings. Just don't order from Amazon renewed. Review Title: I purchased this phone as both renewed and unlocked
Review Content: I purchased this phone as both renewed and unlocked. The condition was excellent with no scratches or mars that I could tell. There were no issues switching from my old phone to this phone with my carrier (Visible) using my carrier's website, and this did not require speaking with anyone from my carrier. I'm pleased with the eSIM. The phone already had a screen protector. If I had known I probably wouldn't have purchased a screen protector. I like the looks of the phone. The camera bar on the back looks good to me (better than multiple lenses in a square or circle like many other phones). I'm not worried about scratching the lens as I would be with the other phones. It doesn't rock when placed on a flat surface. I like the color. Mine's old bay (similar to a periwinkle blue). I'm familiar with the Android UI, but I'm still getting used to Pixel's UI. On my old phone (another Android) it was easier to close all open programs. Also, I liked the way apps appeared when grouped together a little more on my old phone. With Pixel you have to keep swiping all the way to the left (past all the open apps) to get to Clear All. With Pixel you cannot see beyond the 4th app in a group, at least (to my knowledge) not without a separate app to organize your apps. This could be a good thing if you don't want an app to be obvious to shoulder surfers. I like having the fingerprint reader on the screen. The 3-button controls are also on the screen. I'm thrilled not to have all the bloatware I had with my old phone. I really resented my old phone manufacturer for preventing me from removing its preinstalled apps. It charges a bit slow (about 2 hours for full charge). I'd say the ability to hold and use a charge is good but not outstanding. I'm going to have to charge it daily. The display is bright and clear. Some reviewers have commented about the bezel being large, but I barely notice it. I prefer the plastic (8a) to a glass back. I think it looks good. I put mine in a case, so it appears just as shiny as a glass-backed phone would. The case does make it a bit harder to utilize the double-tap the back feature. The phone is fast, but I hear the Tensor processor isn't as fast as Snapdragon 8. I don't expect it'll be an issue for me. I'm not looking to run games in HD at 60+ fps. Photos are excellent. I like the quick flip gesture that switches between rear and front camera and the selfie illumination (screen turns white to shine light on your face) for selfies. Review Title: Well clearly, I was not satisfied to receive a phone with a significantly degraded battery
Review Content: Well clearly, I was not satisfied to receive a phone with a significantly degraded battery. So, I called Amazon Customer service to explain the problem and request a replacement. I did this on the same day I received the phone. The representative was helpful and told me he would send out a replacement immediately, and even upgrade the shipment method for no extra charge. He also told me, both in conversation and in writing to “use the box the replacement comes in to return the original.” That way, I would not be without a phone while waiting for the replacement to arrive. The day the replacement was scheduled to arrive and but had not, I called Amazon customer service back to inquire about the status. Much to my surprise, I was told the replacement phone order had been cancelled by the third-party seller because the original had not been returned. This irritated me for two reasons: (1) I had never been notified the replacement order had been cancelled—apparently, had I not called Amazon was simply going to drop the issue, and (2) I was specifically told by Amazon Customer Service that I did not need to return the original until the replacement was received. I told the agent this was unacceptable and wanted the replacement sent to me, as had been previously arranged. When it became clear that she would not be able to help me, I asked to speak with her manager. After providing her with my phone number, she said her manager would call me back. That phone call never happened. The following day I called Amazon customer service again, now the third time trying to get this issue resolved. I explained the steps I had taken thus far and was put on hold so the representative could verify if my replacement order “was legit.” When I asked what “legit” meant, she said she needed to verify if this was unusual activity on the account because it was a phone purchase. I told her that of course it was legit, as I had email documentation regarding the entire process! After being on hold, she came back and told me the replacement phone would be delivered within 5 days. She also said she would personally call me on that day to verify that it was received. I asked her to clarify that I would receive the replacement first, prior to sending the original back, according to the instructions I had previously received via email. She looked up that email and saw it said: “Please feel free to use the box the replacement comes in to return the original…” After reading that she placed me on hold again. After a minute or so, she came back on the line and asked if she could place me on hold for an additional few minutes. I asked why. She said she was trying to find out what went wrong with the first replacement order. When she came back on the line, she told me “to be on the safe side” I should return the original defective phone first to receive a replacement. I reiterated that this was unacceptable and that I had held up my end of the bargain and done exactly as Amazon had told me to do. I wanted the replacement sent first before I returned the defective phone. She said the email I received was in error and the person who sent it made a mistake—the defective phone would need to be returned before the replacement is shipped out. I told her that while I understand that people make mistakes, I did not think I should be penalized (i.e., be without a phone for at least 5 days) for a mistake that Amazon made. She apologized for the mistake but made it clear that I would not receive a replacement until the original was returned. I informed her I would be writing a negative review. To summarize: I was sent a defective phone, was given incorrect information about how to replace it, had the replacement order silently cancelled without being notified, and Amazon refused to follow through on the terms of their agreement. One star.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Product Title: Amazon.com: Samsung Galaxy S20+ 5G, 128GB, Cosmic Black - Fully Unlocked (Renewed), S20+ Plus 5G : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: Mine was a refurbushed model, not a single scratch on it, looks brand new & no issues when i turned
Review Content: Mine was a refurbushed model, not a single scratch on it, looks brand new & no issues when i turned it on the first time & no issues since then. Yes, it did NOT come with the Samsung box, Samsung cable & usb wall charger. I personally do not care! due to i have a box full of samsung usb cables and wall chargers from my old Samsung phones i bought before. It did come with the tool to remove the sd & sim card & that is the only thing i needed. I had no intent & plan of upgrading my samsung s10+ to the samsung s20+. But at the price and buying prior refurbished samsung i am beyond happy i did it! First, The 5G is very quick & compare to older version what ever its called. which i did not believe until i went online away from my house WIFI service and its very quick. Note: not areas have 5G service. The overall phone response is very quick and smooth. The bixy button is gone (thankgod). The quality of the screen resolution is outstanding & wow its clear! It has a few more minor whistles & bells features compare to the samsung s10+ Nothing to noticable. I do like the new front camera location and its small size & its looks better. I also like you see less of the frame around the curved screen. I know & dont care if there is a technocal name for it. Overall the phone looks great & i didnt get a case this time due to i think looks better with out one. I know, but i rarely & never drop my phone (my s10+ back up) Reference to the camera & quality of the picture which was not a selling point for me. You will notice a much better picture & video quality. The phone over all is a tad thinner & tad taller which i think it makes it easier to hold and use. The battery life seems to be better but i have not fully tested it yet. Charging it seems to be quicker & again i have not fully tested it against my s10+. Now, is the samsung s20+ worth buying if you already have a s10 & s10+??? I love my s10+ its great phone! The only reason i got the s20+ was the price $700. But if you can afford one (full price) or find one at great price like i did then YES get one!!!! I could have lived very happy with my s10+ with no regrets if i didnt see this s20+ on amazon! Review Title: Not the issue here so far
Review Content: Not the issue here so far. Tested every feature that I would actually use and it runs smoothly and quickly. From a full charge in the morning before I go to work, and with moderate usage throughout the day, it is generally down to about 80% by the time I go to bed (usually between 1:30 and 2:00am). I am upgrading from a much earlier model Galaxy and the camera (both still and video) quality is spectacular comparatively. Particularly in low light. Verizon SIM card transferred over without issues and that Samsung transfer app was a God send for getting all of my stuff (including pix, wifi passes, etc.....) over to the new phone. The lack of an SD slot makes me a bit nervous, but this one is the 256 gig model so hopefully, I won't have to do much relocating of files, images and videos over to my PC with the space that there is on here. Physically, the phone was in pretty good shape. Though there were a few minor scuffs on the back, the glass for the screen AND the camera lenses were flawless. And, I always use a case/holster anyway, way back since the old flip phone days. So, I will never actually SEE the body of the phone anyway. All in all, up to this point, I feel like the investment was good. There is 90 days worth of warranty so if I stumble across something that is a deal breaker, I can return it. If you are looking for a phone that won't cost as much as a cheap automobile, this "renewed" option may be something you can look in to. I will be trying it again when it is time to make another upgrade. Review Title: This 3rd phone though is excellent so far
Review Content: This 3rd phone though is excellent so far. Condition, I would say is practically new. Case and Screen were blemish free, not even signs of fingerprints. The phone is Verizon branded, but does not impact phone service or use. It is unlocked and work with my Tracfone sim through T-Mobile. Testing battery life, but it seems close to normal after a few years of use. Used it all day and I still had 25% battery remaining with really heavy use. Data transfer went flawlessly with no hick ups, very easy and straight forward. Even the sim was immediately recognized without having to call the carrier. Everything seems to be in good working order. The person who owned this phone 1st really took care of it, you can tell. Other than the branding issue on start up and a notification telling me my sim is not a Verizon sim, everything seems to be in good working order. This is an upgrade for me coming from am Galaxy A20s. The upgrade was immediately noticed. And 256gb memory is just enough for me. I carry books, music and movies in my phone and this has handled everything I have thrown at it without issue. The camera is great and takes amazing photos compared to my last phone. Buying through Amazon renewed is a crap shoot really, it depends on the last user(s) and what may have happened to the phone, I can imagine the phone's people are turning in. I'm sure most have issue from over use and drops, to phone malfunctions in general. And from studying the vendors who sell the phones you really have no idea what they might do with them once they are rehabbed, Water damage, electronic issues, even screen replacements. All the phone are going through private phone companies who refurb them and send them back out. Like I said, 3rd times the charm and I lucked up on what I think is an excellent buy. Would I do again, sure, but make sure to check out the phone thoroughly during your 90-day return window. I will continue to test out and report back if any issues popped up. But so far so good. Check the vendor rating and issues reported in reviews. Typically, they spell out possible issues with phones or vendors selling them. I have always believed in recycling items, especially electronics. So do your part and make sure they don't end up in landfill somewhere. I have liked Samsung products for years and this still holds true with this phone. I don't need the latest and greatest, but I know I have a few years still before a newer model takes it's place. Furthermore, I usually hold on to a phone for 2–3 yrs, depends on the phone. Oh yeah, 5G is the hits. Very smooth and fast, no delays when surfing the web, everything just flows like a hardwired home system. 120 mhz is smooth and haven't noticed any hang-ups. Yes, I would buy again through Amazon renewed. But I'm sure you could find the same product locally at your local phone store. I'm happy with purchase and would recommend with caveats. Check your phone carefully, run it through is paces and test everything, camera, sound, display and any function you think is important and even those you might not think is important. test all settings and make sure all your setting take effect. This phone is loaded with options and it took about 3 hrs to transfer and update this phone once I started things up. Gaming is great, and the display is amazing. No glitches during game play. It's almost to fast that I can't keep up visually. So two thumbs up on buy. Finally moving like most with an upgraded phone. Review Title: This phone has a vibrant screen and has a great camera
Review Content: This phone has a vibrant screen and has a great camera. The touch screen is responsive. I do like the fact it identifies likely scam callers. Now I need to figure out how to tell the phone to automatically ignore likely scam callers. The eye comfort setting is nice and easy on the eyes in my room at night. The 256 internal storage makes up for the lack of internal storage. This has many ways of identifying you by using a pin, figure print, and or face recognition. These are strong pluses for the phone. There are features that I like, but some of the basics can improve. It is missing a headphone jack so good luck finding an adaptor that allows you to talk on a headset and charge your phone at the same time. It takes a few attempts to unlock my phone using my figure print. The battery drains really fast, and I leave my phone on the charger most of the day. One time while at the gym, the volume level was constantly changing when I was at the gym using my headphones to listen to music and playing a game. The headphones would be blasting and hurting my ears, and after adjusting the volume, it would either go up again or go down to a whisper. I wonder why the phone gets hot near the camera area. Getting hot for no reason is not a good sign of reliability. Hope this phone lasts. It took me a while to find a good switch that allows me to charge the phone and talk in a zoom meeting. I Hope Samsung releases a fix that addresses the erratic volume and getting hot for no reason. I really like the responsiveness of the phone hope this phone is a good investment. Review Content: 1. The photo quality is comparable to or maybe better than the pixel 3a in my opinion (I'm not really an expert here)- the pictures look crisp and detailed which is important to me as mostly I take my kids pictures with my phone. 2. The battery life of this phone is much better. It can last me the whole day. At 10 pm I still have 30% battery and I was on my phone a lot- mostly browsing but did watch a little youtube also. 3. Screen size is bigger on this phone- if you are looking to put it in a pocket this may be a bit big. Since I carry it in my purse I don't mind, and I kind of enjoy the big screen for my youtube habit. Picture quality when watching video seems superior also. 4. Bloatware apps- annoying. The pixel definitely felt way cleaner out of the gate. On this phone I had to delete a lot of apps and then disable or hide away in folders others that can't be deleted. In the end it's not a dealbreaker for me, but it created some pain in the initial setup of the phone. 5. This phone has facial recognition, but it hasn't been working that great for me. I will probably try to go in and redo it and see if it improves at all. It would be nice if it worked- but mostly I am using the fingerprint sensor. I actually preferred the physical fingerprint sensor on the back of the pixel because it worked consistently, and the one built into the screen on this phone seems a bit finnicky. Overall this one has more "advanced" unlock features but I preferred the reliability on the pixel. I know this comparison is only so good because Pixel already has a 4a and soon a 5a, but maybe it will help someone. Overall I am happy because I got a nice camera, great battery life, and nice video quality on a mid range phone. The Amazon renewed phone had no defects at all that I could tell. I don't think the charger with it was original, but it was certainly worth the savings for the renewed price. One more tip- I hated the Samsung keyboard for some reason. So I downloaded the google Gboard on it which made me much happier. Review Title: I ordered the Ultra 2 when it had a little markdown for Black Friday
Review Content: I ordered the Ultra 2 when it had a little markdown for Black Friday. I was worried about what I would find when I opened the package. I was afraid it would look used and have a flimsy band or that the buttons would not work properly or maybe the battery would be showing some age. I started to feel some buyers remorse and the watch had not even arrived yet. When the FedEx truck pulled up, I was floored by how quick the package arrived. The box was in great shape and somewhat similar to apple packaging. As I opened the package and started unboxing everything, my fears started melting away. The watch was properly wrapped and included a very nice, durable charging cable. The watch band does not feel like a cheap knockoff. It might be genuine for all I know. It feels rugged yet very comfortable and I even wear it when I sleep. I fully charged the watch before wearing it. I checked the battery health and it shows 100%. Wow! This watch is in excellent, like new condition. I am super happy that I made this purchase. The battery life is terrific. The sleep tracking seems to be accurate. I have customized the watch face to inform me of everything that I wanted to see. I could not be more pleased. I think you’ll be happy too. Review Title: So I got the device a month ago
Review Content: So I got the device a month ago. And the advise I want to give to new buyers is to buy from a reputable seller and it should be "shipped by Amazon" to eliminate all inconveniences. So how was the phone? Quality wise, it's exactly what I ordered. Excellent Condition and Like New. Yes there's some scratches on the back and a couple on the screen but honestly, you would even notice it unless it's being faced with harsh sunlight. For the phone itself, it's good. Battery: really good when you use wifi but average when you're always in data. It warms up sometimes when using data Camera: really good, exactly what you would expect from a pixel. My only problem is it's intense on HDR😂 Display: I like the 90hz it's smooth but I'm not really impressed considering I cam from a Samsung. Don't let that discourage you tho because Samsung is hard to beat when it comes to displays. Even the mid-rangers can compete with flagships. Speaker: Not loud enough for my liking. But I do like the front firing speakers. Fingerprint sensor: it's actually not bad. Unlike how people here describe it😂 maybe update it to Android 13 because a lot of bugs get squashed. Overall, I enjoy and love this phone, especially the Camera. But I have to say there's some things that I miss from Samsung. But no regrets here😄. And lastly, a big thanks to Chubbiestech for being super reliable, I highly recommend this seller. Review Title: Both phones looked brand new
Review Content: Both phones looked brand new. Not even a hint that it was renewed. There is so much to say about this phone but there isn't enough space to write it. Nice glass - front: Gorilla Glass Victus back: Gorilla Glass 6 Has a built in Google Tensor chip. One thing you can do with that is download a language and you have live translate built in without being online. When you wake up it goes through a Google Assistant Routine, time, weather, news + It does take a day to learn how to navigate the screens but it's worth sticking to it. Double tap the back of the phone with one finger and it brings up your chosen app. There are dozens of reasons to buy this phone that I don't have text room to say. The camera is quite good and the night shots show up like you are in daylight. There are 2 versions of the Google Pixel 6 128GB storage, 256GB storage. This is the 128GB storage phone. I bought a 512GB sd card but you can't use it - no sd card slot. So now, I can't put movies or a lot of songs on the phone. I'm going to look for a USB C OTG adapter and see if I can get my 512GB sd card to show up. Other than the storage issue, this is a great phone and I'm glad I got it. Product Title: Amazon.com: Samsung Galaxy A23 5G, 64GB, Black - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: ##### This Verizon 5G UW Version Only Has Two Cases Available!
Review Content: ##### This Verizon 5G UW Version Only Has Two Cases Available! As a cellphone, this Galaxy A23 5G UW is fantastic. It is an awesome upgrade from a 2014 Galaxy S5. It has great reception, reliable connection to Verizon's network, plus a headphone jack and a microSD card slot that it shares with the SIM card. It currently has a 32 GB microSD card installed, loaded with 13 GB's of mp3's, plus 5 GB's of GPS map data for the HEREWeGo GPS app. No issues whatsoever. There is one niggle to report, however - cases, or the lack thereof. There are actually two versions of the Galaxy A23 - the regular 5G version and this Verizon specific 5G UW version. The UW is so named because it supports Verizon's Ultra Wideband 5G, also known as millimeter wave 5G and C-band 5G on bands N260, 2N61 and N77, in addition to standard 5G on band N78. This necessitates some internal differences that led to a slight change in position of the Volume and Power button. They are about 3/16" lower on this 5G UW version. In practical terms, this means that all of the hundreds of Galaxy A23 5G phone cases that you see listed will NOT function on this version. They will fit, but the case buttons will not work because they do not line up with the buttons on the phone. There are only two cases that actually work and both are thirty bucks: one from Otterbox, search for ASIN B0BVGWGBL4 , and the Itskins - Hybridr Solid Case for Samsung Galaxy A23 5G Uw - Purple and Transparent. That's it. The Otterbox only comes in black and the Itskins in purple and transparent. 11/13/2024 Update Just purchased a second one for myself since my own 2014 Galaxy S5 is starting to lose service in more areas due to 4G LTE frequencies being repurposed for 5G. Activated without issue on Page Plus Cellular, which is now a Verizon owned MVNO. Now have signal pretty much everywhere, both 5G and 4G LTE. The Samsung One UI interface is snappy, with no lag perceptible. This second unit came updated to Android 14 and One UI 6.0. The first one is running Android 13 and One UI 5.1. I was able to copy over all of my data via the Samsung SmartSwitch app, no problem. I also moved over the 64 GB microSD card from my Galaxy S5 to this Galaxy A23 without difficulty, which saved a ton of transfer time for my music mp3's. 05/22/2025 Update I wanted to add that contrary to another review, the A23 5G UW does have NFC. I've included a picture of the pull down shade showing its icon - it's the third button from the left. I use it with my YubiKey 5 NFC security key to store and access OTP's and Passkey's; although there is an issue with the Yubico Authenticator app not being able to access the camera for some reason. This makes it impossible to use this phone to add a new account to the YubiKey via QR code, though you can still input the key manually. However, there is no problem reading the YubiKey 5 via NFC - just hold the key against the back of the phone, next to the camera island. I also added a picture of the phone in the Otterbox case, to illustrate the the button alignment issue with standard A23 5G phone cases. Review Title: Needless to say, there is absolutely nothing rugged about this phone
Review Content: Needless to say, there is absolutely nothing rugged about this phone. Its basically a 2010s smartphone design. Lots of plastic (that is marketed as rugged). Its almost an old Galaxy SII in build quality. Similar to a 2010 Android phone, battery life is atrocious. On a normal day with about 20% light usage (emails, 4-6 short phone calls, occasionally a couple YouTube videos) I get about 6-8hrs from 100% charge to 10% and a red battery bar. I initially thought I had a bad battery and ordered a brand new one, only to end up with identical results. Its filled with Samsung/Verizon crap bloatware and an OS that replaces perfectly useful Android apps (clock, Digital Wellbeing, etc) with way less functional Samsung versions for absolutely zero reason. If you're using it as an unlocked (cue: other than Verizon) phone, you also get constant popups telling you that you're not using a Verizon SIM card (duh). Annoyingly, these can't be disabled. GPS also died on mine after a couple months - so there's that. The USB port - which is covered on most rugged phones - is fully exposed on this one. Every time the humidity goes above 60% I get inundated with moisture alerts that disable charging. This thing is absolute garbage. If you're looking to spend whatever money this costs at the time you're reading this, consider just throwing it in a toaster. Review Content: however the screen has momentary flashes of lines going across vertically halfway through the screen from time to time it's not so often that it's unusable you can watch a whole movie and you wouldn't see it probably happens once a day or twice a day definitely some screen driver circuitry damage the Samsung Galaxy X cover 6 Pro was purchased as "renewed" I was expecting a returned or open box unit. Headphone jack is at the top which is very nice running Samsung's oneUI skin with Android 12 definitely a improvement over Android 10. edit update: no changes have occurred phone is operating as expected the momentary flashes persist but have not increased in occurrence they don't bother me. strangely does not occur in landscape mode for like viewing videos or photos, I've noticed. the vertical lines only appear when I'm in portrait mode in any situation. Battery life is well hasn't gotten any better I'm planning on buying a new battery since it is replaceable so that's not something I'm going to take a star off since well you can improve the situation at your own peril it's not like it's a permanently installed battery like other undesirable modern smartphones.
