Review Title: These are exactly what I have been looking for in a Bluetooth wireless earbud
Review Content: These are exactly what I have been looking for in a Bluetooth wireless earbud. There’s an app you need to download to your device and it has some really great features. You can customize your own settings. There are a few different “modes” you can save a preset for such as travel, relaxation, and focus. There also built in nature sounds you can listen to in the event you just want to relax but not listen to music and not hear background noise. There’s also a great feature that allows you to turn on/off background noise. I.E. you want to go for a run on the street, you can allow background noise filter through while listening to music so you can hear cars approaching or other noises in the area. Both buds work independently. You can wear one or both for phone calls and music. Phone calls do come in in stereo, unlike other top tier earbuds that only allow calls in one ear or the other. I saved some money and bought the “refurbished” or “repackaged” version. I was skeptical in doing so, but everything showed looking like it had never been touched. I highly recommend this purchase. Review Title: The inherent features paired with the features "unlocked" by using the app are awesome
Review Content: The inherent features paired with the features "unlocked" by using the app are awesome. It's not overly complex to be confusing or annoying, I basically setup the EQ once when I first installed it, and never had to mess with it again. The "Hear Through" feature is awesome--though realistically it's only partially useful, in that it allows me to hear outside noises enough to know that someone's talking to me, but since I'm listening to something else, I still can't hear them. But the buds detect when one is no longer in proximity to the other and auto pause your media when you take one out to talk to someone, which is awesome. Until you forget and take the other one out and hold them in your hand, not realizing that the buds are in range of each other and started playing again. BUT, having the Hear Through on is better than being absolutely deaf to the world, regardless. The App has different "profiles", or Moments, as they call them, which is nice, though I wish you could customize them more or create your own, but realistically I've not needed more than the three given, just to have one with Hear Through on and one with Hear Through off -- and since they can be swapped through the notification area on your phone, you don't even have to unlock your phone in order to enable/disable the feature. I received these exactly a month ago today and at first I tried to make an effort to use them as much as possible, now it's just second nature to take them everywhere I go. I've not really had many connection issues--or, many bad ones. The only issues I tend to have are when my phone is in my left pocket (which is where I normally keep it), when doing work and moving around/bending down, a lot. It seems that my body (which isn't a large one, mind you) causes some connection issues, but it's a brief stutter at best. Moving my phone to my right side--even in the back pocket--eliminates this entirely, since the right bud is the "Master". But if I'm just walking around, it's never been an issue. What surprised me the most is when I took them out of their case and they reported that they were Connected, my phone's Bluetooth was off, and then my wife's music started playing--and she was in the back yard! It's definitely not a problem to have your phone across the room - in fact it seems to help some of the random "body meat-related" connection stutters. Overall I simply love these earbuds and would absolutely recommend them to anyone looking for a good truly wireless earbud. Review Title: (I probably differ from the way others evaluate comfort
Review Content: (I probably differ from the way others evaluate comfort.) Airpods can at first seem very comfortable, but I always have the uncomfortable feeling that they are going to fall out, so walking around like a book is on your head or something is uncomfortable for me. The Jabra units provide a degree of comfort in that they are secure and I have confidence that I could do a cartwheel, and they won’t fall out. To some that may be an "uncomfortable feeling" ... to me, that itself plays into what I call comfortable. But, no, they do not "hurt", I’ve worn them in the office for 3 hours straight - and they don’t “hurt my ears”. The Hear-Though functionality is not perfect, there’s a pretty loud hiss accompanied with the amplification. One can always hear ambient noise if not playing music, but the muffled outside world from the ear-plug effect is good enough such that you do not hear ambient noise during playback. This is great for sitting on the couch to listen to a podcast or youtube while my wife is wanting to watching TV. The TV is not heard during the podcast experience. They do not fall out, (Apple Airpods fall out easily for me). These connect/disconnect quickly from Bluetooth settings on devices. YouTube vids on MacBook Pro suffer 1 second "skips-outs" of sound - but only when 2 devices are simultaneoulsy connected. No skip-outs when only 1 device is connected. But these is no lag, or latency during the playback of YouTube videos ... just these random second-long skip-outs of the Audio. It’s enough to be annoying. Also, I hear: "Divice disconnected ... two devices connected ..." at times. This has nothing to do with the item above, it’s less frequent. Hear-Through works, but you also have amplified static hiss which you would not normally hear. (1) When I double press on the right ear bud, (hear-through toggle off/on). the app's hear though switch doesnt follow. (Pretty minor issue, but noticed.) (2) The equalizer has no effect at all. None. I’m using iPhone Xs Max, iOS.

Review Title: Now, lets talk about sound quality
Review Content: Now, lets talk about sound quality. I love the app that Jabra offers, which I am able to adjust the sound settings to my preference. Loving bass, I attempted to see how hard it could kick, and I was very impressed with their range of sound. The HearThrough setting works really well actually, sometimes I wonder if I should replace my grandpa's hearing aids with these. But really, I go out on a run with my dog and I can hear when cars are coming by, and if someone stops to ask to pet her I'm not caught off guard. The sound quality for phone calls lacks a little bit. I have found that the person on the other end of my calls can't make out what I am saying because it picks up all of the extra background sound. Overall, this aspect could use some work as others have mentioned it as oversensitive. Sorry, but I have another critique, and it has to do with the Voice Assistant. Maybe it is just iPhone users, but when I push my right ear bud for Siri it takes about 2 or 3 seconds to start listening. I get frustrated at that point and just type what I wanted to ask. Not a big issue since I don't use the feature often, but it would be nice to have it working well. Some people have touched on how these buds fit in their ears, but I really like the fit. Nothing frustrates me more than buying an awesome piece of technology just to find out it doesn't fit right for me. But, these slide right in the ear without any work, and the design helps you easily understand how they should look and fit in your ear. Overall, these Jabra true wireless buds are a solid choice for connectivity strength, sound quality, and great battery life. Review Title: The earbuds fit snuggly without being uncomfortable, and they remain in place with high confidence t
Review Content: The earbuds fit snuggly without being uncomfortable, and they remain in place with high confidence that they won't come out during the daily commute, or bimbling around the office, though I would not trust them on a workout. Good incoming call quality, acceptable outgoing and reasonable though imperfect reduction of wind noise. Fantastic for podcasts, these are perfectly decent for music. It has run a week without charging the 'base' with a total time of over 12 hours, so I believe the 15 expected, at least so far. - Bluetooth: if the phone is in my left jacket pocket, the sound cuts out periodically whilst walking ... seems there is a specific issue with that for my personal use case. Moving the phone to *anywhere* else resolves it. - Video: somewhat noticeable lag between lips and sound, presumably an overhead of bluetooth as I have not had a bluetooth headset that does not do this. Not a cheap purchase, but I use them so much now that I can heartily recommend these, even at this price. Review Title: So, what is it like going to Samsung after so long?
Review Content: So, what is it like going to Samsung after so long? Back in the day, only Apple rivaled Samsung when it came to the best hardware. Samsung can no longer make that claim. Granted, this phone is excellent, but OnePlus, LG, and Apple are all on the same level in terms of quality build. This phone feels heavy in your hand. I personally like that, but someone coming from an Apple might be very disappointed. Going light weight was not a big consideration here. It seems like they were more focused on packing as much as possible into this phone. That leads to a big issue. Samsung has been cowed into trying to be like Apple and removed both the headphones jack and sd card slot. I see no real reason for this beyond saving money. Apple and Samsung claim that they can’t fit it in, or that no one uses them anymore. Both of those are nothing but lame excuse. Both LG and Sony put both items into their last flagships. LG in fact released HD audio to go with the headphones jack. After using both phones, I REALLY miss both those items. They added a huge amount of functionality and made doing certain things so much easier. They did add the latest and greatest 5G and Wifi connectivity to this phone. That sounds great, but I haven’t noticed it all. I even live in an area where 5G is everywhere. There might be more speed, but everything in my area was already fast. It’s hard to really notice a difference unless you are running a speed test. So, this phone is S-Pen compatible. Great. It would be really good if it actually came with an S-Pen, but you’ll have to pay more for that. By more I mean $40 for an s-pen designed for the Ultra, that is missing some functionality. That’s right, you can’t do gestures. If that’s important to you, you need to wait for the S-Pen Pro to be released “later” in 2021. That one will have a BT connection. That really seems like a fumble on Samsung’s part. I can understand making the s-pen optional and not having a silo for it, like on the Note, but not having the full-blown version available at launch feels like they are missing an opportunity. If people get the regular s-pen, decide they don’t use it, what’s to motivate them into getting the pro version? The S-pen can be handy, but it only makes sense if you get a case that can hold. Thankfully Spigen makes one that is cheap and works well. On the plus side, this phone has the fastest, most accurate fingerprint reader I’ve ever used. It’s easily twice as fast as the one LG was using. The ultrasonic format really makes a difference. When I first used the Huawei P20 Pro, I was blown away by how good that camera was. The things it did were unprecedented in a camera phone. I used a number of phones after that one, and none of them ever matched what Huawei could pull off. Samsung crushed it with this camera setup. The flexibility it offers is unmatched. From wide angle to super zoom, it’s all there. Some of the tricks they pull off with this camera are truly impressive. From how it combines photos for optimal exposure to the foolish 100x superzoom, the things you can do with this camera are insane. The 100x is nothing you’ll want to use a lot. It’s usable, but not overly clear. Still, the mere fact that you can take a usable 100x photo with this phone is mind blowing. When I say “usable” I mean a photo that is identifiable. It’s nothing I’m going to want to hang on a wall, but it might help trying to identify something. If there is one thing camera doesn’t do great, it’s exposure. It tends to over expose, but that’s it. That’s the only real issue I can find and it’s minor. You might see the 108MP sensor and think you can take some insane RAW photos with that. To a degree, that’s true, but with a sensor like that, you’d need a HUGE amount of light to be able to get good results. There is a reason why Samsung does pixel binning to get its incredible results. On its own 108MP in a sensor that size is not really usable, except in ideal conditions. I love a good wide-angle camera. LG was always a proponent of the wide-angle, and over the years, it’s really come in handy. It’s not something you use a lot, but when you need it, nothing beats it. You get two tele-photo lenses here. The 3X is great for framing your photos, and the 10x allows you to do things that no over phone I’ve ever used has allowed. The 10x really comes in handy for sunsets and times when you can’t get close to your subject. I usually don’t do a write up on charging, but in this case, I think it’s needed. You have wired 25W or wireless 10W. I love that flexibility. It’s not all good though. You know what really stinks? Paying through the nose for a phone, opening the box, and not getting a charger. That’s right. No charger in the box. If you want one, you’ll be paying for it. It’s hard to wrap your head around the fact that they charge you over $1,000, but couldn’t give you a charger. I can’t remember the last time I got a phone with no charger. Till now, OnePlus had the best screen I’d seen in a phone. It makes sense that Samsung would beat them, considering OnePlus got their screens from Samsung. This screen is amazing. It’s not just it’s looks either. They did some impressive trickery here too. The adaptive refresh is amazing. The big issue with a 120 refresh rate is the battery it burns through. With adaptive turned on, it adjusts. Reading a book or something similar – it drops as low as 10. This saves a huge amount of battery life. It’s good. It’s not LG V60 good, but it’s good. There have been times when the LG V60 lasted me for two days with normal use. This one has the same battery, but doesn’t last that long. It will easily make it through the day and night though. Welcome to the worst part about this phone. I know why Samsung doesn’t fix it too. To be honest, I hate the Samsung apps, I hate the excessive bloatware, and Bixby is the worst virtual assistant I’ve ever used. The UI is the more frustrating of the issues here. The main reason is tied to the fact that this is an Android phone. Why do you want to be so different from stock when it’s actually hindering the experience instead of improving it? I understand what Samsung is trying to do. They want to be Apple. They want their own ecosystem, they control, and reap large profits off of. That’s why they have their own assistant, apps, and UI. I’d applaud them for that, if they grow a pair and divorce Android. The only way all the apps, bloatware, assistant, and UI make sense if they are on their own. Just do it already. Become the third option, because as it stands now, your software is awful. It’s trying to sit on a fence, which means it’s not as good as it could be on its own, and it’s NO WHERE as good as stock Android. Now, if you are a handy when it comes to Android, you can remove a lot of the junk off this phone, via ADB. But, stop and think about that for a moment. You just paid top dollar for a phone, and now, you have to waste a solid hour of your time stripping off all the garbage they piled on there. How is that acceptable? If this phone was running software close to stock and didn’t have the bloatware issue, we’d be talking about a legendary phone. One of the best phones ever made. Instead, we have some of the best hardware ever combined in a phone, with steaming pile of dung laid on top of it. Again, if Samsung finally broke free of Android, I think things would be very different. They might also be watching Huawei very closely to see how everything pans out for them. Huawei was forced off Android and now runs its own OS and ecosystem. If it goes well for Huawei, I would not be surprised to see Samsung finally pull the trigger. They already have the OS. It’s been in their Smart appliances for years. I know I’ve bashed Samsung a lot here, but there are some things that do that are excellent. The first one I’ll mention is something that falls into the useful category. It’s their side tabs. The default is your recent apps or apps you’ve pinned. This comes in handy since I don’t like either of Samsung’s default launcher options. You can also add more tabs like weather and select contacts. I first used this with the S6 Edge and I’m glad it’s still around. Now for the thing that Samsung does best, and by best, I mean no one is even close. A deep dive into the sound settings will take you to an EQ setting. This is not impressive on its own, since most other makers offer this. What Samsung does that no one else does, is it gives you a hearing test and creates a custom sound profile for you. As someone who has hearing loss, the impact this has is incredible. The only thing I don’t understand is why it’s so buried. I mean you need to dig to find this thing. I find it rather ironic that Samsung is more on board with Windows integration than any other maker I’ve used. Samsung imbedded the features needed and allows you to use apps in Windows. The others I’ve used require you to download an app and you cannot use apps in Windows. This is a handy feature to have for anyone using an Windows PC. They also support the cut and paste feature. Copy on your phone – paste on your PC and vice versa. I have to relate one final frustrating issue with Samsung’s software. The last three phones I used all were on board with Google’s autofill for apps. That made signing into a new phone an easy experience. Samsung has its own thing. I spent quite a while hunting down passwords that I hadn’t used in nearly two years. There is a factor to consider, if you’ve only used Apple or Samsung products. You’ve been spoiled. By buying the most popular phones, you’ve always had a massive selection of cases and accessories. As someone who’s been using the fringe players for years, I’ve been stuck with only a few choices when it comes to cases. Sometimes it was very difficult to find cases, or I had to pay more than I would have liked. Having a massive selection does add to the value, since you end up paying less for cases as everyone tries to undercut each other. On top of that, you can find the crazy cases that include extra battery, wallets, and added functionality. If you’re using a Sony or OnePlus, you can only dream about such a thing. This becomes even more of a value I you are one of the people in a program like Amazon Vine. I was able to get three cases for this phone, through Vine. Before this, only once was I able to find a case for my phone. Another factor is that there are also apps on the Play Store that are dedicated to tweaking the Samsung experience. Some of them are quite useful. This is something you don’t find when using the minor players. Is this phone a good value? No. I’m sorry at its retail price, it’s not. The LG V60 might have a weaker camera and older processor, but it’s a far better value. The OnePlus 9 Pro, is a slightly better value, if we are talking about a full priced phone. If you want this phone to be a value, you need to land this phone for $900 or less. Anything higher just isn’t worth it. If you’re going to pay full price for this phone, you might want to look at the iPhone. I do not like iOS, but they have an excellent build, great camera, no bloatware, and fast updates. If money is not an issue and you love Samsung – yes. If money is no issue and you want the best camera – yes. If money is no issue and you want the best Android phone – maybe. If money is an issue and you want a great Android phone – buy the LG V60. If you want a clean Android experience – buy the Pixel 5 or OnePlus 9 Pro. If money isn’t an issue and you want the best phone – buy the iPhone 12 Pro Max. If you need to have a sd card and headphones jack – buy the LG V60. If you need to have a sd card and headphones jack, but hate LGs software – buy the Sony Xperia 1 II.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Review Title: ##### Google Pixel 9 Peony Refurbished Excellent || Geek Squad Agent Review
Review Content: ##### Google Pixel 9 Peony Refurbished Excellent || Geek Squad Agent Review Geek Squad Agent Review! Not a single scratch or ding on this thing! No scratched screen. No dings on any part of the phone or camera. Looks absolutely brand new! The only thing I will nitpick a little, is that it did arrive with no charge at all. Which made setting it up a little time consuming as it needed to be at 20% for the device set up. It also came with a charger. It did NOT come with a SIM ejector like stated. This may be an issue for others who do not have direct access to SIM keys. A normal paper clip or bobby pin will do as we use them at work all the time. Was not locked to any carrier like other reviews have said happened to theirs and took my SIM card immediately. It has ESIM or SIM tray (which I was looking for in the reviews and none specified. I had to do my own research) Set up is easy tho there is a ton and I mean a TON of features to this thing. More than I've ever seen on any iPhone or Samsung device. Super personalizable. It's going to take a while to go through all of them. I work for a Geek Squad so setting up phones is in my daily routine. It was also the correct color as some reviews stated they received the wrong color. I definitely have to get used to the new keyboard and I type a little funny now. But that's common with adjusting to a new phone. As well as not being used to the notification noises so I'm slower to respond. No fault of the phone either. As someone who hates both iPhone and Samsung having owned both and worked on both. I'm hoping this will be an amazing change for me as I've read and observed. We VERY RARELY ever get Google Pixels at Geek Squad to fix or look at and that should say something in itself on these devices. Device does get warm. (As any device does) But not blazing hot like most Samsungs and sometimes older iPhones. I've had the screen on for a long period of time to test this. And had multiple apps open. Device also has a built in Diagnostics system similar to the one we have at work. It is located in your settings. Mine failed zero diagnostics and is in perfect condition. Both cosmetically and in hardware. So far the battery is an absolute TANK. It is a little slow to charge. But that charge lasts hours. Easter was busy today. So setting up took time. That 20% battery has lasted 3 hours for me so far and it's barely budged. Over all review so far is absolutely perfect. I will update as time goes on! Review Title: ##### Moto G phones are affordable and usually easy to switch out
Review Content: ##### Moto G phones are affordable and usually easy to switch out.... Arrived overnight which I was surprised and pleased about. I did not realize it was a little smaller than my 2022 Moto G Stylus but not by too much. This is my second Moto G Stylus and I am really a fan of this brand of phones. I just don't see any point to buying such expensive phones. The Moto G phones are reasonably priced and work really well. I've tried a variety of phones through many years. IF you are someone who doesn't feel the need to impress people with an insanely expensive phone then the Moto G stylus is a great phone for you. I think my first phone was a Moto G Power but now I'm sticking with the Stylus as it works tremendously well for me. It's been hugely durable for me because I put it in a good protective case. I have dropped my phone multiple times in the house, the car and a few times outside. Thank goodness it's never stopped working and I'm thrilled that it's held up for me. The battery life was very good for quite a while. But considering I bought this as a renewed phone a few years ago and use it throughout the day every day. So in the last four months of my 2022 phone it stopped holding a charge for more than a few hours. But I want to point out that I started buying renewed phones as it saved me money and they worked great. Even a brand new Moto G stylus is well priced. They have always been reliable and storage capacity has never been an issue (unless I go on a pet photo binge ;) which is often). Then I buy some additional storage. You can bypass the info below IF you don't have AT&T: By Monday I wasn't able to get my new Moto G phone to completely switch over all my stuff from the old phone today because it would not accept my current nano SIM card. AT&T provided zero help over the phone and actually told me I could get a new SIM card at THE DOLLAR TREE!! Which I stupidly went to and was told they don't sell that item. Told me that I will have to buy one which rather ticked me off considering I'm on a plan that I paid for 12 months up front. I made another trip to AT&T on Tuesday and told the tech what I was experiencing and needed a new nano card. The tech pulled the nano card out of my current phone and put it back in the new phone. He did a few things on the screen and ignored answering my questions. Handed me my phone and said it was working now. He couldn't be bothered to explain to me why the phone kept messaging that the SIM card was not current. I was a little confused as I'm not at all knowledgeable on phone technology. I asked another question about completing the conversion and the tech shrugged and told me it's a self help situation. WOW so apparently when you buy your phone elsewhere you get bare bones help from AT&T. So be prepared if you end up having this issue. It could be possible that I placed the sim card into the phone backwards but I was very careful with it. Anyway by Wednesday I replaced the broken C charger at a nearby store and FINALLY completed the conversion! Hallelujah! I hope I can prevent others from having this type of delay in converting the files into the new phone. The phone is working well as expected but AT&T greatly disappointed me this time around. The phone service has been constant and that's why I stay. Moto phones are the best way to have a good reliable phone. Make sure you have a good quality C charger cord for charging. Review Title: The phone arrived quickly and in good condition
Review Content: The phone arrived quickly and in good condition. No visible cracks, scratches, dents, anything Battery is in good health, and easily lasts the entire day with moderate use. I only charged it to 80% and with about 5 hours of active use today with various tasks (watching videos/movies/tv, video calls, texting, reading, music, navigation, some light gaming, and a lot of downloading) it is sitting at 47%. The average person uses their phone for about 4.5-5 hours a day. That is 33% discharge for a full day's use. There are a couple overcharge protection features which I find quite cool as a tech nerd, but others may find annoying. They can both be easily turned off (but I would advice against that because they really do help preserve your battery's health. Just my two cents) Using the phone, it feels smooth and responsive. I never feel like I'm having to wait for something to load or register my input. It did shove a bit of bloatware on me (even beyond the AT&T stuff), but it was all easily uninstalled/disabled. The screen is very good looking. Great color depth, plenty bright, and it's not a dust/fingerprint magnet! The microphone and speakers are both decent. Nothing mind blowing, but it doesn't sound horrible. Same goes for the cameras. The plastic frame doesn't evoke the kind of "premium" feel that a metal one would, but this isn't a flagship phone and it seems durable. The buttons all feel sturdy and have good travel. I do quite like the pleather back! I've had zero connectivity issues with wi-fi, bluetooth, cell service/data, and NFC. I really like the stylus, even if it's just a simple capacitive one and not a fancy active stylus. It adds some good functionality and it's quite intuitive to use. I particularly enjoy the handwriting calculator, it is surprisingly versatile. Overall, this phone is a joy to use and a much appreciated upgrade from my old one. And a steal for the price! - IP52 rating means you have to be a bit more careful around water - Not super powerful, may not be suitable for heavy gaming It's a very solid, affordable, mid-range phone, and I'm glad I bought it! But don't expect it to knock your socks off (except for the battery life, that's pretty crazy)       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))       28 people found this helpful Helpful  Sending feedback...Thank you for your feedback. Review Title: I am very impressed with the ANC on these
Review Content: I am very impressed with the ANC on these. I have a pair of Bose Quietcomfort headphones, and these are about 90% as quiet as those, which is REALLY good for earbuds. I did get some memory foam ear tips to replace the silicone ones, but honestly I don't think they make much of a difference. I can tell immediately when the ANC turns on, so I know it's not just the ear tips that are blocking out the sound around me. I work at a busy hospital, and these are absolutely amazing for helping me regulate myself on my breaks. The only thing I notice is that these do such a good job of cutting out the background noise, they can sometimes make specific sounds stand out. For example, if I'm sitting at a café, I can barely hear the barista making coffee and banging cups and plates around, but I can distinctly hear the people talking at the table next to me. This is true of my Bose headphones too, but to a lesser degree. These don't work miracles - just get earplugs if you need total quiet. This is my biggest issue with these earbuds. Sound quality is obviously one of the most important aspects of earbuds, and these sounded awful right out of the box. Way, way worse than my $30 pair that I was using before. They were extremely tinny and sounded like I was listening to music coming from a different room. I spent a good 2 HOURS adjusting the settings in the app to try to make them sound good, and I did eventually get there, but if you don't want to spend the time doing that, I honestly don't recommend these. The app has a lot of ways to customize the sound, but you really have to get in there and micromanage everything if you want them to sound decent. I went through the "HearID Sound" setup, which made a difference, but I still had to go into the EQ and adjust it while listening to several different types of audio in order to create a profile that worked across the board for the types of things I usually listen to (jazz, rock, and podcasts). I am not an audiophile, but I can tell my Bose headphones sound a lot better - however, at this point, I am not bothered by the quality of these ones. I'd say they're a 3.5/5 on overall sound quality, but a 1/5 out of the box. I guess it's possible I got a bad pair, but considering I did eventually get to a good point with them, I don't think that's the case. I'm not sure if it's because they're refurbished (box was completely sealed and unopened though), but I only get 4-5 hours of battery life with ANC on, opposed to the 7 hours they advertise. Could be worse, but my previous non-ANC earbuds lasted me a good 10+ hours, so I find this a bit frustrating because I like to have them in all day due to my noise sensitivities. I my actually get a second pair so that I always have one that is charged. I chose these earbuds primarily because of the ear hook. I use an electric scooter to get to work, and I struggled to keep my previous earbuds from falling out due to the vibration. These stay put very well, and the hooks don't feel uncomfortable at all. They're bigger than other earbuds because of this design, but still very pocketable, and the case isn't too bulky. If you're looking for a pair of true ANC earbuds that won't fall out, will last at least 4 hours, and you're okay with taking some time to play with the sound settings, I highly recommend these. After using them for a month, I am happy with my purchase. Hope this review helps you decide if these are for you!       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Review Title: I bought this phone because it was specifically stated to work with both Verizon and T-mobile sim ca
Review Content: I bought this phone because it was specifically stated to work with both Verizon and T-mobile sim cards. Well, I was left extremely disappointed. Out of the box, you receive the phone (which itself is in very good physical condition), the sim card removal tool, and a usb charging cable (with no actual 12v wall outlet plug, you need to buy that separately). The phone, when powered up, you'll discover is a Verizon branded phone. I followed the instructions by completing initial setup and updates via my home wi-fi network, then inserting my t-mobile sim card. Well, the phone, no matter what, refused to accept the card and allow me to make calls or use data. In fact, it would give me a message 'sim card locked - not a verizon sim card.' After wasting hours trying everything imaginable, I came to the conclusion that this really isn't an unlocked tmobile phone. How did I find this out? Well, I tapped on a message on the screen which gave me a 'Sorry, your device can't be activated on another carrier's network right now' message from the My Verizon app installed on the phone. So I tried the same sim card on my own FULLY unlocked Motorola One phone (purchased from a different amazon vendor months ago) and it fired right up and let me use calls data straight away. I'm guessing this vendor is doing nothing for testing except for running a stock verizon sim before shipping these out. Extremely disappointed. Time and money wasted. Moral of the story is: stick to fully unlocked phones, and avoid carrier branded phones. Because they will be very hit or miss. Review Title: The speaker is great
Review Content: The speaker is great. This was an upgrade from a 110 I’ve had for 6 years, and the difference in sound is absurd. This thing will shake your walls. I brought it to a house party where it was paired with a 710. It held its own, and honestly, I think for most people the 520 is a better choice even if the bass may not hit quite as hard. If you’re the one who brings the music to your parties, the ability to roll this thing outside and use it on battery is incredibly useful, and its slightly shorter size makes a huge difference in portability and how obtrusive it is in your home. I didn’t use my 110 too often, but I was glad to have it when I needed it. My one complaint was that the sound just didn’t hit hard enough in large spaces or outdoors. Not the case with the 520. Review Title: When I finally tried them, one earbud was noticeably louder than the other, and I could hear static
Review Content: When I finally tried them, one earbud was noticeably louder than the other, and I could hear static. I initially thought I was losing hearing in one ear, but after swapping earbuds, the issue persisted on the opposite side. I adjusted all settings through the app, did a firmware update, and reset everything, but nothing worked. I was about to return them but gave it another shot the next day. After playing around with different tracks, they eventually just started working correctly. I noticed there bluetooth info from the previous owner. I deleted this info, but I doubt this would've caused this problem. I've been using them for three days now, and the battery life is slightly better than my P30 earbuds. These last about 8 hours, whereas the P30s initially lasted that long but dropped to about 6.5-7 hours after a month. I expect these to follow the same trend. Before I start on the sound quality, you must know that these sound like crap out of the box. You have to adjust the equalizer settings to to your liking. Even if you choose the preset equalizer, it should be good enough. The sound quality is similar to the P30, and for cheap earbuds, it’s impressive. I would give these a 8 out of 10 for sound quality. I also own Sony and Bose earbuds, and while I still prefer my Sony WF-1000XM4, these are surprisingly close in sound quality. Plus, I don’t mind if these get damaged. Noise cancellation isn't great in the wind, but at a fraction of the price of premium brands, it’s hard to complain. Noise cancellation is good enough to keep things quiet when my wife is snoring in bed.

Review Title: The app has nice features and is easy to use
Review Content: The app has nice features and is easy to use. Tuning them to your ears seems to improve SQ a bit. Noise cancellation is effective and smart. Not going to block out as much noise as, say, a $200 set of Bose earbuds, but it does a good enough job to mow the lawn with an electric mower and more or less silence that noise as long as you have something playing. Not quite effective enough to block out the sound while onboard an airplane if you have the kind of seat you can afford if you're buying this product :) In fully transparent sound cancellation mode, it will still block out the drone and constant noise of something like an electric bike's motor, or wind noise, but will allow the sound of non-constant (upcoming car, person behind you yelling about how you don't deserve to exist) through. For the money, very good. Battery easily lasts 3 hours, may be longer or shorter depending on what you have playing at what volume level. By mixing and matching the included (cheap) silicon inserts I was able to find a good-enough fit for me. Not everyone has the same size hole on each side of their head. What I don't understand is why products like this don't have a breathable charging case. They're marketed as and intended to be used by active people. Active people sweat. Plopping these yucky drenched earbuds into their charging container and then shutting it lets them sit in their stew. I typically let them air out and even wipe them clean after each use before holstering them into their little cave. I was paranoid that one of these would slide out while cruising at 20 MPH and would be gone forever, but I can say that they stay pretty securely in your head. I do find myself fidgeting with them quite a bit, but that might just be me. Fit could be better but is very good considering it's the first product I found, the price, and the fact that they're made to fit Everyone. Look no further! Review Title: ##### Phänomenaler Klang, tolle Bedienung, gute Telefonie, ich bin begeistert!
Review Content: ##### Phänomenaler Klang, tolle Bedienung, gute Telefonie, ich bin begeistert! Nachdem mir der Q30i eine zu schlechte Telefoniequalität auf der Gegenseite hatte und für die phantastischen Liberty 4 Pro keine passenden Earbuds gefunden habe, habe ich beide schweren Herzens zurückgesandt und Soundcore mit den Space A45 noch eine letzte Chance gegeben. Der Klang ist gitantisch: Tonal absolut ausgewogen, satt und trocken im Bass aber nicht überzogen, die Stimmwiedergabe ist perfekt. Beim Equalizer habe ich das Standardprogramm "Bass Reducer" eingestellt, was bei meinen JBL Live 670 der Studioeinstellung, also Studiobedinungen entspricht. Ich mag die einfache Einrichtung und die perfekte Bedienung, da sich die Steuerung programmieren lässt, Meine Einstellung: Links Pause / Wiedergabe, rechts laut / leise und auf beiden Ohren Transparanzmodus ein / aus. Auch die Telefoniefunktion funktiniert in Auto in der Bahn und in der Stadt vergleichbar den Liberty 4 Pro und dort deutlich besser als bei den P30i und auch besser als beim Q30 Kopfhörer, welche nur in ruhiger Umgebung funktionieren. Einziger Wehmutstropfen: Meine Gehörgänge sind auch für die mitgelileferten XL-Earpads zu groß, ich habe allerdings welche in meiner Sammlung gefunden, die passen (und bei den P30i sowie bei den Liberty 4 Pro nicht passten). Während ich die Liberty 4 Pro ständig beim Kauen sowie bei jeder Kopfbewegung verloren habe und auch die P30 i nicht fest saßen, sitzen die Q45 durch die andere Gewichtsverteilung trotz ihres hohen Gewichtes (vergleichbar mit den Liberty 4 Pro), sehr sicher in meinen Ohren. Resümee: Klare Kaufempfelung! Gratulation an Soundcore für die Space A45! Review Title: The blood oxygen monitoring and ECG capabilities give me real peace of mind, especially during worko
Review Content: The blood oxygen monitoring and ECG capabilities give me real peace of mind, especially during workouts. The sleep tracking has helped me understand my patterns better, and the heart rate notifications have caught irregularities I wouldn't have noticed otherwise. As someone who sits at a desk all day, the activity reminders genuinely motivate me to move more. The S6 chip makes everything snappy - no lag when switching between apps or asking Siri. Battery easily lasts a full day with moderate to heavy use, and the fast charging means I can top up quickly while getting ready in the morning. Being able to respond to texts, take calls, and control music without pulling out my phone is incredibly convenient, especially during workouts or when my hands are full. The always-on display is bright enough to read in sunlight, and I love that I can check the time with just a glance. The construction feels premium and durable. I've knocked it against walls and doorframes countless times with barely a scratch. The sport band is comfortable for all-day wear and easy to clean. The charging cable is proprietary (wish it was USB-C), and some third-party apps can be slow to load. Also, if you're an Android user, you're out of luck. This watch has genuinely improved my daily life in small but meaningful ways. Whether you're fitness-focused or just want convenient notifications, the Series 6 delivers excellent value. Review Title: If there’s one thing Google consistently nails, it’s the camera
Review Content: If there’s one thing Google consistently nails, it’s the camera. And the Pixel 7 Pro continues that tradition with a vengeance. The triple-camera setup—featuring a 50 MP wide lens, 12 MP ultra-wide, and a 48 MP telephoto—paired with Google’s AI-driven software, delivers photos that are frankly astounding. I’ve used it in all sorts of lighting conditions, and it never disappoints. Night Sight, in particular, is a game-changer. I’ve taken photos in near darkness, and the results are bright, clear, and detailed without that nasty noise you often get from other smartphones. The Super Res Zoom also surprised me. Zooming in up to 30x, I expected pixelated messes, but somehow Google’s AI magic produces crisp, usable photos that I wouldn’t expect from any smartphone. A fun bonus is the Magic Eraser feature. It’s incredibly satisfying to just tap and remove that random passerby in the background of an otherwise perfect photo. And the new Cinematic Blur video feature gives you that nice DSLR bokeh effect for those who, like me, dabble in mobile video shooting. However, the camera bump… oh boy. I get that Google needed space for those advanced sensors, but the protrusion is hard to ignore. It makes the phone wobble when flat, and in my case, it even interfered with wireless charging in my Tesla. It’s one of those small annoyances that doesn’t ruin the experience but can be a dealbreaker for some. The 6.7-inch OLED display on the Pixel 7 Pro is one of the most stunning screens I’ve ever used. The colors are vibrant, blacks are deep, and everything looks razor-sharp thanks to the QHD+ resolution. Whether I’m gaming, watching Netflix, or just browsing, it feels immersive. The 120Hz refresh rate makes a noticeable difference when scrolling or switching between apps. Everything feels buttery smooth and responsive. Even outside in bright sunlight, the screen holds its own, making it easy to see details. The curved edges, while mostly aesthetic, add a premium feel to the phone’s design. Now, here’s where things get a little less rosy. The in-display fingerprint reader—while improved over previous models—still leaves something to be desired. It’s slow compared to what other phones offer, and it’s finicky if your fingers or the screen aren’t perfectly clean. There were moments where I’d try multiple times to unlock the phone, which, let’s be honest, is annoying when you’re in a rush. And then, as mentioned earlier, there’s the camera bump. Aesthetically, I’m not a fan, but practically, it’s worse. Without a case, it feels like you’re always risking scratching the lens or tipping the phone over on a flat surface. It’s a trade-off for such a powerful camera system, but still a bit of a nuisance. On the software front, the Pixel 7 Pro is a breath of fresh air. Stock Android 13 with zero bloatware. I can’t overstate how much I appreciate that. No unwanted apps cluttering up the system, and the phone runs fast and smoothly right out of the box. Plus, with Google’s hardware, you’re always first in line for Android updates, which is a nice perk for long-term users like me. In summary, the Pixel 7 Pro is a beast of a phone, especially if you’re big into photography or simply enjoy a clean Android experience. The camera is easily the best I’ve used on a smartphone, and the display makes using the phone a real pleasure. That said, the fingerprint reader could be better, and the camera bump is definitely a love-it-or-hate-it feature. If you’re like me and value cutting-edge camera tech and a clutter-free phone, the Pixel 7 Pro will not disappoint. Just be prepared for a few quirks along the way. Come to today, the Moto Razr 2024+ absolutely blows the Samsung out of the water, especially in terms of practicality. The external screen is actually usable, you're not limited to any special widgets or apps. Highly recommend, especially if you can snag it for $389 like I did. My renewed item was practically new, sans OEM box/charger. Seller offered great support with my order as well. Review Title: I am writing this review because I was hesitant to buy a "renewed" phone, and unsure what I would ge
Review Content: I am writing this review because I was hesitant to buy a "renewed" phone, and unsure what I would get. Well, I'm here to tell you I have been pleasantly surprised. The phone arrived early from what was quoted by Amazon. Emails came automatically from FedEx and were fairly accurate. I ordered the phone on a Friday before a Monday federal holiday, and Amazon quoted it to arrive Tuesday. Within the next 24 hours I received an email from FedEx saying to expect a delivery on Monday, between ~8am and noon. There were a couple follow up emails and the phone did eventually arrive a little after 1pm. Already I was pleasantly and unexpectedly satisfied with the service as the phone had arrived a day earlier than expected. The only downside was that Verizon was unable to activate the phone over another phone, because there was no sim card installed. Even before receiving the phone I was afraid that I would not get an unlocked version or something else would impede my ability to get this one working to replace the one I had just lost. After an hour or so trying with Verizon tech support they finally indicated I needed to go to a Verizon store and get a free sim card. I was able to get to the store nearby before they closed. The process was easy and fast, and I had the phone connected and my phone number back in no time. It took a couple of tries to get accounts set up and synced, but my "new" phone is essentially the same as the old. The phone sent to me by Re-Cell was in great shape. If there were not a few very minor dings on the top and bottom of the body of the phone I would think it was brand new and unused. Someone must have replaced the screen, or the person who owned it before installed a screen protector and good case, because the screen and back of the phone show no signs of wear and tear, let alone damage. So far no operations have been less than my previous new S22 Ultra. In fact, I may even be getting better battery life from this one, which could have as much to do with having a phone cleaned of old files, etc, but I get the impression that either the battery was replaced, or this phone was not used heavily before it was refurbished. This phone "feels" newer than the one I lost, which did have a couple scratches on the screen. Other than having to spend money on a new phone, (my Wells Fargo credit card phone protection does not cover lost phones, only theft) the only major downside to losing my old phone was the time I spent looking for it, and going through the process to get this one and set it up... a story I will not tell here. From my experience with Amazon Renewed and Re-Cell, I do not plan to buy another new phone when the time comes that I ever need another. I will find the phone I want here and buy it used in excellent condition like the one that was shipped to me. Very satisfied with this experience. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple iPhone Xs Max, 64GB, Gold - Fully Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: ##### Il mio primo rigenerato Amazon, vi racconto tutto
Review Content: ##### Il mio primo rigenerato Amazon, vi racconto tutto. Veniamo all'oggetto della recensione: l'iphone. Una volta tirato fuori dall'orrenda bustina di plastica che lo conteneva, l'ho accuratamente ispezionato rilevando un piccolo segno marcato (circa 1x1 mm) nella parte superiore sinistra dello schermo, dove il display si unisce al notch. A questo si aggiunge un piccolissimo segno (non so come altro definirlo) tra lo schermo e la scocca, nella parte inferiore sinistra. Entrambi i segni sono pressocchè invisibili ad una prima occhiata, occorre esaminare con cura il telefono per rilevarli. Il resto (scocca, schermo, bordi, ecc) è come nuovo. Amazon Renewed dichiara che il telefono "non presenta imperfezioni estetiche visibili tenendo il prodotto a una distanza di 30 centimetri", e direi che la promessa è stata assolutamente mantenuta, ben oltre le aspettative. Esaurita la parte estetica, accendiamo il telefono: l'avvio è immediato, i colori, la luminosità e la presenza dell'opzione True Tone mi fanno pensare che il display è originale Apple, difatti la mancanza del True Tone è solitamente indice di un display non originale o quantomeno più economico di quelli normalmente usati da Apple. Anche il codice IMEI riportato fisicamente sul "cassettino" della Sim corrisponde a quello indicato nelle informazioni del telefono, cosa che mi permette di ipotizzare che il telefono non è il risultato di un assemblaggio di più pezzi provenienti da altri telefoni. La configurazione è avvenuta senza difficoltà e dopo un accurato test di tutta la sensoristica e delle varie parti (Face Id, prossimità, luminosità, touch & 3d touch, giroscopi, tasto muto, volume, power, flash, ricarica wireless, altoparlanti, ecc ecc) non ho rilevato malfunzionamenti o problemi di alcun genere. Il telefono è arrivato con iOs 14.8, versione che se non ricordo male è stata rilasciata intorno a settembre 2021. Analizzando il seriale è possibile determinare l'anno di produzione: il mio nuovo amico risulta essere stato assemblato a Chengdu intorno alla seconda metà di settembre 2018. Facendo due conti, il telefono è rimasto "in giro" da settembre 2018 a settembre 2021, poi non è stato più aggiornato e quindi presumo utilizzato. La batteria presenta una capacità massima dell'80%, in linea a quanto indicato nelle condizioni del prodotto su Amazon. Di sicuro è stato usato non poco, ma il fatto che possa leggere quel valore è un altro ottimo indicatore, significa infatti che la batteria è ancora quella originale, altresì avrei un avviso di "batteria non originale". La scocca posteriore è priva del marchio CE, che di solito identifica i telefoni nati per il mercato Europeo. Ma niente paura, in questo caso significa solo che questo telefono era originariamente destinato al mercato americano o asiatico. Tuttavia, poichè la fotocamera non produce il rumore dello scatto quando è in modalità silenziosa, propendo per il mercato USA. In quello cinese infatti, se non è cambiato qualcosa, i telefoni devono per legge emettere sempre il rumore dello scatto fotografico, così da impedire scatti "rubati". Dura lex, sed lex! Infine faccio una delle ultime ma più importanti prove, vado sul sito Apple e tramite codice seriale verifico la garanzia: e qui ecco la sorpresa (bella)! Non solo il prodotto è regolare, non ci sono allarmi e il seriale è corretto, ma risulto addirittura coperto dall'AppleCare+ fino al 17 di questo mese, mica male :-). Concludo (finalmente, direte voi!): in questo momento sono estremamente contento del mio acquisto, l'iphone è praticamente nuovo e funziona bene. Direi un bel 5 stelle tanto ad Amazon quanto al venditore NEGOZIOREALE, che hanno superato le mie aspettative. Se state leggendo questa recensione, e non importa quando, significa che il telefono sta continuando a funzionare bene. Al primo accenno di problema state sicuri che verrò subito qui ad aggiornare la mia recensione. Imperfezione tra display e scocca di meno di un 1 mm in basso a sinistra (esaltata graficamente per farvela vedere) Cassettino sim con Imei (parzialmente oscurato da me ovviamente) Imperfezione display 1x1 mm in alto a sinistra (esaltata graficamente per farvela vedere)

Entrambi i segni sono pressocchè invisibili ad una prima occhiata, occorre esaminare con cura il telefono per rilevarli. Il resto (scocca, schermo, bordi, ecc) è come nuovo. Amazon Renewed dichiara che il telefono "non presenta imperfezioni estetiche visibili tenendo il prodotto a una distanza di 30 centimetri", e direi che la promessa è stata assolutamente mantenuta, ben oltre le aspettative. Esaurita la parte estetica, accendiamo il telefono: l'avvio è immediato, i colori, la luminosità e la presenza dell'opzione True Tone mi fanno pensare che il display è originale Apple, difatti la mancanza del True Tone è solitamente indice di un display non originale o quantomeno più economico di quelli normalmente usati da Apple. Anche il codice IMEI riportato fisicamente sul "cassettino" della Sim corrisponde a quello indicato nelle informazioni del telefono, cosa che mi permette di ipotizzare che il telefono non è il risultato di un assemblaggio di più pezzi provenienti da altri telefoni. La configurazione è avvenuta senza difficoltà e dopo un accurato test di tutta la sensoristica e delle varie parti (Face Id, prossimità, luminosità, touch & 3d touch, giroscopi, tasto muto, volume, power, flash, ricarica wireless, altoparlanti, ecc ecc) non ho rilevato malfunzionamenti o problemi di alcun genere. Il telefono è arrivato con iOs 14.8, versione che se non ricordo male è stata rilasciata intorno a settembre 2021. Analizzando il seriale è possibile determinare l'anno di produzione: il mio nuovo amico risulta essere stato assemblato a Chengdu intorno alla seconda metà di settembre 2018. Facendo due conti, il telefono è rimasto "in giro" da settembre 2018 a settembre 2021, poi non è stato più aggiornato e quindi presumo utilizzato. La batteria presenta una capacità massima dell'80%, in linea a quanto indicato nelle condizioni del prodotto su Amazon. Di sicuro è stato usato non poco, ma il fatto che possa leggere quel valore è un altro ottimo indicatore, significa infatti che la batteria è ancora quella originale, altresì avrei un avviso di "batteria non originale". La scocca posteriore è priva del marchio CE, che di solito identifica i telefoni nati per il mercato Europeo. Ma niente paura, in questo caso significa solo che questo telefono era originariamente destinato al mercato americano o asiatico. Tuttavia, poichè la fotocamera non produce il rumore dello scatto quando è in modalità silenziosa, propendo per il mercato USA. In quello cinese infatti, se non è cambiato qualcosa, i telefoni devono per legge emettere sempre il rumore dello scatto fotografico, così da impedire scatti "rubati". Dura lex, sed lex! Infine faccio una delle ultime ma più importanti prove, vado sul sito Apple e tramite codice seriale verifico la garanzia: e qui ecco la sorpresa (bella)! Non solo il prodotto è regolare, non ci sono allarmi e il seriale è corretto, ma risulto addirittura coperto dall'AppleCare+ fino al 17 di questo mese, mica male :-). Concludo (finalmente, direte voi!): in questo momento sono estremamente contento del mio acquisto, l'iphone è praticamente nuovo e funziona bene. Direi un bel 5 stelle tanto ad Amazon quanto al venditore NEGOZIOREALE, che hanno superato le mie aspettative. Se state leggendo questa recensione, e non importa quando, significa che il telefono sta continuando a funzionare bene. Al primo accenno di problema state sicuri che verrò subito qui ad aggiornare la mia recensione. This speaker is easily loud enough to hear from all ends of the average home, and a great distance outside as well. Perfect for poolside, beach, and tailgating situations. If you are looking for a good Bluetooth speaker with rich sound then give this thing a shot. You won’t be disappointed. Review Title: I also own a JBL flip 6 which is about more or less a third of the volume in size
Review Content: I also own a JBL flip 6 which is about more or less a third of the volume in size I'm comparing it to the JBL flip 6 because it's a very popular Bluetooth speaker that you may already own or you have a friend that does. The sound core boom 2 does not sound super great out of the box. It's very bassy and the vocals can be muddled. With the app you can slightly boost up some of the treble features and a completely changes the speaker. So I have the left and right sliders on The equalizer slightly bumped up and the second to right and left sliders boosted up kind of towards the middle. The bass button on the actual speaker is separate to The equalizer and I leave it on. I would only probably turn it off at max volume, which should only be done in an outdoors party because this thing does get pretty loud. So I compared my JBL to this thing about 8 ft away from me in a bedroom. The sound core at half volume is roughly as loud as the JBL at full volume. They both perform great but the sound core has way better overall range then the JBL. It's noticeable in the lower bass and lower vocals range. But the entire range is very crisp and clear once it's set up in the soundcore app and it maintains clarity until about the 85% range of volume, then you may want to make adjustments to The equalizer to smooth it out. It doesn't sound bad but pushing any speaker to the max is going to have issues. For the price this is a fantastic buy. I use the JBL because it's small and packs quite a punch in its weight class. I also have an outdoor party speaker the block rocker Plus but it's massive and is more of like a beach/pa speaker for me. The size of the speaker is roughly about the size of a specialty loaf of bread, like a Keto bread or something more artisan. It's got to handle that's built into the actual box and is kind of light feeling. If you find this thing on sale pick it up. Also check out the renewed version, I saved like almost 50 bucks and it's got a couple light scratches and scuffs that you can't see unless you're holding it. Review Title: I'm not the rattling license plate kind of bass guy, but I like quality, accurate bass way higher vo
Review Content: I'm not the rattling license plate kind of bass guy, but I like quality, accurate bass way higher volumes than most people can tolerate. This speaker isn't impressive on that level at all, but it is impressive for something the size of a large bread loaf. The lowest notes drop off in volume and the bass drum isn't crisp like a sealed 12, for obvious reasons. But I still find myself turning the bass boost off on a lot of situations to be respectful of neighbors. Battery life is great. I try to keep it plugged in just so the music never quits, but never think twice about setting it unplugged on the workbench with bass on for hours on end, or using it to watch movies and shows in bed for hours. I build lots of things, usually overbuilt, and am highly critical of poorly engineered plastic crap. This feels remarkably solid. Silicone buttons don't feel like they'll leak or break. Handle is beyond overkill. Grill over speakers is very stiff. Passive woofers on side are exposed, but slightly recessed like an hd phone case. I even left the back port uncovered for a day of rafting once and it didn't die. Impressive Bluetooth distance too. Review Title: I'm used to using the tempered glass screen protectors which can't be used on this one
Review Content: I'm used to using the tempered glass screen protectors which can't be used on this one. I've tried a couple of the flexible film ones with it but wasted the money because couldn't get them to install properly(without air bubbles everywhere). The phone screen is soft. It will get dents/creases in it if not careful(I put a light crease in mine trying to install a screen protector). When opened its not perfectly flat, there's a shallow area where the fold is but it's not visually noticeable with the screen on at all. Only noticeable by touch and visually when the screen is off. The non expandable memory isn't a feature I like. 128GB isn't a whole lot nowadays, especially when it's common for apps to be 1GB-3GB(like games and Facebook). I used to keep my games, photos, and entertainment/social media apps on a SD card but now I'm just being a lot more selective with what I install and quick to uninstall something if it's not being used regularly, whereas with expandable memory I'd just leave them on the SD card. I read that it will no longer receive updates from Samsung so Android 14 is going to be the last operating system upgrade for it. Size is the reason I bought it. Got tired of carrying phones that only fit in back pockets and still have 1/4 of it sticking out. With this I get the same size screen but can put it in any pocket. It's unlocked compatible with GSM and CDMA service providers so works with all the major ones. All in all it's a good phone loaded with features, looks and functions like a new one for 1/2 the price,and it's second life is helping the planet with saving resources and landfill space. A good buy for cheap people like me who cares not 1 bit about having the newest model phone. Product Title: Amazon.com: iOn Audio Pathfinder 320 All Weather Bluetooth Speaker (Renewed), Black : Electronics
Review Title: Don't know why these are not available new
Review Content: Don't know why these are not available new. Bought 2 of them refurbished. The first one was flawless, the second one had a few scratches and some left over adhesive from a sticker on it. I am not sure if they were actually refurbished or just repacked in the original boxes. I am very happy with them. They are really loud. Have both by the pool and can here them over 600 feet away clearly at volume 28 out of 30. One would be more than enough in an enclosed space. The battery life is great. Played continuously over 7 hours at almost max volume and didn't die yet. Trick is keeping the slide cover open to cool the speaker. The cover has a usb charger inside to charge your phone while using the unit. I keep it open to radiate the heat out of it. They are hefty and weigh about 25 lbs but have wheels and a retractable handle which helps. The build quality is solid . Metal protection around the speakers and it truly does broadcast in 270 degree field. The mids are located on the sides and tweeters are located above the woofer in front. The mids are really high powered and broadcast real far. The bass does boom if you adjust the app or manually on the dial on its face. Each are adjustable on the app as well as the unit. The app controls volume also. Getting both to sync is sometimes alittle tricky. One is the master and the other is slaved. If you forget which one is master and try to connect your Bluetooth to the slave it won't work and you have to restart the sync process by shutting down and pressing the sync buttons on both units. The Bluetooth 5 range is incredible on each . I can broadcast from my phone to one of the units over 100 ft direct sight. When both are paired together they must be within 75 ft or so of each other or one will shut down because it won't hold the sync. The lights are off, on with rotating colors or beat with the music. Cant see the lights during the day but night they look cool. Bottle opener is nice too. If you want to remotely control the volume or adjust the output of each high, mid and low you need the app. Its easy yo use and no bloatware. Overall I will purchase again if one does happen to not work anymore, but I don't see that happening. You will be very pleased if you want a loud speaker that's clear and has long battery life. Review Title: After reading some of the other reviews about this (and similar) models, that the main complaint was
Review Content: After reading some of the other reviews about this (and similar) models, that the main complaint was battery life long term. Once I did the math on the price difference between a refurbished vs new model I realized I could replace the battery several times over before arriving at the cost of a new model (which may well have similar long term issues). This wasn't a big deal to me if there were some dings/scratches (so long as it worked) becuase I'd purchased this with the intent of taking it to Softball Games/Practices for the teams warm ups and walk up music. It needed to be loud and easy to use, but prettiness was way at the bottom of the list as I knew it would suffer some abuse with constantly loading / unloading with all the rest of our gear, plus dusty/dirty softball fields and rain. after a short season with it, it's a mess visually but is still working flawlessly. Battery life long enough for a double headers (at least 4 hours) - so far cord/phone storage was a nice touch as well for those of us who constantly lose cords. The range of the blue tooth was just ok. on a softball field I'd need to leave my phone on the bench near the unit otherwise I'd lose connectivity from one side of the diamond to the other. This isn't really a complaint as any small bluetooth speaker is pretty much going to function that way. the sounds quality wouldn't be what I'd want to listen to music in my home as there are better speakers, but for outside / self contained and for the price it was just fine. I personally couldn't care less about the bottle opener either, nor have I had an opportunity to try it. Review Title: As for the actual phone it is waterproof as it survived being lost in a lake for a couple hours, the
Review Content: As for the actual phone it is waterproof as it survived being lost in a lake for a couple hours, the hinge is durable, I know I flopped on it enough times that it would have broken if it was going to. The speakers are wildly loud and good. Straight up works as well as a high quality drug store Bluetooth speaker and I never heard bad distortion even at the highest volume I turned it to, I never needed to turn it up all the way. I loaded my MP3s on it and used the heck out of it's music player which does pale in comparison to the iPod software or the Spotify interface but it worked perfectly. The camera is pretty mid, captures photos and video on par with phones from 2010 but if you want to send a video via text that requires forethought as you need to record it as an attachment otherwise the video file will be too big. Receiving pictures and videos can be difficult too, if a sender puts more than one image or a large video (over 1024kb) the attachment has to be downloaded to be viewed and that is best done on a computer since the file system on the phone is weird and doesn't always open the right downloaded pictures. Downloading PDF documents and viewing those is a breeze and was useful to me as I needed to download and navigate schematics often. Email is difficult since modern security doesn't allow direct logins on this interface, you'll need to create a one time key on a computer to authenticate this phone but once you're in it works great. Browsing the web is again difficult as some websites are built like something that isn't built well and won't work on this phone. A lot do though including Wikipedia and YouTube, reddit does not work. The calendar and alarm clock both work better than anything else I've used though you are limited to system sounds for the alarms. I love this phone but due to a recent job I've had to get a smartphone, on that note this is a great intermediate device when switching from apple to android since it makes you think about how to use it. 10/10 will go back to this phone if I can later into this job. Review Title: When I received this phone, it was still someone else’s it seems
Review Content: When I received this phone, it was still someone else’s it seems. It was set to Spanish and still had another persons info in it. Don’t know how that could’ve possibly been cleared to resell but here we are! Luckily the reset pin was set to the default (0000) so after translating the menus, I eventually figured out how to reset it. Other than this strange issue, I’d say this is one of the best flip phones I’ve had. The biggest issue I have found is, when you add custom ringtones (via plugging it into your computer and moving files) the files do not actually play the song file once they’re in the phone. To fix this, instead of setting your ringtone in the settings, you just need to go to the files and set it that way. Unfortunately there doesn’t seem to be a way around this for notification tones, so you’re stuck with the default ones. I was happy to see that it could handle large photo files though! If not for the sound file issues, I would rate this 4 stars! 5 stars if amazon wasn’t lying about the extensive testing and factory reset they were supposed to do. It seems like other people had this issue as well. Next time, I’ll buy it new instead. Sorry, we failed to record your vote. Please try again Sorry, We failed to report this review. Please try again

Product Title: Amazon.com: Kyocera Duraxe E4830 Epic AT&T Flip Smart Phone 16GB Rugged PTT Wi-Fi LTE Black (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: El mio llegó con un golpe perceptible en la parte izquierda del dispositivo, 2 rasguños grandes que
Review Content: El mio llegó con un golpe perceptible en la parte izquierda del dispositivo, 2 rasguños grandes que si eran perceptibles a distancia. Como el mismo vendedor dice, parece ser un teléfono resistente. Lo que me hace pensar que estos rayones no fueron hechos por descuido sino por algo un poco más contundente. Fuera de este aspecto que realmente me incomoda, trataré de dar una reseña útil para los posibles interesados en este producto. 1.- Se escuchan perfecto las llamadas. Y aparentemente está desbloqueado para todos los servicios de telefonía en la región. 2.- Es resistente, como ya dije es un teléfono que parece resistente y no se siente hueco o barato. 3.- Tiene cierta calidad; Kyocera es marca japonesa así que no es un producto de baja calidad, es totalmente para uso profesional. 4.- las teclas se sienten excelentes; Comparado con otros modelos como el CAT Flip s22 o los nokia flip actuales. Este se lleva el premio al ser exactas y precisas, te acostumbras de inmediato a la forma de escritura. 5.- Tiene configuración en español. Aunque hay algunos errores de traducción es completamente legible esta configuración 6.- El sonido es excelente en los altavoces, casi es como uno de esos sony ericcson de antaño. 7.- Conexión Wi-fi. El teléfono tiene configuración para configuración de internet inalámbrico a un ruter. 8.- El diseño del teléfono es excelente parece que vale cada centavo. (excepto por el logo de AT&T, que me molesta personalmente, arruina todo) 9.- teclas programables: Tiene distintas teclas en los bordes y dentro del mismo teléfono que tienen funciones programables, puedes acceder a configuración , conectividad y reproductor de música fácilmente programando estas teclas ( incluyendo una naranja que es la tecla SOS). 1.- La batería; Conectado al Wi-Fi la batería dura aproximadamente 8 horas, quizá menos. Sin el wifi o datos moviles conectado dura casi un día, pero no más. 2.- Constantemente tienes que cuidar de la batería (física); Me explico, hay una función dentro del teléfono que te recomienda activar que es "cuidado de la batería". Esto hace que cuando lo conectes toda la noche o por un tiempo prolongado solo cargue al 80% Para no dañar la batería con picos de energía. Toda esta experiencia resulta molesta; Debido a que no deberíamos preocuparnos por activar este tipo de funciones en pleno 2024. 4.- La red móvil (datos móviles). Dure una semana sin datos móviles debido a que no hay una explicación clara de como configurarlos en el empaque. Al parecer hay que configurar manualmente la red móvil introduciendo una contraseña de la misma compañía, entre otros datos; información que esta disponible en linea. Con ningún celular tuve que hacer esto antes. Me pareció nuevamente, algo reamente extraño para estos tiempos. 5.- Configuraciones: Hay una serie de configuraciones molestas que pareciera que hay que hacer cada que quieres utilizar el teléfono. Me refiero a entrar a configuración de iluminación de pantalla, encender y apagar redes. 6.- La multimedia; el reproductor de música es pésimo con opciones limitadas, solo reproducción aleatoria y siguiente. Afortunadamente tiene un puerto Jack para conectar audífonos, pero todo esto se va al traste debido a la muy mala calidad de audio en la que reproduce, es increíble. 7.- Whatsapp; se puede descargar whatsapp ya que el teléfono cuenta con navegador web. Por tanto puedes entrar a descargar esta aplicación (tiene algo similar al Android 10). Sin embargo una vez descargado empieza la pesadilla. Puedes conectarlo como dispositivo vinculado. Lo cual es bueno sin embargo la navegación es desastrosa, no hay forma de navegar por los chats y al seleccionar una conversación esta no se abre. Puedes descargar aplicaciones de apuntador pero la verdad son riesgosos y difíciles de instalar mediante un software que no tiene que ver con Kyocera. 8.- El peso; el dispositivo en sí es algo pesado como para llevarlo en un bolsillo del pantalón, es un bulto que termina posicionándose de manera horizontal en tu bolsillo y te llegas a sorprender a ti mismo acomodándolo para que no te moleste al caminar. 9.- El correo electrónico; Nunca pude configurar el correo electrónico en este dispositivo, ni gmail, ni outlook, ni un correo de la empresa en donde trabajo. Desconozco el motivo, realmente intenté configurarlo. Por esta razón no fue útil en la oficina. 10.- función e compartir internet: Esta opción no funciona el dispositivo lanza una leyenda (que desaparece de inmediato) que te avisa que esa función no funciona correctamente. Es realmente extraño. 11.- La lampara; El teléfono tiene una función de linterna pero es realmente poco lo que ilumina. Por lo menos comparado con otros dispositivos similares es increíble que ilumine tan mal. (también tiene una opción para parpadear con esta luz) 12.- Pantalla interna y externa; si no te molesta que no puedas cambiar la configuración de visualización de pantalla externa o interna entonces no es un punto negativo. Pero algo básico en un teléfono hoy en día es la personalización de las pantallas. En este caso el teléfono no cuenta más que con funciones de quitar y poner el reloj o la visualización de la fecha. Pero poco más no hay manera de configurar el idioma (por default en ingles) de la pantalla externa o la forma en que se muestra el reloj en la pantalla. En resumen; era un entusiasta de los Feature Phone; estos últimos años intenté encontrar un modelo que se amoldara a mis necesidades que no son muchas. Y tras varios nokia (modernos) , un cat flip s22, varios BLU, etc. El que acabó con mi paciencia fue este teléfono. Hay que aceptar que estamos condenados a subsistir mediante placas aburridas de vidrio negro. Me rindo. Review Title: Sound quality is the main reason I’d recommend them
Review Content: Sound quality is the main reason I’d recommend them. Bass is punchy and satisfying, vocals stay clear, and the overall balance works well across pop, hip-hop, podcasts, and YouTube. They can get loud without sounding harsh, and if you like a fuller low-end, they deliver that “fun” sound JBL is known for. Noise isolation is decent from the ear tips alone, and any added noise control features depend on the version you have, but for the price point they do a good job helping you stay focused in everyday noisy environments. Battery life has also been reliable. I don’t feel like I’m constantly charging them, and the case makes it easy to top up between uses. Controls are simple and responsive, and the earbuds feel like something you can toss in a bag and use daily without babying them. Overall, the JBL Tune Buds 2 are a practical, good-sounding choice if you want strong bass, clear vocals, stable Bluetooth, and a comfortable fit at a reasonable price. Review Title: ##### Renewed-Excellent Arrived in Perfect Condition with 100% Battery Health/Capacity
Review Content: ##### Renewed-Excellent Arrived in Perfect Condition with 100% Battery Health/Capacity I ordered an Amazon Renewed refurbished iPhone Air 256GB (unlocked) from Amazon in March 2026. Apple initially released the iPhone Air in September 2025, so any given unit couldn't be more than 6 months old. For that reason I took a chance by ordering a unit in "Excellent" condition, rather than "Premium" condition, for $80 less. (As of a week later, Excellent units are even cheaper compared to Premium units.) The phone arrived in perfect condition. Not a scratch on it. And even better: its battery health/capacity is 100%, which is far better than Amazon promises for "Excellent" condition units ("Battery: >80% of original battery life"). The OS reports that the phone was first used in October 2025, and only went through 7 battery cycles. So, it seems like it's a unit that someone bought new and returned almost immediately. In my experience, these "Amazon Renewed" phones come from a variety of vendors. My iPhone Air came from "T4C We Track Serial Numbers." --Yes, weird name (maybe a warning to buyers who might try to swap phones by returning a different phone?). But they provided a perfect product. As to the iPhone Air, I settled on it after trying a few different phones, including the iPhone 15 Pro Max, the iPhone 16e, the iPhone 16 Plus, and the iPhone 17e. I had always thought of the iPhone Air as a terrible compromise: larger (but not largest) screen, lesser camera, and far less battery capacity. However, I wanted a slightly larger screen than the standard 6.1 inches, and I don't really prioritize my phone's camera.
