Product Title: Amazon.com: Soundcore Sport X10 True Wireless Bluetooth 5.2 Workout Headphones, Rotatable Ear Hooks, Deep Bass, IPX7 Waterproof, Sweatproof, 32H Play, Sport Earbuds, Gym, Running (Renewed) : Electronics
Review Title: My wife got these for Fathers Day which I have had these now for a few months and these are just fab
Review Content: My wife got these for Fathers Day which I have had these now for a few months and these are just fabulous. I wanted some BT earbuds for my PC gaming as well as my IPad Air 4/Iphone SE3 and happy with the price/performance. I wanted the red since black is hard to find IF they come off (mine have yet to come off and I love the ear hooks) since people at work have Apple (or other brands) earbuds which are black and if they loose one (sometimes happens) hard to find in the shade/dark areas hence Red (or white) is easier to find. The fit is wonderful so that at work they stay on my ears and do not fly off which is what I wanted (I have big ear canals) and the BT comes with 5 sizes so very flexible on how they fit. The sound is excellent and I have no latency when gaming on my PC but you can download the Soundcore app and change the mix to your liking which is great. The sound for gaming is also excellent even using steam link on my IPad Air 4 annd also for music/youtube. Be it on th PC, iPad or Phone. There really is no noise canceling which I really don’t care for (I don’t expect earbuds to match headphones honestly) but for my use these work wonderfully. I have worn them out in the rain and they still work great. I get a good 8-9 hrs of use till I charge them (I can go longer) and the case does hold juice so the earbuds can be recharged without being plugged in. It takes a little use to the volume controls for pause/play/fast forward/skip etc but once your use to that it is easy. Review Title: I use the Arctics GameBuds (refurbished) for my pc, and they work great, they’re very comfortable wi
Review Content: I use the Arctics GameBuds (refurbished) for my pc, and they work great, they’re very comfortable with multiple ear tips, easy to setup just a simple usb C dongle, they last right around 12 hours of listening, and they have completely adequate audio. The only issues I have with them are slight connection issues, they don’t stay connected if you’re very far at all away from what they’re connected to, and more importantly, even if I simply put my arm in front of one of them it sometimes disconnects! The other, more glaring issue, is that the software for me was causing serious issues with how I have my audio setup, it was causing issues with discord, recording, and just games in general, I believe this is due to it adding multiple different audio devices to select from in windows. There is a saving grace in this as you don’t even need the software for really anything besides EQ (may be very useful if you, for example, think they’re lacking in bass!) and you can setup controls a bit better, but not necessary to use! Review Title: The original owner of this phone traded/sold it to Amazon (through some process) and Amazon then tur
Review Content: The original owner of this phone traded/sold it to Amazon (through some process) and Amazon then turned around and shipped it directly to me without even removing the Scotch tape that was holding the box closed. When I first opened the Amazon box, I was really relieved. The phone was shipped inside the original OnePlus box and even included the original charger and signature red USB cable. The phone appeared almost brand new, until I went to remove the SIM card tray. As you can see in the attached picture, there is absolutely no way an inspection (professional or otherwise) could have missed that damage. It looked and felt like someone had been chewing on the SIM tray after the chewing, they may have hit it with a hammer. They did enough damage that the SIM tray release mechanism (that you usually trip with the SIM removal tool) was completely gone. The tray was wedged in so hard, I was concerned for a moment that they may have glued it. At this point I called Amazon. I informed them that this phone is damaged and possibly unusable. Moments before ordering this phone, I stopped at Best Buy and bought an awful Moto phone to hold me over, with the idea that I could return it as soon as my Amazon phone arrived. Since the blatant errors are 100% on Amazon, I had assumed they could get a replacement phone out to me pretty quickly (I even told them I didn't care if it was even the same model as long as it worked). I was wrong. The woman told me that the world's largest store was unable to get me a replacement phone in under 7 days. I was kind of shocked. I then told her that because of their neglegence, I was going to lose $100+ dollars (the return window for the phone would be firmly closed), to which she told me how sorry she was and asked if there was anything else she could help me with. As soon as the call was completed, I finally got the SIM tray out, it was a lot tougher than that little bit of plastic would lead you to believe. When the tray came loose, out flew the previous owner's SIM card as even more proof this phone was never even given a cursory glance. To make matters even worse, I woke up the next day to Best Buy having this exact same unlocked phone (but brand new) selling for $20 less than the "Amazon Renewed" version. I would suggest you consider skipping the renewed by Amazon devices and possibly look for a mom & pop reseller on here instead. The odds are good they could spare a few minutes to examine the phone before sending it out. Lastly, OnePlus makes great phones (which do work fine on Verizon), please don't let my long winded review turn you off.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Review Title: In case anyone else is considering doing the same on an N10 (billie) be aware the T-Mobile (BE88CB)
Review Content: In case anyone else is considering doing the same on an N10 (billie) be aware the T-Mobile (BE88CB) and a Metro (BE88CF) version of the firmware is later than the OxygenOS 10.5.7 that UBPorts needs to install over, BUT there is no MSM tool to roll these back to the earlier firmware version. I tried dirty flashing UBports over stock and it soft-bricked after the bootloader. had to EDL flash to get it working again. Spent weeks trying to hack a MSM tool to get it to flash Global (BE86AA) 10.5.7. Got it 90% working but it wasn't enough to get ubports to take. I couldn't find a single other person who was able to make it work either. Moral of the story is if you get a Tmobile / Metro version of this phone, send it back and don't waste your time like I did, lol I tried forcing the install and it soft-bricked after the bootloader. Review Content: To use this on any network other than T Mobile, you will need to have you Nord N10 unlocked from T Mobile's network. If the phone is shipped to you locked, then you will have to either return it, or activate it on T Mobile and then satisfy their device unlock criteria: Unlock Eligibility for Mobile Devices on Postpaid Plans The device must have been active on the T‑Mobile network for at least 40 days on the requesting line. If the device was financed or leased through T‑Mobile then all payments must be satisfied and the device must be paid in full. If the device is associated with a canceled account, then the account balance must be zero. T‑Mobile may request proof of purchase or additional information in its discretion and certain other exceptions may apply. Unlock Eligibility for Mobile Devices on Prepaid Plans At least 365 days must have passed since the device was activated on the T Mobile network. If the device was activated less than 365 days ago, then the Prepaid account associated with the device must have had more than $100 in refills during that period for each line active on the account. In addition, more than 14 days must have passed since the device was purchased. No more than 2 mobile device unlocks have been complete per line of service in the last 12 months. Review Title: For the money, I'm not sure that this can be beat
Review Content: For the money, I'm not sure that this can be beat. Plenty of RAM for any non-gaming app out there, very responsive touchscreen, bright, great speakers and mic. I usually root my phones and also use 3rd party home apps, but with this phone I haven't seen a need for either. I'm a Metro customer and the SIM swap from my old phone worked without issue from the Metro app with no charges to my account. I also appreciate the fact that OnePlus did not include a ridiculous amount of bloat. Overall great value and I couldn't be happier! Oh, I purchased 2 and they both came without a single scratch anywhere. The one downside is that you will have to purchase a Warp charger. I have 2 for home and 2 for the car. Both are 3rd party warp chargers from Amazon and they have no problem hitting the 30w charge rate. They were significantly cheaper than OEM. Killer! Review Title: When I first got these they worked as described in my original review below
Review Content: When I first got these they worked as described in my original review below. But after about 2 months the battery life in left one started falling off a cliff. I contacted Anker and they replaced them immediately. The replacement pair worked well, but after a couple months the left one again started running out of charge after an hour or so. The right one was down, but would still go 4 hours. Not good, but better than the left one. I reached out to Anker and sure enough, like others have reported here, the warranty is only 90 days from date of original purchase. This was stated nowhere in the original listing, but there was actually no warranty info shown in the original listing, so, whatever. Currently, the left one - in spite of showing as fully charged in the app - only lasts about 5 minutes. The right one goes about an hour. Anker customer support was quick to respond, but wouldn't help. So, while it looks like these "refurb" units currently aren't available at the moment, I'd suggest you don't buy even the new versions of these. They just aren't reliable enough. I don't mean like "Surprise! I got you some ear buds!", rather, I mean I wasn't expecting much out of these - they're TINY, and while the specs say they'll last up to 10 hours on bluetooth, most reviews here said they were getting a lot less than that. I set them up (a bit fiddly with the app) and fully charged them. First night the right one lasted about 3 hours and the left of only about 5 hours. Not good. Thought I'd give them one more chance and fully recharged them and the second night they both made it about 6 hours. Okay, getting better. Third night? I managed to get a full 9 hours of sleep (don't be jelly) and when I woke up they were happily chugging along with an audiobook - with 20% charge remaining. They've been like this since. Surprise! -They're TINY ( I've got nimble fingers and these buggers are a challenge to not drop on the floor when handling them) -The charging case is completely impossible to use in the dark (Which way does it open and which ear bud goes into which charging slot....?) -Getting them paired to your device the first time is fiddly (The app you have to use for this isn't plainly obvious in any app store) -They're TINY (once you get your ear tips chosen they just pop right into your ears and they stay put and don't stick out at all - perfect for this side sleeper!) -They sound VERY clear (they're not for listening to thumping bass music, but for audiobooks, podcasts & sleepscape music they're PERFECT) -They got to a VERY low volume (it's odd that most headphones don't actually sound clear at extremely low volumes. These do) -Good battery life (give them a few full charge cycles and keep the volume levels low these should work all night) -They don't loudly announce "BATTERY LOW!" when the battery gets low. (You toggle this off and on in the app, but it's off by default) Can't speak to their longevity, but a couple weeks in and they seem stable. They're solidly built and seem like they'll last awhile. I'll definitely report back here with an update if any quality issues arise. If you need some astonishingly unobtrusive sleep buds just get these. Have patience while getting them set up, and give them a few full charge cycles and you should be all set. Review Title: I never once jonesed for an Apple Watch — mainly because they are huge (and pricey for me) — so I al
Review Content: I never once jonesed for an Apple Watch — mainly because they are huge (and pricey for me) — so I always settled for the smallest and least expensive Fitbits instead (I’ve had 3 different models). They were sufficient, but the last one was a big disappointment. So I took another look at the smallest and lowest priced Apple Watch. I found the latest model 40mm SE 3, used but in excellent condition, for $180 on Amazon. I would’ve never guessed it was used at all if it wasn’t for the scotch tape on the packaging — and it appears to even still be under the original warranty. Awesome! The differences between this and the higher-end models were things I didn’t need (like slightly faster battery charging time, more time between charges, ECG app, SpO2 sensor, water resistance, etc.). PROS: I like the wide array of watch faces and customization options for most of them. My personal favorite is the one that includes the option for a 5-hour weather forecast. If you install other faces, you can easily switch between them directly from the watch. I have one with a second hand ready to swipe to for times when I want or need that. One of my favorite features is the ability to set and name alarms by speaking it: “set alarm at 1pm to start getting ready for appointment.” And likewise set and name countdown timers: “set timer to check laundry in 1 hour.” I use this often and it works better than it does on even the iPhone or iPad. The one feature that justified the price for me was the crash/fall detection and emergency SOS. I will be 70 next year and although I’ve never had an issue that required any of this so far (knock on wood), you never know. CONS: I was originally not thrilled that I’d have to charge it every day instead of having it last several days (like my Fitbits did). But I found that I easily get thru a full day (plus) after an hour of charge time. So now I just set an alarm to remind me to charge it every night before bed, so now it’s a habit and no problem. That said, the documentation says it runs up to 18 hours on a full charge so I’m not sure how I manage over 24 hours without even resorting to low-power mode. From what I understand, the 18 hour figure is ‘typical use’ and I guess don’t use it ‘typically.’: I don’t use it for music or phone calls, I have the display on the lowest brightness (which is plenty bright), and I don’t use the “always on” setting for the display. So no complaints there! The Health app on the iPhone that interfaces with the watch could be more organized, but the watch itself certainly does more than a standard watch and does many of those things easily — once you know how. One of the things I truly dislike is the silicone band, but that applied to the Fitbit as well. I find them all intensely uncomfortable, too fiddly to put on and take off, and the Apple one pinches me every time I slip the tail end of the strap into the slot that goes under the band. The bands also look too wide on my narrow wrist. But it was simple to find something better on Amazon for everyday wear as well as a band for dressier occasions. They are also a lot easier to swap out than the mechanism on the last two Fitbit watches I had. It’s still a pretty darn big watch, but if it wasn’t, it wouldn’t be as useful either. And it only took me about a week to get used to the size which was faster than I expected. BOTTOM LINE: I’ve been using it for almost 3 weeks now and have been very happy with it. It takes a little bit of getting used to and there are a ton of settings between the iPhone interface and the watch itself, but I’ve had good luck Googling for help with most of those. And once I found the settings I liked, I hardly deal with any of that anymore. If you use an iPhone or iPad, the interface is familiar enough — all things considered — but I also enjoy solving puzzles so that makes figuring it out less bothersome to me. The cons I mentioned aren’t anything I can fairly deduct stars for because they came as no surprise. That is, I knew what I was in for before I got it. And I was more often pleasantly surprised. At this stage the only thing that would ding stars for me is if it goes bad too quickly. [More](javascript:void(0))[Hide](javascript:void(0)) There was a problem filtering reviews. They were sufficient, but the last one was a big disappointment. So I took another look at the smallest and lowest priced Apple Watch. I found the latest model 40mm SE 3, used but in excellent condition, for $180 on Amazon. I would’ve never guessed it was used at all if it wasn’t for the scotch tape on the packaging — and it appears to even still be under the original warranty. Awesome! If you install other faces, you can easily switch between them directly from the watch. I have one with a second hand ready to swipe to for times when I want or need that. One of my favorite features is the ability to set and name alarms by speaking it: “set alarm at 1pm to start getting ready for appointment.” And likewise set and name countdown timers: “set timer to check laundry in 1 hour.” I use this often and it works better than it does on even the iPhone or iPad. The one feature that justified the price for me was the crash/fall detection and emergency SOS. I will be 70 next year and although I’ve never had an issue that required any of this so far (knock on wood), you never know. I was originally not thrilled that I’d have to charge it every day instead of having it last several days (like my Fitbits did). But I found that I easily get thru a full day (plus) after an hour of charge time. So now I just set an alarm to remind me to charge it every night before bed, so now it’s a habit and no problem. That said, the documentation says it runs up to 18 hours on a full charge so I’m not sure how I manage over 24 hours without even resorting to low-power mode. From what I understand, the 18 hour figure is ‘typical use’ and I guess don’t use it ‘typically.’: I don’t use it for music or phone calls, I have the display on the lowest brightness (which is plenty bright), and I don’t use the “always on” setting for the display. So no complaints there! The Health app on the iPhone that interfaces with the watch could be more organized, but the watch itself certainly does more than a standard watch and does many of those things easily — once you know how. One of the things I truly dislike is the silicone band, but that applied to the Fitbit as well. I find them all intensely uncomfortable, too fiddly to put on and take off, and the Apple one pinches me every time I slip the tail end of the strap into the slot that goes under the band. The bands also look too wide on my narrow wrist. But it was simple to find something better on Amazon for everyday wear as well as a band for dressier occasions. And it only took me about a week to get used to the size which was faster than I expected. I’ve been using it for almost 3 weeks now and have been very happy with it. Review Title: When it came in, I charged it, gave it to her, told her to set it up, and have fun
Review Content: When it came in, I charged it, gave it to her, told her to set it up, and have fun. After a day of setting it up, she told me she wasn’t gonna use it until she got a case. In that time, I started to play with it; testing the front screen the way I planned on using it. I was right, it is my ideal phone. For just watching a quick video, sending a quick text, scrolling the web while on the crapper, and switching to the next song, the phone closed is all I need. After playing with it for 2 days, my iPhone 12 Mini is too damn big. If you’re into gaming, this phone will play anything. If you’re into emulation, it will play EVERYTHING upscaled. Couple this with the GameSir g8, and you have a beast of a gaming phone. Back to my wife. She’s been using it as her daily driver for around a month, and while she was hesitant at first cuz she loved the apple evo system, but after a few weeks and a Galaxy Watch 4 later, she is happy that she switched over. She loves that she can play Burnout Revenge (her favorite game) whenever/wherever. She loves the compact size, and uses a belt clip case like it’s 2005 all over again. Her only issue is the shit battery compared to her iPhone. When she’s working and not using it, it lasts her all day, but when she has downtime, it dies almost instantly. So, if that’s a concern for you, either carry a charger or a portable bank as well. Review Title: I bought this as an Amazon Renewed Premium, shipped from the Networkstore
Review Content: I bought this as an Amazon Renewed Premium, shipped from the Networkstore. Even though my phone keeps telling me that I can have 12 months of AI Advanced Upgrade, it never lets me enroll. Amazon or the Networkstore don't tell you that you don't get this benefit that Google offers. That is a two-hundred-dollar offer that I can't take advantage of. That is the only reason for the one star off. Someone evidently already used this offer for this phone. I love the AI tools in this phone. I like using Gemini. It is probably a little more direct and less friendly than other AIs I have used. But it may be more accurate, because it provides the backup for its answer. The photo AI tools are good, but limited. It has restrictions with using people in your AI images. Overall it is fun to play with, but still a little frustrating with getting the prompts to work as you want. I like all the little hidden features, like tapping the back of the phone for a set action. Activating Gemini anywhere you are and on whatever app or page you are on. The phone hearing a song that is playing in the background and showing the title of the song on your lock screen. There is so much to like about this phone. I am excited to continue exploring and using the phone. As far as the Amazon Renewed Premium, I wanted to make sure that I got a phone that was in like new condition and had the one-year warranty that the Renewed Premium offers. So you pay less than a brand new phone, but more than a typical renewed phone. I think it was worth it. The only thing I didn't think through and they didn't let you know that you can't take advantage of the 12 months of AI Advantage from Google. Other than that, I would recommend this phone and I would recommend Amazon Renewed Premium. Review Title: I own three of these Belkin chargers
Review Content: I own three of these Belkin chargers. Two of them are the 3 in 1, and this review is for the 2 in 1. The pad below also works great for a wireless AirPods case or a second phone. The charge speed is as fast as I’d expect and this is easy to use. The cord length is sufficient allowing one to manage complicated night stand, kitchen, or office situations. The power brick is a little large given the size of this product and that’s sort of disappointing since it does less than the larger 3 in 1 Belkin offerings. There a few other ways this version is inferior to the larger ones. For whatever reason, the plastic on this version seems to attract lint and dust in a way that the larger versions I own have not. It doesn’t matter ultimately, but it’s an observation nonetheless which suggests that even though the charge and magnet strength is the same, perhaps this is made out of different materials. Review Title: I am coming from an iPhone 16 Pro Max, and honestly I've gotten quite bored with Apple's "walled gar
Review Content: I am coming from an iPhone 16 Pro Max, and honestly I've gotten quite bored with Apple's "walled garden" iOS. I have been eyeing foldable phones for a while and preferred a phone with clean android is, good support, and an unlocked bootloader if I wanted to use custom ROMs. This left one clear choice - the Google Pixel 10 Pro Fold ​The Tensor G5 Chip: initially, I was concerned about this one, as most high end Android devices stick with the tried and true Qualcomm Snapdragon SoC. My concerns were definitely unwarranted. This chip was made by Google in partnership with TSMC (the same company that makes Apple’s chips). It’s estimated to be over 30% faster than the previous Tensor G4 chip and it is definitely no slouch. It runs buttery smooth for all the tasks I throw at it, primarily watching videos, writing emails, and web browsing. I have not tried gaming as I am not an avid gamer. Had I been looking for bleeding edge ray trace enabled gaming performance, id probably have gone with a Qualcomm equipped phone. Ingress protection - this device is ​IP68 rated. This is a big one. This phone is the first foldable in North America with this high of a rating. It’s fully dust-resistant, which was the "Achilles' heel" of previous folding phones. ​The "Gearless" Hinge: It works great and is rated to last over 10 years of folding ( tested for 200000 folds, or 50 times a day EVERY day for over 10 years. ​Weight & Bulk: it is definitely not light, weighing in at a hefty 258 grams. In comparison, my iPhone 16 pro Max is 227 grams. This means that this phone is 13% heavier. With all that said, I still do not find this phone overly heavy or distracting at all. It feels premium and is built solid as a tank. ​Display: the cover display measures in at a respectable 6.4" and is much wider than, say, a similar competitor such as the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 6. The inner (8") screens give up to 3,000 nits of peak brightness, making it one of the best phones for outdoor use in direct sunlight. the cameras on the Fold not quite on par with the standard Pixel 10 Pro or Pro XL, but this is expected in a foldable . For day to day nonprofessional uses, the camera is still quite good, but if you want the BEST cameras, id go with iPhone, Samsung, or Google pixel 10 pro. ​Capacity: the phone has a 5,015mAh battery. Coming from an iPhone, I found no issues with battery life, which says a lot considering apple products always have great batteries. This Google device holds its own ​PixelSnap (Qi2) : this phone has magnetic wireless charging (similar to MagSafe), which makes it easy to snap on accessories and chargers. This may not seem like a lot, but once you get used to it, you will never want to go without it. I went with an unlocked renewed version of this phone as it's been on the market for about 6 months now, and I didn't want to use my phone carrier to upgrade as I anticipate using my carrier upgrade perks to get the rumored iPhone foldable at some point in the future. Let me say, the phone I received was immaculate. I literally could find no indications of wear or prior use. The third party seller, SoonerSoft Electronics, shipped the phone overnight and it was received promptly the following day. I will definitely add this seller as a favorite! This phone is wonderful for tech enthusiasts, people looking for a capable multitasking phone, using integrated AI tools, and social /multimedia consumption. If this fits your uses, you can't go wrong!       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))       8 people found this helpful Helpful  Sending feedback...Thank you for your feedback. A nice surprise is that they charge super fast (much faster than my old Beats) and pressing the "On" button once will tell you exactly how much battery is left. Review Title: Returned the watch
Review Content: Returned the watch. The microphone intermittently functioned, the scratches were bothering me, and new watches are only $100 more than this beat up thing. Yes, $100 isn’t cheap, but overall it was worth the extra cost. My new Apple Watch 7 has a larger screen and no signs of use. It’s worth the upgrade, especially when Amazon describes the refurbished watch “like new” when that is clearly not the case. Calls from the refurbished watch only worked half the time, and the speaker sounded muffled. Just pony up for a new watch, which are discounted right now for an apple 7, and be happy. Hope this updates helps you decide. Ok, the watch costs less than new, but that’s about where the good stuff ends. It did include a usb charger (Samsung brand! 😟) generic charging cable, off-brand white strap, and poorly packaged in a generic white box. Literally nothing was done to “recondition” the watch. First thing I had to do was clean off the former user’s grime that coated the watch back (yuck!). This took some soap, water, and a toothbrush to clean out the little crevices. Screen and case came with minor scratches overall, with one more annoying, more pronounced screen scratch that really bugs me. Battery was completely depleted, which is not good for lithium batteries. C’mon, for the money you could at least clean and charge the thing! It’s not in terrible shape, but very clearly used. It certainly was not refurbished in any way that I can tell. Imagine buying the watch from your mom after she wore it for a year and you get the idea about my watch’s condition. Not abused, but certainly used. I’m torn. This was not a great purchase, and I’m left wondering if its worth the $150 less than new price. Hard to say. Just don’t believe the product description claiming “appears new” because that is far from the truth. Set your expectations accordingly if you purchase from the “Camera Guyz”. They just take the watch, toss it in a nondescript box with whatever knockoff bits they have laying around, and mail it to you. Look, you’re still paying a lot of money, so there’s no reason not to expect a quality product. Amazon says I have a 90 day warranty, so there’s time (accidental pun) to evaluate it further. Yes it works. Yes, I will eventually add more wear and tear to the watch when wearing. Yes, the “appears new” description is complete fiction. Overall value is debatable. One star for inaccurate condition description and an annoying screen scratch. Review Title: Great for the price! I’ve used various Noise Canceling headphones from Soundcore, JBL, AKG, Sennheis
Review Content: Great for the price! I’ve used various Noise Canceling headphones from Soundcore, JBL, AKG, Sennheiser and Beats… all at different price points, and none work quite as well as Bose. The difference isn’t earth shattering… but it’s noticeable. I have zero fatigue after long plane flights and find myself adjusting volume less between flying and walking between terminals. The real test for me is how the headphones sound as you close a car door, or put away dishes, and these handle both tasks well! The sound signature on Q35’s is arguably better than newer models, although warm and un-exciting. Unless you need a Google button, save yourself some money and buy the base model 35’s over the 35 ii’s. Video latency was imperceptible for me, and there are plenty of aftermarket ear pads and accessories. Battery life for any bose headphones seems to suffer. And for what it’s worth, I would not pay full retail, but I would pay the refurb price in a heartbeat. [More](javascript:void(0))[Hide](javascript:void(0)) There was a problem filtering reviews. Review Title: For $65, these earbuds are a steal
Review Content: For $65, these earbuds are a steal. I got it excellent condition and I found no scratches or blemishes in the case or in the earbuds. When it came it looked just like new aside from the box it came in. It even came with eartip sizes and as expected, it came with the charger. Aside it from being used, it was easy to pair with my samsung phone and has a ton of settings with Galaxy Wearable app. Ambient sound technology is also pretty good and you can tweak the ambience levels too. One hiccup is the latency is noticeable (literally just pausing and unpausing will have latency) for this reason I don't recommend these for gaming on a computer. I'd recommend these strictly for phone use and skip these if you plan to use them on PC. I also did a lot of research and found MANY people complained about it not fitting or hurting. In my case, it doesn't hurt and for fitment I just put on the largest ear tip. I guess it's varied depending on ear size and I didn't have issues. All things aside, overall great earbuds. Review Title: I never was able to get good bass response when listening to music, even though I followed all of th
Review Content: I never was able to get good bass response when listening to music, even though I followed all of the steps indicated on the manufacturer's web site. I tried all of the different tips that came with the earbuds, but none of them provided a secure fit. I would invariably have to adjust the fit while outside, just doing regular yard work, nothing very strenuous. Adjusting them also meant affecting the playback, as there is almost no way to touch them without doing so. Sometimes this means stopping and starting playback (minor inconvenience), but often this "touch" was interpreted by the buds as a skip to the next episode (a real pain, since I had to go back to the phone adjust the app to pick up where I wanted to be on the previous episode). Finally the fit was so poor that one fell out, and has been lost forever. After looking for the earbud for a good while, I gave up; they aren't worth keeping, anyway, Never buying earbuds from Samsung again. Review Title: This is a review both for the AirPods Pro (2nd gen), but also for the Amazon Renewal program
Review Content: This is a review both for the AirPods Pro (2nd gen), but also for the Amazon Renewal program. I'm not bought into the Apple ecosystem and have no plans to do so, but I won a pair of these at a work event, and they changed my life. Seriously I'm so much more productive because I don't have to listen to the loud project manager sitting next to me on calls all day - that's how good the active noise canceling is. If that's what you're looking for in a pair of earbuds, I've tried and failed to find anything comparable that didn't sacrifice on some other criterion (battery life first and foremost). But here's the deal about the Amazon Renewal thing... I got another pair of honest-to-goodness AirPod Pros in perfect condition with all the accessories at a sizeable discount (though as I write this the same product sold by Apple is discounted down to $190, which is what I paid for this pair :) ). While Amazon isn't my favorite company, and I've had both good and bad experiences with it, I'm happy to help reduce their (and by extension, other companies') environmental footprint by buying a perfectly good product at a cheaper rate just because somebody else's expectations of it weren't met. The packaging of all the accessories was great, the product itself was, as mentioned, indistinguishable from a brand-new set, and I was incredibly happy with them. Now, after finding out that my wife is one of the unfortunate people who are susceptible to vertigo from using noise-canceling headphones, it didn't make sense for us to have 2 pairs, so I decided to return the set I bought Renewed. After a little bit of uncertainty around the return process (the UPS driver will bring a printed label for my otherwise unlabeled package? Review Title: I scored these at nearly half off — crazy deal
Review Content: I scored these at nearly half off — crazy deal. And because I saved that much, I had enough left to grab the Protect Plus 3-Year Plan. That covers accidental drops, spills, and even mechanical/electrical breakdowns after the manufacturer warranty ends. If something goes sideways, they repair or replace it — no drama. For headphones I’m using daily, that kind of peace of mind is a no-brainer. Mic quality is surprisingly solid too. I’ve used it for calls, Discord, and meetings — everyone said I came through clear without that muffled or cheap Bluetooth mic sound. Not studio quality, but way better than I expected for this price. They’re lightweight and super comfortable — no clamp fatigue, even after long sessions. I’ve worn these for hours at a time without needing a break. One feature I really like is the ability to stay connected to both my phone and my PC at the same time. No need to keep switching back and forth — it just handles both seamlessly. I can take a call on my phone, then go right back to music or Zoom on my desktop without touching anything. Bluetooth vs wired? Here’s how it works: when you use them over Bluetooth, you get everything — active noise cancelling (ANC), transparency/ambient mode, touch controls, built-in mic, auto on/off, and voice assistant support. But the second you plug in a 3.5mm cable, the headphones switch to passive mode — meaning all of that shuts off. No ANC, no transparency mode, no touch controls, no mic, no auto on/off. You basically just get basic wired audio like old-school headphones. It still works in a pinch, but you're giving up all the smart features. That’s why I mostly roll wireless — it’s just a better experience. Battery life is excellent — I’ve been getting about 40 hours with ANC off, and 30+ hours with it on. It charges back to full in around 2 hours. Plus, it’s got auto on/off when you unfold or fold the headphones, which helps conserve battery and adds to that premium feel. Bottom line — clean sound, smart features, solid mic, long battery life, lightweight and comfy, and backed by a strong warranty. And at nearly 50% off? No regrets. I am tracking battery usage throughout the day with different levels of use- screen open and closed, dormant or playing videos - and it seems as though this particular device doesn't deplete battery any more than would be typical for a phone this age. I suspect this particular phone was very gently used to begin with. Example: battery depleted about 10-15% overnight with no use, not plugged in. With heavier usage the battery use goes up to about 10% per hour. Not sure if there's anything I can adjust/disable to make this more efficient. My old phone would give me 1.5 to 2 days of a charge with regular use so this will be an adjustment. The screen is beautiful and easy to see. Samsung is an upgrade overall for me and I am pleased with how smooth it runs. Nice on-screen keyboard, etc. I am not tech savvy so there are probably too many customization options for me personally. I really just want a phone that works well for calls, that I can text on and use internet and maps periodically. This should do the job just fine. No SD storage and no headphone jack. I guess that's becoming customary. The device doesn't seem flimsy at all. That being said, I would get a case ASAP in the event of inadvertent drops - it happens. Signal and connection seem good, as does speaker quality. The fingerprint sensor is on the side near the volume buttons. Not sure I am crazy about this placement and it never registers the first time for me, but I think that's probably a user (me) problem. Overall I had a very good experience buying Renewed. Anyone who is interested in trying a flip smartphone, this is very economical option without a major commitment. I will update my review accordingly if, within 90 days, anything goes haywire on the device. I'm sure its been lightly tossed on the bed, dropped into a pocket, and placed into a purse with other items that most likely caused the cosmetic flaw on the case. The phone has only been open while in use, so only fingers and weather touched the screen. A screen protector has never been applied to the phone. Review Title: judge it as fair to good condition
Review Content: judge it as fair to good condition. There is a great deal of obvious pitting and scratching all around the edges, although not on the screen itself. It is definitely visible from more than 12 inches away. I'll be putting it in a case to protect it, so hopefully that won't matter if it's just cosmetic. I just worry that this phone went through the wringer with it's previous owner. It definitely looks like it's been dropped a few times... I have to say, compared to my current phone, a Galaxy Note 9, also purchased as a refurb over 4 years ago, this one is a disappointment. That one was pristine when I received it. Still looks great due to it being in a case, but the battery is starting to go, doesn't hold a charge very long, and gets really hot, really fast. Also the speaker is going and since I use it for work and do a lot on speakerphone, that's critical for me. I too chose this Galaxy Note 20 as it's the last in the line that has the SD slot. Now I just have to go searching for a user manual online so I can figure out how to transfer all my data and memory/sim/etc. Once I actually, hopefully, get to use it, I'll come back and update my review. Update: I've had this phone for a couple of months now, and to say I'm underwhelmed is putting it mildly. Cosmetically, it definitely was NOT in perfect condition. Very obviously used hard by previous owner. But I can deal with that. What I can't deal with is the poor volume control, the fact that it cuts in and out, and locks up. I find I have to restart it far to often to get it to work. Not what you want in a phone. I use my phone a lot for work and not being able to rely on clear sound is a deal breaker. And it's not like I'm walking around and the signal is fading in and out. I live in an urban area, and talk to others in same area, and half the time I can't hear them or they can't hear me, or the sound cuts in an out. So very annoying. It's going back. I'd better get a full refund or I'm going to be even more ticked. This one was a rip-off in my opinion. Completely opposite experience from my first refurb phone. Review Title: I purchased two of these Samsung S24 Ultra 5G phones using the Amazon Renewed program
Review Content: I purchased two of these Samsung S24 Ultra 5G phones using the Amazon Renewed program. Both were listed as "Excellent" condition, intended to replace my aged out S9+'s. As shown in the photos, the retailer did an excellent job of packaging, supplied both phones with chargers and Sim pin removal tools. I charged both phones, and spent a little over a week validating their software, their sim status, and their IMEI information. The battery cycles and battery life are both as expected. The phones were unlocked, and I could find no defects at all. Once I was satisfied the phones were "Excellent" as described, I took them to my carrier for activation. The activation process was a breeze, and both phones are working amazingly well as was expected. I could not be more please with the Amazon Renewed process, nor the vendor who provided the phones. Although still inside the 90 day return window, I don't expect to have any issues with these high quality Samsung phones. I rate this entire process 5 stars. looking forward to the added features, Android 16 OS, and all else that comes with these phones. I would highly recommend this process if you're goal is to upgrade an aging phone without considering a brand new device. Review Title: great earbuds
Review Content: great earbuds. i bought them to use at work while still being able to have full spacial awareness, and they have been great so far. theyve been so great that i use exclusively these while at home, and on occasion have one on in the car to take calls. battery life is incredible, i have fallen asleep with my white noise playing on loop and wake up with a little battery left. spatial audio is very good, you can change the sound studio different ways to increase the feeling of being in an airy room. my only complaint with these is the touch sensitivity; it requires more pressure than most other brands and there is lag between the press and the function. overall fantastic buy for the price. though they were Renewed, they came in perfect physical condition with the original box in a previously opened state. edit: the spatial audio feature of these is better than the "immersive" audio effect of my Bose QuietComfort Ultra, TBH. these are really good earbuds, but if i had to ask for an improvement, i would like these to have a shorter stem and a more responsive/less laggy touch sensors. It's still the normal life expectancy per full charge, but because it has to charge each bud for so long considering their life span per charge, it runs out of battery after one full bud charge. Zero connection issues so far. (Looking at YOU Raycon) All in all, they're very nice earbuds, and at this price for a renewed pair that'll almost certainly arrive in like-new condition, it's an amazing deal. Product Title: Amazon.com: Samsung Galaxy Buds+ True Wireless Earbud Headphones - Black (Renewed) : Electronics
Review Title: The buds came clean and in an A- grade
Review Content: The buds came clean and in an A- grade.. there were only a few very small scratches on the case, but the buds themselves were clean and perfect. It seems everything that should have been included was indeed there: a variety of ear hooks, tips, a charger, and a manual. As far as comfort goes, the bare ear hooks (which aren't hooks at all) work best for my ears. The others hurt after a while, and having to turn them to secure them in your ear becomes bothersome. I sacrificed a small amount of noise blocking without the tight seal in your ear. If you work out, the hooks are essential. I can verify that even dancing with the barest hooks will cause the buds to slip out. Speaking of noise, these buds block out sound well enough that you might not even need noise cancelling when listening with them. Of course, the ambient noise function allows most sounds to pass though like normal, but it takes a tad bit of time to get used to. If high ambient sound isn't good enough, extra-high should do it. It makes normal sounds (when buds are out) sound louder than they really are, which is good for those with slightly impaired hearing. The ambient sound function works well to the point that I feel in control of whether or not I want to hear somebody. I don't often need to take them out when talking with someone. These buds have fair bass, but I'm used to wall-breaking, ear-tickling bass. Although these buds don't have that, they are still very good. The bass-boost toggle in settings helps this, too. Volume is also very clever here. You often won't need max volume, since they block sound well enough. And the tighter the seal to your ear (with ear hooks), the louder the sound will seem. Review Title: One of the standout features of the JBL Clip 4 is its built-in clip, which allows me to easily attac
Review Content: One of the standout features of the JBL Clip 4 is its built-in clip, which allows me to easily attach the speaker to my clothing or a bag. This has been really convenient and makes it easy to take the speaker with me wherever I go. The speaker is also waterproof and dustproof, which has been great for outdoor use or in damp environments. One aspect of the JBL Clip 4 Portable Speaker that I've been somewhat disappointed with is the battery life. While it's not terrible, I do find that I have to charge it fairly frequently if I'm using it frequently or at high volume. This can be a bit of a hassle, especially when I'm on the go and don't have access to a power source. That being said, the battery life is sufficient for most of my needs and it charges quickly, so it's not a major issue. It's just something to be aware of if you're planning on using the speaker for long periods of time without access to a charger. Overall, I'm really happy with the JBL Clip 4 Portable Speaker and would recommend it to others. It's a small but mighty speaker that has proven to be extremely versatile and convenient. The clip feature and waterproof/dustproof design make it a great choice for anyone in need of a portable speaker for on-the-go use. Review Title: For reference of review, my regular home listening setup includes two 5" JBL LSR305 bookshelf speake
Review Content: For reference of review, my regular home listening setup includes two 5" JBL LSR305 bookshelf speakers and a JL Audio D110 10" subwoofer. I've listened to many genres of music on it, from many flavors of EDM, to rock, metal, bass music, and ambient. It's really quite incredible how the multiple integrated speakers fill a room or open space with an impressive frequency range. The low end is quite punchy. When turned up, you can hear and almost feel a thumpy kick drum or bass line through an interior home wall. To be clear, you won't be feeling any sub bass or other very low frequencies due to the size of the speaker diaphragm, and it would be unfair to expect that. However, what it does put out is, again, impressive. The mid range is strong. Vocals are clear and remain undistorted at higher volumes. Guitars, synthesizers, and percussion come through nicely. Where this speaker unfortunately falls a bit short is the high end. It's particularly noticeable with cymbals: a just-audible distortion and fuzziness, but it's important to remember we're talking about a portable wireless Bluetooth speaker for $100. For the price point, the sound quality is very good. I highly recommend it for sound and portability alone. Sound quality aside, everything else is as advertised and expected. Bluetooth pairing works normally. Apparently this speaker supports JBL's party mode where adjacent JBL speakers can replicate audio from one source to all of them; I haven't tested that feature. Product quality is good. It looks sleek, feels nice in the hand, and the rubber trim is helpful to prevent it from moving about on uneven surfaces. Battery life is good: it will last upwards of 16 hours at low volume as tested by playing calm music during sleep, and recharging with USB-C is speedy! Review Title: About the same time, I purchased a Bose SoundLink Flex
Review Content: About the same time, I purchased a Bose SoundLink Flex. Both have equal performance and are priced with dollars and cents of each other. When I purchase each, I also bought aftermarket silicone speaker protectors (~$12) to ensure a dent-free life and the ability to attach a nice carrying sling/shoulder strap. A good/inexpensive investment. On/off buttons, volume & Bluetooth pairing buttons are located on the Flip 6, however, if one would like to change the default bass and treble tones, you will need to download the JBL Portable app that matches your electronic devices OS platform. I use an iPhone and have had no issues. The app is a basic equalizer control feature one might use in addition to your devices native audio settings. In other reviews and promotional videos, much attention is paid to the waterproof features of JBL’s cylindrical Thermos shaped BT speakers. I suppose this might be relevant if I were to use the speaker while bathing in the tub or shower, however, common sense dictates using a bit more care in where one puts the speaker in the bathroom to begin with. One of the most interesting features is PartyBoost. PartyBoost allows the user to daisy chain other JBl PartyBoost compatible Bluetooth speakers together to play music from a common phone or similar. I assume each speaker would need to be located within a ~26ft radius, which is generally accepted as the average range of Bluetooth antenna technology. Visually, JBL’s Bluetooth speakers are very cool. They come in a variety of colors. My Flip 6 is black, like about everything else I own in personal electronics. JBL even offers camouflage patterns, though I doubt one might catch many deer or elephants with Metallica thrashing away. Perhaps playing tunes to celebrate a good hunt makes more sense. The end caps of all the cylindrical speakers vibrate when passively resonating sound energy from the front firing woofer/tweeter speakers. Visually, it’s fun, although I’m not sure if it’s indicative of anything else other than air being pushed to and fro about the plastic speaker carcass. After using the speaker for a while, I’d say I like it as much as my Bose SoundLink Mini, which is kind of the benchmark for mini Bluetooth speakers. Tiny speaker, big sound, zero distortion. If you are interested in an easy to pair, easy to use, quick charging, long battery life (10-12hrs), great sounding and good looking small Bluetooth speaker, the JBL Flip 6 is a great unit. I purchased this speaker “renewed” at around $96. It arrived in a generic box, with instructions, minus the chunk of paracord one might use as a wrist or back pack attachment. Oh well. In perfect condition. Do spring for the aftermarket silicone bumper. Review Title: ##### The BEST for very small and sensitive ears! But if you need a replacement, good luck!
Review Content: ##### The BEST for very small and sensitive ears! But if you need a replacement, good luck! Its a love/hate relationship with these. When they work, their amazing!!! (These are the Sleepbuds 1, not the 2) But at least 2xs a month they refuse to connect and I jave to go about the extensive process to factory reset them. I find soundcore has better noise canceling, but any other brand (thats not cheap) is too large and hurts my ears. As far as comfort goes, these are the BEST EVER!!! One fell out of my ear while asleep a while ago, and my cat stole it, Ozlo was kind enough to provide a discount to purchase a replacement ear bud.... it shows up with no silicone tip/body... which would have been another 20$ to order, I was not aware. Another thing I was not made aware of before purchasing the replacement sleep Bud was that a computer, not a cell phone is required to activate and pair the replacement sleep bud. It took so long for me to be able to replace the Sleep bud that I had to wait a day and a half to get a ride to the library to spend 4 hours having one of the little old lady Librarians help me figure out how to get their computer to accept having anything plugged into a USB port. Which I completely understand the libraries don't want people using random thumb drives and other things. But in the end Oslo ended up refunding me everything except for the actual cost of the original sleepbuds do to the ridiculous amount of time it took for me to get my replacement earbud delivered and working. Other than that these are the most amazing sleep buds that have ever been made, especially if you have sensitive or very small ears. I truly wish I could leave a five-star review but I would feel bad because that's not 100% accurate especially since they're connectivity issue does not help with relaxing for sleep at night. They have quite a long battery life also. They're just way too expensive for not having any active noise canceling, they're masking sounds that are included with the app that is free with them work very very well [More](javascript:void(0))[Hide](javascript:void(0)) There was a problem filtering reviews. Review Title: ##### Considering one? JSYK "Excellent" is 1 below "Like New"!
Review Content: ##### Considering one? JSYK "Excellent" is 1 below "Like New"! I thought the excellent condition was the best, but it's just 1 step below after I looked it up. There are 4 tiers - Premium(Like New), Excellent, Good, Acceptable. Excellent condition was the best available and for the price and what it is, I'm still happy with my purchase. My Excellent condition S24 came with a small scrape on the bottom left corner of the metal(not the screen & see pictured. White dot on screen is a light reflection) which scraped the Violet color off, and deep around the rear cameras are a few fine pieces of debri that I tried my best to clean out and I did get some out, but the rest got pushed down even further into the crevices. Regardless, a phone case will hide the scratched paint and lens protectors will hide the debri. It's all bound to happen, I know. I already knew I would get a generic wall charger and cable, but I actually got a Samsung fast charging wall charger and a generic charging cable. I also ordered it unlocked, as I have AT&T but am moving and my new location doesn't have good service, and I will need to change it to US Cellular. Note: DO NOT get the T-Mobile one assuming it will work with your US Cellular phone; it will NOT. you need to get an unlocked one. I put my SIM card in and it worked. I am in the updating loop process..just keep installing the updates and eventually you'll get all the patches. This is my 2nd time purchasing a renewed cellphone from Amazon. The process is easy and if you aren't happy with the phone, simply return it and have another one sent. they won't all be perfect but a little effort and you can get a great phone for a fraction of the cost. I had purchased a renewed S10+ a few years ago. I received the wrong color and sent it back and I should have returned the next one I got because I was second guessing the condition of the cameras and I was right - the .5 was blurry in spots and there was dust underneath the stock lens indicating it's been taken apart and poorly put back together. I continued to use the phone until today, because while I can live with the camera issues, my S10+ was becoming outdated and not compatible with certain things and I didn't like the curved sides of the screen. If you are considering a renewed phone from Amazon, definitely inspect it when it arrives - check the screen under different light levels and at different angles. pay attention to the cameras. test the cameras. take pictures utilizing all of the cameras. if there is anything you are unhappy with - return it FOR FREE, and get another and try again. Review Title: Honestly, if you've never experienced a high end smartphone you'll probably love this one
Review Content: Honestly, if you've never experienced a high end smartphone you'll probably love this one. The battery life is great, I'm okay if I miss a days of charging my phone. Screen size is great at 6.5 inches, pretty light weight too. It's up to date as far as Android software... The camera takes acceptable shots in light and darker areas for the price range of the phone no big bells or whistles though. Expandable memory! Gotta love phones that still have an microsd slot. Headphone jack? Yep it has that too. The power button doubles as a fingerprint scanner. So far it has been 100% and zippy quick. Overall, It does what a normal midrange phone should do! On a negative side though, there's a good delay when switching between heavy apps. It's not frustratingly annoying but definitely noticeable. The sound quality isnt the best, even at maximum levels, it's just okay. Colors are not vibrant or vivid, just good... You won't get that crisp 4k imagery when watching videos or viewing high def pictures obviously. Vibrations isn't super strong, no 5g, just as bunch of minor things that can be overlooked. Space could be an issue, 32 gigs is pretty stingey, but that's what the expandable memory is for. It's a good phone for the price. Would I recommend? Review Title: ##### Excelente compra - Aquirido con Chubbies tech
Review Content: ##### Excelente compra - Aquirido con Chubbies tech Respecto a la nueva regulación de Samsung en México de mandar una notificación a los celulares adquiridos en el mercado gris, a mi por el momento no me ha llegado nada, y espero que no me llegue, si llegara a pasar voy a actualizar esta reseña. Cuando llegó el teléfono se encontraba en excelentes condiciones, yo diría que un 9.5 de 10, ya que traía algunos rayones en el marco, lo cual es normal por uso y con una funda ni se nota, respecto al vidrio de la pantalla este traía un rayón, pero afortunadamente era muy pequeño y no afectaba a la pantalla ni el funcionamiento, con una mica se evita que se raye más. Respecto al hardware me llegó tal cual se pidió, de 256 Gb, 12 Gb de Ram, negro y completamente funcional en las cámaras, bocinas, micrófonos, sensores, redes, carga inalambrica, etc. Respecto a la vida de la batería, con la aplicación Acu Battery, se determinó que llegó con un 87% de vida, lo cual consideró es una buena vida, aunque a veces siento que cuando se le demanda mucho uso, su batería se acaba rápido apesar de ser de 5,0000 mAh. Al ser reacondicionado y no saber que le hicieron, no me atrevo a ver si aun es sumergible. Llegó con un cable, cargador y pin para extraer la bandeja sim, pero como no se ven de buena calidad, seguiré usando mis propios cables y cargadores originales de Samsung, esos los tendré de reserva. En general es un super equipo, no estoy nada arrepentido de la compra ya que prácticamente llegó como nuevo, y no tuve ninguna restricción en México con la tarjeta SIM de mi proveedor (AT&T también se probó con Telcel y funcionaba bien). Review Title: Unlocking bootloader - Took ~1 hour just because OnePlus's web form is broken to generate unlock tok
Review Content: Unlocking bootloader - Took ~1 hour just because OnePlus's web form is broken to generate unlock tokens. You will need to call/email customer support. They will need IMEI, serial, the unlock code you get with fastboot commands, and the PCBA/PCB number. Google how to find them; not super hard. Only took as long as it did because I was messing with the broken web portal for too long. Got an unlock token with 20 minutes of asking. 10/10, thanks Sasha. Flashing recovery/ROM(LineageOS) - Comes out of the box with the required android version. No need to upgrade/downgrade stock ROM. Very convenient. I just use the LineageOS recovery, but there's no reason you couldn't flash TWRP. Rooting - With unlocked bootloader, simply install custom recovery of your choice and flash Magisk. I had 0 issues getting Magisk/Zygisk/LSPosed flashed/enabled. If you're sticking with stock ROM, I have no idea how easy/hard it is to root. Got rid of stock ROM pretty much immediately. I have not tested how well Zygisk hides root from apps, as I don't bank on my phone. Notes - I did have an issue after enabling some magisk modules where I broke the speakers and sound and had to reflash LineageOS. I believe the offending module was either MIUI Core/Camera, Lineage Dialer, Viper4Android FX master, or cloudflareDNS for Magisk. Even so, resetting everything and reloading backups/ configuring settings took am hour or two. Notes - The LineageOS camera is bad. Really bad. If you're using the phone for the camera, either stick with stock ROM or flash a dedicated camera ROM. I did not test stock ROM camera. I also have an issue where sometimes the first call of the day I make, my mic doesn't work, but hanging up and calling back fixes this. Conclusion - Between the T-mobile LG V20, moto g7 plus, and this phone, this phone is the best and easiest to unlock at the pricepoint. It's so great, I've gotten 2 of them. Update: had an issue with both phones where they could not receive texts(could send texts just fine). To fix, with the phone on, remove and re-insert the sim card. I only needed to do this once and the text issue has been resolved. Review Title: If you're looking at this device, you're probably already familiar with all the good things about it
Review Content: If you're looking at this device, you're probably already familiar with all the good things about it, so I'll just mention the nitpicks I have: 1) Fingerprint sensor on the side power button leaves a lot to be desired. It frequently fails to detect my finger even though you have to scan it at all kinds of angles during setup. I often find I need to switch hands and unlock it with my right hand as the fingers on my left hand never seem to register correctly or at the correct angle. The fingerprint sensor is even more annoying once you put the phone into a case. The power button is recessed in the case which makes getting a good read even more cumbersome. I don't think a different style case would make much of a difference (and a thicker case would certainly make it worse). Why can't phones go back to the fingerprint sensor on the 'home' button (and go back to *having* a home button. But I digress...) 2) Bloatware. OMG, the bloatware. Initial setup takes absolutely forever because of all the bloatware that insists on downloading on first run. Beyond the usual Google stuff I'll never use, T-Mobile throws on a bunch of junk games and other "sponsored" fluff. Beyond *that*, the T-Mobile app itself sets a persistent notification until you "finish setup". Clicking that to make it go away takes you to a series of screens in the T-Mob app where you have to uncheck even more bloatware that it wants you to install (none of which is required to use the device). And once you get through all that, debloat the useless junk, and think you're done, each system update installs new or re-enables old bloatware you have already removed/disabled. So, if you're setting this up for the first time, just leave the bloatware installed until you've applied all the system updates or you're going to be doing it multiple times. **Carrier Locked**: Note that I'm not factoring this into the rating. In case you miss it in the listing, this is the T-Mobile version of the N200 and is carrier-locked to their network. I'm not reviewing T-Mobile's unlock policy here, but before buying, please make sure you understand the following: - T-Mobile *WILL NOT* unlock this device for you. At least, not at first. Despite it not being a subsidized device and you fully owning it, their system will not allow it to be carrier-unlocked until it meets the same requirements as one they subsidized. Per their unlock policy, you will have to use it on T-Mobile for 40 days (if using a postpaid plan) or 365 days/1 year if using a pre-paid plan. So, if you're currently a T-Mobile customer, this should work fine; you just won't be able to unlock it to use elsewhere until after 40 days or 1 year of use depending on your plan type. **Update 2025-10-06**: Despite having this active on T-Mobile for over a year now, they still refuse to unlock it. They say they can't find it in their system. So if this item is still listed, and you're looking at the T-Mobile version, you can expect it to ONLY work on T-Mobile -- do not expect them to unlock this. - SIM cards from T-Mobile MVNOs (Mint, MetroPCS, etc) or subsidiaries (Sprint, nTelos, etc) will NOT be accepted in this. I use Mint and foolishly expected it to work since they're now fully owned by T-Mobile. Nope. Review Title: Oneplus are acting like this phone was stolen and keep wanting more obscure serial numbers buried de
Review Content: Oneplus are acting like this phone was stolen and keep wanting more obscure serial numbers buried deeper and deeper. I didn't even know that some of those serial numbers existed. Am I about to get a visit from the police??? I've had my new SIM for a month now and really need to activate it... but I'm stuck paying absurdly higher prices on my FIOS landline that's gotten out of hand. I'm not happy about that. It would have been cheaper for me to buy a more expensive phone from someone else. I'm going to have to contact Mint and ask for an activation extension while my other phone I just bought takes another week to come in. And if anyone is wondering, if I activate the new SIM, I lose my land line and start having to pay for the SIM, and since I don't have a working cell phone, I lose all phone connection. That's not good for someone with really bad health problems. There's also the second issue of not bothering to install and "move into" this phone because when a bootloader gets unlocked, it forces a factory reset and WIPES THE ENTIRE PHONE. My whole point of picking a fully unlocked phone is to "deGoogle" (check wikipedia for the long answer) and remove all their spyware and Tmo bloat with Lineage (see RAM below). I let my old Google logins expire and I'm not creating a new one where they demand my phone number just so they can track me forever (see "privacy" below). This phone is a DE2118. This number is critical for the product page. When selling used phones, DETAIL AND ACCURACY IS EVERYTHING! I don't know why it's missing. You can find this model number in Config / About / Version, along with a couple other places. Know what you're getting. This product falls below "Amazon Renewed" standards. The phone was packed loosly in a small box with a dinky bubble wrap sleeve. Expect the phone to be tumbled badly by the shipping company. For the people who are complaining about endless problems that are unfixable, this bubble wrap sleeve is NOT enough to protect the phone if it was dropped by the shipper. If you have problems, you need to immediately return the phone under Amazon's policies. The card eject pin was hiding under a box flap. I almost missed it. The screen protection plastic film didn't even cover the top or bottom sections of the screen. Another thing I really don't like is that the charger is a generic USB-2 5v 2a Samsung charger with a USB A to C cable. This should have been a 9v USB-C fast charger (as stated by the manual) if it were really "equivalent" like "Amazon Renewed" advertises. The USB-C cable fits snugly into the phone but is only 3 feet. It is not enough to go from a floor power strip to a desktop. If you need a USB-C fast charger and didn't get one, you need to immediately return this phone under Amazon's policies and mention "failed equivalent" in the reason box. The fingerprint sensor on the power button is questionable and cranky. I never messed with it long enough to figure out if it was really having hardware problems or if it was a bad design. If anyone is curious, this phone did a 400meg Android 12 security update to the Nov 5, 2023 release. I don't know how many others it will officially get, but it won't get Android 13 (not at least from the telco). News Flash: It just decided to update to the Dec 5 patch. Looks like this one is 95megs. The telcos are about a month late with most Android security updates. It looks like this update broke my adb connection and installed cooking videos on the left screen. Way to waste my data and battery with useless videos. No telling how much RAM that's eating up (see below). Oh well, I'm about to factory reset this thing anyways... On the Config / Status page, I do have some concerns that "Bluetooth address" is listed as "Unavailable". Once I got this thing set up, I was going to pick up a BT headset. If you prefer to use a headset with your phone, you may need to pick up a wired one. If you're wondering why this phone can be so slow, have a look at "free -m" in "adb shell". This gets technical, but I'll try to keep it somewhat simple. OnePlusN200TMO:/storage/emulated/0/DCIM/Camera $ free -m I copied this down shortly after I started ADB access. The missing 512megs is probably used by the graphics driver. The rest of the 3.5g of RAM is being eaten by Tmo bloat and Google spyware. There's also 1g in the swap partition (see wikipedia for the long definition). When this phone (or any with too much bloat and swap) "goes out to lunch", physical RAM is being swapped to disk (flash chip) in and out until the request you made finally has enough physical RAM to complete. Notice I just mentioned "flash chip". Flash is very slow and has a very limited write life cycle (see "flash memory" on wiki) and will die a very early death if thrashed by swap. For some of you people who keep having crashing problems with nothing running after factory resets, there's a good chance your flash "disk" got burned. Your phone is now e-waste. This is true for ANY phone or portable device. It's the same thing as a microSD card failing. As consumers, we absolutely hate having our device die an early death, but manufacturers love it because you have to buy a new phone much sooner. As a side note, I did a dive into settings and tried to disable the bloatware to get some RAM back. I wasn't very successful. Remember I never installed anything on this phone because I'm waiting and waiting and waiting for the bootloader unlock code. If you're an advanced user, be sure to download the newest versions of ADB and flashboot from the official google site. I was hoping to back this phone up with "flashboot fetch", but it doesn't support it. Go figure. (TWRP isn't supported on this phone, either.) This could have been a good way to image backup the phone since many Android backup methods are "mediocre" at best. Also note that I've read many reviews of people upgrading to a new phone and their cloud backups NOT restoring when they should have (they wouldn't have been helped by "fetch" in this instance). So everyone be careful when moving over to a new phone. Your best bet is to move everything to the microSD card and copy that to your computer BEFORE making a big change. The adb command can be used in "pull" mode if you're advanced. It's odd how Google installs so much spyware but can't get that data back to the phone. While looking for a possible way around the bootloader lock, I did come across *#808# that enters Engineer Mode. You can do a number of specific self tests and see some of the lesser used serial numbers if you dig deep. If you dig REALLY DEEP, you can find menus in chinese, and this really upset me. Why? I knew Oneplus was made in china, but not also programmed there, too. China isn't known for privacy. While installing LineageOS will remove a lot of their spyware and some of the back doors, it won't remove the ones that are baseband processor related. That device has its own little CPU and operating system (a little sub computer within your phone) and controls things like the cellular modem, microphone, and may have unrestricted direct access to the main operating system depending on how it's implemented. If I wanted the CCP to be spying on me, I would have bought a cheaper Xiaomi. If your're curious about privacy, head back over to wikipedia and look up: Spyware, Internet privacy, Data privacy, Privacy violation, Targeted marketing, De-anonymize, Mobile security, Surveillance capitalism, Zombie_cookie. That's just to get started. Wiki also sanitizes a lot of this information, so real stories tend to be more gruesome. Ever wonder why illegals crossing the border take the battery out of their phones? Because "off" isn't really "off". Keep that in mind when reading all the wiki pages. Don't believe me? For the past month, this phone has been sitting "off" as a paperweight on top of my desk... Just waiting and waiting and waiting for that bootloader unlock code... One day it turned "on" and started making noises. It took me a minute to figure it out, but the phone received an Amber Alert and decided to turn back "on". Supposedly these also happen for weather, but the past month has been quiet here. Now ask yourself how an "off" phone suddenly decided to turn itself "on". (hint: baseband processor mentioned above.) As a final privacy note: If someone was stalking/spying on you as much as Google, the phone manufacturer, and the telcos, if that person was caught, they'd be thrown in prison for a very long time. Something to think about. Moving on... The phone I got has a screen in near perfect shape. I was pleased about that. On the back side is a rather noticable dent that I'm hoping didn't hit the battery. It hasn't charged hot, pushed out the back cover, or burst into flames, so I think it's ok. Since I don't have the bootloader unlock code, I can't say anything about voice quality. The biggest reason I went with this phone was 5G support and most likely easy HD audio in my coverage area (probably better than 4G HD audio). I dumped my previous cell phones and kept my land line for so long because cell-to-cell calls suck badly, and I'm in a major metroplex, so that shouldn't happen. I was really hoping to test this out. I never bothered trying out the 4 cameras and video recording. I did pick up a new 128g SDXC card, but I'm not motivated to do tests on a camera I'm about to return. I'd rather have 1 or 2 cameras in a phone that are high quality rather than having extra cameras that are useless. In a budget phone, we still have to pay for the extra useless cameras which just drives the price up and manufacturer profits down. They're nothing more than case bling. I never bothered trying to figure out battery life since I still can't use this phone. If you do a web search, there's usually a way to pop the back off and unsolder the battery for a swap out for most phones. If you're semi technically inclined, you don't have to be stuck with a used battery that's a few years old. Note that all the spyware bloat I mentioned above will really drain an otherwise usable battery. Swap reads and writes to flash and back are very energy intensive. Most sites ignore this in their reviews. Since this is a Tmo phone, make sure you have Tmo towers nearby and you should be happy with connectivity. I've read too many reviews about people buying a phone and the supported tower is across town and they get lousy reception. Don't be like that. My friends with Tmo phones get good enough reception where I live. In the past CDMA has sucked here, but that's going away, thankfully. So what are my final recommendations in this overly long review??? If Oneplus ever got me my bootloader unlock key on time, I would have flashed LineageOS (probably the hard way since it's a de2118) and would have likely kept this phone regardless of the problems I mentioned. My phone needs are minimal given my health problems and I can't work. I like the slightly larger screen given my eyesight problems, too. My usage would involve the phone (obviously), GPS and open source maps, and the camera to document some of my hardware and projects. Review Title: I purchased one of these Kraken V3 Pro headsets from a thrift store of all places
Review Content: I purchased one of these Kraken V3 Pro headsets from a thrift store of all places. It didn't come with a dongle so I had to purchase a used dongle (RC30-0346) one off eBay. I used Razer's headset pairing utility and paired the two. Upon testing the mic I noticed it was not picking up any sounds no matter the settings in windows and/or Synapse. However, the mic worked perfectly fine when the headset was directly plugged into my PC via the three notched aux cord. I then proceeded to update the firmware on both the dongle and headset thinking maybe the mic not working was a firmware issue. Note: in order to update the firmware you must exit Synapse completely. I remember at one point the green "Next" button was darkened but I went ahead and clicked on it and it proceeded to the next step in updating the firmware. The issue continued to persist. I then decided to purchase another unit (this one) refurbed. The mic works perfectly fine out of the box, no issues what so ever. Now that I have both units side by side the new one (refurbed unit) notably has a tighter fitment whereas the thrift store one with the mic issue looks stretched and widened. Conclusion: these headsets must be treated gently when taking off and put on the head. DO NOT grab it from one ear cup and yank it off your head because doing so will deteriorate the cable inside the head band which is responsible for the mic to function properly wirelessly. Also Razer customer service was unaware of this issue.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))       6 people found this helpful Helpful  Sending feedback...Thank you for your feedback.
