Review Title: (1)The ear pads fully cover the ears but are a bit stiff
Review Content: (1)The ear pads fully cover the ears but are a bit stiff. They are still comfortable, but because they seal so tight, they can get a bit sweaty and uncomfortable. I give them a 6/10 for comfort when wearing them for longer sessions. The softer pads on the Steelseries are just more comfortable. (2)Battery life is abysmal. 6 hours and they are done and they take quite a long time to charge. So if you game a few hours, set them on the desk and walk away, come back and game a few more hours, or watch some movies or such you are getting close to needing to charge. Unacceptable. I can use my SteelSeries all day and never need to charge them. 3/10. (3)Haptics. It's a total gimmick. It just vibrates your ears and will probably make them itch. And those haptics drain on the battery that much more, so you better remember to hook them up to charge every single time you take them off. 1/10. (4)Microphone. Sounds pretty good but you have to detach it when not in use. It doesn't slide up into the case as most good sets do. I don't want to have to track down the damn mic when I need it in some drawer. I want to reach up, pull it out, and use it. 5/10. Overall it's a decent pair of headphones if you can get them on a deep sale. The battery life means you will be a slave to the charging cable and the haptic feature is useless. Mine are sitting on a shelf and I am back to the trusty Steelseries. Review Title: This S25 FE works great as promised
Review Content: This S25 FE works great as promised. It looks totally new. I don't see any imperfections. So far in my 2 weeks of using it, it has worked fine with T-Mobile. The phone includes the charging cable but not the charging head itself. The phone includes the little needle tool to open the SIM card tray. However I had T-Mobile give me an e-SIM, so I no longer use a physical SIM card anymore. My one complaint about the S25 FE is that the screen is wider (and taller) than the S22, so it can be hard for my thumb to reach the other side of the screen when using the phone with one hand. The S25 is actually smaller than the S25 FE, so the S25 probably won't have that problem. If you buy this phone, I hope yours works and is not like a dud like the 1-star reviews. I guess you can return it if it does fail. So far, this phone is working great for me. If anything bad happens with this phone, I will update my review. Product Title: Amazon.com: Motorola Moto Razr+ 5G 2023, 256GB + 8GB RAM, Black - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: There are two major things that really hold this phone back
Review Content: There are two major things that really hold this phone back. 1 - The cameras are bad. When you compare them to the cameras on the S23 Ultra, it's a blood bath. They get beaten in every conceivable way. In fact these are the worst cameras I've used in a long time. One thing that helps, do not grant access for Motorola to touch up your photos. It does an awful job. 2 - The software Motorola uses is awful. The gestures they use for the camera and flashlight are great, just about everything else is bad. For example, they let you setup folders in your app drawer. That's great for people who like to organize things. Too bad it's half baked. You can't put them in any order. They are in the order they are created. So even if you plan out how you are going to create them, they'll never be in alphabetical order thanks to a default Google and Motorola folder already existing. The app drawer is more of an annoyance than another borderline fatal flaw. They broke the updates on this phone. When I got it, it was stuck on the November 1, 2023 security update. There was no way to update it on the phone. If you had it check, it always said it was using the latest software. Research proved that there were multiple updates, including a firmware update available. Come to find out, this is a known issues on some Motorola phones. How do you fix it? You have to download their rescue software to a PC, enable developer mode on your phone, then have it do a "rescue". Rescue means you're phone is getting wiped. Having the phone get reset to get your updates is terrible. It's even worse considering that their phone migration is no where near as good as Samsung's. It's going to take you hours to get your phone back the way you want it. Here is the real kicker. After going through that, there is no guarantee that I'll be able to get OTA updates. I might have to reset the phone each time I want to update it. Then we have the fact that Android 14 has been out for about a year and there is no ETA for it on this phone. They say it's coming, but I'm not holding my breath. If you don't care about software updates and security patches, you might love this phone. For me it leaves a bad aftertaste in my mouth. The software woes continue. I spent far too long troubleshooting a problem with Android Auto. When the phone is closed it would not connect. Instead it kind of freaked out. Turns out that no one at Motorola put in a bypass for Android Auto and the external screen. It treats it like any other app. This means you have to keep the phone closed, unlock the phone so the external screen unlocks, and then plug it into your car. This will make the permission prompt show up for the external screen. After that it works much better. Motorola decided to create it's own software for connecting this phone to Windows. Sure, you can use Link to Windows, but unlike Samsung, you can't stream apps. Instead they cooked up their own half baked Windows app. Who's idea was this? You're stretched so thin on the software side you can't provide monthly updates, but you wasted the resources on a Windows app, when one already existed, and does a better job. Review Content: I used it alot for gaming, a lil mobile gaming but mostly xbox cloud gaming with a ps4 controller with no problems. Been playing cod bo6 and forza horizon 5 on it mostly. Unfortunately i ran my phone over with a forklift about a month ago n broke my screen, i just did an insurance claim n got reimbursed n decided to upgrade to a note 20 ultra since it's the same price as this was when i originally bought it. I originally bought it for $356 before tax n it was worth every penny, i think it's going for $250 rn u can't beat that. BUT MAKE SURE YOU GET A VERY DURABLE CASE. The screen can hold up to alot but the back cover is pretty weak glass. I put it in a case when i bought it and i switched carriers like 3 weeks later i pulled the phone out of the case to change the sim and the back glass had several giant cracks n i don't even know how i did it i was still babying the phone at the time. Speaking of carriers i used this phone with straight talk and spectrum mobile with no problems. The screen has a bright beautiful picture and the colors are really vibrant. The phone feels solid and the all glass design has a pleasant feel to it. I liked having it out of the case but its glass and i know how i am with phones so i kept it in a case all the time. There's so many features to this phone i was still learning some all the time n i don't feellike listing them all but the one i learned today from the phone repair lady is that even though my screens broke n the touch doesnt work i can still control the phone n do everything like normal using the spen. That would've been great to know ive been controlling it with a ps4 controller for a month Hopefully the note 20 ultra is an upgrade and doesn't feel like a downgrade otherwise I'm coming back to the note 10+       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))       22 people found this helpful Helpful  Sending feedback...Thank you for your feedback. Review Title: This phone came in excellent condition and it works amazing! It was worth every penny and then some!
Review Content: This phone came in excellent condition and it works amazing! It was worth every penny and then some! You're always a little skeptical when you buy anything used, let alone something that was formerly damaged, repaired, and then re-sold. But, as I said before, it was meant as my side-phone so as long as the storage I had heard about with this phone held true the cosmetics and things of that nature didn't matter. But the fact that it came looking like a brand new phone was truly icing on the cake. I initially was just going to get the Note 10, I had ordered it and everything and then in the process of looking into what memory card I was going to get along with some of the accessories people favored, I saw some people had said they hated that it didn't come with a memory slot. And I was like wait, what!!! I thought I had done my homework on it and missed that entirely and that was a deal breaker for me. Needless to say I canceled that one and ordered this 1 and I'm extremely glad I did. I'm a check to make sure I put the right seller I bought from bcuz I wanna make sure they get the credit they deserve and hopefully I help bring them business. And here's to also hoping you guys get the same quality phone then I ended up with bcuz we all kno everybody's experiences are different. But I have no gripes with this phone at all. I'm even getting used to the power button on the left side of the phone. Lolz, its starting to make using my regular one feel kinda wierd. Smh. But I ordered mine from Chubbiestech. I think I spelled that right. But shouts to them, amazing quality phone, that came fast, and theres honestly no bad things I could say about it. The phone it was replacing was a J7 Samsung Galaxy Prime, which is prehistoric now. Lol. And I was just gonna get another one of them bcuz it was just meant for storage and I was used to using it for that purpose for many a year, but 200 dollars for an old and used phone.... This was literally going from the stone ages to the Matrix in 0 to 60 seconds. But anyway, I hope this review helped sway at least a few people. It's a great buy for that price! Oh, and I didn't rate the face recognition bcuz I still haven't used it. I'll come back if I ever decide to. But stuff like that isn't that important to me. Review Title: I am puzzled about the negative reviews here
Review Content: I am puzzled about the negative reviews here. I got my Samsung Note 10+ from Amazon Renewed via Re-Cell and I couldn't be happier. The phone looks brand new, as in unused. There were 2 small mishaps which a quick call to Re-Cell fixed. The first is that I didn't get an Spen, and they were very apologetic about that, they shipped it immediately. The second was that the phone had a screen protector which had an air bubble. I don't like screen protectors so I simply popped it off. They offered to send me a return box (shipping label for free shipping) and resend me a phone without a screen protector though. I spent the first day setting up my phone (unlocked but I use T-mobile) and everything was smooth. As a rule I never hop on the new tech bandwagon (5G) the first year out. There's not much difference between the 2021 Note20 and the 2020 Note10 but for 5G. For now the difference between 4G and 5G is not perceptible by users who are not streaming gamers and I would argue that even heavy streaming gamers won't see much improvement. 5G for the next few years is nothing but HYPE . If my luck with this refurbished phone continues I will once again go with refurbished for the 5G version next year. I don't mind being "one year behind" with my smartphone and I refuse to sign long term contracts. Another advantage of this approach is that you get all the fixes and software updates when you buy last year's model. Brand new models are always full of bugs. Face recognition and fingerprint security work great! I have been a Google pixel loyalist so far and I have to day Samsung Note 10 UI is far better than Pixel. Review Title: It has the worst battery life of any iPhone I've ever owned, and I have owned ONLY iPhones since the
Review Content: It has the worst battery life of any iPhone I've ever owned, and I have owned ONLY iPhones since the first version was released 17 years ago. This is the second iPhone 14 that I've bought from the renewed store . The first one I bought on December 4th, 2023, and I could not have been happier with the phone. It arrived in brand new condition, and performed flawlessly. On the recommendation of a friend, I checked the battery health and charging after having it for MONTHS and it was at 100%! I was thrilled! Unfortunately, on July 30 of this year I dropped it, and it was beyond repair. I immediately went back to the Amazon renewed store and purchased another iPhone 14 because my experience with the first one was so fantastic. It arrived in new looking condition, exactly like the one I bought in December 2023. It was not scratched or anything really noticeable, it just seemed to be "worn" a little bit, but I fully understood that it was a renewed phone, and any cosmetic issues were not that important to me, including the color, which, when my iPhone is in its case, you cannot tell what color it is anyway. Unfortunately, I DID NOT look at the battery health and charging when I first got the phone 38 days ago, but I did look at it about two weeks ago, and it said 93%. I thought, ok, it's a renewed phone, it's not going to have 100% battery life. Well, I just looked at it today and it's now at 90% battery health and charging. I have it completely set up for optimized battery life. I have lost emails and messages that I was in the middle of composing, and the phone just dies. I've been in the middle of important phone calls when the phone dies, simply because I had just fully charged it a few hours before that, and thought I would be fine for hours to come. I just had a total shoulder replacement surgery a week ago, and I was on the phone with my doctors office yesterday about my first post-op appointment, and my phone died in the middle of it. I thought I had HOURS left before the phone would die. Then I had to plug it in, and wait for it to come back alive, so I could call my doctor back and hopefully not wait a half hour after losing my place in line. On top of that is also has issues with the touchscreen being glitchy, and sometimes I have to tap on things several times to get them to work. As I said, I have been an iPhone owner/user since the very first version came out 17 years ago. I've always loved all my iPhones, and I will continue to be an iPhone user for the rest of my life. This is in no way reflection on Apple iPhones whatsoever. They are an amazing and fantastic piece of technology. I think I just got a bad one for the first time in my life. Luckily, I have just checked and I have until November 6th to return this phone, and I WILL be returning it. Am I expected to buy a new one and get that shipped to me, transfer all my information from this phone to the new one, and then return this one? I am actually still paying for this phone on my Amazon Prime American Express card! Or, do I return this phone and wait until the refund has been issued and then buy another phone? Then wait until that is sent to me. I would not have a phone for at least a week in the interim, and we all know these days that's a practical impossibility. Like I said, I just had a total shoulder replacement surgery last Monday, September 9th, and have several upcoming follow up appointments, and physical therapy appointments. I also have several other non-related medical issues that definitely require that I have a phone. I just don't know what to do. So, I had the phone shipped to UPS and recorded the unboxing to alleviate any accusations that I, the customer, caused any damage. The phone looked fine. I purchased "excellent" condition, which speaks to the visible condition of the phone. I can see the scratch on the screen from more than a foot away, but my concern was more about the condition/performance of the phone. I wish Amazon would assist more with returns, as it seems many were left unsatisfied. I hope that my experience becomes more the norm. I had a lot of anxiety over this and I'm glad it worked out, but I feel it would be hit or miss in general if a return is needed. Review Title: I needed a new phone fast after my cat knocked mine into the sink ☹️ Rice fixed it for a while, but
Review Content: I needed a new phone fast after my cat knocked mine into the sink ☹️ Rice fixed it for a while, but it was only temporary before it died altogether. I hate buying phones and avoid it whenever possible. 99% of mine belonged to someone in my family first. And i was good with that. Needless to say, my cat didn’t wait for someone in my family to upgrade. I was on my own this time. Okay.... that’s not entirely true. My grandma had an iPhone 7 sitting around so that held me over in the meantime. Going from an iPhone 11 Pro Max to an iPhone 7 was….bad. It was too dam small, in every possible way. 32 gigs of memory!! I needed an upgrade. Fast. My 11 year old was bullying me relentlessly. And that’s on me. They had my old XR (formerly my dad’s) I scoured FB marketplace. I’d decided upgrade a little, so I could feel better about the switch. I didn’t want to feel backed me into a corner by my cat’s recklessness. I would get a slightly newer model in a fun colour. Marketplace had plenty. Sending message after message from my iPhone 7, I worried. “This person seems too eager”, “this one has been posted so long”, “I want a purple, but the only purple one listed has less storage space” and “the pretty green one has a small crack”, “this guy lives 2 hours from me” and “Battery life? Errr last time I checked it was like 74%?….no, I can’t take a screenshot of it, it’s turned off”…. “cash only please” Etc. So much pressure. What happens if the thing doesn’t work? That’s $300+ down the drain. I knew I couldn’t afford new. But I hated the idea of buying something used from a stranger on Facebook. I didn’t want to get scammed, and I also didn’t want to settle. That’s when I remembered good ol’ Amazon. Maybe I’d check there. Just for funsies. Probably out of my budget, but it couldn’t hurt. Sure enough, refurbished devices selling “like new!” Mostly same cost or less than what I’d found so far. Surely there was a catch? I read through everything, tested by Amazon, includes all the specs, unlocked, I can pick the colour, the storage size, the condition, etc. AND I could have it delivered to me tomorrow??! With a warranty?!! I recovered from my brief stint of disappointment after learning the 12’s don’t come in yellow. Then fought hard to decide between mint and lavender. The lavender would take an extra day to arrive. Mint it was!! As promised, it arrived the next day. It was in beautiful shape. 128g’s, mint green, not a single scratch, 86% battery life. All for less than I would have paid to some stranger for a 64g with some “small scratches” Once my case and screen protector arrived I excitedly set it up and synced my data. After becoming used to facial recognition, having that yanked away, and dealing with a 7 for over 2 weeks— I was desperate for the convenience of Face ID. I had been using my fingerprint. Like a *caveman*. Not to mention I have Blink 182 tickets, and it specifically states facial recognition is required to access the mobile tickets. Idk if that’s true, but I needed Face ID!! I googled, I contacted apple support. Fixing it could be upwards of $300. That’s almost what I paid for the whole phone!! I realllllly didn’t want to be stuck without a phone again. But I also wanted one fully functioning. So I reached out to Amazon support and explained. The rep was incredibly helpful (as most Amazon reps are) and after bts failed, she advised the ship was a 3rd party seller, and she send a message to them. “If they don’t fix it by (insert date) contact us back and we’ll make this right” she encouraged. I’m ngl. I was nervous. I didn’t have high hopes, having dealt with 3p sellers on Amazon in the past. At least Amazon had my back, ig. The concert wasn’t till July. Even without facial recognition, it was loads better than the 7. I could make do in the meantime. The seller came in clutch though, and my worry was unwarranted. They responded within minutes. They were receptive, apologetic, and more than willing to help. As I’d anticipated, they offered a refund or exchange, as soon as they received the return. I explained my concern with not having a phone for several days or more; and the merchant offered to overnight a replacement as soon as the return was dropped off. I could deal with one day without a phone! I gratefully accepted. That was Saturday night, we made plans to catch up Monday for the return instructions and for them to overnight it. Monday I reached back out; and they were ready to ship, BUT they *had no more green….* 🫢 SHOCK THIS WAS A HUGE BUMMER.It’s silly I know, and the definition of *first world problems “.. but I mean…. My change of heart about this whole phone thing HINGED ON THE FUN COLOUR. Without it, I was just a person…out $350… because my cat was thirsty while I was watching YouTube while washing dishes. I needed a cool colour. Plus, I’d already gotten the matching case! Clear with mint green borders. It wasn’t even a fun blue… it was a dark, serious, navy blue. It was pretty and classy, but I wanted something fun. I even asked if he had any older models in yellow 😭😭 no luck, They told me they’d be restocking in a day or so. Still, no greens or purples came in. Ugh. Reality was setting in. I was going to have to settle. It was fine, I thought. At least it would be a fully functioning phone. No. I wasn’t ready to let go. They assured me I could take my time to decide, and I asked if we could wait another week in case one came in. If it didn’t, *then* I would choose from the options available. I messaged them Wednesday afternoon, bracing myself for the answer…. THEY GOT IN PURPLE! YAY. They sent a label, I dropped it off, sent a photo, and had my new phone the next morning. they’d said overnight shipping… but wow! I’d dropped off the return around 3pm, and had the replacement by noon the next day. I didn’t even have my new case yet 😅 Despite the Barney-Esque colour scheme my mint green case created, the lavender is GORGEOUS and I’m actually sort of glad the green didn’t work out. Don’t get me wrong, the green is also gorgeous.. but in the end I’m glad I ended up with the lavender. I was overjoyed when I was prompted to set Face ID during setup. Worked brilliantly, as did everything else. Great packaging, no cosmetic flaws, amazing battery life, customer service was great, and best of all… ITS PURPLE! Can’t wait to pair it with the new case. I’m so glad I went this route where I have some peace of mind as a buyer. I’m grateful to the seller for being so helpful and patient with me as insufferable as I must have seemed making such a fuss over colour preference If you’re nervous buying a phone used or refurbished too, hopefully you can take comfort in knowing- this seller is legit. You receive a good quality product, and, speaking from experience, they’ll gladly help resolve any issues you may run into. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple AirPods Pro - 1st Gen (Renewed) : Electronics
Review Title: However, this is the first time I’ve ever purchased a used/refurbished/ renewed pair
Review Content: However, this is the first time I’ve ever purchased a used/refurbished/ renewed pair. But since I lose them all the time, I thought it may be a cost effective option for me. Unfortunately, my device was defective out of the box! My Airpods Pro didn’t come with all of the materials that come in the original box and the charger I received [packaged separately] was not even an apple brand. This didn’t bother me much, as I have more than enough accessories for this item. The device itself appeared clean and undamaged. When I opened the device to check the battery status, it was dead [Apple has a policy of not sending their devices fully charged for shipping safety reasons, so I assumed the previous owner received the item new and returned them without charging it more]. I connected the airpods to my OFFICIAL Apple charger from a previous device and the battery light immediately glowed green. Confused, I then proceeded to pair it to my phone. The first attempt was successful. I checked my battery notification screen on my iPhone and the airpods case displayed a full 100% charge, yet the airpods themselves were each dead at 1%. After a few seconds of charge, they reached 7% [charging speed rare, but not completely unheard of], so I took the case off the charger and went to test out the sound quality. As soon as I took an earpiece out- the entire device went off. The case and pods still read as charging on my phone even though I had removed them from charging moments before. I could not find the devise in my drop menu, so I went into settings to manually pair the AirPods again- but they wouldn’t sync. After 4/5 times connecting and forgetting device, I attempted to reattach the charger- NOW the AirPods case is on 0% but the earpieces are both on 13% 🙄. As soon as I plug them back in, the airpods sync again and I am able to hear the pairing chime on my earpiece. SECONDS LATER the airpods die and the phone shows they are on 0% *charging* WHILE they are still in my ears! Like I said, I’ve had a ton of airpods, I know how to troubleshoot most any problem they give me. I’ve never had to deal with this kind of headache before- ESPECIALLY on day 1. I’m so over it! I’m going to an Apple store first thing in the morning. This was a horrible experience. So yes, my usage probably doesn't mirror most, yet for those who are looking just for a lowkey, hang-about 2nd smartphone without breaking the bank (or contract), I am quite happy with it. Product Title: Amazon.com: Samsung Galaxy S21 5G, US Version, 128GB, Phantom Gray - Unlocked (Renewed) | Unlocked : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: Delivery was very good
Review Content: Delivery was very good. I saw it was shipped on the 25th. On the 30th, I received an SMS from DHL saying they planned delivery on Oct. 3rd, but on the same day I got an email asking for copy of national ID and content description for clearing customs. I am not a Morocco residents nor citizen, so I sent my foreign passport instead. On the 3rd, Amazon tracking info said clearing custom was delayed as additional documents were needed. So I called DHL, and the rep said it would be delivered on the 4th instead. On the 4th, I saw a newly posted message about delay on Amazon tracking. I called DHL various times but couldn't get to anyone. I then sent an inquiry by email and get a response shortly saying it was being taking care of. Then late afternoon, I got the package. Upon arriving, the seal of the packing had an opening large enough to put in a hand but not for getting the phone out, so I didn't complain. Unpacked, the inner packing of the phone was in excellent condition, very much like the original packing but had no Samsung marking, rather, it had a marking of "amazonrenewed". There was a film covering the screen, like on a new phone. The phone appeared in excellent condition, only had a small scratch at the back when I looked in detail, and a hair of scratch on the screen that is only visible under bright light and in a particular angle. I tried but couldn't turn on the phone - there was no response. The box also included a USB-C cable and a cheap non-Samsung charger made in China. I used my own Samsung Charger to charge the phone. After plugged in, it showed the battery was at 0. So I let it charge to full. After started, it turned out fully unlocked. My Morocco sim card works with 4G. The phone's software looked already reset, but I reset it myself anyhow. Then updated to the latest system with Android 12, and loaded many apps I need. During about the first week, the battery appeared quite poor. With medium usage it lasted about a day. I tried all necessary settings to conserve battery, but it didn't seem to help much. These couple days, it becomes much better, lasting about 45 hours. I read it was likely due to some AI processes either from Android 12 or Samsung doing the learning work at first. But it's pretty bad the phone doesn't show any info. I would say I am very happy with the phone. And this is after having a terrible experience in the past with Samsung. The last Samsung phone I had was S7 Edge bought in Thailand (I am a traveler), new at a Samsung store for perhaps ~$800. I actually wanted the normal S7 (without the "edge"), but it was out of stock then. I never liked the "edge", it was a silly design in my mind. The phone worked well initially, but in the coming couple of years I had a terrible experience. About 5 months later when I was in Vietnam, the screen started to show shaded bands across. As I was wondering how or if I should return to Thailand to get the phone serviced, the bands disappeared after a month. Then about another 7 months later when I was in Azerbaijan, the phone couldn't start after I did a system update. So I couldn't use the phone for a couple weeks until I reached Tbilisi in Georgia when I had someone flashed it. About a year later, it died on me again when I was in Morocco. I had someone re-flashed it, but it was not successful. About 1 month later I reached the city of Fes where there is a Samsung service center. After checking, they said there was something wrong with the motherboard. Very shocking! I've never had such problem in my life with all the phones and computers, cheap or dear, and this was a flagship! So eventually, I sold it to a local repair shop for $200, for which they said they only needed the screen. That was end of 2017. So I never bought a Samsung again, and would definitely not buy one at the full price. I admit the S series is not worthless. At least, I like the camera. But I never had a chance to buy one at a largely reduced price (I won't buy from just any second-hand sellers). So now, the Amazon reviewed phone with some warranty got me interested. Yes, I have some risk, but to me with the past experience, the risk is not much higher than getting a new phone from Samsung, plus, I am putting in a much lower bet now. Product Title: Amazon.com: Samsung Galaxy S21 5G, US Version, 128GB, Phantom Gray - Unlocked (Renewed) | Unlocked : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: From the moment you lay eyes on the Galaxy S21, it’s evident that Samsung has crafted a device meant
Review Content: From the moment you lay eyes on the Galaxy S21, it’s evident that Samsung has crafted a device meant for the high-end market. The sleek contours and premium materials give it an unmistakable aura of luxury. The 6.2-inch Dynamic AMOLED display is nothing short of breathtaking, offering vibrant colors, deep blacks, and impressive brightness levels. Whether you are streaming your favorite series or scrolling through social media, every experience is elevated by this stunning showcase of visual brilliance. Underneath the hood, the Galaxy S21 5G is powered by the latest Exynos or Snapdragon chipset (depending on your region), ensuring lightning-fast performance for multitasking and gaming alike. The device handles everything with remarkable ease, and the inclusion of 5G capabilities means you can harness incredibly fast download and upload speeds. With options for up to 256GB of storage and 8GB of RAM, you won't find yourself wanting for space or speed. Samsung’s camera system is one of the standout features of the S21. The triple-lens setup, including a 12MP ultra-wide, a 12MP wide, and a 64MP telephoto lens, allows users to capture stunning images in various conditions. The Night Mode is particularly impressive, ensuring that low-light photos are as crisp as those taken in bright daylight. The addition of advanced video features, including 8K recording, cements the Galaxy S21’s status as a powerhouse for mobile photography enthusiasts. While the battery life is generally sufficient to get through a full day with moderate use, heavy users may find themselves reaching for a charger by late afternoon. The 4000mAh battery powers some serious capabilities, but if you plan on extensively utilizing 5G and the phone's camera, be prepared for a potential drop in endurance. Fast charging and wireless charging options are a plus, but the slightly underwhelming battery performance keeps the S21 from achieving a perfect score. Herein lies the crux of the matter—while the Samsung Galaxy S21 5G dazzles with features, performance, and design, it comes at a steep price. For many, this puts it out of reach, especially considering the current market of other high-quality smartphones that offer comparable features at a lower cost. The premium branding does lend a certain prestige, but that may not be enough to sway budget-conscious consumers.

When I opened the Amazon packaging, I saw an Apple AirPods Pro boxed sealed and in pristine condition. I unwrapped it and opened the box and it was like opening a box for a pair of brand new AirPods. Everything down to the cable was properly placed and the headphones along with the case didn’t even look like they had been touched! AND THESE ARE RENEWED! It’s like I bought a pair brand new for less amount of money. A4C Online is absolutely amazing for how they packaged this product and the condition of these renewed AirPods Pro is beyond my belief. I truly didn’t expect the quality I received. As for the headphones themselves, jaw dropping amazement. From the noise cancellation, to the quality of the headphones, it’s all amazing. The noise cancellation is beyond belief. I set these up, put them in my ears while I listened to my fan, and turned on noise cancellation. Boom. The sound of the fan disappeared, like magic! The noise cancellation doesn’t block out every loud noise like movies, but it’s much better than anything I’ve ever used. Transparency is wonderful and definitely allows me to hear around me while I still listen to the music or video I’m listening to. I’m not sure if their are better headphones out there that do transparency better, but seeing how I’ve never seen headphones have this kind of feature, it’s definitely one of the reasons I bought these, especially so I can be at work and keep both headphones in without having to just leave one in so I may listen to what’s around me. The sound quality is crystal clear and makes me hear more of the music than I ever thought I could. The spatial sound turns music into a surround sound experience that was way better than I expected. The spatial sound was a little hard to setup, but that may just be because I’m an idiot. May take a few times, but you’ll get it eventually if you have the same problems I had. So far using these headphones, the only bad thing I can say about them is that the bass might be a little lower than I expected? But it’s not a big deal to me as I enjoy more of the quality of the sound rather than heavy bass, so if you really need to have heavy bass in your headphones, these might not be for you. As for the battery life, I haven’t had them long enough to know how well they are especially since these are also renewed. Thank you A4C Online for these wonderful headphones. I still cannot believe these are renewed headphones and am so glad I bought these from you! Thanks again. If you’re looking for a pair of AirPod Pros, you’re definitely making the right choice buying from them. The battery life is quite decent. After about 4 or 5 hours the battery life will drop to about 75%. Much more than I expected from a renewed product. Transparency is not as affective as I had originally thought. I have to turn down my music if I want to be able to hear anyone else. I wish they made it so you could increase the transparency to be louder otherwise I have to keep my music down low. Otherwise an excellent product still and I recommend buying these renewed AirPods.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

I don't care what budget it comes from, but I'd appreciate if you could spare $162.18 to one long-time customer who really wants to keep believing that Amazon has great customer service. Please make this right. Review Title: An ESN (Electronic Serial Number) that is marked as blacklisted indicates that the phone has been re
Review Content: An ESN (Electronic Serial Number) that is marked as blacklisted indicates that the phone has been reported lost or stolen, or it has outstanding unpaid balances. This status prevents the device from being activated on any network. A blacklisted phone cannot be used for service until the underlying issues are resolved. Here are the key points regarding a blacklisted ESN: Reported Lost or Stolen: The device has been flagged by the previous owner or carrier as missing. Unpaid Balances: The phone may be linked to an unpaid bill or financial obligation, which also leads to its blacklisting. Activation Issues: Carriers will not allow activation of a blacklisted device, making it unusable for calls, texts, or data services. Purchasing a phone with a blacklisted ESN can lead to significant issues: Immediate Deactivation: The phone may initially activate but will stop working shortly after. Limited Resale Value: Blacklisted devices have a much lower market value compared to unlocked or clean ESN devices. Legal Risks: If the phone was acquired through illegal means, there could be legal repercussions.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Review Title: Understanding who controls eSIM involves several key players and technologies
Review Content: Understanding who controls eSIM involves several key players and technologies. Mobile Network Operators (MNOs) — They are responsible for providing eSIM profiles and managing user subscriptions, enabling users to switch networks easily. Device Manufacturers — Companies like Apple and Samsung design devices that support eSIM technology, influencing how users interact with their mobile networks. Entitlement Servers — These servers are critical in the eSIM ecosystem, controlling access to mobile network services and managing user entitlements. Review Title: The phone was not damaged in any way
Review Content: The phone was not damaged in any way. It looked like a brand new phone, right out of the box! Not only that, but it functions flawlessly. I don't use all of the features (and it has a lot of them), mostly because I don't do social media stuff, or take many pictures. However, taking pictures is absolutely amazing! There are sooooo many options: like filters, colors, cropping, picture size, frame size, etc. There's just a ton of them. There is also Biometric features, which I appreciate. I had the S9+ and the fingerprint reader was on the back. If you use the fingerprint feature on this phone, make sure you set a passcode or pin as well. The fingerprint reader is on the screen. It shows as a pop-up. Of course you have to go through the fingerprint set-up first, and can choose more than one finger/thumb. My concern is that if the screen gets damaged where the reader is, the screen probably wouldn't be able to be able to read your print. It does NOT have an iris scanner. This IS a 5G phone, but it can connect to 4G and other networks as well. I believe there might have been a SIM card, but I honestly don't remember. I took the SIM from my other phone and put it in this one, so I didn't need it anyway. I use AT&T pre-paid, and it works fine. Right out of the box. I don't know if it's unlocked to a variety of different network or service providers. My service provider is AT&T, and the phone I got from this seller is also AT&T. My recommendation to anyone considering purchasing this phone, would be to contact the seller, first and ask about supported service providers. If you have AT&T, it's a total win! :) This phone charges super fast, and the battery life is fabulous. For my usage, anyway. You absolutely have to use a fast charging cable, or you'll ruin your phone. I believe it came with a USB cable, but I can't remember if the block was included. Either way, if you need to get a charging block, and/or cable, MAKE SURE they're fast charging!!! I thought the cable it came with was too short for my needs, so I bought a new one on Amazon that is specifically for the S23+...and phones like it. Another recommendation I have is to get an Otterbox. BEFORE you start using the phone. If you drop it, then a lot of money was spent for nothing. The camera lenses on the back protrude. I personally have the Otterbox Defender series, as the case itself prevents the camera lenses from touching any surface when you lay the phone down. It's the same if you lay it face down. The cover prevents the face from touching the surface of anything. I would seriously consider getting a high quality case with this phone, instead of a cheap knock-off. (Not all cases are created equal.) The phone is constructed of metal, not plastic, so it feels very well made. It's not a light phone, but not super heavy, either. At least to me. The phone doesn't come in an original box. At least mine didn't. It came with the phone and charging cable. I can't remember if it came with the little key that opens the SIM slot. If it doesn't, you'll need to get one. It also doesn't come with a manual. Also, unless you get the S23 Ultra, there is no stylus. If that's what you're looking for, the S23+ doesn't have that capability at all. You aren't able to get an S Pen with it, as the S Pen wouldn't function, even if you bought one and tried. I would also like to mention that it's super easy to transfer your data and contacts (and whatever else) to the S23+. I don't have any idea about transferring from an Apple product, though. Samsung is my go-to for phones. As for settings, there are too many to list. There is a specific one for the battery that I would like to mention, however. It makes it so your phone doesn't charge over 80% when fully charged, which is important. The phone won't overcharge that way and end up ruining your battery. As for call settings, there are a lot of those as well. For people that are hard of hearing, there are options for that. If, on the other hand, you'd like to protect your hearing and how loud the phone can get while listening to music or talking on it, you can limit the volume. It has features for the blind, but I don't know what that entails. It also has the car feature, but I don't know anything about that. I don't drive. Review Title: As a real hearing aid, something to hear others talk? For me, worthless
Review Content: As a real hearing aid, something to hear others talk? For me, worthless. I hear people better when I take them out. For that I should give 1 or 2 star rating. I hoped while my reg hearings were being repaired these would get me by. Nope. But. The sound quality for TV, computer, phone, and MUSIC! GREAT! I can enjoy music again. Our pellet stove is 8 feet away and noisy. The noise suppression all but blocks it out. The set up was super easy. I had my audiologist print out my hearing chart, or lack of hearing chart, took a pic with my I-phone, it quickly programed the Airpods and suddenly Janis Joplin sounded good again! Outside noise is blocked. I tried every ear pad that came with this and find the fit, ehh, so so. I have to be careful or they fall out. Left ear hurts after a half hour or so. Not the inner ear, but where it pushes on the cartridge. Getting used to it. Why did I keep them? Because of the sound quality when I do use them. Oh, and whoever designed the case after a greased water melon seed should be beat with something slick and hard to hold on to. A little embossed pattern on the case would have done a lot. And a better latch. If you drop these even a few inches the lid opens and the Airpods make a dash for the door. Dam near dropped one in the toilet. Caught it just in time. Luckily many aftermarket cases out there. And of course in Apple's weird system, a charger wasn't included and it takes a different one than my I-phone. Luckily I found one that fit and ordered a couple more. Youtube videos for how to set up are a must. I do have issues switching between my reg hearing aids and these, but usually not too bad. One time it's automatic, next time I'm in settings on my phone. But really not a big deal. Would be 5 star if they stayed in my ear and actually worked as a low grade hearing aid. But worth it for everything else. By programming like a hearing aid, sound quality is great!!! And blocking background noise is very nice. Might save on marriage counseling by not hearing each other. Review Title: (These are the reasons I couldn't give 5 stars
Review Content: (These are the reasons I couldn't give 5 stars. Had I not caught these issues — especially the charger — I would likely have been frustrated enough for 1 or 2 stars.) I'm coming from the S22 Ultra so the UI was immediately familiar, with many similar features and an easy transition. The biggest improvement is the processor — App installation, gaming without lag, browsing, music from the internal speakers, all noticeably better across the board. Most notably for my usual activities, game downloads that took 2+ minutes on my S22 Ultra now complete in approximately 10 seconds on the S23 Ultra. The difference is genuinely dramatic. I transferred approximately 128GB of apps and data wirelessly from my S22 Ultra in about 40 minutes. A USB-C to C cable would have been faster, but after the water detection warning I didn't want to use a cord for that step. The 40 minutes was likely influenced by the transfer speed of the older S22 Ultra as the source device. After the transfer, everything was loaded exactly as it was on my previous phone — it connected to my WiFi without entering a password, and my Samsung biometrics remembered passwords for each app, making it seamless to use immediately. The battery does not overheat the way the S22 Ultra is well known to do, which was a major concern of mine going in. The condition was as described. There were two very small micro cracks near the edge, but after applying a screen protector they are completely invisible. If they ever become visible I'll simply use a liquid glass repair solution. After extensive research I'm not concerned about the screen integrity. The camera is phenomenal. I was always impressed with the S22 Ultra camera, but the increased resolution makes every shot noticeably more vivid. Photos look almost better than real life, with no extra steps needed — just point and shoot. The 512GB storage is more than I'll likely ever need, even with a heavy volume of photos, videos and apps. I don't see myself coming close to capacity. I spent considerable time deciding between the S23 and S24 Ultra. After thorough research the benefits of paying several hundred dollars more for a marginally better camera and minor improvements weren't justified. This phone represents an incredible upgrade at a very reasonable price. Edit: After using for about a month i wanted to note that the battery lasts for an extreme long time, the photos are absolutely incredible, the processing speed... is unmatched, I used to lag, or have apps crash, now everything is seemeless. This is just an amazing phone!

Review Title: I waited about a week before posting to get a feel for the device and ensure everything works well
Review Content: I waited about a week before posting to get a feel for the device and ensure everything works well. Before the full review I want to note that I posted an unboxing video. The phone arrived in bubble wrap with a generic 10 watt charger included. Do not use that charger — plan to purchase a minimum 45 watt charger and a high quality cord. Using the included charger may cause battery overheating, slow charging, and long term battery damage. Another concern was that when I plugged the phone in for its initial full charge, I received a water detection warning. I tested three of my S22 Ultra cables that have never had issues and got the same warning each time. I used a small cool fan briefly, stood the phone upright. Just be cautious and double check your charging port before use. The water detection warning has not returned once since that first day — the fix worked completely. The phone also did not come with a SIM card removal tool. If you don't have one, the back of an earring works surprisingly well as a backup — that's always been my go-to. Luckily I had my own tool for the SIM swap.

Review Title: I severely cracked the screen on my older phone and the screen replacement was pretty expensive
Review Content: I severely cracked the screen on my older phone and the screen replacement was pretty expensive. This slightly newer model offered a significant upgrade ( I had an S22 Ultra and the S23 Ultra was a big jump in improvements) So instead of sinking money into the screen, I could get a newer model and more memory than I had before. I was upgrading from 256GB to 512GB so this seemed like a great deal. Because the phone is older, it took hours to download what felt like a million updates and get the phone up to date. Then doing Samsung Smart Switch took a while too. So I had hours into this before I even tried to activate it with Xfinity Mobile. When I did finally get to that part, I entered the IMEI number Xfinity Mobile said "Your phone is compatible but may be locked to another carrier". At that point I was crushed, I already was behind and needed a working phone. I immediately messaged the seller through Amazon to find out what could be going on. They replied a few hours later only to say they were sorry and offer a refund or replacement. So now I would be looking at more days without a working phone . I would have to spend hours wiping the phone data, mailing it back and then more hours to install updates and switch everything again on a new device. I really didn't want to send it back if there was any way for it to work. After reading more on Xfinity's site I saw this "Some carriers will automatically unlock their customers' phones after a period of time. Some carriers will only unlock your phone if you ask them to." and there are unlock services out there as well. The unlock services do not seem to be doing anything any different than your carrier can do so I decided to call Xfinity Mobile and see if they could help. But I also have to wonder why these mobile phone resellers do not just truly unlock the phones with a service since this is their business. They seem fine to put the burden on whoever buys it to figure it out. Xfinity Mobile was able to successfully get the phone active after about an hour on the phone with them. So I am really glad I didn't just send it back. Who is to say the replacement would not be the same thing all over again?This was an education in renewed phones but if this was my business I would offer this guidance right away in a troubleshooting section or email before I would have someone send back a "locked" phone. My time is valuable so all this messing around with the phone still costs me. It took time away from work and caused stress. This does take away from the value of the renewed phone being cheaper than a brand new one. Overall though the device itself was mostly as expected. The color is nice. The screen was in good shape with no scratches. It had a plastic sticker cover on it. The only minor scratches I saw were around the camera lenses on the back and around the edge of the lens. (not like the listing says - no scratches from 12 inches away as per the "excellent" description) Not a deal breaker though either as the camera appears to work fine. See my photo. The battery arrived not charged and at about 12% which was not that big of a deal. It charged fast and has held a charge. So as far as the device itself goes, it is a good device and matches the listing.

Review Title: I inspected it
Review Content: I inspected it. There are wear marks on the case and crown but the face was fine. I put a screen and case protector on it and it looks fine. I checked the battery life and it’s down to 85%. I’m sure that’s going to be fine. I know it can be replaced it I want to later. The sports band is not an Apple product but I don’t care. I quit buying Apple Watch bands years ago. I can buy 3 or 4 of these perfectly fine knockoffs for the price of one Apple. Other than the scuffs and battery it works as it should. Down with overpriced stuff and thumbs up for cheaper rebuilt semi quality stuff. Kinda like a rebuilt transmission. As for the functionality of the watch, it's fine except for the battery life. I have to charge it part way through the day IF I want it to last all day. On more than one occasion, by 4:00 pm, I got the 10% battery left message and then it is dead until I get it on a charger. Now, I'm going to have to spend $100 to get the battery replaced. AND - the watch charger that came with it, does not work. Yes, I took the piece of plastic off of it before trying it out. I'm beginning to regret my purchase. I guess I could see if I can replace the battery myself but I don't want to perform surgery on a piece of electronics at my age. The battery will be around $25 and the tool kit will be around $30 plus shipping and handling. Still saving money though. Maybe I can start a side hustle replacing apple watch batteries and save enough to go on vacation in the tropics or buy a small can of pineapple juice. Found a video tutorial that walked me through turning off a number of the functions of the watch to save on battery. I am pleased to report that after doing that, I can now wear it 10 or 11 hours and the watch will still have mid 70's battery left. I shouldn't have to do this but I did so Now I can wear it and not worry about taking a charger to work with me so I can charge it over my lunch break. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple iPhone 14 Pro Max, 128GB, Space Black - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: Unfortunately, the phone I received was nowhere near "Excellent
Review Content: Unfortunately, the phone I received was nowhere near "Excellent." The biggest issue is the camera system. One of the main reasons I chose the iPhone 14 Pro Max was for its three-camera setup. However, only one camera works properly in Photo mode. In Video mode, two cameras work, while the third doesn't work at all. The 0.5x ultra-wide camera is completely unavailable, and the 5x zoom function doesn't work either. This is especially frustrating because I'm an up-and-coming mechanic, and I regularly use the 0.5x camera to take photos in tight spaces while working on customers' vehicles. It's an important tool for my job, not just a feature I wanted. I upgraded from an iPhone 13 Pro Max where two of the cameras had failed, so I was excited to finally have a phone with all three cameras working. Instead, I ended up with another phone that has camera issues. At that point, I could have saved money by buying an iPhone 14 Plus with only two cameras and probably received a phone that actually worked. Another concern was that the phone was not properly factory reset. The packaging states that Amazon Renewed devices are supposed to be factory reset before being resold. However, when I powered it on, it started up like a normal phone instead of taking me through the initial setup process. It appeared the previous owner had simply signed out of their Apple ID rather than the phone being completely erased and reset. I contacted Amazon Customer Support to request a replacement since the phone was defective. I was told there were no more iPhone 14 Pro Max devices in Excellent condition available to send as a replacement. However, when I checked the same Amazon listing, it still showed the exact same phone in Excellent condition available for purchase. I don't understand why replacements weren't available when the listing indicated more were in stock. I would have been happy to return the defective phone in exchange for a properly functioning one. I understand that Amazon Renewed products are used, and I wasn't expecting a brand-new phone. However, I did expect to receive the condition I paid for and a device with all advertised features working correctly. A phone with a partially functioning camera system should never pass inspection as "Excellent," especially when customers are paying a premium for that condition. Overall, this experience was extremely disappointing. Amazon Renewed is supposed to give customers confidence that devices have been inspected and tested. Based on my experience, the inspection process failed, and customer service did not provide a reasonable solution. Review Title: These are really superb headphones when you accept the following realities:
Review Content: These are really superb headphones when you accept the following realities: - The drivers (and active noise cancelling) burn out and go berserk in about a year - You cannot reasonably pair them to more than one device, as they freak out - You absolutely must use the soundcore app to EQ out most of the bass in order to get proper sound quality I have two pairs, one about a year old and one a couple months old. The year old ones will crunch and screech (literally like an alien screaming in your ear) when music has a loud or busy mix, or when you lie down on your ear on a pillow while ANC is on, or if they're turned up too high. They also occasionally go into "earthquake" mode, as I call it, with ANC on, where it sounds like an earthquake in your ears until you take them out and put them back in. They're only useful as backups for when the other ones die or get lost for, say, a quiet podcast. If them paired to my phone and laptop at the same time, and come into range of one device while they are paired to another, they will always panic and act unpredictably. Sometimes they disconnect from both entirely, or half their volume and "connect to both" but really they are connected to one and unstable. There is zero upside to having them paired to more than one device. I think only Apple Airpods have really figured this out and its because they write the firmware for all three devices, so. Not a fair fight really. The microphones are AMAZING. An actual replacement for a bluetooth headset, and better than my regular iPhone mic. I used these at work for a while when I was doing phone sales. 100x better than any Airpods I've used. I bought my first pair on TikTok for $15 and my second for $25. Both a fine price to pay. I see these trade offs as pretty much fine for me. I've owned every type of airpod except the maxes and wear headphones 10+ hours a day 5 days a week. When EQ'd, these are pretty much as good as Airpod Pro 2nd gens. Without the EQ they are a bassy mudfest. They last like 5+ hours on one charge even when they're old. My #1 reccomendation for bluetooth headphones. The tiny little hearing aid batteries die in them all anyway, whether you get $300 ones or $20 ones. And these are 100x better than the no name ones you'd get at a discount store for the same price.

Yes, it meets the described spec of >80% for their “Excellent” condition, but will going to be into the Apple service condition in a couple of weeks. Returned to Amazon/Woot and waiting for refund. After reading a ton of reviews I decided to give it one more shot and get a “Premium” condition directly from Amazon.com. Most of the reviews of these phones were much better than all of the other vendors. They are definitely more expensive but come with a 365 day warranty vs 90 day and spec at >90% battery life. Phone arrived today. It was VERY nicely packaged in a SEALED shrink wrapped professional looking box. Opened the box and found a phone with what appeared to be the original Apple protective film still in place on the front and back. Battery was dead so after a quick charge I was able to check battery health…… 100% and 0 charge cycles. Basically this is a brand NEW, NEVER USED phone. I can’t say how impressed I was after three bad experiences. I saved a couple $hundred compared to BB or Apple and got a brand new phone ….. It’s all about the journey  !!! This is a dishonest and deceptive practice, and I strongly advise others to avoid this seller. Buying a phone should not come with the risk of it being remotely disabled due to someone else’s unpaid balance. Review Title: The condition was as if brand new, the S pen was included
Review Content: The condition was as if brand new, the S pen was included. And 512GB of memory? Wow! No more dealing with SD cards and figuring out where things are stored. All for $424 and 12 months to pay with no interest on my Amazon CC. My history of of cellular phones goes back almost 40 years to car phones. As to PCS hand held phones, 25 years. Many Nokias, then Windows Phone, then very grudgingly, Android, only because my beloved 950XL does not have voice over data and technology moved on. I got a Samsung A52. I have had phones that I didn't particularly like, but none have I hated as much as that A52. SO many stupid things, constant misbehaviors. I can't tell you how many times I threw that puppy against the wall. Good thing it has a great case. Well, Mr. Samsung. All is forgiven with this S22 Ultra. This is the first phone I've ever had that did not allow a "no lock" option. I've never had reason to lock my phone from prying eyes or fingers. No big secrets and I don't lose my phones. Anyway, this phone requires some form of security...god, I've come to hate that word...but I found the fingerprint unlock to work well, so that hurdle crossed without pain. I really, really hate doing things on the tiny screen and keyboard of a phone. The Microsoft Phone Link has been a god send, letting me use a big monitor, keyboard and mouse for messages and other purposes. SO much nicer and easier. Well, it just got better with the Samsung DeX feature. Plug the phone into a USB port on the PC and now you have a work station. (Historical note: My Windows Phone could do this with the optional docking station a decade ago.) Now I can use the Samsung Snapseed (like Adobe Lightroom, but FREE!) and ExpertRAW apps with the comfort of a real keyboard and mouse. A number of YT reviewers complained about the battery life. Gee, I'm running video games and movies all day, why does the battery suck? Even then, they reported that it could run all day. I'm happy to report that with the light duty of phone, text, some GPS, and other odds and ends, the battery life is great. Down 20-30% after a day of that kind of use. The Samsung Camera app is thorough and easy to use. I say this having tried other camera apps, and even a short lived Pixel 8 phone. I ditched that in less than a day, the camera app was SO clunky. Then in the hardware background, the Ultra claims to have a larger sensor...this is always good...than its S22 cousins and with a higher pixel count. 108MP? Wow. My first digital camera had 2.1MP. The S pen and note feature is amazing and I'm just starting to learn all of its capabilities. The phone updated to Android 14 and 6.1 OneUI w/o issue. Samsung guarantees several more years of OS upgrades and seven years of security upgrades. The summary is that for only the third time in 25 years do I love a phone and not just tolerate it. I can't imagine someone not liking this phone, and the differences between this and the just out S25 are not worth $1000 bucks. Product Title: Amazon.com: Samsung Galaxy S22 Ultra 5G, US Version, 128GB, Black - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: I bought this phone in refurbished/excellent condition
Review Content: I bought this phone in refurbished/excellent condition. After reading multiple reviews on multiple refurbished phone listings on Amazon, my biggest concern was (always is) getting one with a damaged screen, cameras, or having it not truly be unlocked. I've had this phone less than 24 hours, but here's my take SO far (I can't speak for other people, these are just my experiences): 1) Yes, it was (for me) truly, 100% unlocked. Not even an ex-carrier logo when I first turned it on! (My previous 'unlocked' refurbished phone has a T-Mobile logo when turned on) I was quite happy/impressed about this. 2) No scratches (that I could see) on the front/touchscreen. There are multiple, TINY scuffs on the sides (not part of the touchscreen)/top edge/bottom edge of the phone - which I fully expected w/ a refurbished phone, and I'm totally fine with it (and this is if I'm REALLY nitpicking - they're really not that bad, though. It's just not FLAWLESS, which - again - I'm fine with). 3) 99% flawless on the backside - the ONLY thing I can see is a TINY scuff on the edge of one of the cameras (not the actual camera/glass screen itself), and this is cosmetic - it doesn't affect the quality of the camera (that I've noticed). 4) S-Pen pops out like it should, seems to be fine. 5) Charges just fine so far - both wireless and wired. 6) Popped in my SIM card (US Mobile, uses T-Mobile network), and it worked instantly. No phone/SIM-related problems so far. Everything - and I mean everything (data, wallpapers, photos, Samsung Notes from my previous phone, sounds/ringtones, apps, folders, etc) - transferred from my old phone perfectly (Samsung Smart Switch app). 7) Fingerprint reader works fine for me so far - and that's with a plastic-y (TPU?) screen protector that I put on it. I haven't noticed any real issues thus far - if anything changes, I'll update my review. OVERALL: For me, yes it's definitely worth the money. Review Title: I ordered the iPhone 15 Pro Max refurbished and it arrived last night
Review Content: I ordered the iPhone 15 Pro Max refurbished and it arrived last night. After spending a good 3+ hours setting it up, I realized the lens for the main camera was broken. From the outside, you can’t see any issue. It wasn’t until I opened up the camera app that I actually saw it didn’t work. “Renewed Premium” carries a certain standard with it, and this certainly does not meet that in the slightest. On top of that, upon calling customer support, I was told that I would not be able to do anything unless I deactivated the phone and remove my Apple ID from it. Wouldn’t have been the end of the world if I needed to go back to my other phone for a bit, however, in order to set up this phone with the eSIM, deactivated my previous SIM card. Upon explaining all of that to customer support, I was told there was nothing they could do unless I deactivated this phone (leaving me without a phone until they received this and shipped me a new one) I was then told to call Apple to see what they can do, when honestly, this is their mistake. Either way, I called apple and it was going to be another set of hoops to jump through with scheduling appointments and all that. Plus since I didn’t have apple care, if they needed to repair the camera, I would still be without a phone. So even if Apple was able to help fix this, the issue of me not having a phone would still be there. Had I broken this camera myself - I would certainly except those terms given there’s not much else I could do. However, this was given to me in this condition and for Amazon to leave me with the responsibility of fixing their mistake due to carelessness in inspection and quality control is absurd. So whether I like it or not, I am now STUCK with the responsibility of cleaning this up since my account is connected to this phone now. What at one point could have been a great gift to myself has turned into the biggest hassle I’ve experienced buying/returning anything, probably ever. I’m going to give this one more shot as I’ve now ordered another iPhone from them to be delivered shortly, however, it’s also required me to spend another ~$1000 in having that iPhone sent prior to me getting my refund. This is absolutely ridiculous and unacceptable. Even if this next phone is perfect, I’m likely never going to order from the Amazon refurbished store again. I’ll either go straight to Apple refurbished, or brand new, for any of my future phone/laptop/device purchases. On top of all this hassle, I’ll certainly have to spend another few hours setting up my replacement phone once it arrives. All the time I’ve invested into this so far has NOT been even close worth the “nice discount” on a premium refurbished phone that should have arrived without issue to begin with. Amazon - take note. Change your policies. Making this the customer’s mess to clean up is not acceptable. I’ll plan to update this review if anything changes. But like I said, even if the next phone I ordered is perfect, I still give this a 1-star review for all the hassle and lack of responsibility the company took to resolve this. P.s. i’ll also add that I am a quite understanding and peaceful person. The person I spoke with from customer support was doing his absolute best to help me, but this was clearly a bigger issue than he had the power to solve. I requested to have this escalated to upper management and was told the same thing. Whoever is the one making decisions about what can and can’t be done needs to hear about this. Product Title: Amazon.com: Beats Studio Pro - Wireless Bluetooth Noise Cancelling Headphones - Black (Renewed) : Electronics
Review Title: I bought this product because my ears get fatigued from AirPods (Pro) sometimes but I want to still
Review Content: I bought this product because my ears get fatigued from AirPods (Pro) sometimes but I want to still listen to my audiobooks. I also wanted something for airplane trips. Sleeping with earbuds on the plane is painful and then I’ve had one or both fall out and roll under my seat or way back under someone else’s seat, which is really gross. Even though they are a bit heavy, they are very comfortable.I have small ears, so these fit really well—right inside with no pressure on the cartilage. If you have big ears or a big head, I don’t know. It might be worth a try anyway. I love being able to control the volume on the device, unlike my AirPods where you have to pull out the phone to control the volume. I have a few cons though. I can’t really wear these outside or for intense workouts because if I get sweaty, they slide around on my ears. My son would wear these while mowing the lawn and I thought I could too, but it didn’t work well. I got sweaty and they slid around and broke the audio seal, letting in a lot of background noise. And they don’t have the noise cancelling capability that AirPods do. When I mow with the AirPods, I only hear a little background noise. With these headphones I still hear a lot of background noise. Same thing goes for using the vacuum cleaner and even at the car wash. With AirPods, I hear nothing. With these, I have to turn the volume way up to drown out the background noise. This concerns me for flights because I want everything tuned out except my audiobook or maybe a movie. But the Bluetooth range is awesome!! With my AirPods, the phone has to be in fairly close proximity or it will lose connectivity. With these headphones I can go way down the street away from my phone and they will still be connected! I will have my phone plugged in inside the basement and go all the way out to the mailbox or to the neighbor’s house and still be connected. It’s like a dream! I can go places around my home and property with these headphones I couldn’t go before (with the phone left inside somewhere). They also are comparable to AirPods in regards to phone calls, Google meet, or FaceTime. I haven’t worn them long enough to determine battery life. My hope is they will last on a cross country or international flight with constant use. AirPods definitely don’t. So these headphones have not replaced my AirPods, but I certainly prefer them in certain situations over others. I’m happy I bought them!
