Product Title: Amazon.com: Sony WF-1000XM5 Truly Wireless Bluetooth Noise Canceling Headphones - Black (Renewed) : Electronics
Review Title: The headphones themselves are phenomenal
Review Content: The headphones themselves are phenomenal. These are the only earbuds I've ever used which I could not improve with EQ. I'm literally using the default, flat EQ because that sounds best to my ear. Incredible. I bought these as an upgrade over the Anker Soundcore Space A40, which compare favourably for the money. I can EQ the Anker to sound fairly close to the Sony, but the Anker lacks a sparkle and clarity which I can only seem to get out of the Sony. If you can't afford the Sony, the Anker would be a decent alternative if you're comfortable with a slight decrease in sound quality. Sony's Android software is horrible. Sony needs to fire every product manager and director involved in that abomination. Installing the software, one is bombarded with seven thousand modal dialog boxes informing the user of a million different features, asking intrusive questions, and generally just being annoying. The spam doesn't stop once you proceed through the initial setup. At all times, weird popups appear to distract you from your task. The UI controls feel clunky and severely lacking polish, like something made by a garage startup company. There are a limited number of EQ presets, and you cannot add more. There are only 3 slots for custom EQ configurations, a pointless limitation in the age of software. Changing between EQ presets causes the sound to cut out for about 500 milliseconds, which severely impedes the ability to compare custom EQ and fine-tune them. Astonishingly, the "Flat" EQ preset does NOT sound identical to a "Custom" EQ preset which is set to a flat configuration. Two flat EQ profiles that do not sound the same. I have no idea what is going on, but this makes no sense. I personally find the default "Flat" EQ to sound best, but I would like to boost the bass very slightly, and I can't do this, because as soon as I move that slider, the Sony software forces me to start editing the "Custom" EQ preset, beginning from a flat EQ profile, which does NOT sound the same as the "Flat" profile. It is thus impossible to modify the default, "Flat" EQ profile, which is pretty infuriating because these headphones are very expensive. The sound isolation is phenomenal. The memory foam ear tips appear to be doing almost all of the heavy lifting. I have a large box fan near me, and when I insert the headphones with noise cancellation disabled, I can barely hear the (normally quite loud) fan. Activating noise cancellation removes all remaining noise. I can't speak to the rest of the frequency spectrum, but compared to the Anker Soundcore Space A40, these Sony earbuds are SILENT. It's an eerie silence. I wasn't expecting the noise cancellation to be this good. Note that it will depend heavily on whether the earbuds seal your canal correctly. On initial insertion, I didn't get a good seal, and I wondered if the noise cancellation was working at all. Overall I think these earbuds have incredible potential. Their performance reputation is well deserved. However, Sony clearly does not care about its customers and their day-to-day experience. Incredible hardware paired with infuriatingly bad software. Sony is lucky that the default performance of these buds is so good, otherwise I would want to return them. Update #1: I did some research and found that Sony makes replacement ear tips, model EP-NI1010, but Sony's authorized online reseller in Canada does not sell them! These ear tips appear unavailable within Canada, and will cost over $100 to import from overseas. Total customer service disaster. I contacted Amazon customer support, who offered a partial refund for the missing earbud tips, or a full refund if I return the product. They also recommended that I reach out to the seller to ask them to send the missing tips, which I have done. Update #2: I discovered, buried within the Sony Headphones Connect Android app, that I can request replacement ear tips from Sony! Tap the "System" tab, then scroll down and tap on the text "Determines Optimal Earbud Tips". Do the "Test The Wearing Condition" test. After the test has failed, you will see an option: "The earbud tips may be too small ... If none of the supplied earbud tips fit, you can request other types of earbud tips. Click here to order." You can then select your country and fill out a form to request replacement earbud tips. After entering my address, I received the message: "We have received your request for new earbud tips. Please allow 7 to 10 business days for processing and delivery." I didn't enter my credit card information, so it appears that these will be free. We'll see what happens. I should note that after filling out this form once, the option does not appear again, even if you reinstall the app. To get the option to order replacements again, go to the "System" tab within the Sony Headphones Connect app, scroll to the bottom and select "Initialize Settings", then choose "Initialize App/Headphone Settings". Update #3: On the recommendation of other buyers, I bought the SpinFit Omni ear tips as a replacement. I got the small size, which is about 1 mm smaller than the medium Sony ear tips size that I have access to. On comparative listening, there is a slightly better sound from the Sony memory foam ear tips, but the SpinFit Omni are quite competitive. The Sonys are warmer and give better punch to bass frequencies. The sound isolation is also slightly better, but only slightly. Memory foam surprisingly seems to make a difference! Update #4: Sony reached out to me via email to clarify my shipping address, and have confirmed that they are shipping replacement ear tips to me. Yay! Update #5: Sony did not provide any tracking information for the replacement ear tips, and I received phone calls from FedEx indicating that I was not home to receive the package. It turns out that Sony sent the ear tips using FedEx Direct Signature requirement, and they are now being held at some location, and I must physically go there with my ID. I am disabled and cannot travel to this location, and FedEx will not allow another person to pick up the package instead. It makes no sense to ship a cheap replacement part with an expensive and inconvenient signature requirement. I get Amazon packages left at my front door every day without issue. I emailed Sony to request that they call FedEx to waive the signature requirement, and ask FedEx to make a redelivery, which is how FedEx insists upon resolving such situations. Update #6: I called Sony and, to their credit, had one of the best customer support experiences of my life. Their phone tree is a horrible labyrinth of pain and suffering, but once I got through to a human on my THIRD call, that human was truly wonderful and clarified that Sony had contacted FedEx with my request, but was waiting on a response. Sony said they would email me when there is a resolution. Update #7: The package finally arrived, but with no notice. I found it in my mailbox when I checked my mail. It contained the WRONG replacement ear tips. The replacements are silicone, but the XM5 earbuds are supposed to come with memory foam ear tips. I am heartbroken. This ordeal has wasted way too much of my time. This is a terrible way to treat customers who keep giving unlimited second chances to make things right. I have emailed Sony to ask them to send the correct part. Update #8: I did some comparative listening between the new silicone replacement ear tips that Sony sent (YY2963/BQ-TPKIT), the original Sony memory foam tips (EP-NI1010), the SpinFit Omni, and my Sennheiser HD-600 open back headphones. The new Sony silicones seal much easier and better in my ear canal compared to the Sony memory foam ones, providing shockingly improved noise cancellation. These are by far the best noise cancelling ear tips currently in my possession, however this may be due to fitting my ear canal better. Recall that the Sony memory foam ear tips I currently have are one size too large for me. The SpinFit Omni feel slightly too small by comparison. The Sony silicone tips are very competitive with the Sony memory foam tips, but have slightly less clarity, slightly muddier bass, and louder bass. The Sony memory foam tips have tighter bass which can sound punchier at times, and add a high end clarity and sparkle which, although very slight, really elevates the immersiveness of the sound for certain tracks. Going back and forth, I really feel the silicone tips are very competitive, and ultimately it comes down to a matter of taste: do you prefer a warmer tone, or a tone with more sparkle and clarity? I prefer clarity, especially now because I suffer from derealization due to prior COVID infection, so my conscious experience feels distant and removed from reality, as if I am experiencing reality through a television screen. Enhanced clarity of sound brings my conscious experience closer to what I used to experience before my disability. So I still give the edge to the Sony memory foam tips, although when listening to a panel of several songs, I'm not confident that I could tell them apart from the Sony silicone in a blind listening test. The SpinFit Omni featured noticeably less bass, higher treble, sounding almost tinny and a little bit shrill, and very noticeably inferior noise cancellation. However, to SpinFit's credit, the Omni tips still provide very good performance, especially when compared to other headphones such as the Anker Soundcore Space A40 mentioned earlier in this review. The Sony silicone tips sounded clearly superior to the SpinFit, however only when wearing the medium size; the small size sounded very similar to the SpinFit, suggesting that the seal quality within the ear canal is a critical factor, and the next larger size of SpinFit may be competitive with the Sony silicone. The Sennheiser HD-600 open-back headphones performed surprisingly poorly, and while I do prefer them to the SpinFit, and while they do sound very good, they featured weaker bass and slightly too elevated treble tones for my taste. My conclusion is that the Sony WF-1000XM5 with Sony memory foam ear tips remain the gold standard. I would really like Sony to send me the correct ear tips that I bought and paid for, because the memory foam seems integral to the sound of the XM5 earbuds. The only reason to pay so much money for a pair of wireless earbuds is to achieve the best possible sound quality, and achieving this is now a critical accessibility need for me since my disability compromises the way that I perceive sound. I actually require the product to perform at its best in order to enjoy music in the way that an able-bodied person could with inferior earbuds. Update #9: It has been 3 months since my purchase. I tried to make Sony's replacement tips work for a while, but they keep sliding out of my ears when I am just a little bit sweaty, or for about an hour after I take a shower. I gave up and requested a partial refund from Amazon. After some convincing, they relented and gave me the refund, which I have now immediately spent on a pair of AZLA SednaEarfit MAX Standard tips. Despite being silicone, these tips produce a frequency response nearly identical to the original XM5 foam tips. @aaronloudnwireless on YouTube has a video comparing the frequency response of the original Sonys, the AZLA, and also the Comply TrueGrip Pro. At this point, I have paid almost as much out of pocket to make up the difference between new and used XM5s, and purchasing the used model was a waste of time. To Amazon's credit, they are the only party who provided meaningful customer service on this issue; both Sony and the seller let me down. I don't know if I would recommend purchasing XM5s based on the experience so far, though the sound quality remains stellar. I popped in the original ear tips for another quick listen today, and the improvement in quality between those and Sony's replacement silicone tips is noticeable. This product is such a hot mess.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))       [Report](javascript:void(0)) Sending feedback...Thanks, we'll investigate in the next few days. Review Title: Upon booting the phone it was not fully charged, where it already had an account on the phone
Review Content: Upon booting the phone it was not fully charged, where it already had an account on the phone. The seller claimed the phone was unlocked, however, the phone booted with t-mobile software and was not factory reset. This prompted me to reach out to Samsung to confirm if the phone was unlocked or not where I was told by the rep after providing the IMEI information that the phone is locked to T-mobile carrier. I next contacted t-mobile and the rep stated that the phone is not eligible to be unlocked, which rendered the phone unusable. This ordeal has been a huge inconvenience due to the fact I spent money on the phone with guarantee it would be unlocked and working. The seller had responsibility to ensure the phone was wiped of all previous user data, as well as ensuring the phone was not restricted to any carrier. If so, I would not be writing my review to warn others. I should not have had to go through so many hoops to confirm the validity of the phone when the phone should have been in the 'unlocked condition' as described on Amazon. I am recommending that AMAZON put in place a system that requires the SELLER to verify that the phone is unlocked by loading IMEI info before we as the CUSTOMER complete the purchase to prevent this from reoccurring. I have reached out to the seller to resolve this issue and have sent the phone back to receive a full refund. This experience has made me question Amazon's standards in regards to electronics where I do not have confidence or faith in purchasing any phone that is claimed to be unlocked from its Amazon sellers. Not until Amazon can guarantee that sellers will be true to their listings. In addition, the seller should be more mindful and considerate of the phones they are selling to people as we are spending real money and trusting that they will send us a phone that works and is truly unlocked with no restrictions as described. Please be aware of the risks you are taking when purchasing a "refurbished" or "renewed" phone from Amazon as you may not recieve the item as it is described on Amazon. Review Title: I purchased this Motorola Razr+ 2025 through Amazon on April 20, 2026
Review Content: I purchased this Motorola Razr+ 2025 through Amazon on April 20, 2026. The phone was not even four months old when it developed a line along the edge and became increasingly difficult to close. The phone was otherwise in good condition. I contacted the seller expecting a reasonable resolution, but the seller did not take responsibility for the problem. I then contacted Amazon Customer Service multiple times. This is where the experience became extremely frustrating. Amazon representatives repeatedly told me they would help. I was told the seller would assist with a replacement or refund. When that did not happen, another Amazon representative told me the warranty team had been contacted and that I would receive refund/replacement confirmation within 72 hours. I waited, and no one contacted me. I contacted Amazon again and was then told that the seller was not helpful and that Amazon had filed an A-to-z claim against the seller. The representative specifically told me that the guarantee reimbursement would be credited to my original payment method and that I would receive confirmation within three business days. I have since spoken with multiple additional Amazon representatives, including a manager. I have been sent links that lead me in circles, told to contact different departments, and even had one representative tell me she was submitting an appeal before leaving the conversation without providing confirmation or a reference number. At this point, I have spent far too much time trying to get a resolution for a phone that should not have developed this type of problem after less than four months. The most disappointing part is not just the defective phone—it is the lack of accountability and the repeated runaround after purchasing an expensive product through Amazon. I would strongly recommend that Amazon and the seller take responsibility for resolving defective products instead of making customers repeatedly explain the same situation to different representatives. I purchased this phone expecting it to last much longer than four months. Instead, I have spent weeks trying to get someone to take responsibility. Very disappointing experience. A total mess       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Review Title: I have had it for over a month and it works great
Review Content: I have had it for over a month and it works great. Overall. 1. The finger reader under the screen is really bad. My old LG had it on the back and it was 100% reliable and super fast. You grab the phone and it's ON. With the Samsung, it's hit and miss. Maybe 50% success and you have to look where you put the finger and how. It's not intuitive at all and makers should go back to normal readers. 2. The face recognition is useless as the camera has to face you and you have to face the camera. Forget unlocking the phone while on the table (must be tilted first), or next to your body. Or if you wear sunglasses. Or with facial cover (in winter) or while you drink or eat... I would take back or side fingerprint reader any time. And no, Apple is not any better. 3. The USB port is very loose and detaches from USB cable (many tested) with the slightest touch. Forget charging in your bag. 4. The camera app is not user friendly. Like you have to switch between photo and video settings to take video. My phone 10 yrs ago had a dedicated video button in photo settings for a quick video snap. 5. The general UI is wonky. Not my first Samsung but I don;t remember the last one S6 was this bad. 2. It doesn't lag. It has 12 GB RAM. Much better than most of new phones. 3. It's cheap! It's so much better deal than virtually any new cheap phone and better than new phone double or triple its price.

Review Title: First thing - my unlocked phone came to life with the AT&T boot up screen
Review Content: First thing - my unlocked phone came to life with the AT&T boot up screen. That scared me, and I came back to the listing to read again to be sure it was supposed to be unlocked. I proceeded to set up the phone for use, in my own way. I won't go into details, but setup wasn't exactly standard. The phone upgraded from Android 14 to Android 16, then downloaded several security updates. I logged into her Google account, and added the phone, then used Samsung's utility to transfer all files and data via USB cable. Losing the grandchildren's photos would be worth more than my life, but that worked quite well. With the phone almost ready for use, I went to her former carrier, and requested that the phone number be released for transfer to my own carrier. Wait, and wait, and wait and finally they came through. The moment of truth was upon me. I went to my carrier's site, and started activation of the unlocked AT&T phone. That went smoothly. I guess the phone really is unlocked. This IS a refurbished phone, I must assume that someone installed the AT&T app and other software before returning the phone for some reason. Factory reset didn't rid the phone of AT&T branding for some reason. I am pretty impressed with this device, so far. I love the 12 gig of RAM - quickly disabled the RAM boost because virtual memory can and will wear out your - cough - "disk drive". I refuse to call the storage "memory", even when being misused for virtual memory. I fully expect this phone to last to 2030, and beyond. (Our budget phones have always been pushed a year past end of support, without scratches and other damage.) Overall, it took me about six hours to get this device ready for my wife to continue setting it up. I did some minimal debloating. Why do phones come with so much pre-installed crap? I still have some stuff to remove, but that will require installing ADB, and digging deeper into the OS. I will return at some point to update this review. She will find any and all problems with this phone in short order! I will most likely return in a few months to get another one for myself. (I'm always 8 to 10 months behind her on upgrading to a newer phone!) For the price, this refurbished or renewed phone seems a great bargain! Merry Christmas everyone! Review Title: The package arrived a day early, which was nice and unexpected
Review Content: The package arrived a day early, which was nice and unexpected. My phone was put into what seemed like a generic Android phone box, which, I’ll let you know damn near gave me a heart attack when I opened. Inside were a few things. Charger and charging brick are standard but the cable feels pretty nice and the brick is a good size. Standard plastic holder inside. Nothing more, nothing less. No complaints. For the actual phone, it was inside of a plastic zip bag. The bag itself was scratched up so it was difficult to see the phone inside until i took it out. Overall, 9.5/10 for cosmetics. Then, the battery. My particular phone came with 80% battery health, which I personally don’t mind. I have the means to be able to get it replaced when the time comes, and to be honest was a relief after my last IPhone 11 from another seller had 100% battery health, just for it to be a non-Apple battery and cause all sorts of problems. Overall, I have no complaints with this phone. It’s in great condition in my book. Mic, speakers, cameras, haptics, everything (as far as I’ve been using it) has been in perfect order. Based on other reviews, whatever phone you get from this seller honestly depends on luck. It’s trivial, and that should never be the case, but if you can, I’d say take the risk. Worse case scenario you return it and get a full refund and try again. Overall, I’m very happy with my purchase. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple iPhone 11 Pro, 256GB, Space Gray - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: We got the phone and it looked great, seemed to work fine
Review Content: We got the phone and it looked great, seemed to work fine. Except it would not connect to cellular. After a week and a half of going round and round with our phone carrier, we finally figured out the phone was not fully unlocked as the listing had set. We initiated a return and were told we would be refunded when the phone was received and checked. I was initially told by the Amazon CSR I spoke to that as a courtesy, they would issue the refund as soon as the item showed it was picked up by UPS. After waiting a few days and no sign of refund, I called again. I was told by this CSR that I was given incorrect info, Amazons policy was to issue the refund when it’s received and checked. OK. So I wait again. I was told that once the phone was received, it could be up to 30 business days for it to be checked and refunded—but it rarely takes that long. I was given the date it was received. More waiting, then a full 30 business days after it had been received I called again to check on refund. It had not been initiated, but that CSR was initiating it. It literally took a full month and a half from the time Amazon received it (not from the time UPS picked it up—from the time Amazon actually received it back at their facility) for my refund to post. And the reason it was being returned was because it was misrepresented in the listing (not being fully unlocked), not because we changed our mind or anything frivolous. That did not matter and there was no courtesy or concession for what was their mistake in the first place. If you do get anything Amazon renewed, beware. If it works (like the 2nd phone we ordered did), it’s great and a wonderful option if you can’t afford fully new. But if there’s a problem you will get the run around, delays and misinformation from Amazon’s CSRs. They claim to stand behind all renewed products, but they will absolutely drag their feet and claim “it’s our policy” while you’re left waiting endlessly. So when it comes to Amazon renewed, don’t be blinded by the great prices and guarantees…it’s definitely “buyer beware”! There is a small caveat: When nothing is playing in the earbuds and it's currently relatively quiet in your environment, there is a very apparent white noise that plays in the earbuds. It's an audible hiss. I've researched it and it seems it's the ANC microphones doing their thing and no company has discovered the technology to prevent that yet. Not sure why you'd be wearing these in a quiet room with nothing playing through them, but just know that it does that. Comfort - my ears are very sensitive to cartilage fatigue and these are outstandingly comfortable. I wear them for hours at a time. Connectivity - connecting to my phone was a clusterflup! It was glitchy, twitchy, and I was close to giving up returning the earbuds after trying for like an hour! Im an android user (Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra), so maybe Apple has a better connection quality with these buds. I'm not sure if it's a "Bose" issue or a "Refurbished" issue. Controls - the controls of the earbuds aren't confusing and actually seem pretty cool. Tap once to pause/play, twice to go to next song, thrice to backtrack a song, swipe upward on the earbud stick to raise volume, downward to lower volume, hold left earbud to change between ANC Quiet mode and Transparent mode, hold right earbud to engage AI assistant. They are great ONLY WHEN THEY WORK PROPERLY. It has happened endless times where I'll try to pause a track and it'll instead skip to the next one. Or I'll slightly adjust my earbuds and it'll stop, and I mean STOP not "pause", the audio entirely (which is not supposed to be an option??) and I have to trigger the AI assistant to get the audio going again so I don't have to get my phone. Sometimes the left earbud will just suddenly stop being in Quiet mode and will go Transparent. Today, I received a phone call and I single-tapped the earbud to answer, just to hear the AI assistant tell me "Call Ignored." Very frustrating and a big reason why I ended up returning these earbuds and won't be gambling on getting a different refurbished pair. Phone App: Bose's app could definitely use an upgrade. The connection is a little shoddy with the earbuds, but overall the app is does not have an engaging interface and it's not intuitive to navigate or understand all the options. Battery life - is okay. I only use it with ANC on max, which drains the battery faster but it lasts for a few hours which is what it promises but just keep that in mind. If you throw them in the case unplugged (assuming the case is charged) it'll charge them up pretty fast. While I highly recommend Bose Quietcomfort, I cannot comfortably recommend this generation refurbished, even in excellent condition. Although I am ultimately returning this pair, I am absolutely hooked on Bose Quietcomfort line of earbuds and have just decided to look elsewhere. Ended up finding a brand new unopened box of Bose Quietcomfort Ultra Earbuds 1st Gen at the same price as these ($140) on eBay. Observations: The high level basic differences are: 1) about a $100 difference; 2) three vs. 12 months return period: 3) battery level of 80% vs. 90%. Recommendation: After considering the factors, I decided to look into how much a replacement battery would cost, which is $40 right now. However, starting with the iPhone 8 (i think), Apple started sealing the cases, which requires a heat gun to separate the case because of the extra waterproofing adhesive. To breakdown the addition $100 cost, subtract the $40 battery from that, leaving $60 for an additional 9-months (or $6.67/month) to "insurance" to return the phone if issues come up. Carrier Lock: I decided I wanted an unlocked version, and that appears to be another feature that is included with Premium Renewed, with the majority of carrier locked versions being offered as renewed only. Conclusion: For the additional $100, I elected to go with the Renewed Premium. I rate both the Renewed and the Premium Renewed as 5-stars. Review Title: I’m very disappointed with the noise canceling on the JBL Tune 770 headphones
Review Content: I’m very disappointed with the noise canceling on the JBL Tune 770 headphones. They struggled to eliminate deep airplane engine roar during a normal flight. Most of the engine noise seemed to be converted into loud white noise, except for the very deep thrum. I actually checked to make sure the headphones weren’t touching the seat and conducting the thrum directly to my ears. When the engines roared even more during landing, the JBL crackled as they tried to maintain the noise canceling. As for the rest of the sounds around me, nearby conversations were more understandable than with my AKG headphones. In comparison, my AKG N60nc can nearly eliminate the deep roar of plane engines during flight. The roar of braking plane engines comes through somewhat, but the AKG have never crackled. High frequencies come through fairly well (crying children, for example), but the mids are more muffled than the JBL. Due to the size of the ear cups, I would classify these JBL headphones as on-ear, not “over ear”. They’re very comfortable! They have a pad on the headband where the AKG dig into my head, so that problem is fixed. The sound quality was satisfying when I tested both music and video. But the noise canceling is a dealbreaker for me. My AKG are also on-ear, and its ear cups are even smaller, and yet somehow it manages to do a much nicer job with the noise canceling. Review Title: I ordered an Amazon Renewed Galaxy s20+ 5G Unlocked in November of 2023
Review Content: I ordered an Amazon Renewed Galaxy s20+ 5G Unlocked in November of 2023. I got a $1000 phone for $400. The phone is freaking awesome! Screen quality and camera are exceptionally great. Even better than many of Samsung's flagship phones that have come out since the s20+ was released in 2020. The phone has become an important tool for my landscaping business (mobile check deposits, plant identification, and work documentation). However, I dropped it a few months ago and the camera stopped working. So I happily ordered another Amazon Renewed Galaxy s20+ 5G Unlocked. But much to my despair, the phone I received had a cheap, very low resolution screen and poor quality camera in it. I've ordered three of the renewed phones over the last few months in the hope of getting a true Galaxy s20+ 5G that isn't full of junk replacement parts. All three phones I ordered were advertised as having the same quality screen and camera as an original manufactured s20+ direct from Samsung. But all three of them contained cheap, junk components!!! The first of the three phones I ordered was dropped by me about a week after receiving it. The cheap screen in it shattered to pieces. I probably could've lied about the damage and returned the phone for a refund, but that would've been very dishonest behavior. So, I took the loss. I returned the second phone I ordered soon after receiving it and learning that it too contained junk components. I attempted to resolve my concerns about the poor quality components installed in the third phone I ordered by emailing the small business that sold it to me through Amazon. They placed a card in the box with the phone that said to contact them directly. However, Stallion ReQuip's reps failed to provide a resolution to the problem. They kept asking me for information I had already provided to them and they never sent me the return shipping label they said they would send to me. I don't know if their reading comprehension is lacking or they know they are selling phones that are different than what they are advertised as being and they had no intention of fixing the problem. So I initiated a return through Amazon and am now writing this review. If you are looking for a cheap, junk version of a Galaxy s20+, which isn't actually a true s20+, then feel free to order one of these falsely advertised phones. Or, you might be better off buying a lessor quality new phone for the money that will actually contain the parts it is supposed to have in it. But if you're looking for a great deal on a previous flagship model phone with original quality replacement parts, then go elsewhere. These businesses are not fully honest and transparent about what they're selling. And, Amazon Renewed phones, at least for me, are no longer the great and exciting bargain they once were. As for my original renewed purchased s20+, I took it to a local small business electronics repair shop today and got the camera replaced for $95. It only took about 45 minutes. So much better than burning through $600+ and wasting days and weeks dealing with sellers and making returns. Review Title: Both the quality of the audio and noise cancellation to my “average” ear is pretty great
Review Content: Both the quality of the audio and noise cancellation to my “average” ear is pretty great. The sense I got from reading reviews of competing products on Amazon (namely the Bose Quiet Comfort & Sony 1000s) was that the Beats looked and sounded good but weren’t very strong in the noise cancellation department. I’ve now had a chance to use these on my weekly commute (2+ hr flight each way) and the noise cancellation on these has not disappointed. As other reviewers have noted, all noise is not eliminated, but a lot of the lower rumbling engine noise (on the plane) or fan noise (in my office) is blocked out. The only thing I’ve noticed isn’t blocked out as much are human voices (more noticeable if I’m not playing any music/audio). I mainly use these with my iPhone but haven’t had any issues pairing with an Android phone (Pixel 2 XL) or laptop (a Chromebook). It’s amazing how much lower volume I can have these on compared to the standard Apple earbuds that came with my iPhone 7. My ONLY complaint after 5-6 weeks of use is that the noise cancelling feature on the first pair that I received from Amazon would periodically fade off and on during flights. I went through all of the troubleshooting (updating software, etc) but nothing fixed the problem so I took them in to an Apple store for repair, and was sent a replacement pair the following week at no charge that have worked great. This was definitely a hassle, but for me was worth saving the $$$ taking a chance on the refurbished item. It’s also worth noting that I’ve purchased 5-6 refurbished items on Amazon and this is the first time that I have had any sort of technical issue with a purchase. All in all I’ve been very satisfied with the look, sound, and noise cancelling capabilities of these headphones. This is my second pair of Beats (bought my first ones way back in 2008) and love having the Bluetooth connection/ditching the cord. If you’re looking for an all-around solid pair of wireless noise-cancelling headphones then I’d definitely recommend getting these ... you might just want to shell out the extra money for a brand new pair if you don’t want to deal w/potential issue on refurb front. Review Title: Todos los intentos de actualizar el dispositivo fallaron y hubo errores que me decían que «acudiera
Review Content: Todos los intentos de actualizar el dispositivo fallaron y hubo errores que me decían que «acudiera a un centro de servicio», lo cual es inaceptable si se trata de un teléfono que se supone que está listo para usarse sin usar. Este tipo de problema suele estar asociado con el flasheo incorrecto del firmware o con dispositivos que se han modificado fuera de los canales oficiales del fabricante o del operador. Cuando las configuraciones del firmware y el hardware no se alinean correctamente (por ejemplo, los cargadores de arranque específicos de un operador frente al firmware desbloqueado genérico), pueden interrumpirse las rutas de actualización, inhabilitar funciones e incluso crear riesgos de estabilidad a largo plazo. Pasé dos días enteros solucionando problemas (probando diferentes métodos de actualización, restablecimientos y opciones de recuperación), básicamente haciendo el tipo de trabajo que cabría esperar de un técnico, no de un cliente. Ni siquiera las opciones de asistencia profesional, como Geek Squad, estarían a la altura, lo que demuestra lo problemáticos que pueden ser estos dispositivos una vez que se modifican de esta manera. Después de investigar más a fondo, encontré muchas otras reseñas que describían exactamente el mismo problema, lo que sugiere claramente que no se trata de un error puntual, sino que forma parte de un patrón. Parece que algunos vendedores externos están tomando atajos restaurando o «desbloqueando» dispositivos de forma inadecuada, lo que compromete su funcionalidad. Esto puede infringir las políticas de la plataforma sobre el estado de los dispositivos y las descripciones precisas de los anuncios. En resumen: no se trataba de un producto reacondicionado correctamente, sino de un dispositivo mal modificado que no debería haberse vendido como «renovado». Si estás pensando en comprarle a este vendedor, no lo hagas. Ahórrate tiempo, frustraciones y riesgos, y opta por una fuente confiable. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple Watch Series 8 [GPS, 41mm] - Midnight Aluminum Case with Midnight Sport Band, S/M (Renewed) : Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry
Review Title: Compré este reloj en condición "Excelente", pero de excelente no tiene casi nada
Review Content: Compré este reloj en condición "Excelente", pero de excelente no tiene casi nada. Debería estar catalogado como "Bueno" o "Regular", porque siendo sinceros, sí tiene rayones bastante perceptibles que incluso se sienten al pasar el dedo. Entiendo que es un producto reacondicionado; el problema es que lo venden como “Excelente” y no debería ser así. En cuanto a funcionalidad, llegó impecable. Todo funciona sin problema y la salud de la batería llegó al 87%. En las fotos que agregué se puede ver que desconecté el reloj a las 11:40 a.m. y para las 11:41 p.m. aún tenía el 48% de batería restante. Esto, claramente, con la pantalla siempre activa (AOD) apagada. Con el AOD encendido noté que la batería sí se descarga muchísimo más rápido; le calculo que en vez del 48%, a esa misma hora me habría quedado un 18% o incluso menos. Algo que no me gustó para nada es el cargador genérico incluido. Supuestamente es de la marca Steren, aunque lo dudo, porque la verdad se siente de muy mala calidad (como un cargador muy barato de los que ves en el tianguis). Tardó más de una hora solo en lograr encender el reloj, ya que el equipo llegó con la batería completamente muerta. Llegué incluso a pensar que el reloj estaba defectuoso porque no encendía, pero después de un largo rato por fin lo hizo. Este cargador es de muy baja potencia y provoca que el reloj se caliente bastante; la carga de 0 a 100% tomó más de 2 horas. Si consigues el cable de carga rápida original de Apple, este modelo se carga por completo en unos 45 minutos, ya que el Series 8 sí soporta esta tecnología (me parece que está disponible del Series 7 en adelante). Conclusión: Sí recomiendo la compra (lo compré por un precio de $3,530.27 MXN), pero hagan la inversión de adquirir el cable original (cuesta $649 MXN) para que puedan aprovechar la carga rápida y no tengan que estar esperando más de 2 horas. Por mi parte, aún estoy indeciso sobre si regresarlo o quedármelo, únicamente por los rayones, ya que se perciben demasiado, si no hubiese sido una excelente compra. Bueno, esa fue mi experiencia espero y les sirva.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Review Title: Finally, as the screen sizes have increased, I decided, ok, there are apps that I may find useful as
Review Content: Finally, as the screen sizes have increased, I decided, ok, there are apps that I may find useful as well as the integration of my Google Calander and Contacts with my phone. But, while sure, I could spend over a grand on a new phone, it just did not seem to me to be a wise use of my money. I had read that a lot of smartphone addict aficionados look for the latest and greatest.....or maybe they did not like the color of their new phone....so they sent it back. Rather than winding up in landfills as a lot of returned Amazon merchandise does, unfortunately, Amazon was wise enough to create their refurbished division in which various refurbishers compete for customer's business. I thought, why not give it a try. I purchased the phone from a company named Kiss in Manhattan where I grew up. They had a high positive rating so I picked them My phone arrived the next day despite the fact that I did not pay for overnight shipping. Unfortunately, as I understand it, the ripples of the COVID situation put them out of business. As for the phone, when I opened up the box, I was shocked. In terms of appearance, there was absolutely no way I would have known it was a refurb....not a mark on it. As far as function is concerned, I used various apps to test it, and it passed. I have been using it since the first week of August. My estimate of battery life remaining is upwards of 90 percent. Of note, at Batteries and Bulbs, I can replace the battery for something like 70 dollars still putting me way ahead of the game since the phone was under 400 dollars. Add a Microcenter 512 MicroSD card for about 50 dollars and I have a phone with 3/4 of a terabyte, far more storage than I anticipate ever using.

Product Title: Amazon.com: Samsung Galaxy Note 9, 128GB, Ocean Blue - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: The phone is very elegant looking, especially with its curved display
Review Content: The phone is very elegant looking, especially with its curved display. As such, it would look very nice put upon a pedestal in our living room. However, I did not find the phone in an art store. I purchased it to use every day as my mobile phone. What is the Note 9 made of? Simply put, it is basically glass placed over a metal frame which again is fine if you want to display it on your bookshelf, but not particularly practical. Unless a person is downright foolish, just about everyone puts a case on it. You can forget about using one of those clear cases that let the beauty of the phone shine through. Drop it and you are facing an expensive repair. I was using the Unicorn Beetle Pro case with a belt clip which I never used. The phone dropped on the stairs and the inner part of the case broke. I was not really upset about that for the simple reason it saved the phone. Now I am trying an Outbox Defender which looks pretty robust. How about the curved display? Yes, it looks rather elegant, but does one really need it for functionality? The answer is absolutely not. It only serves to make designing a screen protector problematic. As for screen protectors go, I think they are necessary and I have just resigned myself to the fact that the edge adhesives are going to wear out and to simply replace them every once and awhile. They are not particularly expensive. We as consumers really should not put up with this nonsense. Most of the smartphones made these days have similar designs. They reinforce the notion of built-in obsolescence, or in actuality, built-in fragility. Yes, technology changes very rapidly. But, the basic technology of how these phones communicate does not. There is absolutely no reason that we should have to get a new phone every year. They should last far longer than that in my humble opinion. The question is how can we communicate this to the manufacturers? We can't boycott them because they all pretty much do the same thing. It is something it think about.....just saying. Review Title: I got the Note 20 because it's the last Note (currently) that has an SD card slot; I'm absolutely ag
Review Content: I got the Note 20 because it's the last Note (currently) that has an SD card slot; I'm absolutely against some company gouging me hundreds of dollars extra for a 256GB phone when a 512GB SD card is under 50 bucks. The drawback to that is this phone came with pretty much nothing at all but a charging cable, which isn't really adding any value. It took me some time to find a way to get the SD card slot open, without their custom tool, because on this phone at least the hole is waaayyyy too small for a paper clip. I finally unwound the spring from an ink pen, which was small enough and stiff enough to release it. Seriously leave out the cable that probably everyone in the world has by now and put that tool in! It's needed for the SIM even without an SD card. Speaking of SIM, moving my line to this phone was trivially simple. The phone was apparently on T-Mobile previouisly and I'm on Verizon, and everything worked flawlessly right from the phone. Put the SIM in, turned it on, and followed the instructions. Done. I got a Note because, well, I've been a Note fanboy since the 4, when my old Droid with the hardware keyboard gave up the ghost, because of the S-Pen. It's not something I use every day, but when I do use it, there is literally no alternative that works like the S-Pen. If Samsung ever stops putting that on their phone I'll probably move on to something more affordable. This is my first ever refurb, and this one at least is exactly what one would hope; it physically indistinguishable from a brand new phone. Even close observation in the light reveals no scratches or blemishes, it hasn't crashed or exhibited any wonky behaviour (knocks on head), and it's significantly snappier than the old one. That's not just because it has more resources, I think it's because the UI has been tweaked. For example when scrolling a long list this phone's "inertia", how long it scrolls untouched after a flick up or down, is much higher than the old phone, so it's considerably faster to browse by scrolling. I'm sure other improvements have been made as well, and together they translate into a much more responsive feel. The OS itself is similar to the Note 8, really, but it has even more bloat and unremovable cruft in it. For exampe there's "AR" functionality now, but even though I have nothing AR, and if I do it's highly unlikely I'll use this phone in conjunction with it. There's an "AR Zone" that can't be disabled, can't be removed, can't be told not to nag me with notifications, can't be managed in the slightest. Seriously Samsung, get off your high horse. You don't know what I want my phone to do; fine if you want to have that enabled by default, why do I care? But can't disable it or remove all the massively huge list of permissions? Want to rub some salt in there for me? It's also considerably more in-your-face nagging about things; like I haven't figured out how to get it to stop nagging me to save passwords for web sites, as if the last fifteen times I'd change my mind. Stuff like that isn't helpful, it's obtuse and rude. Migration was a PitA, but that's normal, so I mention it anecdotally. Samsung's "Smart Switch" does make it less than heinously atrocious, but "Everything" isn't (everything), and it still took me days to get all my appointments and other things loaded in. Once I find my browser bookmarks and get them in I'll finally be done. Least favorite part of getting a new phone is setting the @*&#% up. I can back up and restore a computer with trivial ease but no phone maker yet is smart enough to do that with a phone. Pathetic. I considered only four stars because of the missing SD card tool. Not sure how many folks would be able to figure out how to open it with the hole being about 2/3 the diameter of a paper clip, which is by the way what Verizon recommends using if one can't find the tool. I have no straight pins so I don't know if they work, but if I did I'd still want to file the point off to be sure I didn't damage anything. But overall a VERY happy camper. If you like Android it's likely you'll be satisfied with this phone, and if you've never had an S-pen you'll probably be hooked. lol       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))       235 people found this helpful Helpful  Sending feedback...Thank you for your feedback. With the S20 Ultra, You have to make sure your finger is in exactly the right area of the phone, in just the right position and keep it there for exactly the right length of time and it will work the first try maybe 3/4 of the time. 3- Flashlight sucks. Considerably. Might as well just use a candle. 4- the touch response is too good. If you think about swiping the wrong thing, you get a new window or changed settings. Relax. 5-the screen and back of the phone, I'm convinced were specifically designed to attract dust, debris, fingerprints, smears etc. It's disgusting. If I were a stranger and saw my phone I'd immediately think I was a slob. A case is a necessity, not only because the phone I'm pretty sure is plastic. I thought the S20's were aluminum, maybe I just don't know how cheap aluminum is? I'm not confident at all in the durability of this phone or the screen, I'm glad I bought the protection plan. (The covering over the precious camera however, is in fact resistant to debris and fingerprints). 6-why is this screen so big, but my status bar with the time and battery life so unreasonably tiny? I'm looking down my nose holding my phone out like I'm 90 years old trying to read the paper, it's absurd? Can you change that? 7-simplified and boring drop down menu/notification screen. Feels dumbed down for boring people. Less personal 1- Arrived in pristine condition. You'd never know it was refurbished. I can't find a flaw or scratch anywhere. And after seeing reviews and pictures, I looked for them. 3-battery life is phenomenal. I had no memory of how long a full charge should actually last until I took my S20 ultra out for it's first day on the town. 4-It has an SD card slot. I was able to switch over a lot of information from my old phone. I am not in fact 90, I'm only 39, but I still don't like all this saved information in clouds or saved to Google acts etc. Doesn't feel right, I want my information on an object I can hold in my hand. 5-it's not an iPhone. I think we can all agree that's a win. 6- it's 5G. Turns out 5G isn't as widespread as the TV lead me to believe. I've seen it connect to 5G once and I drive all around Western New York. But that's still fun 7- other than little changes to the UI, updates and external components... It's virtually the same thing as my S9+. Which I loved. So that's a big deal for me. I don't have to spend time relearning how to use it. With the difference in generations, I was expecting bigger changes. I liked my S9+ better. If they could have kept that design and just upgraded the insides over the years instead of needing new actual phones designs, I'd have been thrilled. If my S9+ was still functional, that would be ideal really (I'll miss you S9+ 💋) Having only dealt with the S9+ galaxy, that it the standard I'm judging from. The S20 Ultra feels genuinely fragile in my hands as opposed to the S9+. It feels like a lower quality phone and I do not anticipate the screen or case holding up over the years that I plan on keeping it. So I would recommend the protection plan offered. Review Title: Fully unlocked Galaxy S20 Ultra (Renewed) ordered from thegadgetdeals on Amazon Marketplace to repla
Review Content: Fully unlocked Galaxy S20 Ultra (Renewed) ordered from thegadgetdeals on Amazon Marketplace to replace my Galaxy S9, which I have really enjoyed over the last 3 years but is now too slow and not enough storage for my liking. I went with the S20 rather than upgrading to an S21 primarily because of the expandable storage available with the S20 [I'm bummed Samsung is going away from this - it was one of the great things that set them apart from Apple... boooo!]. Anyway, Verizon has pretty much refused to restock their S21 Ultra 512 GB during the last 4-6 months, hence I ultimately pulled the trigger on this phone. Regarding the product according to the seller: arrived quickly and as promised. Few scratches on back cover that I care nothing about at all (expected as this is a refurb). Otherwise, seems in great condition. Came with a charger as promised. I was nervous about ordering unlocked phone as I have always purchased through my carrier, but I inserted my Verizon sim card, and it seems to be working great. Regarding the phone itself (S20 Ultra versus my old S9): FAST - by far what I'm happiest about. My old phone was really dragging in responsiveness. Front (selfie) camera noticeably WAY better. Rear camera - I'm sure is better, but I expected to notice a huge difference and other than the fact that I can zoom in a lot more, the quality when I zoom in isn't just over the moon better than my old phone (ie, on 8x zoom, photos from the 2 phones look similar). But I will say, the "live focus" that resembles the "portrait mode" of an iPhone makes me excited. Plus there's other nice features, like zooming out (wide view), etc. Overall happy with this. NEGATIVES..... my only complaint that I hope doesn't ruin my experience with this phone is the FINGERPRINT READER. The actual reader on the back of the S9 was seemingly perfect. I LOVED it - almost never had issues. Why, WHY?! did they go to a digital one. It seems to work fine without a case or screen protector. I've tried a few cases thus far that all claim to work well with the reader but NO. With case on, it works like 25% of the time (followed all the directions). And honestly, I'm not sure I blame the cases - seems like everyone is having issues with this. I'm ordering some screen protectors that have decent reviews and *fingers crossed*. Oh, also, this phone is big, like huge. I think (hope) I'll get used to it, but wow. Samsung, please review the size of female pockets before designing your next phone. Product Title: Amazon.com: Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra 5G, 512GB, Lavender - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: The screen is ridiculous in the best way
Review Content: The screen is ridiculous in the best way. That 6.8-inch Dynamic AMOLED with the super-smooth 120Hz refresh rate feels like butter, whether I'm doom-scrolling X at 2 a.m. or editing photos outside in bright sunlight (the brightness is no joke, it legit gets stupidly bright). Colors pop without looking cartoonish, and watching anything HDR on it is basically a religious experience. The cameras… okay, look, I’m that annoying friend who takes way too many pictures, and this thing spoils you rotten. The 200MP main sensor is overkill in the best possible way—zoom in on a photo you took from across the street and you can still read the text on someone’s shirt. 100x Space Zoom is mostly a party trick (it gets shaky past 30x unless you’ve got tripod arms), but 10x optical is actually usable and looks clean. Night mode is straight-up witchcraft; I’ve taken shots in near darkness that look like they were taken at dusk. Performance is boring in the best way possible—it just never stutters. I’ve got 50+ tabs open in Chrome, Spotify running, editing 4K video in CapCut, and it doesn’t even break a sweat. Battery life surprised me too. With heavy use (always-on display, 5G, location on, lots of camera), I’m still ending most days with 30-40% left. Throw it on a 45W charger and it’s at 70% in like 30 minutes. The S Pen is lowkey one of my favorite things. I use it for quick notes when I’m too lazy to type, doodling on screenshots, and signing PDFs without printing anything. Feels way more natural than I expected. - It’s a big boy. One-handed use is a stretch (literally). - Fingerprint magnet on the back, but a case fixes that. - Still some Samsung bloatware, though it’s gotten better. If you’re the kind of person who wants the absolute best Android phone and doesn’t mind the size or the price tag, the S23 Ultra is still holding the crown going into late 2025. Even with the S24 Ultra and S25 Ultra out, I’m not feeling upgrade itch at all. This thing is just that good. 9.5/10, would (and probably will) buy again. Review Title: The reason I wanted a flip phone is because I constantly break/crack the screen on the standard phon
Review Content: The reason I wanted a flip phone is because I constantly break/crack the screen on the standard phones. It does not matter if I buy the most expensive bulletproof phone case. Those cases only protect the phone/screen if the phone falls on an edge or back side. If the phone lands on an object anywhere on the screen, they automatically crack the screen. Not with a flip phone. Once closed, the screen is protected and if you buy a case for it like I did, now it's truly bulletproof. I've accidentally dropped my phone so many times and no damage to the screen at all. My phone case also protects the small outside screen. I actually like this version with the small screen in the front. Makes it harder to damage it. The larger the screen, the bigger the chances of damaging it like the standard phones. When flipped closed, takes up way less space in my pants pockets compared to a non flip phone. No chance of it slipping out my pocket. The phone case I added does make it bulkier but if you're not using one or a really thin skin type cover, pretty thin sleek phone. It does not have an external SD card slot for memory. Whatever memory the phone comes with, that's it. This also makes it harder to track, save, and transfer files like pics and videos. It does have wireless charging (I wouldn't have bought it if it didn't) however, it is slow. I believe the wireless charging is rated at 5W max. Wired charging is fast though (30W max). I just prefer wireless charging because all charging ports (on all phones) do wear out over time and eventually fail preventing from charging the phone. The crease in the middle of the screen starts becoming noticeable on the screen after so much use, abuse, and flips. This doesn't bother me and I don't really notice it when watching videos but others are super sensitive to this and want perfect screen clarity always, so keep that in mind. This tradeoff for having a flip phone is worth it to me. This flip phone screen technology is still new so I expect the screens to only get better in the future. Overall, love my phone and don't regret this purchase.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))       4 people found this helpful Helpful  Sending feedback...Thank you for your feedback. Product Title: Amazon.com: JBL Flip 7 Portable Waterproof Speaker, Black (Renewed) | Drop-Proof, Bold Pro Sound with AI Sound Boost, 16Hrs of Playtime, PushLock System with Interchangeable Accessories : Electronics
Review Title: The Flip 7 is a really well-made speaker
Review Content: The Flip 7 is a really well-made speaker. It's smaller, lighter, looks better in my opinion, and is easier to throw in a backpack or even a bike bottle holder. If portability is your top priority, JBL did a great job. Sound-wise, though, I ended up preferring the Bose for the way I listen to music. In a small to medium-sized room, the Bose sounds fuller and deeper. It almost feels like it has a tiny built-in subwoofer. The JBL has punchier mid-bass and can hit a little harder, but it doesn't reach into the lower sub-bass the same way the Bose does. In a larger room, the Flip 7 does project a little better, but for me the difference wasn't big enough to outweigh what I liked about the Bose. Outside, neither speaker really produces the kind of low-end that I'd want for an open environment, so the slight advantage the JBL has in projection wasn't enough to change my mind. For some context, I'm coming from an older Anker Soundcore Boost that finally gave up. Surprisingly, I still think the Soundcore Boost has more "thump" than either the JBL or the Bose. Both of these newer speakers are much cleaner and clearer, though, with better overall sound quality. I think the Flip 7 is a great speaker for someone who values portability and durability. If you're riding a bike, traveling, spending time at the park, or just want something that's easy to carry around, it's an excellent choice. If your primary use is listening indoors in a small or medium-sized room, I personally preferred the Bose SoundLink Plus enough that I decided to keep it instead. Neither speaker is bad, they just excel in different areas, and for my use case the Bose was the better fit. Review Title: Installed and used Samsung Smart Switch app to transfer all my old S8+ phone apps, settings and file
Review Content: Installed and used Samsung Smart Switch app to transfer all my old S8+ phone apps, settings and files to the new one, using wifi direct phone-to-phone. Easy to do but took almost 5 hours to complete due to lots of apps plus huge number of files on the old phones SD card, which automatically transferred to the main 128gb system storage on the new phone. A few settings, like themes and wallpapers, were not applied during this process, but were easy to fix after. I also have a couple of apps that are licensed and locked to a specific device, (Norton360 and IGO Navigation) and had to uninstall them from both phones then reinstall on the new one. For Norton, I also had to go to my Norton account on PC, remove the old phone and add the new one. Not an issue, just a consideration and a few extra steps. Would have liked to have SD card support, but had researched and knew going in that the 128gb built-in storage would be more than adequate for my needs, including for about 70gb of photos and MP3 audio files I had on the 128gb SD card of my old S8+ phone. I do wonder why it needs 39gb of storage for system files though. Almost 4GB more than on the old phone. That seems extremely excessive to me, but might just be the difference between Android 9 on the old phone vs Android 13 on the new one (after all system updates). Another consideration, which is not really a complaint, as I knew it would happen, is that getting all of the 30+ OS, security and other updates took almost 2 full days to accomplish from a freshly factory reset phone, which this is. This is something that should not be allowed to happen according to the default automatic processes and schedule, as that could take weeks. You need to manually go to Settings / Software Update / Check for Updates, and download and install the recommended system update. Then repeat and repeat and repeat again, as many times as needed, until it says no more updates are needed. If you ever need to do a factory reset, you may need to do it all over again. If you ever sell your phone, remember to do a factory reset to remove all of your personal apps, settings and data, and let the new owner know that they might need to redo this system software update process. Final note: If you are upgrading to 5G for the first time, and have an old 4G SIM card in your old phone, you will need to get a new 5G SIM from your carrier in order to have 5G capability. For the phone I bought, and my carrier, this was Verizon. I chose to do this only after finishing all of the Smart Switch and system upgrades described above, which only needed wifi. I've never used it for that long, but I've used it for several hours at high volume and it never died. It also recharges to full battery in just a few hours. It's very quick to link up via Wi-Fi and I've walked a good distance from it and it doesn't lose connection. There are cheaper Wi-Fi speakers on the market, but from what I've read, the sound quality isn't usually as good as this product. I would recommend spending a few extra bucks for this one. If you want something you can walk around with, look at the JBL flip 5 or 6. If you want a huge block-party type speaker, this one might be a little small. However, if you're in the middle and want a nice backyard speaker, this is definitely the one. When used indoors, it is really loud. Review Title: A lot of the online consensus claims that jumping from a 45mm Series watch to the 49mm Ultra isn't t
Review Content: A lot of the online consensus claims that jumping from a 45mm Series watch to the 49mm Ultra isn't that noticeable of a screen difference. I completely disagree. The switch to the flat sapphire crystal glass changes the entire experience. Because it doesn't curve off at the edges like the Series 9, the usable screen real estate feels massive. Add in the 3,000 nits of brightness, and the display is incredibly crisp and visible from across the room. Is the watch huge? Yes, it is objectively a large, thick piece of titanium. But despite the visual bulk, it is surprisingly balanced on the wrist. It doesn't feel like you are wearing a brick, and it is comfortable enough that I sleep in it every single night without any discomfort. The biggest quality-of-life improvement coming from the Series 9 is the battery. Being able to track sleep all night and wake up without needing a "panic charge" to get through the workday is a game-changer.

The switch to the flat sapphire crystal glass changes the entire experience. Because it doesn't curve off at the edges like the Series 9, the usable screen real estate feels massive. Add in the 3,000 nits of brightness, and the display is incredibly crisp and visible from across the room. Is the watch huge? Yes, it is objectively a large, thick piece of titanium. But despite the visual bulk, it is surprisingly balanced on the wrist. It doesn't feel like you are wearing a brick, and it is comfortable enough that I sleep in it every single night without any discomfort. The biggest quality-of-life improvement coming from the Series 9 is the battery. Being able to track sleep all night and wake up without needing a "panic charge" to get through the workday is a game-changer.

Review Title: I bought this phone with the hope that it would work with US Mobile's service, which it does
Review Content: I bought this phone with the hope that it would work with US Mobile's service, which it does. I really like my pooled data plan with them, but I wanted a device on T-Mobile's network, as I have had very good service from a T-Mobile 4G WAP at some rural locations. At my home, neither Verizon nor AT&T work very well as a backup for my Internet service, but T-Mobile has 5G coverage in my area. I had a "Dark Star" SIM that was already activated, and dropped it into this phone. Once the battery was charged, I was able to power the phone on and place phone calls and send text messages. However Internet didn't work, even using Chrome browser on the phone itself. I've already become familiar with adding an APN to other devices, so I followed the instructions from US Mobile's site to add the "Darkstar" APN, and configure it for tethering, which is the main purpose of this device. The disappointing part has nothing to do with this phone, which seems to be working perfectly well. The phone is running on AT&T's network, not T-Mobile. While the service is still poor at my home, I tried it at a few different locations, and found a couple of places nearby where the speedtest.net results were very impressive, with download speeds over 120Mbps and upload speeds over 80Mbps. However, I also found places that were essentially "dead zones" for data, even though the phone still showed a 5G connection. I briefly tried this phone with a US Mobile "Warp" SIM, which connected to Verizon's network. I was able to place a call, send a text message, and connect to the 4G service available here. The speed is similar to another 5G smartphone I have from another reseller. I did not have to make any APN adjustments, it just worked. SUCCESS!!! Took some time, but I am finally on T-Mobile's network (using US Mobile's "Light Speed" network) and now have weak 5G coverage at my home. I have to put the phone in a window to get the 5G service. If I move it to the interior, I get 4G service which is actually slightly faster than Verizon's 4G. A VoIP call while tethered on the 5G network was a bit spotty. My speedtest.net speed is showing 24Mbps down and 3Mbps up with 648ms latency while on 5G and tethered via WiFi. Unlike the "Dark Star" and "Warp" networks, I had a good deal of trouble switching to the "Light Speed" (T-Mobile) network. I did two 1-hour long support chat sessions, but still didn't have phone, sms, nor mms service. By adding the correct APN, I did get Internet service. I inadvertently left the phone on while charging it after the last troubleshooting session. While it was charging, it downloaded a 1.9GB update. I'm not sure what all updated, but the OS updated from Android 11 to Android 12. The phone service started working after the requested reboot. It requested a WiFi connection to complete updating, so I set that up and ran the update option from the Android settings menu. The sms & mms services started working about 20 minutes later. One of the notifications seemed to suggest the carrier initiated the update, but I don't know if that was the OS update, or something else. This phone does seem to work well in the car while tethered via WiFi to my Android radio for Waze maps and YouTube streaming while driving. I haven't done any long trips, but I have gone through areas I know to have poor coverage, and didn't notice any interruptions. Review Title: This isnt just deceptive advertising (from Amazon renewed) but a public health risk
Review Content: This isnt just deceptive advertising (from Amazon renewed) but a public health risk. The lithium battery warning sticker on the box should have been next to a biohazard warning. Edit: Amazon told me I couldn't post the above review of this product. Well, since writing the review I have purchased a pair of new, clean Bose QC ultra earbuds from a different retailer. Here's my review of the earbuds: The sound quality is remarkable and combined with the noise cancelling it's almost unnerving. The buds themselves are so comfortable it doesn't feel like I am wearing anything (I have smaller, fairly sensitive ears too). Several times I had to take one out just to assure myself I was hearing sound through them and not accidentally blasting surround sound, only to remember I had windows open to traffic noises and a fan on, etc. I found that I needed a combination of sizes of ear plug and ear wing (I don't know the technical terms for the silicone bits). Despite my small ears, I needed a larger ear plug on one side and it made the noise cancelling absolute. The app, and I have other Bose products with poorly performing apps, so I was concerned, worked well. Tip: if you started trying them out before using the app, go ahead and put them back in the case and follow the instructions it gives you pair to Bluetooth, even if you're already paired. That was the only hiccup I found. From there put them on and go through the options, learn and try the gestures. It gives in app demos and training. I read ppl had problems with it shutting off while listening to asmr or meditation, I haven't had that issue. But I have found that side lying with higher noise cancelling gives weird soft techno-noise feedback because of the pillow on the anc sensors. A few said the "floor" (sound of noise cancelling without audio) had a hum-- try other ear plug sizes and create a custom "mode" and adjust the noise cancelling to a level without any floor hum. Also make sure hair or head coverings aren't brushing against the earbuds if you're getting weird anc sounds. So far I am very happy with my new /clean/ Bose QC ultra earbuds. I highly recommend them for ppl who need the quiet in noisy environments and/or who want to be immersed in soundscape/music/ cinematic settings. Just don't order from Amazon renewed. Product Title: Amazon.com: Google Pixel 8a 5G, 128GB + 8GB RAM, Obsidian - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: I purchased this phone as both renewed and unlocked
Review Content: I purchased this phone as both renewed and unlocked. The condition was excellent with no scratches or mars that I could tell. There were no issues switching from my old phone to this phone with my carrier (Visible) using my carrier's website, and this did not require speaking with anyone from my carrier. I'm pleased with the eSIM. The phone already had a screen protector. If I had known I probably wouldn't have purchased a screen protector. I like the looks of the phone. The camera bar on the back looks good to me (better than multiple lenses in a square or circle like many other phones). I'm not worried about scratching the lens as I would be with the other phones. It doesn't rock when placed on a flat surface. I like the color. Mine's old bay (similar to a periwinkle blue). I'm familiar with the Android UI, but I'm still getting used to Pixel's UI. On my old phone (another Android) it was easier to close all open programs. Also, I liked the way apps appeared when grouped together a little more on my old phone. With Pixel you have to keep swiping all the way to the left (past all the open apps) to get to Clear All. With Pixel you cannot see beyond the 4th app in a group, at least (to my knowledge) not without a separate app to organize your apps. This could be a good thing if you don't want an app to be obvious to shoulder surfers. I like having the fingerprint reader on the screen. The 3-button controls are also on the screen. I'm thrilled not to have all the bloatware I had with my old phone. I really resented my old phone manufacturer for preventing me from removing its preinstalled apps. It charges a bit slow (about 2 hours for full charge). I'd say the ability to hold and use a charge is good but not outstanding. I'm going to have to charge it daily. The display is bright and clear. Some reviewers have commented about the bezel being large, but I barely notice it. I prefer the plastic (8a) to a glass back. I think it looks good. I put mine in a case, so it appears just as shiny as a glass-backed phone would. The case does make it a bit harder to utilize the double-tap the back feature. The phone is fast, but I hear the Tensor processor isn't as fast as Snapdragon 8. I don't expect it'll be an issue for me. I'm not looking to run games in HD at 60+ fps. Photos are excellent. I like the quick flip gesture that switches between rear and front camera and the selfie illumination (screen turns white to shine light on your face) for selfies. I'm not used to the camera app's settings yet though. I like Google's security features. This was a major selling point for me. My old phone was past security updates, so I was vulnerable. I'm pleased that I have a few more years of regular software updates. The biometric unlock is really easy to use. After installing everything including my old apps, I have 87 GB free (I have the 128 GB memory version), so there's plenty of space. The overall value of this phone is great. You could spend 3-5X the cost of this renewed phone for the newest flagship model from another manufacturer. You'd have a moderate gain in processor power, but little/no gain in camera hardware. The newest model would have a couple more years of guaranteed software support, but for me, that isn't worth paying 2-4X extra. Pixel 8a will get software updates through May 2031, which is great. Review Title: Well clearly, I was not satisfied to receive a phone with a significantly degraded battery
Review Content: Well clearly, I was not satisfied to receive a phone with a significantly degraded battery. So, I called Amazon Customer service to explain the problem and request a replacement. I did this on the same day I received the phone. The representative was helpful and told me he would send out a replacement immediately, and even upgrade the shipment method for no extra charge. He also told me, both in conversation and in writing to “use the box the replacement comes in to return the original.” That way, I would not be without a phone while waiting for the replacement to arrive. The day the replacement was scheduled to arrive and but had not, I called Amazon customer service back to inquire about the status. Much to my surprise, I was told the replacement phone order had been cancelled by the third-party seller because the original had not been returned. This irritated me for two reasons: (1) I had never been notified the replacement order had been cancelled—apparently, had I not called Amazon was simply going to drop the issue, and (2) I was specifically told by Amazon Customer Service that I did not need to return the original until the replacement was received. I told the agent this was unacceptable and wanted the replacement sent to me, as had been previously arranged. When it became clear that she would not be able to help me, I asked to speak with her manager. After providing her with my phone number, she said her manager would call me back. That phone call never happened. The following day I called Amazon customer service again, now the third time trying to get this issue resolved. I explained the steps I had taken thus far and was put on hold so the representative could verify if my replacement order “was legit.” When I asked what “legit” meant, she said she needed to verify if this was unusual activity on the account because it was a phone purchase. I told her that of course it was legit, as I had email documentation regarding the entire process! After being on hold, she came back and told me the replacement phone would be delivered within 5 days. She also said she would personally call me on that day to verify that it was received. I asked her to clarify that I would receive the replacement first, prior to sending the original back, according to the instructions I had previously received via email. She looked up that email and saw it said: “Please feel free to use the box the replacement comes in to return the original…” After reading that she placed me on hold again. After a minute or so, she came back on the line and asked if she could place me on hold for an additional few minutes. I asked why. She said she was trying to find out what went wrong with the first replacement order. When she came back on the line, she told me “to be on the safe side” I should return the original defective phone first to receive a replacement. I reiterated that this was unacceptable and that I had held up my end of the bargain and done exactly as Amazon had told me to do. I wanted the replacement sent first before I returned the defective phone. She said the email I received was in error and the person who sent it made a mistake—the defective phone would need to be returned before the replacement is shipped out. I told her that while I understand that people make mistakes, I did not think I should be penalized (i.e., be without a phone for at least 5 days) for a mistake that Amazon made. She apologized for the mistake but made it clear that I would not receive a replacement until the original was returned. I informed her I would be writing a negative review. To summarize: I was sent a defective phone, was given incorrect information about how to replace it, had the replacement order silently cancelled without being notified, and Amazon refused to follow through on the terms of their agreement. One star.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))
