Review Title: Mine was a refurbushed model, not a single scratch on it, looks brand new & no issues when i turned
Review Content: Mine was a refurbushed model, not a single scratch on it, looks brand new & no issues when i turned it on the first time & no issues since then. Yes, it did NOT come with the Samsung box, Samsung cable & usb wall charger. I personally do not care! due to i have a box full of samsung usb cables and wall chargers from my old Samsung phones i bought before. It did come with the tool to remove the sd & sim card & that is the only thing i needed. I had no intent & plan of upgrading my samsung s10+ to the samsung s20+. But at the price and buying prior refurbished samsung i am beyond happy i did it! First, The 5G is very quick & compare to older version what ever its called. which i did not believe until i went online away from my house WIFI service and its very quick. Note: not areas have 5G service. The overall phone response is very quick and smooth. The bixy button is gone (thankgod). The quality of the screen resolution is outstanding & wow its clear! It has a few more minor whistles & bells features compare to the samsung s10+ Nothing to noticable. I do like the new front camera location and its small size & its looks better. I also like you see less of the frame around the curved screen. I know & dont care if there is a technocal name for it. Overall the phone looks great & i didnt get a case this time due to i think looks better with out one. I know, but i rarely & never drop my phone (my s10+ back up) Reference to the camera & quality of the picture which was not a selling point for me. You will notice a much better picture & video quality. The phone over all is a tad thinner & tad taller which i think it makes it easier to hold and use. The battery life seems to be better but i have not fully tested it yet. Charging it seems to be quicker & again i have not fully tested it against my s10+. Now, is the samsung s20+ worth buying if you already have a s10 & s10+??? I love my s10+ its great phone! The only reason i got the s20+ was the price $700. But if you can afford one (full price) or find one at great price like i did then YES get one!!!! I could have lived very happy with my s10+ with no regrets if i didnt see this s20+ on amazon! All in all, up to this point, I feel like the investment was good. There is 90 days worth of warranty so if I stumble across something that is a deal breaker, I can return it. Review Title: This 3rd phone though is excellent so far
Review Content: This 3rd phone though is excellent so far. Condition, I would say is practically new. Case and Screen were blemish free, not even signs of fingerprints. The phone is Verizon branded, but does not impact phone service or use. It is unlocked and work with my Tracfone sim through T-Mobile. Testing battery life, but it seems close to normal after a few years of use. Used it all day and I still had 25% battery remaining with really heavy use. Data transfer went flawlessly with no hick ups, very easy and straight forward. Even the sim was immediately recognized without having to call the carrier. Everything seems to be in good working order. The person who owned this phone 1st really took care of it, you can tell. Other than the branding issue on start up and a notification telling me my sim is not a Verizon sim, everything seems to be in good working order. This is an upgrade for me coming from am Galaxy A20s. The upgrade was immediately noticed. And 256gb memory is just enough for me. I carry books, music and movies in my phone and this has handled everything I have thrown at it without issue. The camera is great and takes amazing photos compared to my last phone. Buying through Amazon renewed is a crap shoot really, it depends on the last user(s) and what may have happened to the phone, I can imagine the phone's people are turning in. I'm sure most have issue from over use and drops, to phone malfunctions in general. And from studying the vendors who sell the phones you really have no idea what they might do with them once they are rehabbed, Water damage, electronic issues, even screen replacements. All the phone are going through private phone companies who refurb them and send them back out. Like I said, 3rd times the charm and I lucked up on what I think is an excellent buy. Would I do again, sure, but make sure to check out the phone thoroughly during your 90-day return window. I will continue to test out and report back if any issues popped up. But so far so good. Check the vendor rating and issues reported in reviews. Typically, they spell out possible issues with phones or vendors selling them. I have always believed in recycling items, especially electronics. So do your part and make sure they don't end up in landfill somewhere. I have liked Samsung products for years and this still holds true with this phone. I don't need the latest and greatest, but I know I have a few years still before a newer model takes it's place. Furthermore, I usually hold on to a phone for 2–3 yrs, depends on the phone. Oh yeah, 5G is the hits. Very smooth and fast, no delays when surfing the web, everything just flows like a hardwired home system. 120 mhz is smooth and haven't noticed any hang-ups. Yes, I would buy again through Amazon renewed. But I'm sure you could find the same product locally at your local phone store. I'm happy with purchase and would recommend with caveats. Check your phone carefully, run it through is paces and test everything, camera, sound, display and any function you think is important and even those you might not think is important. test all settings and make sure all your setting take effect. This phone is loaded with options and it took about 3 hrs to transfer and update this phone once I started things up. Gaming is great, and the display is amazing. No glitches during game play. It's almost to fast that I can't keep up visually. So two thumbs up on buy. Finally moving like most with an upgraded phone. Product Title: Amazon.com: Samsung Galaxy A23 5G, 64GB, Black - Unlocked (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: There is one niggle to report, however - cases, or the lack thereof
Review Content: There is one niggle to report, however - cases, or the lack thereof. There are actually two versions of the Galaxy A23 - the regular 5G version and this Verizon specific 5G UW version. The UW is so named because it supports Verizon's Ultra Wideband 5G, also known as millimeter wave 5G and C-band 5G on bands N260, 2N61 and N77, in addition to standard 5G on band N78. This necessitates some internal differences that led to a slight change in position of the Volume and Power button. They are about 3/16" lower on this 5G UW version. In practical terms, this means that all of the hundreds of Galaxy A23 5G phone cases that you see listed will NOT function on this version. They will fit, but the case buttons will not work because they do not line up with the buttons on the phone. There are only two cases that actually work and both are thirty bucks: one from Otterbox, search for ASIN B0BVGWGBL4 , and the Itskins - Hybridr Solid Case for Samsung Galaxy A23 5G Uw - Purple and Transparent. That's it. The Otterbox only comes in black and the Itskins in purple and transparent. Just purchased a second one for myself since my own 2014 Galaxy S5 is starting to lose service in more areas due to 4G LTE frequencies being repurposed for 5G. Activated without issue on Page Plus Cellular, which is now a Verizon owned MVNO. Now have signal pretty much everywhere, both 5G and 4G LTE. The Samsung One UI interface is snappy, with no lag perceptible. This second unit came updated to Android 14 and One UI 6.0. The first one is running Android 13 and One UI 5.1. I was able to copy over all of my data via the Samsung SmartSwitch app, no problem. I also moved over the 64 GB microSD card from my Galaxy S5 to this Galaxy A23 without difficulty, which saved a ton of transfer time for my music mp3's. I wanted to add that contrary to another review, the A23 5G UW does have NFC. I've included a picture of the pull down shade showing its icon - it's the third button from the left. I use it with my YubiKey 5 NFC security key to store and access OTP's and Passkey's; although there is an issue with the Yubico Authenticator app not being able to access the camera for some reason. This makes it impossible to use this phone to add a new account to the YubiKey via QR code, though you can still input the key manually. However, there is no problem reading the YubiKey 5 via NFC - just hold the key against the back of the phone, next to the camera island. I also added a picture of the phone in the Otterbox case, to illustrate the the button alignment issue with standard A23 5G phone cases.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Product Title: Amazon.com: Jabra Elite 65t Alexa Enabled True Wireless Earbuds with Charging Case IP55 rated - Titanium Black (Renewed) : Electronics
Review Title: The inherent features paired with the features "unlocked" by using the app are awesome
Review Content: The inherent features paired with the features "unlocked" by using the app are awesome. It's not overly complex to be confusing or annoying, I basically setup the EQ once when I first installed it, and never had to mess with it again. The "Hear Through" feature is awesome--though realistically it's only partially useful, in that it allows me to hear outside noises enough to know that someone's talking to me, but since I'm listening to something else, I still can't hear them. But the buds detect when one is no longer in proximity to the other and auto pause your media when you take one out to talk to someone, which is awesome. Until you forget and take the other one out and hold them in your hand, not realizing that the buds are in range of each other and started playing again. BUT, having the Hear Through on is better than being absolutely deaf to the world, regardless. The App has different "profiles", or Moments, as they call them, which is nice, though I wish you could customize them more or create your own, but realistically I've not needed more than the three given, just to have one with Hear Through on and one with Hear Through off -- and since they can be swapped through the notification area on your phone, you don't even have to unlock your phone in order to enable/disable the feature. I received these exactly a month ago today and at first I tried to make an effort to use them as much as possible, now it's just second nature to take them everywhere I go. I've not really had many connection issues--or, many bad ones. The only issues I tend to have are when my phone is in my left pocket (which is where I normally keep it), when doing work and moving around/bending down, a lot. It seems that my body (which isn't a large one, mind you) causes some connection issues, but it's a brief stutter at best. Moving my phone to my right side--even in the back pocket--eliminates this entirely, since the right bud is the "Master". But if I'm just walking around, it's never been an issue. What surprised me the most is when I took them out of their case and they reported that they were Connected, my phone's Bluetooth was off, and then my wife's music started playing--and she was in the back yard! It's definitely not a problem to have your phone across the room - in fact it seems to help some of the random "body meat-related" connection stutters. Overall I simply love these earbuds and would absolutely recommend them to anyone looking for a good truly wireless earbud. Review Title: (I probably differ from the way others evaluate comfort
Review Content: (I probably differ from the way others evaluate comfort.) The Jabra units provide a degree of comfort in that they are secure and I have confidence that I could do a cartwheel, and they won’t fall out. To some that may be an "uncomfortable feeling" ... to me, that itself plays into what I call comfortable. But, no, they do not "hurt", I’ve worn them in the office for 3 hours straight - and they don’t “hurt my ears”. The Hear-Though functionality is not perfect, there’s a pretty loud hiss accompanied with the amplification. One can always hear ambient noise if not playing music, but the muffled outside world from the ear-plug effect is good enough such that you do not hear ambient noise during playback. This is great for sitting on the couch to listen to a podcast or youtube while my wife is wanting to watching TV. The TV is not heard during the podcast experience. They do not fall out, (Apple Airpods fall out easily for me). These connect/disconnect quickly from Bluetooth settings on devices. YouTube vids on MacBook Pro suffer 1 second "skips-outs" of sound - but only when 2 devices are simultaneoulsy connected. No skip-outs when only 1 device is connected. But these is no lag, or latency during the playback of YouTube videos ... just these random second-long skip-outs of the Audio. It’s enough to be annoying. Also, I hear: "Divice disconnected ... two devices connected ..." at times. This has nothing to do with the item above, it’s less frequent. Hear-Through works, but you also have amplified static hiss which you would not normally hear. (1) When I double press on the right ear bud, (hear-through toggle off/on). the app's hear though switch doesnt follow. (Pretty minor issue, but noticed.) (2) The equalizer has no effect at all. None. I’m using iPhone Xs Max, iOS.

Review Title: So, what is it like going to Samsung after so long?
Review Content: So, what is it like going to Samsung after so long? Back in the day, only Apple rivaled Samsung when it came to the best hardware. Samsung can no longer make that claim. Granted, this phone is excellent, but OnePlus, LG, and Apple are all on the same level in terms of quality build. This phone feels heavy in your hand. I personally like that, but someone coming from an Apple might be very disappointed. Going light weight was not a big consideration here. It seems like they were more focused on packing as much as possible into this phone. That leads to a big issue. Samsung has been cowed into trying to be like Apple and removed both the headphones jack and sd card slot. I see no real reason for this beyond saving money. Apple and Samsung claim that they can’t fit it in, or that no one uses them anymore. Both of those are nothing but lame excuse. Both LG and Sony put both items into their last flagships. LG in fact released HD audio to go with the headphones jack. After using both phones, I REALLY miss both those items. They added a huge amount of functionality and made doing certain things so much easier. They did add the latest and greatest 5G and Wifi connectivity to this phone. That sounds great, but I haven’t noticed it all. I even live in an area where 5G is everywhere. There might be more speed, but everything in my area was already fast. It’s hard to really notice a difference unless you are running a speed test. So, this phone is S-Pen compatible. Great. It would be really good if it actually came with an S-Pen, but you’ll have to pay more for that. By more I mean $40 for an s-pen designed for the Ultra, that is missing some functionality. That’s right, you can’t do gestures. If that’s important to you, you need to wait for the S-Pen Pro to be released “later” in 2021. That one will have a BT connection. That really seems like a fumble on Samsung’s part. I can understand making the s-pen optional and not having a silo for it, like on the Note, but not having the full-blown version available at launch feels like they are missing an opportunity. If people get the regular s-pen, decide they don’t use it, what’s to motivate them into getting the pro version? The S-pen can be handy, but it only makes sense if you get a case that can hold. Thankfully Spigen makes one that is cheap and works well. On the plus side, this phone has the fastest, most accurate fingerprint reader I’ve ever used. It’s easily twice as fast as the one LG was using. The ultrasonic format really makes a difference. When I first used the Huawei P20 Pro, I was blown away by how good that camera was. The things it did were unprecedented in a camera phone. I used a number of phones after that one, and none of them ever matched what Huawei could pull off. Samsung crushed it with this camera setup. The flexibility it offers is unmatched. From wide angle to super zoom, it’s all there. Some of the tricks they pull off with this camera are truly impressive. From how it combines photos for optimal exposure to the foolish 100x superzoom, the things you can do with this camera are insane. The 100x is nothing you’ll want to use a lot. It’s usable, but not overly clear. Still, the mere fact that you can take a usable 100x photo with this phone is mind blowing. When I say “usable” I mean a photo that is identifiable. It’s nothing I’m going to want to hang on a wall, but it might help trying to identify something. If there is one thing camera doesn’t do great, it’s exposure. It tends to over expose, but that’s it. That’s the only real issue I can find and it’s minor. You might see the 108MP sensor and think you can take some insane RAW photos with that. To a degree, that’s true, but with a sensor like that, you’d need a HUGE amount of light to be able to get good results. There is a reason why Samsung does pixel binning to get its incredible results. On its own 108MP in a sensor that size is not really usable, except in ideal conditions. I love a good wide-angle camera. LG was always a proponent of the wide-angle, and over the years, it’s really come in handy. It’s not something you use a lot, but when you need it, nothing beats it. You get two tele-photo lenses here. The 3X is great for framing your photos, and the 10x allows you to do things that no over phone I’ve ever used has allowed. The 10x really comes in handy for sunsets and times when you can’t get close to your subject. I usually don’t do a write up on charging, but in this case, I think it’s needed. You have wired 25W or wireless 10W. I love that flexibility. It’s not all good though. You know what really stinks? Paying through the nose for a phone, opening the box, and not getting a charger. That’s right. No charger in the box. If you want one, you’ll be paying for it. It’s hard to wrap your head around the fact that they charge you over $1,000, but couldn’t give you a charger. I can’t remember the last time I got a phone with no charger. Till now, OnePlus had the best screen I’d seen in a phone. It makes sense that Samsung would beat them, considering OnePlus got their screens from Samsung. This screen is amazing. It’s not just it’s looks either. They did some impressive trickery here too. The adaptive refresh is amazing. The big issue with a 120 refresh rate is the battery it burns through. With adaptive turned on, it adjusts. Reading a book or something similar – it drops as low as 10. This saves a huge amount of battery life. It’s good. It’s not LG V60 good, but it’s good. There have been times when the LG V60 lasted me for two days with normal use. This one has the same battery, but doesn’t last that long. It will easily make it through the day and night though. Welcome to the worst part about this phone. I know why Samsung doesn’t fix it too. To be honest, I hate the Samsung apps, I hate the excessive bloatware, and Bixby is the worst virtual assistant I’ve ever used. The UI is the more frustrating of the issues here. The main reason is tied to the fact that this is an Android phone. Why do you want to be so different from stock when it’s actually hindering the experience instead of improving it? I understand what Samsung is trying to do. They want to be Apple. They want their own ecosystem, they control, and reap large profits off of. That’s why they have their own assistant, apps, and UI. I’d applaud them for that, if they grow a pair and divorce Android. The only way all the apps, bloatware, assistant, and UI make sense if they are on their own. Just do it already. Become the third option, because as it stands now, your software is awful. It’s trying to sit on a fence, which means it’s not as good as it could be on its own, and it’s NO WHERE as good as stock Android. Now, if you are a handy when it comes to Android, you can remove a lot of the junk off this phone, via ADB. But, stop and think about that for a moment. You just paid top dollar for a phone, and now, you have to waste a solid hour of your time stripping off all the garbage they piled on there. How is that acceptable? If this phone was running software close to stock and didn’t have the bloatware issue, we’d be talking about a legendary phone. One of the best phones ever made. Instead, we have some of the best hardware ever combined in a phone, with steaming pile of dung laid on top of it. Again, if Samsung finally broke free of Android, I think things would be very different. They might also be watching Huawei very closely to see how everything pans out for them. Huawei was forced off Android and now runs its own OS and ecosystem. If it goes well for Huawei, I would not be surprised to see Samsung finally pull the trigger. They already have the OS. It’s been in their Smart appliances for years. I know I’ve bashed Samsung a lot here, but there are some things that do that are excellent. The first one I’ll mention is something that falls into the useful category. It’s their side tabs. The default is your recent apps or apps you’ve pinned. This comes in handy since I don’t like either of Samsung’s default launcher options. You can also add more tabs like weather and select contacts. I first used this with the S6 Edge and I’m glad it’s still around. Now for the thing that Samsung does best, and by best, I mean no one is even close. A deep dive into the sound settings will take you to an EQ setting. This is not impressive on its own, since most other makers offer this. What Samsung does that no one else does, is it gives you a hearing test and creates a custom sound profile for you. As someone who has hearing loss, the impact this has is incredible. The only thing I don’t understand is why it’s so buried. I mean you need to dig to find this thing. I find it rather ironic that Samsung is more on board with Windows integration than any other maker I’ve used. Samsung imbedded the features needed and allows you to use apps in Windows. The others I’ve used require you to download an app and you cannot use apps in Windows. This is a handy feature to have for anyone using an Windows PC. They also support the cut and paste feature. Copy on your phone – paste on your PC and vice versa. I have to relate one final frustrating issue with Samsung’s software. The last three phones I used all were on board with Google’s autofill for apps. That made signing into a new phone an easy experience. Samsung has its own thing. I spent quite a while hunting down passwords that I hadn’t used in nearly two years. There is a factor to consider, if you’ve only used Apple or Samsung products. You’ve been spoiled. By buying the most popular phones, you’ve always had a massive selection of cases and accessories. As someone who’s been using the fringe players for years, I’ve been stuck with only a few choices when it comes to cases. Sometimes it was very difficult to find cases, or I had to pay more than I would have liked. Having a massive selection does add to the value, since you end up paying less for cases as everyone tries to undercut each other. On top of that, you can find the crazy cases that include extra battery, wallets, and added functionality. If you’re using a Sony or OnePlus, you can only dream about such a thing. This becomes even more of a value I you are one of the people in a program like Amazon Vine. I was able to get three cases for this phone, through Vine. Before this, only once was I able to find a case for my phone. Another factor is that there are also apps on the Play Store that are dedicated to tweaking the Samsung experience. Some of them are quite useful. This is something you don’t find when using the minor players. Is this phone a good value? No. I’m sorry at its retail price, it’s not. The LG V60 might have a weaker camera and older processor, but it’s a far better value. The OnePlus 9 Pro, is a slightly better value, if we are talking about a full priced phone. If you want this phone to be a value, you need to land this phone for $900 or less. Anything higher just isn’t worth it. If you’re going to pay full price for this phone, you might want to look at the iPhone. I do not like iOS, but they have an excellent build, great camera, no bloatware, and fast updates. If money is not an issue and you love Samsung – yes. If money is no issue and you want the best camera – yes. If money is no issue and you want the best Android phone – maybe. If money is an issue and you want a great Android phone – buy the LG V60. If you want a clean Android experience – buy the Pixel 5 or OnePlus 9 Pro. If money isn’t an issue and you want the best phone – buy the iPhone 12 Pro Max. If you need to have a sd card and headphones jack – buy the LG V60. If you need to have a sd card and headphones jack, but hate LGs software – buy the Sony Xperia 1 II.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Review Title: I am very impressed with the ANC on these
Review Content: I am very impressed with the ANC on these. I have a pair of Bose Quietcomfort headphones, and these are about 90% as quiet as those, which is REALLY good for earbuds. I did get some memory foam ear tips to replace the silicone ones, but honestly I don't think they make much of a difference. I can tell immediately when the ANC turns on, so I know it's not just the ear tips that are blocking out the sound around me. I work at a busy hospital, and these are absolutely amazing for helping me regulate myself on my breaks. The only thing I notice is that these do such a good job of cutting out the background noise, they can sometimes make specific sounds stand out. For example, if I'm sitting at a café, I can barely hear the barista making coffee and banging cups and plates around, but I can distinctly hear the people talking at the table next to me. This is true of my Bose headphones too, but to a lesser degree. These don't work miracles - just get earplugs if you need total quiet. This is my biggest issue with these earbuds. Sound quality is obviously one of the most important aspects of earbuds, and these sounded awful right out of the box. Way, way worse than my $30 pair that I was using before. They were extremely tinny and sounded like I was listening to music coming from a different room. I spent a good 2 HOURS adjusting the settings in the app to try to make them sound good, and I did eventually get there, but if you don't want to spend the time doing that, I honestly don't recommend these. The app has a lot of ways to customize the sound, but you really have to get in there and micromanage everything if you want them to sound decent. I went through the "HearID Sound" setup, which made a difference, but I still had to go into the EQ and adjust it while listening to several different types of audio in order to create a profile that worked across the board for the types of things I usually listen to (jazz, rock, and podcasts). I am not an audiophile, but I can tell my Bose headphones sound a lot better - however, at this point, I am not bothered by the quality of these ones. I'd say they're a 3.5/5 on overall sound quality, but a 1/5 out of the box. I guess it's possible I got a bad pair, but considering I did eventually get to a good point with them, I don't think that's the case. I'm not sure if it's because they're refurbished (box was completely sealed and unopened though), but I only get 4-5 hours of battery life with ANC on, opposed to the 7 hours they advertise. Could be worse, but my previous non-ANC earbuds lasted me a good 10+ hours, so I find this a bit frustrating because I like to have them in all day due to my noise sensitivities. I my actually get a second pair so that I always have one that is charged. I chose these earbuds primarily because of the ear hook. I use an electric scooter to get to work, and I struggled to keep my previous earbuds from falling out due to the vibration. These stay put very well, and the hooks don't feel uncomfortable at all. They're bigger than other earbuds because of this design, but still very pocketable, and the case isn't too bulky. If you're looking for a pair of true ANC earbuds that won't fall out, will last at least 4 hours, and you're okay with taking some time to play with the sound settings, I highly recommend these. After using them for a month, I am happy with my purchase. Hope this review helps you decide if these are for you!       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Out of the box, you receive the phone (which itself is in very good physical condition), the sim card removal tool, and a usb charging cable (with no actual 12v wall outlet plug, you need to buy that separately). The phone, when powered up, you'll discover is a Verizon branded phone. I followed the instructions by completing initial setup and updates via my home wi-fi network, then inserting my t-mobile sim card. Well, the phone, no matter what, refused to accept the card and allow me to make calls or use data. In fact, it would give me a message 'sim card locked - not a verizon sim card.' After wasting hours trying everything imaginable, I came to the conclusion that this really isn't an unlocked tmobile phone. How did I find this out? Well, I tapped on a message on the screen which gave me a 'Sorry, your device can't be activated on another carrier's network right now' message from the My Verizon app installed on the phone. So I tried the same sim card on my own FULLY unlocked Motorola One phone (purchased from a different amazon vendor months ago) and it fired right up and let me use calls data straight away. I'm guessing this vendor is doing nothing for testing except for running a stock verizon sim before shipping these out. Extremely disappointed. Time and money wasted. Moral of the story is: stick to fully unlocked phones, and avoid carrier branded phones. Because they will be very hit or miss. Noise cancellation isn't great in the wind, but at a fraction of the price of premium brands, it’s hard to complain. Product Title: Amazon.com: Soundcore by Anker Space A40 Noise Cancelling Wireless Earbuds(Renewed) | Reduce Noise by Up to 98%, Ultra Long 50H Playtime, 11H Single Playtime, Hi-Res Sound, Comfortable Fit, Wireless Charge : Electronics
Review Title: The app has nice features and is easy to use
Review Content: The app has nice features and is easy to use. Tuning them to your ears seems to improve SQ a bit. Noise cancellation is effective and smart. Not going to block out as much noise as, say, a $200 set of Bose earbuds, but it does a good enough job to mow the lawn with an electric mower and more or less silence that noise as long as you have something playing. Not quite effective enough to block out the sound while onboard an airplane if you have the kind of seat you can afford if you're buying this product :) In fully transparent sound cancellation mode, it will still block out the drone and constant noise of something like an electric bike's motor, or wind noise, but will allow the sound of non-constant (upcoming car, person behind you yelling about how you don't deserve to exist) through. For the money, very good. Battery easily lasts 3 hours, may be longer or shorter depending on what you have playing at what volume level. By mixing and matching the included (cheap) silicon inserts I was able to find a good-enough fit for me. Not everyone has the same size hole on each side of their head. What I don't understand is why products like this don't have a breathable charging case. They're marketed as and intended to be used by active people. Active people sweat. Plopping these yucky drenched earbuds into their charging container and then shutting it lets them sit in their stew. I typically let them air out and even wipe them clean after each use before holstering them into their little cave. I was paranoid that one of these would slide out while cruising at 20 MPH and would be gone forever, but I can say that they stay pretty securely in your head. I do find myself fidgeting with them quite a bit, but that might just be me. Fit could be better but is very good considering it's the first product I found, the price, and the fact that they're made to fit Everyone. Look no further! Product Title: Amazon.com: Soundcore by Anker Space A40 Noise Cancelling Wireless Earbuds(Renewed) | Reduce Noise by Up to 98%, Ultra Long 50H Playtime, 11H Single Playtime, Hi-Res Sound, Comfortable Fit, Wireless Charge : Electronics
Review Title: ##### Phänomenaler Klang, tolle Bedienung, gute Telefonie, ich bin begeistert!
Review Content: ##### Phänomenaler Klang, tolle Bedienung, gute Telefonie, ich bin begeistert! Nachdem mir der Q30i eine zu schlechte Telefoniequalität auf der Gegenseite hatte und für die phantastischen Liberty 4 Pro keine passenden Earbuds gefunden habe, habe ich beide schweren Herzens zurückgesandt und Soundcore mit den Space A45 noch eine letzte Chance gegeben. Der Klang ist gitantisch: Tonal absolut ausgewogen, satt und trocken im Bass aber nicht überzogen, die Stimmwiedergabe ist perfekt. Beim Equalizer habe ich das Standardprogramm "Bass Reducer" eingestellt, was bei meinen JBL Live 670 der Studioeinstellung, also Studiobedinungen entspricht. Ich mag die einfache Einrichtung und die perfekte Bedienung, da sich die Steuerung programmieren lässt, Meine Einstellung: Links Pause / Wiedergabe, rechts laut / leise und auf beiden Ohren Transparanzmodus ein / aus. Auch die Telefoniefunktion funktiniert in Auto in der Bahn und in der Stadt vergleichbar den Liberty 4 Pro und dort deutlich besser als bei den P30i und auch besser als beim Q30 Kopfhörer, welche nur in ruhiger Umgebung funktionieren. Einziger Wehmutstropfen: Meine Gehörgänge sind auch für die mitgelileferten XL-Earpads zu groß, ich habe allerdings welche in meiner Sammlung gefunden, die passen (und bei den P30i sowie bei den Liberty 4 Pro nicht passten). Während ich die Liberty 4 Pro ständig beim Kauen sowie bei jeder Kopfbewegung verloren habe und auch die P30 i nicht fest saßen, sitzen die Q45 durch die andere Gewichtsverteilung trotz ihres hohen Gewichtes (vergleichbar mit den Liberty 4 Pro), sehr sicher in meinen Ohren. Resümee: Klare Kaufempfelung! Gratulation an Soundcore für die Space A45! Review Title: My wife's phone was dead, so there was some drama getting her files transfered, but we had it backed

I had an old umidigi phone that I put the SIM card in and we finally managed to get a text code to go through to start the files being transferred. I was worried I'd need to repair the phone which would cost more than it's worth, but we worked around it. But do keep stuff backed up with Google or Samsung and have a way to get access. My wife was without her phone for just a day and we realized how much stuff we use phones for (finances and work access,etc). It was a bit of a nightmare there until she regained access. Not sure how that bodes for our collective future, lol, but it's stressful to suddenly be locked out. Review Title: I am writing this review because I was hesitant to buy a "renewed" phone, and unsure what I would ge
Review Content: I am writing this review because I was hesitant to buy a "renewed" phone, and unsure what I would get. Well, I'm here to tell you I have been pleasantly surprised. The phone arrived early from what was quoted by Amazon. Emails came automatically from FedEx and were fairly accurate. I ordered the phone on a Friday before a Monday federal holiday, and Amazon quoted it to arrive Tuesday. Within the next 24 hours I received an email from FedEx saying to expect a delivery on Monday, between ~8am and noon. There were a couple follow up emails and the phone did eventually arrive a little after 1pm. Already I was pleasantly and unexpectedly satisfied with the service as the phone had arrived a day earlier than expected. The only downside was that Verizon was unable to activate the phone over another phone, because there was no sim card installed. Even before receiving the phone I was afraid that I would not get an unlocked version or something else would impede my ability to get this one working to replace the one I had just lost. After an hour or so trying with Verizon tech support they finally indicated I needed to go to a Verizon store and get a free sim card. I was able to get to the store nearby before they closed. The process was easy and fast, and I had the phone connected and my phone number back in no time. It took a couple of tries to get accounts set up and synced, but my "new" phone is essentially the same as the old. The phone sent to me by Re-Cell was in great shape. If there were not a few very minor dings on the top and bottom of the body of the phone I would think it was brand new and unused. Someone must have replaced the screen, or the person who owned it before installed a screen protector and good case, because the screen and back of the phone show no signs of wear and tear, let alone damage. So far no operations have been less than my previous new S22 Ultra. In fact, I may even be getting better battery life from this one, which could have as much to do with having a phone cleaned of old files, etc, but I get the impression that either the battery was replaced, or this phone was not used heavily before it was refurbished. This phone "feels" newer than the one I lost, which did have a couple scratches on the screen. Other than having to spend money on a new phone, (my Wells Fargo credit card phone protection does not cover lost phones, only theft) the only major downside to losing my old phone was the time I spent looking for it, and going through the process to get this one and set it up... a story I will not tell here. From my experience with Amazon Renewed and Re-Cell, I do not plan to buy another new phone when the time comes that I ever need another. I will find the phone I want here and buy it used in excellent condition like the one that was shipped to me. Very satisfied with this experience. Review Title: ##### Il mio primo rigenerato Amazon, vi racconto tutto
Review Content: ##### Il mio primo rigenerato Amazon, vi racconto tutto. Veniamo all'oggetto della recensione: l'iphone. Una volta tirato fuori dall'orrenda bustina di plastica che lo conteneva, l'ho accuratamente ispezionato rilevando un piccolo segno marcato (circa 1x1 mm) nella parte superiore sinistra dello schermo, dove il display si unisce al notch. A questo si aggiunge un piccolissimo segno (non so come altro definirlo) tra lo schermo e la scocca, nella parte inferiore sinistra. Entrambi i segni sono pressocchè invisibili ad una prima occhiata, occorre esaminare con cura il telefono per rilevarli. Il resto (scocca, schermo, bordi, ecc) è come nuovo. Amazon Renewed dichiara che il telefono "non presenta imperfezioni estetiche visibili tenendo il prodotto a una distanza di 30 centimetri", e direi che la promessa è stata assolutamente mantenuta, ben oltre le aspettative. Esaurita la parte estetica, accendiamo il telefono: l'avvio è immediato, i colori, la luminosità e la presenza dell'opzione True Tone mi fanno pensare che il display è originale Apple, difatti la mancanza del True Tone è solitamente indice di un display non originale o quantomeno più economico di quelli normalmente usati da Apple. Anche il codice IMEI riportato fisicamente sul "cassettino" della Sim corrisponde a quello indicato nelle informazioni del telefono, cosa che mi permette di ipotizzare che il telefono non è il risultato di un assemblaggio di più pezzi provenienti da altri telefoni. La configurazione è avvenuta senza difficoltà e dopo un accurato test di tutta la sensoristica e delle varie parti (Face Id, prossimità, luminosità, touch & 3d touch, giroscopi, tasto muto, volume, power, flash, ricarica wireless, altoparlanti, ecc ecc) non ho rilevato malfunzionamenti o problemi di alcun genere. Il telefono è arrivato con iOs 14.8, versione che se non ricordo male è stata rilasciata intorno a settembre 2021. Analizzando il seriale è possibile determinare l'anno di produzione: il mio nuovo amico risulta essere stato assemblato a Chengdu intorno alla seconda metà di settembre 2018. Facendo due conti, il telefono è rimasto "in giro" da settembre 2018 a settembre 2021, poi non è stato più aggiornato e quindi presumo utilizzato. La batteria presenta una capacità massima dell'80%, in linea a quanto indicato nelle condizioni del prodotto su Amazon. Di sicuro è stato usato non poco, ma il fatto che possa leggere quel valore è un altro ottimo indicatore, significa infatti che la batteria è ancora quella originale, altresì avrei un avviso di "batteria non originale". La scocca posteriore è priva del marchio CE, che di solito identifica i telefoni nati per il mercato Europeo. Ma niente paura, in questo caso significa solo che questo telefono era originariamente destinato al mercato americano o asiatico. Tuttavia, poichè la fotocamera non produce il rumore dello scatto quando è in modalità silenziosa, propendo per il mercato USA. In quello cinese infatti, se non è cambiato qualcosa, i telefoni devono per legge emettere sempre il rumore dello scatto fotografico, così da impedire scatti "rubati". Dura lex, sed lex! Infine faccio una delle ultime ma più importanti prove, vado sul sito Apple e tramite codice seriale verifico la garanzia: e qui ecco la sorpresa (bella)! Non solo il prodotto è regolare, non ci sono allarmi e il seriale è corretto, ma risulto addirittura coperto dall'AppleCare+ fino al 17 di questo mese, mica male :-). Concludo (finalmente, direte voi!): in questo momento sono estremamente contento del mio acquisto, l'iphone è praticamente nuovo e funziona bene. Direi un bel 5 stelle tanto ad Amazon quanto al venditore NEGOZIOREALE, che hanno superato le mie aspettative. Se state leggendo questa recensione, e non importa quando, significa che il telefono sta continuando a funzionare bene. Al primo accenno di problema state sicuri che verrò subito qui ad aggiornare la mia recensione. Review Title: I also own a JBL flip 6 which is about more or less a third of the volume in size
Review Content: I also own a JBL flip 6 which is about more or less a third of the volume in size I'm comparing it to the JBL flip 6 because it's a very popular Bluetooth speaker that you may already own or you have a friend that does. The sound core boom 2 does not sound super great out of the box. It's very bassy and the vocals can be muddled. With the app you can slightly boost up some of the treble features and a completely changes the speaker. So I have the left and right sliders on The equalizer slightly bumped up and the second to right and left sliders boosted up kind of towards the middle. The bass button on the actual speaker is separate to The equalizer and I leave it on. I would only probably turn it off at max volume, which should only be done in an outdoors party because this thing does get pretty loud. So I compared my JBL to this thing about 8 ft away from me in a bedroom. The sound core at half volume is roughly as loud as the JBL at full volume. They both perform great but the sound core has way better overall range then the JBL. It's noticeable in the lower bass and lower vocals range. But the entire range is very crisp and clear once it's set up in the soundcore app and it maintains clarity until about the 85% range of volume, then you may want to make adjustments to The equalizer to smooth it out. It doesn't sound bad but pushing any speaker to the max is going to have issues. For the price this is a fantastic buy. I use the JBL because it's small and packs quite a punch in its weight class. I also have an outdoor party speaker the block rocker Plus but it's massive and is more of like a beach/pa speaker for me. The size of the speaker is roughly about the size of a specialty loaf of bread, like a Keto bread or something more artisan. It's got to handle that's built into the actual box and is kind of light feeling. If you find this thing on sale pick it up. Also check out the renewed version, I saved like almost 50 bucks and it's got a couple light scratches and scuffs that you can't see unless you're holding it. Review Title: I'm not the rattling license plate kind of bass guy, but I like quality, accurate bass way higher vo
Review Content: I'm not the rattling license plate kind of bass guy, but I like quality, accurate bass way higher volumes than most people can tolerate. This speaker isn't impressive on that level at all, but it is impressive for something the size of a large bread loaf. The lowest notes drop off in volume and the bass drum isn't crisp like a sealed 12, for obvious reasons. But I still find myself turning the bass boost off on a lot of situations to be respectful of neighbors. Battery life is great. I try to keep it plugged in just so the music never quits, but never think twice about setting it unplugged on the workbench with bass on for hours on end, or using it to watch movies and shows in bed for hours. I build lots of things, usually overbuilt, and am highly critical of poorly engineered plastic crap. This feels remarkably solid. Silicone buttons don't feel like they'll leak or break. Handle is beyond overkill. Grill over speakers is very stiff. Passive woofers on side are exposed, but slightly recessed like an hd phone case. I even left the back port uncovered for a day of rafting once and it didn't die. Impressive Bluetooth distance too. Review Title: I'm used to using the tempered glass screen protectors which can't be used on this one
Review Content: I'm used to using the tempered glass screen protectors which can't be used on this one. I've tried a couple of the flexible film ones with it but wasted the money because couldn't get them to install properly(without air bubbles everywhere). The phone screen is soft. It will get dents/creases in it if not careful(I put a light crease in mine trying to install a screen protector). When opened its not perfectly flat, there's a shallow area where the fold is but it's not visually noticeable with the screen on at all. Only noticeable by touch and visually when the screen is off. The non expandable memory isn't a feature I like. 128GB isn't a whole lot nowadays, especially when it's common for apps to be 1GB-3GB(like games and Facebook). I used to keep my games, photos, and entertainment/social media apps on a SD card but now I'm just being a lot more selective with what I install and quick to uninstall something if it's not being used regularly, whereas with expandable memory I'd just leave them on the SD card. I read that it will no longer receive updates from Samsung so Android 14 is going to be the last operating system upgrade for it. Size is the reason I bought it. Got tired of carrying phones that only fit in back pockets and still have 1/4 of it sticking out. With this I get the same size screen but can put it in any pocket. It's unlocked compatible with GSM and CDMA service providers so works with all the major ones. All in all it's a good phone loaded with features, looks and functions like a new one for 1/2 the price,and it's second life is helping the planet with saving resources and landfill space. A good buy for cheap people like me who cares not 1 bit about having the newest model phone. Product Title: Amazon.com: Kyocera Duraxe E4830 Epic AT&T Flip Smart Phone 16GB Rugged PTT Wi-Fi LTE Black (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: As for the actual phone it is waterproof as it survived being lost in a lake for a couple hours, the
Review Content: As for the actual phone it is waterproof as it survived being lost in a lake for a couple hours, the hinge is durable, I know I flopped on it enough times that it would have broken if it was going to. The speakers are wildly loud and good. Straight up works as well as a high quality drug store Bluetooth speaker and I never heard bad distortion even at the highest volume I turned it to, I never needed to turn it up all the way. I loaded my MP3s on it and used the heck out of it's music player which does pale in comparison to the iPod software or the Spotify interface but it worked perfectly. The camera is pretty mid, captures photos and video on par with phones from 2010 but if you want to send a video via text that requires forethought as you need to record it as an attachment otherwise the video file will be too big. Receiving pictures and videos can be difficult too, if a sender puts more than one image or a large video (over 1024kb) the attachment has to be downloaded to be viewed and that is best done on a computer since the file system on the phone is weird and doesn't always open the right downloaded pictures. Downloading PDF documents and viewing those is a breeze and was useful to me as I needed to download and navigate schematics often. Email is difficult since modern security doesn't allow direct logins on this interface, you'll need to create a one time key on a computer to authenticate this phone but once you're in it works great. Browsing the web is again difficult as some websites are built like something that isn't built well and won't work on this phone. A lot do though including Wikipedia and YouTube, reddit does not work. The calendar and alarm clock both work better than anything else I've used though you are limited to system sounds for the alarms. I love this phone but due to a recent job I've had to get a smartphone, on that note this is a great intermediate device when switching from apple to android since it makes you think about how to use it. 10/10 will go back to this phone if I can later into this job. Product Title: Amazon.com: Kyocera Duraxe E4830 Epic AT&T Flip Smart Phone 16GB Rugged PTT Wi-Fi LTE Black (Renewed) : Cell Phones & Accessories
Review Title: El mio llegó con un golpe perceptible en la parte izquierda del dispositivo, 2 rasguños grandes que
Review Content: El mio llegó con un golpe perceptible en la parte izquierda del dispositivo, 2 rasguños grandes que si eran perceptibles a distancia. Como el mismo vendedor dice, parece ser un teléfono resistente. Lo que me hace pensar que estos rayones no fueron hechos por descuido sino por algo un poco más contundente. Fuera de este aspecto que realmente me incomoda, trataré de dar una reseña útil para los posibles interesados en este producto. 1.- Se escuchan perfecto las llamadas. Y aparentemente está desbloqueado para todos los servicios de telefonía en la región. 2.- Es resistente, como ya dije es un teléfono que parece resistente y no se siente hueco o barato. 3.- Tiene cierta calidad; Kyocera es marca japonesa así que no es un producto de baja calidad, es totalmente para uso profesional. 4.- las teclas se sienten excelentes; Comparado con otros modelos como el CAT Flip s22 o los nokia flip actuales. Este se lleva el premio al ser exactas y precisas, te acostumbras de inmediato a la forma de escritura. 5.- Tiene configuración en español. Aunque hay algunos errores de traducción es completamente legible esta configuración 6.- El sonido es excelente en los altavoces, casi es como uno de esos sony ericcson de antaño. 7.- Conexión Wi-fi. El teléfono tiene configuración para configuración de internet inalámbrico a un ruter. 8.- El diseño del teléfono es excelente parece que vale cada centavo. (excepto por el logo de AT&T, que me molesta personalmente, arruina todo) 9.- teclas programables: Tiene distintas teclas en los bordes y dentro del mismo teléfono que tienen funciones programables, puedes acceder a configuración , conectividad y reproductor de música fácilmente programando estas teclas ( incluyendo una naranja que es la tecla SOS). 1.- La batería; Conectado al Wi-Fi la batería dura aproximadamente 8 horas, quizá menos. Sin el wifi o datos moviles conectado dura casi un día, pero no más. 2.- Constantemente tienes que cuidar de la batería (física); Me explico, hay una función dentro del teléfono que te recomienda activar que es "cuidado de la batería". Esto hace que cuando lo conectes toda la noche o por un tiempo prolongado solo cargue al 80% Para no dañar la batería con picos de energía. Toda esta experiencia resulta molesta; Debido a que no deberíamos preocuparnos por activar este tipo de funciones en pleno 2024. 4.- La red móvil (datos móviles). Dure una semana sin datos móviles debido a que no hay una explicación clara de como configurarlos en el empaque. Al parecer hay que configurar manualmente la red móvil introduciendo una contraseña de la misma compañía, entre otros datos; información que esta disponible en linea. Con ningún celular tuve que hacer esto antes. Me pareció nuevamente, algo reamente extraño para estos tiempos. 5.- Configuraciones: Hay una serie de configuraciones molestas que pareciera que hay que hacer cada que quieres utilizar el teléfono. Me refiero a entrar a configuración de iluminación de pantalla, encender y apagar redes. 6.- La multimedia; el reproductor de música es pésimo con opciones limitadas, solo reproducción aleatoria y siguiente. Afortunadamente tiene un puerto Jack para conectar audífonos, pero todo esto se va al traste debido a la muy mala calidad de audio en la que reproduce, es increíble. 7.- Whatsapp; se puede descargar whatsapp ya que el teléfono cuenta con navegador web. Por tanto puedes entrar a descargar esta aplicación (tiene algo similar al Android 10). Sin embargo una vez descargado empieza la pesadilla. Puedes conectarlo como dispositivo vinculado. Lo cual es bueno sin embargo la navegación es desastrosa, no hay forma de navegar por los chats y al seleccionar una conversación esta no se abre. Puedes descargar aplicaciones de apuntador pero la verdad son riesgosos y difíciles de instalar mediante un software que no tiene que ver con Kyocera. 8.- El peso; el dispositivo en sí es algo pesado como para llevarlo en un bolsillo del pantalón, es un bulto que termina posicionándose de manera horizontal en tu bolsillo y te llegas a sorprender a ti mismo acomodándolo para que no te moleste al caminar. 9.- El correo electrónico; Nunca pude configurar el correo electrónico en este dispositivo, ni gmail, ni outlook, ni un correo de la empresa en donde trabajo. Desconozco el motivo, realmente intenté configurarlo. Por esta razón no fue útil en la oficina. 10.- función e compartir internet: Esta opción no funciona el dispositivo lanza una leyenda (que desaparece de inmediato) que te avisa que esa función no funciona correctamente. Es realmente extraño. 11.- La lampara; El teléfono tiene una función de linterna pero es realmente poco lo que ilumina. Por lo menos comparado con otros dispositivos similares es increíble que ilumine tan mal. (también tiene una opción para parpadear con esta luz) 12.- Pantalla interna y externa; si no te molesta que no puedas cambiar la configuración de visualización de pantalla externa o interna entonces no es un punto negativo. Pero algo básico en un teléfono hoy en día es la personalización de las pantallas. En este caso el teléfono no cuenta más que con funciones de quitar y poner el reloj o la visualización de la fecha. Pero poco más no hay manera de configurar el idioma (por default en ingles) de la pantalla externa o la forma en que se muestra el reloj en la pantalla. En resumen; era un entusiasta de los Feature Phone; estos últimos años intenté encontrar un modelo que se amoldara a mis necesidades que no son muchas. Y tras varios nokia (modernos) , un cat flip s22, varios BLU, etc. El que acabó con mi paciencia fue este teléfono. Hay que aceptar que estamos condenados a subsistir mediante placas aburridas de vidrio negro. Me rindo. Review Title: When I first got these they worked as described in my original review below
Review Content: When I first got these they worked as described in my original review below. But after about 2 months the battery life in left one started falling off a cliff. I contacted Anker and they replaced them immediately. The replacement pair worked well, but after a couple months the left one again started running out of charge after an hour or so. The right one was down, but would still go 4 hours. Not good, but better than the left one. I reached out to Anker and sure enough, like others have reported here, the warranty is only 90 days from date of original purchase. This was stated nowhere in the original listing, but there was actually no warranty info shown in the original listing, so, whatever. Currently, the left one - in spite of showing as fully charged in the app - only lasts about 5 minutes. The right one goes about an hour. Anker customer support was quick to respond, but wouldn't help. So, while it looks like these "refurb" units currently aren't available at the moment, I'd suggest you don't buy even the new versions of these. They just aren't reliable enough. I don't mean like "Surprise! I got you some ear buds!", rather, I mean I wasn't expecting much out of these - they're TINY, and while the specs say they'll last up to 10 hours on bluetooth, most reviews here said they were getting a lot less than that. I set them up (a bit fiddly with the app) and fully charged them. First night the right one lasted about 3 hours and the left of only about 5 hours. Not good. Thought I'd give them one more chance and fully recharged them and the second night they both made it about 6 hours. Okay, getting better. Third night? I managed to get a full 9 hours of sleep (don't be jelly) and when I woke up they were happily chugging along with an audiobook - with 20% charge remaining. They've been like this since. Surprise! -They're TINY ( I've got nimble fingers and these buggers are a challenge to not drop on the floor when handling them) -The charging case is completely impossible to use in the dark (Which way does it open and which ear bud goes into which charging slot....?) -Getting them paired to your device the first time is fiddly (The app you have to use for this isn't plainly obvious in any app store) -They're TINY (once you get your ear tips chosen they just pop right into your ears and they stay put and don't stick out at all - perfect for this side sleeper!) -They sound VERY clear (they're not for listening to thumping bass music, but for audiobooks, podcasts & sleepscape music they're PERFECT) -They got to a VERY low volume (it's odd that most headphones don't actually sound clear at extremely low volumes. These do) -Good battery life (give them a few full charge cycles and keep the volume levels low these should work all night) -They don't loudly announce "BATTERY LOW!" when the battery gets low. (You toggle this off and on in the app, but it's off by default) Can't speak to their longevity, but a couple weeks in and they seem stable. They're solidly built and seem like they'll last awhile. I'll definitely report back here with an update if any quality issues arise. If you need some astonishingly unobtrusive sleep buds just get these. Have patience while getting them set up, and give them a few full charge cycles and you should be all set. Review Title: The differences between this and the higher-end models were things I didn’t need (like slightly fast
Review Content: The differences between this and the higher-end models were things I didn’t need (like slightly faster battery charging time, more time between charges, ECG app, SpO2 sensor, water resistance, etc.). I like the wide array of watch faces and customization options for most of them. My personal favorite is the one that includes the option for a 5-hour weather forecast. If you install other faces, you can easily switch between them directly from the watch. I have one with a second hand ready to swipe to for times when I want or need that. One of my favorite features is the ability to set and name alarms by speaking it: “set alarm at 1pm to start getting ready for appointment.” And likewise set and name countdown timers: “set timer to check laundry in 1 hour.” I use this often and it works better than it does on even the iPhone or iPad. The one feature that justified the price for me was the crash/fall detection and emergency SOS. I will be 70 next year and although I’ve never had an issue that required any of this so far (knock on wood), you never know. I was originally not thrilled that I’d have to charge it every day instead of having it last several days (like my Fitbits did). But I found that I easily get thru a full day (plus) after an hour of charge time. So now I just set an alarm to remind me to charge it every night before bed, so now it’s a habit and no problem. That said, the documentation says it runs up to 18 hours on a full charge so I’m not sure how I manage over 24 hours without even resorting to low-power mode. From what I understand, the 18 hour figure is ‘typical use’ and I guess don’t use it ‘typically.’: I don’t use it for music or phone calls, I have the display on the lowest brightness (which is plenty bright), and I don’t use the “always on” setting for the display. So no complaints there! The Health app on the iPhone that interfaces with the watch could be more organized, but the watch itself certainly does more than a standard watch and does many of those things easily — once you know how. One of the things I truly dislike is the silicone band, but that applied to the Fitbit as well. I find them all intensely uncomfortable, too fiddly to put on and take off, and the Apple one pinches me every time I slip the tail end of the strap into the slot that goes under the band. The bands also look too wide on my narrow wrist. But it was simple to find something better on Amazon for everyday wear as well as a band for dressier occasions. They are also a lot easier to swap out than the mechanism on the last two Fitbit watches I had. It’s still a pretty darn big watch, but if it wasn’t, it wouldn’t be as useful either. And it only took me about a week to get used to the size which was faster than I expected. I’ve been using it for almost 3 weeks now and have been very happy with it. It takes a little bit of getting used to and there are a ton of settings between the iPhone interface and the watch itself, but I’ve had good luck Googling for help with most of those. And once I found the settings I liked, I hardly deal with any of that anymore. If you use an iPhone or iPad, the interface is familiar enough — all things considered — but I also enjoy solving puzzles so that makes figuring it out less bothersome to me. The cons I mentioned aren’t anything I can fairly deduct stars for because they came as no surprise. That is, I knew what I was in for before I got it. And I was more often pleasantly surprised. At this stage the only thing that would ding stars for me is if it goes bad too quickly.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))

Review Title: I bought this as an Amazon Renewed Premium, shipped from the Networkstore
Review Content: I bought this as an Amazon Renewed Premium, shipped from the Networkstore. Even though my phone keeps telling me that I can have 12 months of AI Advanced Upgrade, it never lets me enroll. Amazon or the Networkstore don't tell you that you don't get this benefit that Google offers. That is a two-hundred-dollar offer that I can't take advantage of. It is probably a little more direct and less friendly than other AIs I have used. But it may be more accurate, because it provides the backup for its answer. The photo AI tools are good, but limited. It has restrictions with using people in your AI images. Overall it is fun to play with, but still a little frustrating with getting the prompts to work as you want. I like all the little hidden features, like tapping the back of the phone for a set action. Activating Gemini anywhere you are and on whatever app or page you are on. The phone hearing a song that is playing in the background and showing the title of the song on your lock screen. There is so much to like about this phone. I am excited to continue exploring and using the phone. As far as the Amazon Renewed Premium, I wanted to make sure that I got a phone that was in like new condition and had the one-year warranty that the Renewed Premium offers. So you pay less than a brand new phone, but more than a typical renewed phone. I think it was worth it. The only thing I didn't think through and they didn't let you know that you can't take advantage of the 12 months of AI Advantage from Google. Other than that, I would recommend this phone and I would recommend Amazon Renewed Premium. Review Title: I am coming from an iPhone 16 Pro Max, and honestly I've gotten quite bored with Apple's "walled gar
Review Content: I am coming from an iPhone 16 Pro Max, and honestly I've gotten quite bored with Apple's "walled garden" iOS. I have been eyeing foldable phones for a while and preferred a phone with clean android is, good support, and an unlocked bootloader if I wanted to use custom ROMs. This left one clear choice - the Google Pixel 10 Pro Fold ​The Tensor G5 Chip: initially, I was concerned about this one, as most high end Android devices stick with the tried and true Qualcomm Snapdragon SoC. My concerns were definitely unwarranted. This chip was made by Google in partnership with TSMC (the same company that makes Apple’s chips). It’s estimated to be over 30% faster than the previous Tensor G4 chip and it is definitely no slouch. It runs buttery smooth for all the tasks I throw at it, primarily watching videos, writing emails, and web browsing. I have not tried gaming as I am not an avid gamer. Had I been looking for bleeding edge ray trace enabled gaming performance, id probably have gone with a Qualcomm equipped phone. Ingress protection - this device is ​IP68 rated. This is a big one. This phone is the first foldable in North America with this high of a rating. It’s fully dust-resistant, which was the "Achilles' heel" of previous folding phones. ​The "Gearless" Hinge: It works great and is rated to last over 10 years of folding ( tested for 200000 folds, or 50 times a day EVERY day for over 10 years. ​Weight & Bulk: it is definitely not light, weighing in at a hefty 258 grams. In comparison, my iPhone 16 pro Max is 227 grams. This means that this phone is 13% heavier. With all that said, I still do not find this phone overly heavy or distracting at all. It feels premium and is built solid as a tank. ​Display: the cover display measures in at a respectable 6.4" and is much wider than, say, a similar competitor such as the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 6. The inner (8") screens give up to 3,000 nits of peak brightness, making it one of the best phones for outdoor use in direct sunlight. the cameras on the Fold not quite on par with the standard Pixel 10 Pro or Pro XL, but this is expected in a foldable . For day to day nonprofessional uses, the camera is still quite good, but if you want the BEST cameras, id go with iPhone, Samsung, or Google pixel 10 pro. ​Capacity: the phone has a 5,015mAh battery. Coming from an iPhone, I found no issues with battery life, which says a lot considering apple products always have great batteries. This Google device holds its own ​PixelSnap (Qi2) : this phone has magnetic wireless charging (similar to MagSafe), which makes it easy to snap on accessories and chargers. This may not seem like a lot, but once you get used to it, you will never want to go without it. I went with an unlocked renewed version of this phone as it's been on the market for about 6 months now, and I didn't want to use my phone carrier to upgrade as I anticipate using my carrier upgrade perks to get the rumored iPhone foldable at some point in the future. Let me say, the phone I received was immaculate. I literally could find no indications of wear or prior use. The third party seller, SoonerSoft Electronics, shipped the phone overnight and it was received promptly the following day. I will definitely add this seller as a favorite! This phone is wonderful for tech enthusiasts, people looking for a capable multitasking phone, using integrated AI tools, and social /multimedia consumption. If this fits your uses, you can't go wrong!       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))       8 people found this helpful Helpful  Sending feedback...Thank you for your feedback. Review Title: Returned the watch
Review Content: Returned the watch. The microphone intermittently functioned, the scratches were bothering me, and new watches are only $100 more than this beat up thing. Yes, $100 isn’t cheap, but overall it was worth the extra cost. My new Apple Watch 7 has a larger screen and no signs of use. It’s worth the upgrade, especially when Amazon describes the refurbished watch “like new” when that is clearly not the case. Calls from the refurbished watch only worked half the time, and the speaker sounded muffled. Just pony up for a new watch, which are discounted right now for an apple 7, and be happy. Hope this updates helps you decide. Ok, the watch costs less than new, but that’s about where the good stuff ends. It did include a usb charger (Samsung brand! 😟) generic charging cable, off-brand white strap, and poorly packaged in a generic white box. Literally nothing was done to “recondition” the watch. First thing I had to do was clean off the former user’s grime that coated the watch back (yuck!). This took some soap, water, and a toothbrush to clean out the little crevices. Screen and case came with minor scratches overall, with one more annoying, more pronounced screen scratch that really bugs me. Battery was completely depleted, which is not good for lithium batteries. C’mon, for the money you could at least clean and charge the thing! It’s not in terrible shape, but very clearly used. It certainly was not refurbished in any way that I can tell. Imagine buying the watch from your mom after she wore it for a year and you get the idea about my watch’s condition. Not abused, but certainly used. I’m torn. This was not a great purchase, and I’m left wondering if its worth the $150 less than new price. Hard to say. Just don’t believe the product description claiming “appears new” because that is far from the truth. Set your expectations accordingly if you purchase from the “Camera Guyz”. They just take the watch, toss it in a nondescript box with whatever knockoff bits they have laying around, and mail it to you. Look, you’re still paying a lot of money, so there’s no reason not to expect a quality product. Amazon says I have a 90 day warranty, so there’s time (accidental pun) to evaluate it further. Yes it works. Yes, I will eventually add more wear and tear to the watch when wearing. Yes, the “appears new” description is complete fiction. Overall value is debatable. One star for inaccurate condition description and an annoying screen scratch. The real test for me is how the headphones sound as you close a car door, or put away dishes, and these handle both tasks well! The sound signature on Q35’s is arguably better than newer models, although warm and un-exciting. Unless you need a Google button, save yourself some money and buy the base model 35’s over the 35 ii’s. Video latency was imperceptible for me, and there are plenty of aftermarket ear pads and accessories. Battery life for any bose headphones seems to suffer. Product Title: Amazon.com: Apple AirPods Pro (2nd Generation) (Renewed Premium) : Electronics
Review Title: This is a review both for the AirPods Pro (2nd gen), but also for the Amazon Renewal program
Review Content: This is a review both for the AirPods Pro (2nd gen), but also for the Amazon Renewal program. I'm not bought into the Apple ecosystem and have no plans to do so, but I won a pair of these at a work event, and they changed my life. Seriously I'm so much more productive because I don't have to listen to the loud project manager sitting next to me on calls all day - that's how good the active noise canceling is. If that's what you're looking for in a pair of earbuds, I've tried and failed to find anything comparable that didn't sacrifice on some other criterion (battery life first and foremost). But here's the deal about the Amazon Renewal thing... I got another pair of honest-to-goodness AirPod Pros in perfect condition with all the accessories at a sizeable discount (though as I write this the same product sold by Apple is discounted down to $190, which is what I paid for this pair :) ). While Amazon isn't my favorite company, and I've had both good and bad experiences with it, I'm happy to help reduce their (and by extension, other companies') environmental footprint by buying a perfectly good product at a cheaper rate just because somebody else's expectations of it weren't met. The packaging of all the accessories was great, the product itself was, as mentioned, indistinguishable from a brand-new set, and I was incredibly happy with them. Now, after finding out that my wife is one of the unfortunate people who are susceptible to vertigo from using noise-canceling headphones, it didn't make sense for us to have 2 pairs, so I decided to return the set I bought Renewed. After a little bit of uncertainty around the return process (the UPS driver will bring a printed label for my otherwise unlabeled package? And I wasn't actually present when he picked it up, so I had to take it on faith that they did, in fact, do that rather than just swiping the box...), I'm getting my full refund, and presumably, somebody else will become the new owner of this nearly-pristine product which reduced Apple's demand for more product to be created by 2 units (so far). In my mind, this program is a win for everyone (possible exceptions of Apple, and employees of Amazon) and the environment. I know what goes into electronics manufacturing (and what comes out other than products), so I'm really glad to see this happening. Super glad Amazon does all this. Review Title: I scored these at nearly half off — crazy deal
Review Content: I scored these at nearly half off — crazy deal. And because I saved that much, I had enough left to grab the Protect Plus 3-Year Plan. That covers accidental drops, spills, and even mechanical/electrical breakdowns after the manufacturer warranty ends. If something goes sideways, they repair or replace it — no drama. For headphones I’m using daily, that kind of peace of mind is a no-brainer. Mic quality is surprisingly solid too. I’ve used it for calls, Discord, and meetings — everyone said I came through clear without that muffled or cheap Bluetooth mic sound. Not studio quality, but way better than I expected for this price. They’re lightweight and super comfortable — no clamp fatigue, even after long sessions. I’ve worn these for hours at a time without needing a break. One feature I really like is the ability to stay connected to both my phone and my PC at the same time. No need to keep switching back and forth — it just handles both seamlessly. I can take a call on my phone, then go right back to music or Zoom on my desktop without touching anything. Bluetooth vs wired? Here’s how it works: when you use them over Bluetooth, you get everything — active noise cancelling (ANC), transparency/ambient mode, touch controls, built-in mic, auto on/off, and voice assistant support. But the second you plug in a 3.5mm cable, the headphones switch to passive mode — meaning all of that shuts off. No ANC, no transparency mode, no touch controls, no mic, no auto on/off. You basically just get basic wired audio like old-school headphones. It still works in a pinch, but you're giving up all the smart features. That’s why I mostly roll wireless — it’s just a better experience. Battery life is excellent — I’ve been getting about 40 hours with ANC off, and 30+ hours with it on. It charges back to full in around 2 hours. Plus, it’s got auto on/off when you unfold or fold the headphones, which helps conserve battery and adds to that premium feel. Bottom line — clean sound, smart features, solid mic, long battery life, lightweight and comfy, and backed by a strong warranty. And at nearly 50% off? No regrets. If you see it on sale, jump on it.       [Read more Read less](javascript:void(0))       9 people found this helpful Helpful  Sending feedback...Thank you for your feedback. Review Title: I purchased this phone because I could not find a phone that isn't massive but that still had the fe

I am tracking battery usage throughout the day with different levels of use- screen open and closed, dormant or playing videos - and it seems as though this particular device doesn't deplete battery any more than would be typical for a phone this age. I suspect this particular phone was very gently used to begin with. Example: battery depleted about 10-15% overnight with no use, not plugged in. With heavier usage the battery use goes up to about 10% per hour. Not sure if there's anything I can adjust/disable to make this more efficient. My old phone would give me 1.5 to 2 days of a charge with regular use so this will be an adjustment. The screen is beautiful and easy to see. Samsung is an upgrade overall for me and I am pleased with how smooth it runs. Nice on-screen keyboard, etc. I am not tech savvy so there are probably too many customization options for me personally. I really just want a phone that works well for calls, that I can text on and use internet and maps periodically. This should do the job just fine. No SD storage and no headphone jack. I guess that's becoming customary. The device doesn't seem flimsy at all. That being said, I would get a case ASAP in the event of inadvertent drops - it happens. Signal and connection seem good, as does speaker quality. The fingerprint sensor is on the side near the volume buttons. Not sure I am crazy about this placement and it never registers the first time for me, but I think that's probably a user (me) problem. Overall I had a very good experience buying Renewed. Anyone who is interested in trying a flip smartphone, this is very economical option without a major commitment.
